tickets.title: conver.js /find-omissions 呼び出しを現行コマンドと GRAPH パスへ修正
tickets.background:
src/runner.ts の Session D が、アーカイブ済みの旧コマンド /find-omissions-for-next-rfc を実行し、引数にも getSourceFromTickets() が返す metadata.source（RFC markdown パス）を渡している。現行コマンドは /find-omissions で、</path/to/*-GRAPH.json> 形式の引数を validate-graph-arg.js が存在検証する。正しい GRAPH パスは metadata.resolvedPaths.graphPath に格納されており（siprs 実例: ~/…/RFC-ROOT-GRAPH.json）、実行時は常にこのパイプラインが通らないため修正する。

### Goal
conver.js 実行時に、全チケットの review 完了後、Session D が現行コマンド /find-omissions を正確な GRAPH パス引数で実行できるようにする。

### Purpose
旧コマンド /find-omissions-for-next-rfc は .claude/archive/commands/ にアーカイブ済みで実行不能。現行 /find-omissions は </path/to/*-GRAPH.json> 引数を必須とし validate-graph-arg.js が存在検証する。現状は RFC markdown パスを渡すため常に失敗し、find 工程（次ラウンドの omission 生成）が実行できない。この欠陥を解消する。

### Motivation
conver パイプラインの最終工程 find（RFC ADDITION-002 の Goal Gate・機械的フィルタリングによる収束機構）を実際に回すには、現行コマンドへの移行が必須。

### Constraints
- 外部インターフェース（.claude/commands/find-omissions.md・validate-graph-arg.js）は変更しない。runner 側が正しい引数を渡すことに専念する。
- metadata.resolvedPaths.graphPath を主経路、metadata.source からの -GRAPH.json 導出を fallback とする。
- アーカイブ済み旧コマンドファイルには触れない。
- 既存の make/plan/start/review/resolve 工程の挙動を変えない。

tickets.title: conver.js find 後の Slack 通知を list-phases-and-tickets.js 結果＋統合成否へ変更
tickets.background:
現状、find 実行完了後は sendOmissionsNotification が生の OMISSIONS-*.json を Slack 通知するが、list-phases-and-tickets.js の結果（sendSlackSuccess、find 前）が既に飛んでおり OMISSIONS の二重通知は冗長。提案（受け入れ済み）: sendOmissionsNotification を廃止し、find 後に list-phases-and-tickets.js の結果（phasify 統合後の Tickets.json を反映）を送信する。さらに通知には『Tickets.json への統合まで全て成功したか、どこで失敗したか』を載せる。

### Goal
find 完了後の Slack 通知を、冗長な OMISSIONS 通知から『list-phases-and-tickets.js の結果＋統合成否』へ置き換える。

### Purpose
sendOmissionsNotification は find 前の sendSlackSuccess（list-phases-and-tickets.js 結果）と重複する冗長通知。さらに統合成否が通知に載らないため、find → phasify-omissions.js → Tickets.json 統合の成否を Slack 上で一瞥できない。

### Motivation
パイプラインの実行状態（特に find の統合成否）を Slack で確認できるようにするため。

### Constraints
- find 工程そのもの（.claude/commands/find-omissions.md・phasify-omissions.js）は変更しない。
- 通知送信は best-effort（失敗時もループを停止しない）。
- 統合成否の判定は決定的で副作用がないこと。

tickets.title: Add remove-stub.js for fail-safe STUB marker removal and wire usage into start/review/resolve commands
tickets.background:
### Goal
Provide a deterministic, fail-safe script (remove-stub.js) that removes a single resolved [::STUB::] marker line from a source file — and update the three pipeline commands (start-ticket / review-ticket / resolve-ticket) to instruct its use, so that marker removal is scripted and verifiable instead of manual and error-prone.

### Purpose
In the make→plan→start→review→resolve pipeline, resolving a STUB means (a) replacing the stub code with real implementation and (b) deleting the [::STUB::] marker comment line. Today (b) is done by hand-editing source files. There is no removal script, no wrong-line protection, no idempotency guard, and no test. Because find-all-stubs.js reports any line containing [::STUB::], a forgotten or botched manual removal leaves an orphan marker that fails later gates; a wrongly targeted deletion can destroy real code. remove-stub.js exists to make (b) mechanical, validated, and testable.

### Motivation
A repository audit (PX-118 investigation) found: (1) insert-stub.js is defensive (argument validation, ticket-exists check, duplicate-at-line guard, single-line invariant) but removal has no scripted counterpart; (2) the three command files instruct the AI to "remove the [::STUB::] marker" with no tool to do it safely; (3) no test anywhere covers marker removal. The pipeline First-Class Rule and gates already punish unmarked stubs, so the tooling must not be the weak link.

### Constraints
- remove-stub.js is Node.js CommonJS (project standard for .claude/scripts), no new dependencies.
- It must never write Tickets.json or Malfeasance.json; it only edits source files.
- It must never delete a non-marker line (wrong-line guard) nor a line carrying executable code.
- Removal targets only single-line // comments: marker format is "// [::STUB::] <ticket>: <reason> -- <plan>" per validate-stub-format.js / insert-stub.js.
- Follows existing defensive script patterns: insert-stub.js validation style, resolve-ambiguous-markers.js bottom-up editing.
- TDD Red→Green→Refactor is mandatory.

tickets.title: insert-stub.js validation hardening and ticket-add path PX removal
tickets.background:
### Goal
Harden insert-stub.js so STUB markers can only resolve to genuine future work (existing todo non-PX tickets), and route new omission tickets to the max phase so deferred STUBs always reference real, future work.

### Purpose
Prevent the pipeline timeline from being corrupted by STUB markers that reference already-processed tickets (non-todo status) or the ambiguous PX phase; keep every deferred STUB pointing at work that the next round will actually process.

### Motivation
Design review for PX-119 determined that the existing existence-only validation (ticketExists) is insufficient: it permits references to past tickets and to PX, both of which break the timeline. The todo condition, optional ordering check, PX ban, and max-phase append make the deferral path safe and mechanically verifiable.

### Constraints
No change to the phasify-omissions R<round> round-marking or to the runner loadPendingTickets semantics (verified safe via create-tmp-omissions.js non-reviewed pickup). --ticket-key stays optional. Error output must never halt the slash command (retry-until-success).

tickets.title: find-omissions: Preflight stub cleanup & No-External-Excuse enforcement
tickets.background:
The find-omissions pipeline does not converge: 63 unresolved [::STUB::] markers in the siprs crate still reference old completed ticket keys (P0-2, P1-3, P3-1, P3-2, P4-2, P4-3, P5-1, P5-2). On the first run of get-next-check-target-ticket.js, create-tmp-omissions.js runs find-all-stubs.js and mechanically clones each ticket by the key written in the marker. Every find-omissions round therefore re-clones past tickets into new todo tickets, and the loop diverges. Root cause: the AI used external dependency and awaiting human approval as terminal excuses instead of converting each blocker into an AI-executable work item (vendor and build PJSIP in build.rs, add cpal as an optional dependency, run bindgen). Absolute rule: there is no external; every blocker is a work item and approval is not a terminal state.

### Goal
Make find-omissions converge: after this ticket, no [::STUB::] marker may reference a past or non-existent ticket key, no marker may carry a terminal excuse (external / awaiting approval) without an AI-executable work item, and the command runs end-to-end without abort.

### Purpose
The marker key is a forward declaration of which future ticket resolves the stub. A stale key breaks provenance and mechanically re-clones past tickets on every round. The purpose of this ticket is to enforce that invariant mechanically and to give the executing AI concrete, self-contained instructions (stdout/stderr) for every required action.

### Motivation
Two implementation rounds already failed to clear 63 stubs and the loop diverged. The previous design allowed terminal excuses (requires external PJSIP, awaiting human approval) which stopped work instead of scheduling it. The user mandated an absolute rule: no external, no approval-shirking; every blocker is internal AI work.

### Constraints
- Generic, not siprs-specific: the validator and preflight must work on any directory plus any Tickets.json.
- The find-omissions command must never abort; it loops validate-fix-revalidate until green.
- New stdout/stderr messages must be English, self-contained, and Action-directive (remove-stub.js Error/Cause/Action pattern).
- TDD: all new scripts follow Red-Green-Refactor with contract coverage C001-C005.

testExceptions: The final judgment of whether a specific stub is actually resolved in code is not testable as an automated unit test because it requires semantic code inspection (the defect may be fixed through a different mechanism than described); the reason is that it depends on reading the implementation. This is not a defect: the scripts narrow candidates and emit file:line for AI verification, matching the pipeline division of labor (deterministic classification plus AI judgment).

Whether a resolution plan is semantically sufficient beyond the verb-plus-deliverable regex is not testable as an automated assertion because it requires intent judgment; the reason is that the lexicon and verb checks are hard gates and semantic sufficiency is AI-verified at Step 0. This is not a defect: the hard gates make terminal excuses impossible to smuggle through.

The AI fix loop (validate -> fix -> revalidate) as a whole is not testable as a single automated test because the fix step is AI judgment (rewriting a marker, creating a resolving ticket); the reason is that the loop deterministic parts (validator exit codes, zero-progress hard-stop guard) are unit-tested, while the AI rewrite actions are verified by review of the resulting Tickets.json and source markers. This is not a defect: the loop boundary is precisely the deterministic/non-deterministic division of labor.
acceptanceCriteria: Happy path: find-omissions on a tree with resolved-but-stale markers removes them via remove-stub.js; excuse stubs are converted to actionable plans or removed; after phasify every marker references an active ticket key; the command completes end-to-end without abort.

Error case: a stub containing a terminal excuse without a work item fails validate-no-external-excuses.js with exit 1; phasify rejects a merge containing an excuse stub; stderr messages give concrete file:line and an Action directive.

Edge case: MUST RESOLVE with no key is classified orphan and must gain a ticket key or be removed; a marker referencing a nonexistent ticket is orphan; an excuse phrase WITH an actionable plan passes; a marker referencing an R-round (past) ticket fails Check C.

contracts.precondition: Input is a [::STUB::] marker content string.
contracts.postcondition: Returns PASS or FAIL; FAIL carries the specific failing check and a required resolution.
contracts.invariant: A marker whose content contains a terminal-excuse phrase and no imperative work item always FAILS; a marker with an imperative work item always PASSES the lexicon check regardless of the phrase.

contracts.precondition: Tickets.json is parseable and a ticket key is extracted from the marker.
contracts.postcondition: Returns PASS iff the key references a ticket whose status is todo, in_progress, planned, or remanded.
contracts.invariant: A marker referencing a completed (reviewed or R-round), nonexistent, or absent key always FAILS.

contracts.precondition: A valid stub list and parseable Tickets.json are provided.
contracts.postcondition: Every stub is assigned to exactly one of resolvedCandidates, pendingObligations, orphans, excuses.
contracts.invariant: Classification is deterministic; pendingObligations contains only stubs whose key references an active ticket; resolvedCandidates contains only stubs whose key references a completed ticket.

contracts.sourceEdge: clone plus newKey to rewritten stubs
contracts.precondition: phasify clones a stub-derived ticket into a new phase.
contracts.postcondition: The clone stubs[].content ticket key and the source marker line (when --src-dir is given) are rewritten to the new ticket key.
contracts.invariant: No clone in the phasified output carries a marker key referencing a past ticket; a clone with a failing excuse stub is not merged.

contracts.sourceEdge: validate to fix loop to proceed
contracts.precondition: find-omissions is running and stubs exist.
contracts.postcondition: The command proceeds to Step 1 only when validate-no-external-excuses.js passes with zero failures; it never aborts on failures.
contracts.invariant: Each fix round either removes the marker, rewrites its content or key, or creates a resolving ticket, so the loop converges; a round with zero changes yet still failing is a hard-stop diagnostic.

- [Error invariant] On any validation failure, no ticket clone is created and no marker is modified; the pipeline state (Tickets.json and source files) is unchanged.

tickets.title: resolve-ticket: No-External-Excuse enforcement & integer step renumbering
tickets.background:
The resolve-ticket command is the implementation and resolution phase: the AI resolves warnings, stubs, and crimes here. It currently has three escape points that let the AI be lazy: (1) Step 5 allows deferral for vague reasons without forcing an AI-executable work item; (2) the Step 7.5 escape hatch explicitly lists blocked on external dependency and awaiting another team as valid reasons to defer, which is exactly the terminal excuse the project forbids; (3) the convergence loop checks stub and crime counts but never detects excuse-language markers. This ticket integrates the mechanisms built in PX-120 (preflight-stub-cleanup.js for the resolved-stub sweep, validate-no-external-excuses.js for excuse detection) into resolve-ticket.md as hard gates, renumbers all steps as integers (no decimals, no Step 7.5), and adds creation-time excuse rejection to insert-stub.js so a lazy marker can never be written. The resolve command must never abort: excuse detection enters a validate-fix-revalidate loop until zero excuses remain.

### Goal
Make resolve-ticket converge: after this ticket, every resolve run removes resolved-but-stale markers (Step 4), refuses lazy deferrals (Step 6), and completes only when stub count, crime count, and excuse count are all zero. No terminal-excuse marker can be created or survive a resolve run.

### Purpose
The resolve phase is where the AI has the strongest temptation to defer rather than implement. The purpose is to make deferral structurally impossible without an AI-executable work item and an active ticket key, and to give the executing AI concrete, self-contained instructions (stdout/stderr) for every required action.

### Motivation
The pipeline already diverged twice on the siprs crate (63 stubs referencing past tickets). The same lazy pattern appears in resolve: the escape-hatch text itself teaches the AI that blocked on external dependency is an acceptable reason to stop. The user mandated an absolute rule: no external, no approval-shirking; every blocker is internal AI work.

### Constraints
- Generic, not siprs-specific: applies to any directory plus any Tickets.json.
- The resolve command must never abort; it loops validate-fix-revalidate until green.
- All step numbers are integers (1-10); decimal steps are forbidden.
- The Prohibition (no ticket status changes in Tickets.json) is preserved; deferral uses /make-ticket.
- New stdout/stderr messages must be English, self-contained, and Action-directive.
- TDD: all new script changes follow Red-Green-Refactor with contract coverage C001-C004.

tickets.title: Shared function createTicketFromSource for dedicated ticket-creation scripts
tickets.background:
Goal: Provide the shared core used by create-resolving-ticket.js (find) and create-deferral-ticket.js (resolve) to create a quality NEW ticket from a source ticket's deep clone.
Purpose: A new ticket must inherit the source ticket's structural/relational identity (nodeIds, relatedTicketIds, referenceSection, referenceUrls, sourcePaths, rfcDiscrepancies) with ZERO loss, while its content fields are reset so the AI can rewrite them to the NEW work item — never a retry of the past ticket.
Motivation: add-omission-ticket.js already deep-clones (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify) in appendTicket, line 121) and targets the max real phase (lines 113-114), but it writes to _tmp-omissions-*.json, not directly to Tickets.json. find Step 1 and resolve deferral need direct Tickets.json creation (immediate known key for marker rewrite + Check C), non-PX max phase. A shared function avoids duplicating the clone/edit/append/validate logic across two entry scripts.
Constraints: (1) Must never lose relational fields (PRESERVE set: nodeIds, relatedTicketIds, referenceSection, referenceUrls, sourcePaths, rfcDiscrepancies). tickets.background:
Goal: phasify-omissions.js must always rewrite source marker lines to the phasify-duplicate ticket keys after a merge, so the find end-to-end flow (markers → active duplicates) works.
Purpose: The --src-dir flag is never passed by find-omissions.md Step 9 (phasify-omissions.js --graph=$ARGUMENTS), so rewriteSourceMarkerLines (which requires srcDir) never runs — source markers keep referencing the original Step-1 resolving tickets, which phasify freezes as R<round>. 【Constraints】No change to deferral/crimeDeferral/bulk seed behavior; no change to insert-stub/remove-stub/update-stub; backward compatibility for legacy single-marker manifests; C002 all-or-nothing preserved; the grouped manifest format is the cross-ticket contract with PX-130

tickets.background:
【Goal】Mechanize consolidate-stubs Step 4: replace N per-marker update-stub.js CLI calls with one batch command driven by a units decision file
【Purpose】batch-update-stub.js reads the AI-authored decision file, applies every marker edit atomically, merges duplicates, validates, emits the manifest, and runs a three-point verification
【Motivation】The per-marker CLI loop is repetitive and transcription-error-prone; review identified that no completeness check (漏れ) existed — a marker omitted from grouping would silently remain
【Constraints】The grouped manifest shape stays the PX-129 contract; update-stub.js and print-manifest-for-find-omissions.js remain the single-operation building blocks
scope: Path: .claude/scripts/tickets/batch-update-stub.js
Action: new batch consolidation script (read decision file -> resolve lines -> apply updateStub per marker -> merge duplicates -> gates -> emit manifest -> verify clean)

Detail: reads a units decision JSON [{unitId, resolveByTicket?, reason?, plan?, markerLines:[file:line,...]}]; resolves markerLines against the scanned markers; applies updateStub to each; derives keys when absent; merges true duplicates; runs no-excuse/format gates; emits the manifest via print-manifest logic; removes the decision file
Before/After: N per-marker update-stub.js CLI calls -> one batch command; AI authors one structured decision file
API: batch-update-stub.js <decision.json> [dir]; stdin may carry the decision JSON; output is the manifest path + counts + unassigned list
Schema: no Tickets.json change; the decision file is a new transient input consumed on success
Config: no new configuration
Dep: no new dependencies
Non-change item: update-stub.js / print-manifest-for-find-omissions.js keep their single-operation behavior
Non-change why: they are the building blocks; batch-update-stub.js composes them
Impact component: /consolidate-stubs Step 3-4; the completeness gap is closed
Impact nature: the pipeline becomes fully mechanical after one structured decision file; 漏れ/失敗/ゴミ are verified mechanically
Impact response: consolidate-stubs.md Step 3-4 updated; tests/batch-update-stub.test.cjs added
testIntegration: IT: units decision file -> batch-update-stub.js -> markers normalized + manifest file written + tags stripped + decision file removed -> manifest accepted by batch-create-resolving-tickets.js --no-write (one ticket per unit)
IT: a siprs-like fixture where one marker is intentionally omitted from the decision file -> batch-update-stub.js reports the omission
IT: Existing suites update-stub.test.cjs and print-manifest-for-find-omissions.test.cjs stay green
testExceptions: Item: cross-process crash between the manifest write and tag cleanup — Reason: cleanup runs only after a confirmed write; a crash between write and cleanup is an OS-level failure mode, not testable within this tool; this is not a design defect — Alternative: the write-then-cleanup ordering and the post-cleanup zero-tag assertion are unit-tested; crash-window behavior is out of scope.

Item: judging which markers are genuinely out of consolidation scope (already-active-key markers left unassigned on purpose) — Reason: scope judgment is an AI decision by design, non-deterministic, and therefore not testable as a mechanical assertion; this is not a design defect because the tool separates judgment (which markers to include) from mechanical coverage checking (scanned vs assigned) — Alternative: the mechanical coverage check is unit-tested; scope judgment is reviewed in review-ticket.

Edge case: a marker in the scan not in the decision file -> reported as unassigned (漏れ); an already-consolidated tree re-run -> zero edits

scope: Path: .claude/scripts/tickets/validate-stub-format.js
Action: add a --scan <dir> tree-scan mode to the existing single-string validator

tickets.background:
【Goal】Replace the multi-command Step 5 gate with one consolidate-stubs-gate.sh invocation and trim the accompanying explanation to operator-level meaning
【Purpose】The gate is currently 3 commands plus a fragile MANIFEST=$(ls -t ...) subshell that must be copy-pasted, and the explanation walks through each internal script (--for-consolidate / --no-write), which is noise to anyone treating the gate as a black box
【Motivation】Single-script encapsulation makes the gate repeatable, less error-prone, and testable; the description should say what the gate does (what blocks it), not how it is wired
【Constraints】The gate must run from the Tickets.json root; it exits non-zero on any real problem and passes for completed-key re-pointed markers; the Step 5 recovery sequence stays
scope: Path: .claude/scripts/tickets/consolidate-stubs-gate.sh
Action: new shell script — the blocking three-part gate for /consolidate-stubs Step 5

Detail: runs validate-no-external-excuses.js --for-consolidate, validate-stub-format.js --scan ., picks the newest manifests/CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-*.json via 'ls -t | head -1' and pipes it to batch-create-resolving-tickets.js --no-write; set -euo pipefail so any failure aborts with a non-zero exit

tickets.title: Make /consolidate-stubs a hard prerequisite of /find-omissions (manifest gate + Step 1 simplification + full-success artifact cleanup)
tickets.background:
- **Goal**: Make /consolidate-stubs a hard, mechanically-enforced prerequisite of /find-omissions. After this ticket, /find-omissions cannot run (its pre-flight exits 2) until a complete consolidated unit manifest exists under ./manifests/, Step 1 is a two-command manifest-driven flow instead of a 4-class manual classification, and a successful full run deletes the transient manifest + rollback artifacts.
- **Purpose**: Guarantee, via the pre-flight gate, that the pipeline consumes exactly what /consolidate-stubs produces. The consolidate Step 5 gate (consolidate-stubs-gate.sh) already proves: no orphan keys, no terminal-excuse plans, all markers re-pointed to valid keys, and a complete grouped unit manifest emitted. Once that guarantee is mandatory, find-omissions Step 1 no longer needs to re-derive it by hand — it just pipes the manifest into batch-create-resolving-tickets.js. This closes the loop so the two commands form one seamless pipeline (the handoff described in WORK-INSTRUCTION-CONSOLIDATE-FIND-OMISSIONS.md §5).
- **Motivation**: The current find-omissions.md Step 1 (L103-151) is a large self-healing gate: it classifies every marker into 4 classes (resolvedCandidates / pendingObligations / orphans / excuses) and gives elaborate manual manifest-authoring guidance. That logic duplicates guarantees the consolidation already enforces, so it is dead weight once consolidation is mandatory. Transient artifacts (CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-*.json, ROLLBACK-*.json) currently accumulate in manifests/ indefinitely — nothing removes them, and the `ls -t | head -1` selector grows fragile as they pile up.
- **Constraints**: TDD Red-Green-Refactor is mandatory (Supreme Law §1); every new script must be dedicated, testable, and default side-effect-free; cleanup must be idempotent and run ONLY on full find-omissions success (never after Step 1 alone — Q2); the manifest-existence check must be its own script, NOT embedded in validate-graph-arg.js (Q1 — that script's name/purpose stays narrow); ROLLBACK-*.json is removed at the same timing as the manifest (Q3 — a stale rollback would desync markers from the created tickets); cwd-relative manifest file paths (PX-137) are preserved; all messages are English, self-contained, and Action-directive.

acceptanceCriteria: Happy path: with a CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-*.json present, require-consolidated-manifest.js exits 0; find-omissions Step 1 is the manifest-driven pipe flow (review then commit); on full success clean-consolidation-artifacts.js removes the manifest + rollback + empty dir

Error case: with no manifest, require-consolidated-manifest.js exits 2 and prints “run /consolidate-stubs first (Steps 1-5), then re-run /find-omissions” to stderr; clean-consolidation-artifacts.js exits 0 (idempotent) when nothing to remove
Edge case: cleanup leaves non-artifact files in manifests/ untouched and keeps the dir when non-empty; C003 handoff test stays green; validate-graph-arg.js is untouched

**[Happy path] — the complete green run**: a fresh session runs /consolidate-stubs (Steps 1-5) → manifests/CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-<ts>.json + manifests/ROLLBACK-<ts>.json exist → /find-omissions pre-flight passes both `|| exit 2` gates → Step 1 pipes the latest manifest into batch-create-resolving-tickets.js (--no-write review prints {createdTickets, skipped, rewrittenMarkers, dryRun:true}, then the real commit creates one resolving ticket per (sourceKey, unit) group and rewrites every on-disk marker key) → the residual preflight-stub-cleanup.js run reports no new classes → the inspection/merge/rename steps complete → the final step runs clean-consolidation-artifacts.js → manifests/ is gone and the tree is clean

**[Error case] — the missing-prerequisite abort**: a fresh session runs /find-omissions without first consolidating (or after a successful run removed the manifest) → require-consolidated-manifest.js prints a `[find-omissions] BLOCKED:` stderr line with the cause (no CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-*.json) and the action (run /consolidate-stubs first Steps 1-5, then re-run /find-omissions) → exits 2 → the doc flow stops (`|| exit 2`) and zero tickets are created

**[Edge case] — idempotent hygiene**: clean-consolidation-artifacts.js run twice — the first removes the artifacts + empty dir, the second (nothing to remove) exits 0 with no output; a manifests/ containing unrelated.json keeps the file and the dir; a file named CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST.json (no timestamp) or ROLLBACK.json is not touched; the find-omissions handoff note and consolidate-stubs.md L157 sentence still match the consume-and-remove story and print-manifest C003 stays green

- **Goal**: enumerate-ticket-targets.js must stop emitting ORPHAN_TICKET_REF crimes for [::STUB::] text that lives inside quoted string literals or under test-fixture storage directories, so /make-ticket Step 8a no longer forces per-run classification of test data as false positives.

tickets.title: find-omissions: exclude PX phase (phaseId=-1) tickets from inspection queue, tmp-omissions, and R<round> marking
tickets.background:
Goal: Exclude PX phase tickets (phaseId = -1) from the entire find-omissions pipeline so the PX backlog is never re-inspected, re-queued into _tmp files, or rewritten to R<round> status.

Purpose: The PX phase ("[X] Independent Phase", phaseId=-1) holds backlog tickets (140 in tools/conver) that are not part of the phased make->plan->start->review lifecycle. /find-omissions currently inspects ALL reviewed/remanded tickets across all phases, so the PX backlog dominates the inspection queue (140 of 177 candidates in the current tools/conver Tickets.json) and gets consumed by round-marking, diverging from the user decision that PX is out of scope.

Motivation: Audit of get-next-check-target-ticket.js (via create-check-target-tickets-cmds.js / create-tmp-omissions.js) and phasify-omissions.js found PX tickets processed in 4 code paths: (A1) collectReviewedTicketKeys queues PX reviewed/remanded tickets; (A2) collectNonReviewedTickets queues PX non-reviewed tickets; (A3) STUB-derived PX keys pass mergeTicketSources unfiltered; (A4) markPreMergeTicketsReviewed rewrites every pre-merge PX ticket to R<round>. User decision: PX is out of scope everywhere in find-omissions.

Constraints: PX phase id is -1; detection via phase.id === -1 or ticket.phaseId === -1 (verified 0 mismatches in current Tickets.json). All 3 project roots (root, tools/conver, crates/siprs) carry byte-identical copies of the affected scripts (md5 verified) — identical changes must be applied to every copy. R<round> is written only by phasify-omissions; after exclusion PX tickets keep their existing status (reviewed/remanded). PX-1 remanded in tools/conver is normalized to reviewed by the user outside this ticket. STUB-derived PX keys must be filtered too (A3). add-omission-ticket.js appendFoundOmissions continues to stage NEW omission clones in the tmp-omissions PX phase — that is new work, not the PX backlog, and phasify re-phases it out; kept as-is.

### Goal
Every find-omissions artifact (inspection queue, _tmp-omissions, round-marking) is free of PX backlog tickets, so the omission loop converges on the phased P0-P22 work only.

### Purpose
The PX phase is the independent backlog. Inspecting/round-marking it is semantically wrong: PX tickets are not part of the phase-ordered lifecycle and their inclusion makes the queue diverge. Excluding PX makes /find-omissions inspect exactly the phased work that can be re-implemented.

### Motivation
The audit (this ticket Background) demonstrated PX is processed in 4 places. The PX backlog (140 tickets) currently constitutes ~79% of the inspection queue, churning the loop without convergence benefit. The user explicitly decided PX is out of scope.

### Constraints
- phaseId detection: effective = ticket.phaseId !== undefined ? ticket.phaseId : phase.id; PX when === -1 (0 mismatches verified).
- 3 roots (root, tools/conver, crates/siprs) must receive byte-identical changes (md5 verified identical today).
- R<round> remains exclusive to phasify-omissions; exclusion leaves PX at reviewed/remanded.
- tickets.ts loadPendingTickets/checkAllReviewed are unchanged (PX stays reviewed = processed).
- add-omission-ticket staging in tmp-omissions PX phase is NEW work staging, not the backlog; kept.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Eliminate the 4 manual-bypass incidents in the /find-omissions pipeline so the pipeline runs unattended from Step 1 through Step 11.

### Purpose
Each script must refuse to create an invalid state, and when an invalid state is detected it must fail loudly (exit non-zero) instead of silently corrupting downstream artifacts.

### Motivation
Real runs forced manual intervention: (1) resolving tickets inherited foundOmissions/originalTicketKey/sentinel and were misclassified, (2) phasify silently skipped marker rewrite because stubs lost the line key, (3) tmp-omissions findings fragmented across two files, (4) add-omission-ticket created duplicate clones for the same key. Each bypass required a human to repair state by hand.

### Constraints
Edit only tools/conver/.claude; crates/siprs/.claude must remain byte-identical; successful-path behavior must not change; every fix follows TDD Red-Green-Refactor; run-all.js must converge to exactly the 14 pre-existing environmental failures.

tickets.title: Set forNextRound=true in all ticket-creation cores
tickets.background:
### Goal
All mid-pipeline ticket creation (start/resolve/find) marks new tickets forNextRound=true so they are excluded from the current round's processing.

### Purpose
Preserve the 1-round-per-invocation boundary of conver.js: tickets added while a round is in progress must not be picked up by the same run's re-fetch waves.

### Motivation
Without the flag, the re-fetch wave design (PX-146) would immediately re-pick find-generated tickets and blur round boundaries. The current runner counts a ticket as reviewed without verifying terminal status, silently leaving holes.

### Constraints
Initial/setup creation (split-to-tickets, add-tickets-for-phase via bulkAddTickets) must NOT set the flag; only mid-pipeline creation paths set it. The shared low-level utility bulkAddTickets is untouched; the flag is set at the mid-pipeline call sites.

tickets.title: Clear forNextRound at round transition and exclude from re-queue
tickets.background:
### Goal
At the round transition (phasify-omissions.js merge into Tickets.json), clear forNextRound on ALL tickets so the next round can process them.

### Purpose
Make the phasify merge the single round boundary where deferred tickets are released.

### Motivation
PX-143 sets forNextRound=true on mid-round creations; without this ticket they would stay excluded forever. phasify must clear on ALL tickets (existing + merged), not only merged omission clones, because start/resolve/find-Step1 tickets already live in Tickets.json.

### Constraints
Only the phasify merge clears the flag. collectNonReviewedTickets must exclude forNextRound so find does not re-inspect deferred tickets. list-phases-and-tickets must not count them as pending.

tickets.title: Conver readers: forNextRound filtering, safety net, and --max-retries CLI
tickets.background:
### Goal
Make conver's Tickets.json readers (loadPendingTickets, checkAllReviewed) exclude forNextRound===true tickets, add the runLoop-entry safety net clearForNextRound, extend the Ticket type, and add the --max-retries CLI flag.

### Purpose
The readers define what counts as pending this round; the safety net releases tickets stranded by a round that did not complete find; the CLI bounds retries.

### Motivation
Without reader exclusion, forNextRound tickets would be re-picked by the re-fetch waves (PX-146) and checkAllReviewed would never become true, deadlocking find.

### Constraints
Existing filters (reviewed / R<round>) are unchanged; countPhasesAndTickets is unchanged; --max-retries must not collide with -r/--resolve-every (short flag -x).

tickets.title: Runner loop: re-fetch waves, retry cap, and break-after-find
tickets.background:
### Goal
Restructure runLoop so (1) it re-fetches pending in waves to rescue tickets that did not actually reach reviewed, (2) retries are bounded by --max-retries, (3) find runs exactly once when checkAllReviewed becomes true, (4) the loop breaks after find completes (incl. Slack) and conver.js exits.

### Purpose
When conver auto-terminates, far fewer tickets are left as holes, with no other UX change.

### Motivation
The current loop counts a ticket as reviewed after /review-ticket returns without verifying the terminal status, silently skipping holes.

### Constraints
maxCount stays a per-invocation budget of distinct tickets (retries do not consume it); reviewedCount stays a process-cadence counter (resolveEvery timing unchanged); retry-cap exceed notifies and continues (exit 0); break-after-find makes 1 invocation = 1 round.

[Change] per-ticket retry counter bounded by --max-retries (default 3); exceed -> Slack error notify and continue (ticket left as notified hole)
[Change] reviewedCount increments once per distinct ticket (first processing) preserving resolveEvery cadence
[Change] find trigger redefined to !noFind && checkAllReviewed()===true (evaluated at resolveEvery boundaries and end-of-wave)
[Change] after find completes: final resolve -> sendSlackSuccess -> consolidate -> find -> sendFindOutcomeNotification -> return (break)
[Change] runLoop entry calls clearForNextRound (PX-145) before the first loadPendingTickets
[Non-change] printCommandHeader and per-command session flow unchanged

tickets.background:
- Goal: Eliminate the recurring `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token` in pipeline-generated test files at the root, and prove the fix is safe and side-effect-free by automated tests (per user directive for PX-147).
- Purpose: `annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff.js:296-300` (AMBIGUOUS branch) prepends `[ambiguousComment, "", ...lines]`; the `""` renders as a blank line at the file top. Every test file starts with `#!/usr/bin/env node`, so the shebang moves to line 2+ and Node fails to parse. tickets.investigation:
## Evidence from root-cause investigation (2026-08-07, confined to tools/conver)

### 1. Direct defect — annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff.js:296-300
```js
if (definitions.size === 0) {
  const ambiguousComment = `// [::AMBIGUOUS::] Could not locate containing definition for changed line(s) in ticket ${ticketKey} — AI must resolve placement.`;
  const newLines = [ambiguousComment, "", ...lines];  // ← the "" becomes a blank line at file top
  fs.writeFileSync(resolved, newLines.join("\n"), "utf8");
}
```
When changedLinesToDefinitions maps no changed line to a containing definition, the array literal `[ambiguousComment, "", ...lines]` prepends an empty string; `join("\n")` renders it as a blank line between the AMBIGUOUS comment and the original content.

### 2. Reproduced failure (captured mid-cycle)
`tests/add-omission-ticket.test.js` was observed with:
```
1: // [::AMBIGUOUS::] Could not locate containing definition for changed line(s) in ticket PX-144 — AI must resolve placement.
2: (blank)
3: #!/usr/bin/env node
```
`node --check` → `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token` at line 3 (shebang is only valid on line 1). The uncommitted git diff confirmed the annotate script injected the marker + blank (message matches the line 298 template with ticketKey=PX-144). The pipeline AI later removed both lines manually; the file is clean again — the recurring self-heal cycle reported by the user.

### 3. Trigger — IIFE test wrappers are invisible to scope detection
`tests/add-omission-ticket.test.js` adds tests as IIFEs `(function testC005ForNextRound() {…})();`. Direct execution proved `findContainingDefinition(lines, probeLine, ".js")` returns null for a line inside the IIFE body. Cause: `DEFINITION_PATTERN_METAS` (15 patterns in scope-detection-constants.js) only matches line-start `function` / `name(` forms; `(function name() {` begins with `(` and matches none → `definitions.size === 0` fires the AMBIGUOUS branch.

### 4. Compounding — resolve-ambiguous-markers.js:205-206
```js
lines = lines.filter((l) => !l.includes("[::AMBIGUOUS::]"));
```
Removes only AMBIGUOUS marker lines; the blank line created by the annotate branch survives, leaving `\n#!/usr/bin/env node…` after resolution.

### 5. Invocation — runs every start/review cycle
start-ticket.md Step 5a injects annotations; review-ticket.md Step 5 verifies annotations and runs `--check-ambiguous` as a loop guard. The AMBIGUOUS branch therefore executes on every ticket cycle touching a file with unmapped changed lines.

### 6. Test coverage gaps (baseline: all green)
- annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff.test.cjs: 22 tests — processFile (AMBIGUOUS branch) untested
- resolve-ambiguous-markers.test.cjs: 9 tests — no assertion that resolution leaves no leading blank
- scope-detection.test.cjs: 20 tests — no IIFE cases
- scope-detection-constants.test.cjs: 6 tests — hardcodes pattern count 15

tickets.title: require-consolidated-manifest: PASS when stub scan finds 0 stubs, instruct skip Step 1
tickets.background:
The /find-omissions pre-flight gate require-consolidated-manifest.js blocks (exit 2) whenever no ./manifests/CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-*.json exists. But /consolidate-stubs only writes that manifest when there are [::STUB::] markers to group into units — print-manifest-for-find-omissions.js refuses to write when 0 tagged markers exist. Therefore a 0-stub tree legitimately has no manifest, yet /find-omissions is blocked from running its manifest-independent core: Steps 2-7 (the ABC contract-to-test inspection loop over reviewed/remanded tickets), Steps 8-10 (cleanup, phasify merge, phase rename). The prerequisite the gate actually enforces is 'no un-consolidated stubs', which is vacuously satisfied when the stub scan finds 0 stubs.

### Goal
- 【Goal】Make /find-omissions runnable in a 0-stub tree: the pre-flight gate passes (exit 0) when no CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-*.json exists AND the stub scan finds 0 stubs, and stdout tells the operator to skip Step 1 and start the Step 2 inspection loop.

### Purpose
- 【Purpose】The current gate blocks the entire /find-omissions pipeline whenever the manifest is absent, but the manifest is only produced when stubs exist. With 0 stubs the prerequisite is vacuously true, yet the ABC contract-to-test inspection loop (Steps 2-7) — the actual purpose of /find-omissions — is unreachable, so contract-to-test gaps go undetected in the pipeline's steady state.

### Motivation
- 【Motivation】A tree with all stubs resolved is the normal steady state of the pipeline. Without this change, /find-omissions can never run again after a full resolve, silently disabling omission discovery for reviewed/remanded tickets.

### Constraints
- 【Constraints】(1) Behavior must not change when a manifest exists or when stubs exist without a manifest — exit codes and the BLOCKED message stay identical. (2) The stub scan must reuse the same scan /consolidate-stubs Step 1 uses (find-all-stubs.js) so the decision is consistent with the consolidate inventory. (3) No new dependencies. (4) find-omissions.md Pre-flight must keep both gate lines (validate-graph-arg then require-consolidated-manifest), in order — the doc test asserts this.

tickets.title: conver.js EPIPE resilience: conver must not crash on SDK child-process errors
tickets.background:
### Goal
Make conver.js resilient to the claude-agent-acp child process crashing with an unhandled `write EPIPE` during session teardown, and make conver surface a fast, phase-attributable error instead of a generic `ACP connection closed` when a child dies mid-command.

### Purpose
The ACP pipeline is currently disrupted by an EPIPE crash in the claude-agent-acp child. The SDK's `nodeToWebWritable(process.stdout)` (utils.js:42-57, used only in `runAcp()` at acp-agent.js:3617) attaches no `error` handler to the wrapped stream, so when conver closes the child's stdout read-end and the child writes again, the socket emits an unhandled `error` event and the child dies. Conver must (1) prevent the child from hitting EPIPE by guaranteeing the child is dead before the SDK `connectWith` teardown closes the pipe (`shutdownChildProcess`), and (2) fail fast with a clear error when a child dies anyway (`runCommand` child-exit race). A process-level crash guard (`installCrashHandlers`) converts any residual unhandled error into a clean, logged exit.

### Motivation
The user observed the raw trace `Unhandled 'error' event / Error: write EPIPE / Node.js v26.5.0` right after the `🟢 /resolve-ticket P13-3: resolve` banner. The run then aborts via the generic error path with phase `unknown`, which is both confusing and unactionable. The parent conver process does not crash today (session.ts:116-117 attaches `on('error')` to proc.stdin/proc.stdout), but the child crash disrupts the run and the resulting error is misattributed.

### Constraints
- The SDK (`@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` at ^0.52.0) cannot be modified from conver; the defense must live entirely on the conver side.
- `withSession` spawns a real child process (`spawnAgent`, session.ts:71-128), so unit tests must use a mocked `AcpSession` / EventEmitter proc; real-pipe behavior is verified by integration.
- Child shutdown grace must stay short (CHILD_GRACE_MS = 2000ms) so the pipeline is not stalled by teardown.
- Existing error-path contract is preserved: command failures route through notifier.sendSlackError (3 retries) and then process exit.
- The new fail-fast error message must embed the command so runner.ts `getCurrentPhase` (keyword match) attributes the phase without modifying runner.ts.
scope: [src/session.ts] shutdownChildProcess(proc, graceMs) — add. async helper that guarantees the claude-agent-acp child is dead before session teardown: sends stdin EOF, sends SIGTERM, waits up to graceMs for 'exit', then SIGKILL if still alive. Before: withSession's finally does inline proc.stdin.end()+proc.kill() with no wait. After: teardown awaits child death so the child cannot write after the pipe closes (no EPIPE). API: new export used internally and by tests; signature `(proc: ChildProcess, graceMs: number) => Promise<void>`.

[src/session.ts] withSession finally — modify. Replace `try { activeSession?.dispose() } catch {}; proc.stdin?.end(); proc.kill();` with `try { activeSession?.dispose() } catch {}; await shutdownChildProcess(proc, CHILD_GRACE_MS);`. Also route the 30s init-timeout handler through shutdownChildProcess. Before: immediate kill races the SDK connectWith teardown (which closes proc.stdout read-end) against the child's in-flight writes → child EPIPE. After: the child is dead before the callback returns and the SDK tears down the streams. API: none (internal).

[src/session.ts] runCommand — modify. Guard `if (proc.exitCode != null || proc.signalCode != null)` before prompt; attach `proc.once('exit', onChildExit)`; race `nextUpdate()` against a `childExited` promise; remove the listener in a finally. Before: runCommand waits on nextUpdate and only fails via the SDK's generic 'ACP connection closed' (or the 1800s default timeout). tickets.notes:
### Implementation steps
1. session.ts: add `CHILD_GRACE_MS` and `shutdownChildProcess(proc, graceMs)`; 2. route `withSession`'s finally and the init-timeout handler through it; 3. add the child-exit guard + race + listener cleanup to `runCommand`; 4. refactor `disposeSession` onto the shared helper; 5. conver.ts: add `reportFatalError` + `installCrashHandlers`, remove the silent `uncaughtException` swallow and the stale comment; 6. entry.ts: call `installCrashHandlers()`; 7. write RED tests in session.test.ts and conver.test.ts; 8. run `make test-conver`.

### Risks
A child blocked in a write syscall (pipe buffer full) may not exit on SIGTERM — mitigated by SIGKILL after CHILD_GRACE_MS. Awaited teardown adds up to 2s per session; if the SDK's connectWith teardown ever precedes the finally, the child EPIPE could still occur, so the fail-fast race is the safety net. Replacing the silent `uncaughtException` swallow with exit(1) changes failure behavior from 'silently continue in unknown state' to 'log + exit' — intended, but must be verified against the night-loop use case.

### Caveats
The root cause lives in the SDK's `nodeToWebWritable` (no error handler on process.stdout); conver-side defense is a mitigation. The parent's per-stream `on('error')` handlers (session.ts:116-117) already prevent a parent-side EPIPE crash and are retained. `disposeSession` becomes a thin wrapper over `shutdownChildProcess` and is no longer dead code.

### Open items
Whether the loop should continue (skip the dead session and proceed to the next ticket) instead of exiting on child death — the current runner contract is stop-on-error; continuing is a design change for a separate ticket. Whether `uncaughtException` should send a Slack notification (needs error context that process-level handlers lack).

### Future improvements
Propose an upstream SDK fix: attach an `error` handler in `nodeToWebWritable` (or `runAcp`) so an EPIPE on the child's stdout is a handled disconnect, not a crash. Consider draining the child's stdout during teardown instead of kill-first if telemetry shows the SIGKILL path is hit often.

tickets.invariants:
### Normal establishment
- The claude-agent-acp child process is alive and responsive while a runCommand is in flight; runCommand resolves with fullResponse only after a stop update.

### On error
- If the child dies before a stop update, runCommand rejects immediately (never waits past timeoutMs) with an Error whose message embeds the command, exit code, and signal — the error is never swallowed.

### Internal state invariant
- shutdownChildProcess leaves the child process dead (exitCode !== null) when it resolves, and never throws (stdin.end / kill errors are swallowed). runCommand removes its exit listener in all completion paths (normal, error, timeout) so no listener leak or delayed unhandled rejection occurs.

### Boundary
- Child shutdown grace is bounded by CHILD_GRACE_MS (2000ms): if the child does not exit within the grace window it is force-killed with SIGKILL. runCommand's fail-fast applies even when timeoutMs is large; the already-dead-child check runs before session.prompt is called.

tickets.title: conver.js completion resilience: never crash on ACP connection close; reconnect and continue to full completion
tickets.background:
The ACP connection closes during resolve-session establishment (observed at P13-3 and P14-3, both right after the resolve banner). Two cascading failures occur: (1) the discarded connectWith return value (SDK runUntil) rejects with 'ACP connection closed' as an unhandledRejection, and PX-149's installCrashHandlers converts it into process.exit(1); (2) the claude-agent-acp child crashes with an unhandled EPIPE while writing its stdout via nodeToWebWritable. The runner also calls process.exit(1) on any session error (runner.ts:480). Requirement: conver must never exit except at a clearly defined completion point; it must reconnect and continue even when the internal ACP connection drops or unexpected errors occur, so the whole ticket set completes unattended (night loop).

### Goal
Make conver.js complete the full unattended ticket run even when the internal ACP connection drops or unexpected errors occur. Concretely: (1) the conver process must never exit on a recoverable session error (connection closed, child crash, EPIPE, timeout) - it disposes the broken session and continues, retrying the affected phase and, if it still fails, notifying and proceeding to the next ticket; (2) no unhandledRejection/uncaughtException may escape the session layer, and the crash handlers log-and-continue instead of process.exit(1); (3) the only exits are clearly defined completion points: all tickets terminal, maxCount budget exhausted, watcher time-window exited, or a startup config error that prevents any progress.

### Purpose
The ACP pipeline is a long unattended 'night loop': the user starts conver, sleeps, and expects every ticket processed by morning. Today a single ACP connection close during /resolve-ticket kills the whole process (PX-149's installCrashHandlers turns the unhandledRejection 'ACP connection closed' into exit(1); runner.ts:480 also exits(1) on any session error). A mid-run crash wastes the night and forces a manual restart. This ticket makes the session layer and the loop resilient so one transient failure never aborts the run.

### Motivation
The same crash has been observed at P13-3 (recorded in specs/PX-149.md) and again at P14-3 (the current report): the raw trace 'write EPIPE / Unhandled error event' plus '致命的エラー (unhandledRejection): ACP connection closed' right after the resolve banner. PX-149 addressed teardown-time EPIPE but not the connection-close at session establishment, and its new crash handlers made any unhandled rejection fatal (exit 1). The user requirement is explicit: the script must never exit except at a clear completion point.

### Constraints
- The SDK packages @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp (^0.52.0) and @agentclientprotocol/sdk (^1.0.0) are external; the fix must live entirely on the conver side.
- The existing error-reporting contract (sendSlackError with 3 retries) and the PX-146 retry/giveUp ticket mechanism are preserved and reused, not rebuilt.
- Session teardown must stay bounded (CHILD_GRACE_MS = 2000ms) so the pipeline is not stalled.
- TDD Red-Green-Refactor is mandatory; the process-level crash behavior must be testable (mock-based), and real-pipe behavior is covered by integration.
- Exit is only allowed at defined completion points; recoverable errors must never reach process.exit.

acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path] — With an ACP connection that closes mid-session (connectWith/runUntil rejects 'ACP connection closed'), conver survives: withSession rejects cleanly (no unhandledRejection), the session is disposed, the runner classifies the error as recoverable, retries the phase with backoff, and either succeeds on retry or gives up with a Slack notification and continues to the next pending ticket. After all pending tickets are processed (terminal or give-up), the loop returns normally and the process exits 0.**

**[Error case] — A persistent recoverable failure on one ticket (e.g., every session-establishment attempt fails) retries up to maxRetries, then the ticket is recorded in giveUp with a Slack notification (sendSlackError, phase attributed via getCurrentPhase), and the loop proceeds to the next ticket without exiting. The process never calls process.exit(1) inside the loop for a recoverable error.**

**[Edge case] — No unhandledRejection/uncaughtException escapes the session layer: process-level crash handlers (installCrashHandlers) log a distinctive '致命的エラー (uncaughtException/unhandledRejection)' line and do NOT exit. The process exits only at a defined completion point: all tickets terminal, maxCount budget exhausted, watcher window exited, or a startup config error that prevents any progress.**

contracts.precondition: ACP connection closes during withSession or runCommand (child exit, stream end, connection abort)
contracts.postcondition: conver process survives; the failure is delivered to the loop error handler as a caught rejection; the session is disposed; no unhandledRejection escapes
contracts.invariant: No unhandled rejection or uncaught exception escapes the session layer.

contracts.precondition: A ticket phase fails with a recoverable error (or retries exhausted)
contracts.postcondition: The loop retries up to maxRetries with backoff, then marks the ticket as give-up with Slack notification and proceeds to the next ticket; the process does not exit
contracts.invariant: process.exit is never invoked inside the ticket loop except at a defined completion point.

contracts.precondition: Session establishment fails with a recoverable error
contracts.postcondition: Establishment is retried up to a bounded number with backoff+jitter; on persistent failure the error propagates to the loop error handler
contracts.invariant: Establishment retry count is bounded.

contracts.precondition: Session teardown begins
contracts.postcondition: The claude-agent-acp child and its claude-code grandchild are terminated before the next session is spawned
contracts.invariant: No orphaned claude-code process holds the working directory after teardown.

tickets.notes:
Root cause evidence: SDK runUntil (sdk/dist/jsonrpc.js) rejects with 'ACP connection closed' when the connection closes before the connectWith callback settles; withSession discards the connectWith return value; PX-149's installCrashHandlers turns the unhandledRejection into exit(1). The claude-agent-acp child crashes on EPIPE via nodeToWebWritable (utils.js:42-57) which has no stdout error handler.

- [Implementation steps] (1) session.ts: add connectPromise.catch in withSession; catch the prompt rejection in runCommand; spawn with detached:true; extend shutdownChildProcess with process-group kill. (2) conver.ts: reportFatalError removes process.exit(1). (3) runner.ts: add isRecoverableError + retryWithBackoff + rework the catch block to retry/give-up/continue. (4) RED tests in session.test.ts / runner.test.ts / conver.test.ts. (5) update the existing conver.test.ts:159 expectation (a top-level runLoop rejection still exits via entry.ts catch - that is a defined completion point - but per-ticket errors never reach it).
- [Risks] (a) continuing after uncaughtException may leave a degraded process state - bounded by retries/timeouts; (b) detached:true changes child lifecycle (the child survives a parent crash until explicitly killed) - mitigated because shutdownChildProcess always runs in the withSession finally; (c) over-classifying errors as recoverable could cause churn - bounded by retry/give-up limits.
- [Caveats] the child's own EPIPE crash is external (SDK); conver can only reduce its frequency (grandchild kill) and survive it. The entry.ts top-level catch keeps exit(1) for structural failures - that is a defined completion point, not a mid-run crash. retryWithBackoff's delay sleep must not block the event loop (await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, delay))).
- [Open items] confirm the resolve-start connection-close root cause with runtime verbose logs (child exit code / stderr); decide later whether retry parameters should become CLI options.
- [Future improvements] upstream SDK PR to attach an error handler in nodeToWebWritable; a systemic-failure detector that stops early when all give-ups share the same signature; a resumable run manifest so a crashed invocation can resume instead of restarting.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】While a session command is in flight, the conver process holds no pending unhandled promise rejection: every promise created by withSession (connectWith), runCommand (prompt), and the SDK is either awaited or has an explicit .catch/.then rejection handler. The claude-agent-acp child is alive and responsive.
- 【Invariant on error】On any recoverable error (ACP connection closed, child exit, EPIPE, timeout), the conver process survives: the error is caught and routed to the loop error handler; the session is disposed; the child (and grandchild) are terminated; no unhandledRejection/uncaughtException escapes. process.exit is never called from within the ticket loop for a recoverable error.
- 【Internal state invariant】retryCount/giveUp bookkeeping is monotonic and bounded: each ticket's retry counter increments at most once per loop iteration, never exceeds maxRetries before give-up is recorded, and a give-up ticket is not reprocessed in the same invocation. shutdownChildProcess leaves the child dead (exitCode !== null) when it resolves and never throws.
- 【Boundary invariant】Retry/backoff parameters are finite and positive: establishment retries <= RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS, backoff delays within [RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS, RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS] with bounded jitter; the loop exits only when (a) no pending tickets remain, (b) maxCount budget is exhausted, (c) watcher window is exited, or (d) a startup config error prevents any progress - never mid-ticket.

tickets.investigation:
- Evidence from source investigation (PX-150):

1. Crash output anatomy: the report interleaves two stderr streams. (a) conver: '致命的エラー (unhandledRejection): ACP connection closed' - emitted by installCrashHandlers (src/conver.ts reportFatalError) which then calls process.exit(1). (b) claude-agent-acp child (stderr inherited, stdio:['pipe','pipe','inherit']): 'throw er; // Unhandled error event / Error: write EPIPE' at claude-agent-acp/dist/utils.js:46:28 inside nodeToWebWritable().write() - the child wrote to its stdout after conver closed the read-end; nodeToWebWritable attaches no error handler to process.stdout (utils.js:42-57).

2. unhandledRejection source (the discarded connectWith return value): src/session.ts:186 'app.connectWith(stream, async (ctx) => {...})' - the return value (rawConnection.runUntil(...), SDK acp.js connectWith) is discarded with no await/.catch. SDK jsonrpc.js runUntil: 'const closedPromise = this.closed.then(() => { if (opSettled) return new Promise(()=>{}); throw this.closedReason(); }); return Promise.race([opPromise, closedPromise]).finally(...)' - when the connection closes before the withSession callback settles, runUntil rejects with closedReason() = new Error('ACP connection closed') (jsonrpc.js:647). That rejection is unhandled.

3. SDK 'ACP connection closed' construction points: jsonrpc.js:452 (close() rejects pendingResponses), jsonrpc.js:647 (closedReason()), acp.js:180 (attachSession failUpdatesOnClose -> updates.fail). runCommand consumes the same rejection via nextUpdate (SDK acp.js:471 updates.reject), so the loop error path is reachable once the crash is prevented.

4. runCommand fire-and-forget prompt: src/session.ts:255 'void acpSession.session.prompt(command)'. SDK acp.js prompt() attaches .then(onRejected) internally (line 464-472) so the response promise is nominally handled, but hardening with .catch is still required so no rejection path can escape and the failure surfaces deterministically.

5. runner exits on any error: src/runner.ts:458-481 catch block calls sendSlackError then process.exit(1) (line 480). This is the loop's only error handler; a session failure therefore always kills the run today.

6. Crash handlers exit: src/conver.ts reportFatalError (line 16-20) logs and process.exit(1); installCrashHandlers (line 22-31) registers uncaughtException + unhandledRejection -> reportFatalError; entry.ts installs them before main(). dist/conver.js contains them (minified; '致命的エラー' is the 致命的エラー escape), confirming the deployed binary crashes identically.

7. spawnAgent already guards conver's own pipes: session.ts:124-125 proc.stdin?.on('error',()=>{}) / proc.stdout?.on('error',()=>{}) - conver does not crash on its own pipe EPIPE; the crash is the child's stdout (the child has no handler).

8. child lifecycle: claude-agent-acp/dist/index.js redirects console.* to stderr, registers an unhandledRejection logger, handles SIGTERM/SIGINT -> shutdown() (agent.dispose + exit 0), and connection.closed.then(shutdown). It does NOT handle a stdout 'error' event -> EPIPE crash.

9. PX-149 (787212e3) is an incomplete fix for the same symptom: its spec Motivation records the identical crash at P13-3 right after the resolve banner. It fixed teardown-time EPIPE (kill child before SDK teardown via shutdownChildProcess) and added fail-fast child-exit detection + crash handlers, but did NOT address the connection-close at session establishment, and the new crash handlers made any residual unhandled error fatal (exit 1).

10. Root-cause hypothesis for the resolve-start connection close: the resolve session spawns a fresh claude-agent-acp + claude-code immediately after the previous session's teardown. If the previous claude-code (grandchild) survives teardown (orphaned when the child is SIGKILLed after CHILD_GRACE_MS), it holds the working-directory session, and the new claude-code fails to establish -> the ACP connection closes -> the cascade above. Confirmation needs runtime logs (child exit code / stderr) in verbose mode. This is why the scope includes killing the grandchild at teardown (process-group kill).
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- Translatability improvements planned for the code touched by this ticket:

1. runner.ts catch block (lines 458-481): extract the error handling into named functions - classifyError(err) -> ErrorKind, retryPhase(...), giveUpTicket(...). Today the catch does four things inline (sendSlackError, console.error, the connection-hint block, process.exit) which cannot be read top-to-bottom as a narrative. After: 'const kind = classifyError(err); if (kind === "recoverable") { await retryPhase(...) } else { await giveUpTicket(...) }' reads as a sentence.

2. session.ts withSession (lines 169-218): name the connectWith-guard behavior with a comment explaining why connectPromise.catch(reject) is safe (outer-promise settle is idempotent), so the guard is self-documenting.

3. session.ts runCommand: the fire-and-forget prompt + nextUpdate loop is dense; extract the verbose chunk-printing (lines 281-296) into a named function 'writeVerboseChunk(msg)' so the loop body reads: send prompt; read updates; print chunks; stop on 'stop'.

4. Magic numbers: SESSION_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS and CHILD_GRACE_MS already exist; add named constants for retry parameters (RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS, RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS, RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS, RETRY_JITTER_MS) instead of inline literals.

5. Hardcoded recoverable-error keyword list: extract into a module-level constant array RECOVERABLE_ERROR_MARKERS used by classifyError so the list is not an inline magic regex.

6. Out-of-scope code touched only lightly (e.g., printCommandHeader) is left unchanged per the Boy Scout reasonable-scope rule.

tickets.title: Provider-agnostic model/baseUrl configuration (-m/-u) for arbitrary Anthropic-compatible providers
tickets.background:
### Goal
-m を自由なモデル選択、-u/--url を自由な baseUrl 設定として受け付けることで、conver が DeepSeek だけでなく OpenRouter / Ollama 等の任意の Anthropic 互換プロバイダーに接続して動作できるようにする。

### Purpose
現状は session.ts:91 の ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL と session.ts:94 の ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL が DeepSeek に直書きされ、-k も必須（cli.ts:84-88）のため単一ベンダーロックイン。ベース URL とモデルを外部から注入可能にしてロックインを解消する。

### Motivation
OpenRouter は https://openrouter.ai/api でネイティブな Anthropic Messages API を公開し、Ollama（>= v0.14.0）は http://localhost:11434/v1/messages を実装している。claude-agent-acp は Claude Code を起動するため、ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL とモデル env を差し替えるだけで両者へ接続できる。プロバイダーごとの対応を conver 内部に積まず、Claude Code の標準 env 契約に委ねるのが最小で堅牢。

### Constraints
- 既存の DeepSeek 夜間ループがフラグ無変更で動き続けること（デフォルト baseUrl = 現行 DeepSeek URL、デフォルト model = deepseek-flash）。
- 新規依存（npm パッケージ等）を追加しない。
- ACP セッションライフサイクル（session.ts spawn/run/dispose）の構造を変えない。
- プロバイダー検出（URL を読んで挙動を切り替えるマジック）を追加しない。baseUrl は raw パススルー。
scope: Change (path): src/cli.ts, src/session.ts, src/runner.ts, src/conver.ts とテスト4ファイル（src/cli.test.ts, src/session.test.ts, src/runner.test.ts, src/conver.test.ts）。ドキュメントは tools/conver/CLAUDE.md と RFC_ROOT.md。
Change (action): -u/--url オプション追加、-k の必須解除、baseUrl 末尾スラッシュ正規化、ヘルプ文言の一般化。spawnAgent/withSession のシグネチャ変更、LoopOptions.baseUrl 追加、起動ログへの baseUrl 行追加。

Change (api): CliOptions.baseUrl / LoopOptions.baseUrl / SessionConfig を追加。spawnAgent(apiKey, model) を spawnAgent(config: SessionConfig) に、withSession(cwd, apiKey, model, fn) を withSession(cwd, config, fn) に変更。runWithSession も同様。
Change (schema): データスキーマ変更なし。Tickets.json の構造・フィールドは不変。
Change (config): 新 CLI オプション -u/--url <baseUrl>（デフォルト https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic）。-k/--api-key が optional 化。env 経由の上書き（ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL 等）を尊重。
Change (dep): 依存追加なし。@agentclientprotocol/sdk 等の既存依存は不変。
Non-change (item): ACP セッションライフサイクル、Slack 通知（notifier.ts）、tickets.ts、watcher.ts、step-timer.ts、cron-scheduler.ts、check-and-start-loop.ts、process.exit の意味論（必須不足時のみ exit 1）。
Non-change (why): プロバイダー接続性の変更に閉じる。セッション管理・エラー回復は PX-150 で堅牢化済みの直交領域であり、本チケットで触れると回帰リスクが増える。
Impact (component): cli.ts（パース）、session.ts（spawn env）、runner.ts（baseUrl スレッド）、conver.ts（起動ログ）。影響を受けるテスト: cli.test.ts（全フラグ系）、runner.test.ts（baseOptions と withSession モック）、conver.test.ts（起動ログ検証）。
Impact (nature): CLI 表面の追加（新規 optional フラグ）と spawn env の変更。内部シグネチャ変更は TS 型レベルでコンパイル時に検出され、外部プロトコルへの破壊的変更はない。
Impact (response): フラグ無変更の既存呼び出しはデフォルト値により従来通り DeepSeek で動作。-k 省略時は警告ログを出力し、認証必須プロバイダーでは上流エラーとして可視化。ドキュメント（CLAUDE.md オプション表）を更新。

tickets.title: Implement /crystalize-readme: generate usage README or RESIDUE from RFC graph
tickets.background:
- 【Goal】RFC のグラフ（*-GRAPH.json）を入力として、ユーザー向け「使い方 README」を生成する。グラフ検証・OMISSIONS 残存・examples 欠落・grill 未承認などにより README を書けない場合は residues/RESIDUE-<ts>.md に理由を記録する。両系統の成果物とも末尾セクションは必ず「examples（実装サンプル）の仕様と設計」とする。
- 【Purpose】conver の内側ループで RFC → 実装 → 検証を回す過程で「実装はあるが使い方が文書化されていない」状態を解消する。グラフ由来の機械的目次＋実サンプル参照により README 生成の品質と再現性を上げ、実装漏れ・矛盾が発覚した場合は RESIDUE として可視化して将来 /drill-rfc-down でチケット化する起点とする。
- 【Motivation】siprs の RFC-ROOT-GRAPH.json は既に存在するが README.md は空（0 bytes）で、使い方ドキュメントが欠落している。手書き README はグラフと乖離しやすく、機械生成＋決定論検証により「グラフ＝実装＝ドキュメント」の整合を保つ。
- 【Constraints】(1) 決定論でできることはスクリプトに寄せ、AI は非決定論部分（目次編成・examples 仕様・本文合成）のみ担当する（設計原則 §5）。(2) 目次グリルは /grill-me-for-rfc 同様、AI 提案はチェックされ、ユーザーは Yes/No または ABC のみ回答（自由記述を要求しない）。(3) samples は examples に改名（siprs examples/ に整合）。(4) コマンド文書はまず日本語で書き、日本人ユーザー（本人）の点検後に英語へ翻訳する。

testExceptions: Item: Quality of AI-generated README/RESIDUE natural-language prose (TOC wording, examples spec synthesis, section body text). Reason: content synthesis is AI non-deterministic by design (determinism principle §5); the natural-language quality is not testable by an automated assertion because there is no objective correctness predicate for prose. Statement: this is NOT a design defect — the deterministic structure surrounding the prose (TOC validity, trailing examples section, RESIDUE header/inventory schema) IS asserted by validate-*.js in testUnit; only the prose itself is delegated to AI, which is the feature's explicit purpose. Alternative verification: structure validation scripts (check-toc-structure.js / validate-readme-output.js / validate-residue-output.js) + human review of the generated README during the /crystalize-readme smoke run.

Item: Interactive user approval in the TOC grill (Yes/No/ABC response). Reason: the interaction requires a human in the loop; the step is not testable as a pure function because it waits on a human's free choice. Statement: this is not an architectural defect — the scripted proposal pipeline around it (extract-toc-candidates.js → check-toc-structure.js) IS tested deterministically, and the interactive gate is inherently human-mediated by design (mirroring /grill-me-for-rfc). Alternative verification: manual smoke during /crystalize-readme execution; the deterministic parts (candidate extraction, structure validation) are covered by testUnit.

Item: AI's judgment in Step 2 when the graph has no examples-related nodes but examples/ has files — deciding whether to synthesize an examples spec anyway or record a RESIDUE reason. Reason: the decision requires semantic understanding of whether the implementation samples are user-facing, which is not testable by a deterministic predicate; the same input can legitimately produce different human judgments. Statement: this is not a design defect — the determinism principle (§5) explicitly delegates synthesis judgment to AI; the deterministic parts (node-kind extraction, file-existence checks, validate-examples-spec.js) ARE tested in testUnit. Alternative verification: human review during the grill; the deterministic existence checks are asserted by the check-readme-writable missingExamples condition test.
acceptanceCriteria: Happy path (a): a valid graph with no omissions and existing examples writes README.md to rfcDir, and the last section is examples (implementation samples) spec and design
Error case (b): a graph with unresolved omissions / missing examples / failed graph verification writes residues/RESIDUE-<ts>.md with the judgment reasons
Edge case: an invalid graph argument exits with a clear error (exit 2); an empty graph is handled without crashing; check-readme-writable is deterministic for identical inputs

**[Happy path] — a valid graph (clean verification, no unresolved omissions, populated examples/, grill status approved) → /crystalize-readme writes <rfcDir>/README.md** whose last section heading is 'examples (implementation samples) spec and design'; validate-readme-output.js exits 0; update-step-status.js records step4 in CRYSTALIZE-Status.json

**[Error case] — a graph failing any branch condition (unresolvedOmissions / missingExamples / graphVerificationFailed / grillInconsistent) → writes <rfcDir>/residues/RESIDUE-<YYYYMMDDhhmmss>.md** listing each failing reason; validate-residue-output.js exits 0; the smoke target crates/siprs/RFC-ROOT-GRAPH.json is expected to take this branch (siprs has unresolved OMISSIONS)

**[Edge case] — an invalid graph argument (non-existent path / malformed JSON / schema violation) → validate-graph-arg.js exits non-zero with a clear stderr message and NO output file is created; an empty graph (nodes:[]) is handled without crashing (branch b with missingCoverage reasons); check-readme-writable is deterministic for identical inputs (same branch + same reasons across repeated runs)

contracts.precondition: graph.sourceFile is a non-empty string path; the graph has already passed validate-graph-arg schema validation against .claude/scripts/rfc-graph/schema/graph.schema.json (required: sourceFile/mainLanguage/nodes/edges); sourceFile may be home-relative ("~/...") and MUST be expanded via fromHomeRelative() from .claude/scripts/lib/path-utils.js before path.dirname
contracts.postcondition: prints JSON {rfcDir: <abs dirname(sourceFile)>, examplesDir: <rfcDir>/examples, residuesDir: <rfcDir>/residues, readmePath: <rfcDir>/README.md} to stdout and exits 0; the RESIDUE filename is NOT derived here — generate-residue-filename.js (C004) produces RESIDUE-<YYYYMMDDhhmmss>.md at Step 4
contracts.invariant: examplesDir and residuesDir are always located under rfcDir — path.dirname(examplesDir)===rfcDir && path.dirname(residuesDir)===rfcDir for any nested sourceFile

contracts.precondition: graph is loaded and schema-validated by validate-graph-arg; check-readme-writable receives the graph path via --graph=<path> and the derived output paths via a JSON interface {rfcDir, examplesDir, residuesDir, readmePath, residuePath}
contracts.postcondition: returns (a) {branch:'README', reasons:[]} when ALL 4 conditions hold — (1) rfc-graph/verify.js --graph=<path> --source=<sourceFile> reports uncoveredHeadings=[], isolatedNodes=[], unresolvableRefs=[]; (2) no unresolved omissions JSON (omissions-schema.json) under rfcDir/omissions/; (3) examplesDir exists and every node of kind implementation_sample resolves to an existing file under examplesDir; (4) grill status CRYSTALIZE-Status.json records tocApproved:true && examplesApproved:true. Otherwise returns (b) {branch:'RESIDUE', reasons:[graphVerificationFailed|unresolvedOmissions|missingExamples|grillInconsistent, ...]} with a non-empty reason list
contracts.invariant: identical inputs always yield the same decision (deterministic) — no Date.now()/Math.random()/process-dependent value inside the decision; the residue timestamp is injected externally as an argument

contracts.precondition: TOC proposal is a list of headings with levels — input shape [{level:number, title:string}] (produced by extract-toc-candidates.js from graph nodes in document order)
contracts.postcondition: returns {ok:boolean, violations:[{type:'duplicate'|'skippedLevel'|'missingCoverage'|'missingTrailingSection', heading, detail}]}; violations is non-empty iff ok=false; on ok=true the TOC has no duplicate headings, contiguous levels (no H2→H4 skip), full coverage of top-level graph sections, and a trailing examples section
contracts.invariant: the trailing section must always be examples (implementation samples) spec and design — matched case-insensitively

contracts.precondition: a valid 14-digit timestamp string YYYYMMDDhhmmss is available, injected as a CLI argument (e.g. '20260817120000')
contracts.postcondition: outputs a filename matching /^RESIDUE-\d{14}\.md$/ (e.g. RESIDUE-20260817120000.md)
contracts.invariant: filename format is fixed and collision-safe per second — identical timestamp input yields the identical filename

contracts.precondition: README.md content is a non-empty string, provided via --readme=<path> or stdin
contracts.postcondition: passes (exit 0, ok:true) iff the last section heading is 'examples (implementation samples) spec and design'; otherwise fails (exit 1) with a clear stderr message naming the missing/reordered heading
contracts.invariant: every README ends with the examples spec/design section — the validator accepts no README whose last heading differs (case-insensitive)

tickets.title: Redesign /crystalize-readme Step 1 TOC grill: per-heading validated proposals and remove obsolete scripts
tickets.background:
- 【Goal】/crystalize-readme の Step 1（グリル—階層的見出し）を作り直す。sourceFile の内容を前提情報とし、「使い方に絞って技術的詳細内容に踏み込まない README.md の目次（階層的見出し）」を提案する。全ての見出しに階層的に一意な ID（H1, H2-3 等）を採番し、各見出しに対して「内容の提案」を A/B/C または Yes/No で回答できる形で提示する。AI はどれを推すのかを理由とともに明確にする。ユーザーは ID 単位で A/B/C/Yes/No で回答（自由コメント可）。全ての見出し項目と内容が確定するまで Step 2 には進まない。
- 【Purpose】現行 Step 1 の決定論的候補抽出（extract-toc-candidates.js）と構造チェック（check-toc-structure.js）は根本的に誤りであり廃止する。grill-me-for-rfc.md の Question Format Validation Gate（validate-question-format.js）パターンを参考に、提案一つ一つを専用スクリプト validate-toc-proposal.js で検証後にユーザーに提示する。AI の提案記述が揺れないよう機械的に検証する。
- 【Motivation】grill-me-for-rfc の validate-question-format.js と同一スクリプト・同一チェック方法は使えない（対象が RFC 設計グリルではなく使い方 README の目次グリル）。crystalize-readme 専用の構造化バリデータを新設する。
- 【Constraints】この改修で不要になるスクリプトはゴミとして掃除する。extract-toc-candidates.js / check-toc-structure.js とそのテスト（extract-toc-candidates.test.cjs / check-toc-structure.test.cjs）を削除し、コマンドファイルと設計書から参照を除去する。check-toc-structure が担っていた「末尾は examples セクション」の不変条件は新しいグリル設計で維持する。
scope: .claude/commands/crystalize-readme.md — modify: Step 1 を新グリル設計に書き換え（sourceFile 前提 / 使い方に絞る / H1・H2-N の階層的一意 ID / A/B/C or Yes/No / AI 推奨+理由 / validate-toc-proposal.js ゲート / 全確定まで Step 2 へ進まない）。Scripts 節から extract-toc-candidates.js / check-toc-structure.js を除去。
docs/DESIGN-OF-CRYSTALIZE-README.md — modify: §4 フロー / §5 決定論表 / §6 Step 1 / §8 スクリプト一覧 / §12 変更履歴 を新設計に更新。extract-toc-candidates.js / check-toc-structure.js の行を削除。

.claude/scripts/crystalize-readme/validate-toc-proposal.js — add: 構造化バリデータ（id 階層一意 / heading 非空 / contentOptions 2-4 / recommendation ∈ options / reason 非空 / 決定論）。CLI は JSON を stdin で受けて {valid,errors} と exit 0/1 を返す。
tests/crystalize-readme/validate-toc-proposal.test.cjs — add: C001 の Pre/Post/Inv を UT で全網羅（RED→GREEN→REFACTOR、node --test）。
.claude/scripts/crystalize-readme/update-step-status.js — modify: grill 状態を proposedIds / confirmedIds に拡張し、confirm-heading サブコマンドを追加。全提案確定時にのみ tocApproved=true を導出。
.claude/scripts/crystalize-readme/check-toc-structure.js — remove: 構造チェックは不要（ユーザー指摘）。
.claude/scripts/crystalize-readme/extract-toc-candidates.js — remove: 決定論的候補抽出は禁止（ユーザー指摘）。
tests/crystalize-readme/check-toc-structure.test.cjs — remove: 対応スクリプト削除に伴う。
tests/crystalize-readme/extract-toc-candidates.test.cjs — remove: 対応スクリプト削除に伴う。
API contract change: validate-toc-proposal.js は {valid:boolean, errors:string[]} を返す新規 API。update-step-status.js は confirm-heading <id> サブコマンドを追加。既存の approve-toc は全確定導出に置き換え。

Response: CRYSTALIZE-Status.json を拡張し、途中セッションは status サブコマンドで再開可能。Step 1 を再実行する場合は reset-to-step 1 で grill 状態をリセット。
