testExceptions: ユーザーによる ID 単位の対話確認（A/B/C/Yes/No 回答）は自動テスト不能 — 本質的に人間が介在する操作のため cannot test。設計欠陥ではない: 決定論ゲート（validate-toc-proposal）と完了ゲート（update-step-status confirm-heading）は単体/統合テストで検証され、対話ループ自体はそれらのゲートで境界づけられる。
使い方に絞った TOC の AI 合成（非決定論）は単体テスト不能 — 内容合成そのもののため not testable。設計欠陥ではない: 非決定論ステップは決定論的な validate-toc-proposal ゲートで制約され、ゲート自体は単体テストで全網羅される。
実ユーザーとの複数ターンの対話グリル全体は CI ではテスト不能 — ライブ端末を必要とする E2E/手動操作のため impossible to test。設計欠陥ではない: スクリプト化したターン列（validate-toc-proposal → confirm-heading → status 検証）を IT でカバーする。
acceptanceCriteria: Happy path: Step 1 で AI が各見出し提案（階層的一意 ID / A/B/C or Yes/No 選択肢 / 推奨+理由）を、validate-toc-proposal.js が valid:true を返した後にのみユーザーへ提示する。ユーザーが ID 単位で回答し、全見出しが確定したら Step 1 完了 → Step 2 へ進む。
Error case: validate-toc-proposal.js で invalid になった提案はユーザーへ提示されない。AI は errors[] に従い再構成し valid:true になるまで繰り返す。再構成しても valid:true にならない提案はグリルを先に進めない。
Edge case: ユーザーが自由コメントを付与しても AI は受け付けるが、確定には ID 単位の A/B/C/Yes/No 回答が必要。全 ID が確定するまで Step 2 に進まない。確定済み ID を後から変更したい場合は再グリルで扱う。

contracts.precondition: A heading proposal object {id, heading, contentOptions[], recommendation, reason, seenIds?} is passed to validate-toc-proposal.js. id は文字列、contentOptions は文字列配列、seenIds は既に提案済みの id 配列（省略時は空）。
contracts.postcondition: Returns {valid:boolean, errors:string[]} (exit 0/1). valid=true は以下のすべてを満たす場合のみ: id が /^H[1-6](-[1-9][0-9]*)?$/ に一致 / id が seenIds に含まれない / heading が非空文字列 / contentOptions の要素数が 2〜4 / recommendation が contentOptions のいずれかと完全一致 / reason が非空文字列。
contracts.invariant: Validation is deterministic — the same proposal input always yields the same output. A valid proposal always has a hierarchically unique id and a non-empty recommendation reason.

contracts.precondition: status.grill に Step 1 の提案済み見出し id 集合 proposedIds が記録されている。update-step-status.js に confirm-heading サブコマンドが実装済み。
contracts.postcondition: confirm-heading <id> は status.grill.confirmedIds に id を追加して stdout に確認メッセージを出力する。全 proposedIds が confirmedIds に含まれる場合のみ tocApproved=true になり、end-step 1 が steps['1']=done と currentStep=2 を記録できる。
contracts.invariant: 未提案 id の confirm-heading は exit 1 で拒否される。未確定 id が残る限り tocApproved は false のままであり、Step 1 は完了（end-step）できない。

tickets.background:

tickets.title: Rewrite /crystalize-readme Step 2+ into per-section inspection loop with marker-based README/residue generation
tickets.background:
### Goal
Replace the whole-document binary branching (Step 3 check-readme-writable.js -> README-or-RESIDUE file) with a per-section inspection loop. At the end of Step 1 a script (emit-readme-skeleton.js) mechanically outputs a README.md skeleton containing the confirmed heading group plus the trailing 'examples (implementation samples) spec and design' section, each section carrying a work-unit marker. Step 2 analyzes the actual src implementation ticket-by-ticket and transitions each section to either a complete description (marker removed) or an in-place residue record (marker replaced). A dedicated post-loop step resolves the examples section.

### Purpose
Never publish usage prose that cannot be confirmed to operate correctly. Every README section must be backed by implementation evidence (ticket -> spec -> src). Sections that cannot yet be guaranteed are not silently dropped or deferred to a whole-document file — they are recorded in place with concrete evidence of danger/omission/contradiction/deficiency plus the implementation reinforcement required. The in-README markers keep unprocessed work visible and machine-checkable.

### Motivation
The current all-or-nothing document-level decision discards every writable section into a single RESIDUE file when any one section is unwritable, and cannot express 'this section is guaranteed, that one is not' within one README. The redesign allows per-section convergence: writable sections are completed immediately while unwritable sections are recorded with evidence, and the loop keeps running until every TEMPLATE-README marker is resolved.

### Constraints
RESIDUE-<timestamp>.md output is abolished (residue is solely in-README markers). Marker taxonomy is a 1:1 pairing: usage sections carry TEMPLATE-README and resolve to complete or README-RESIDUE; the examples section carries TEMPLATE-EXAMPLES and resolves to complete or EXAMPLES-RESIDUE. tickets.background:
### Goal
Establish the foundation for a self-contained /drill-rfc-down: preflight emits a machine-bindable [VARIABLES] block, the archived io-boundary scripts are restored, the drill script directory is made self-contained, and session-init.js creates the isolated drill session.

### Purpose
- preflight.js must output all resolved pipeline paths as a [VARIABLES] block (VAR=value) so the AI binds them verbatim without interpretation.
- Restore insert-io-boundary-template.js and check-io-stubs.js from .claude/archive/scripts/grill-me-for-rfc/ (referenced by grill-me-for-rfc.md but currently non-executable).
- Make .claude/scripts/drill-rfc-down/ self-contained so drill never references the grill script directory.
- Implement session-init.js that creates/resumes the drill session in $SESSION_DIR = $RFC_DIR/drills.

### Motivation
- grill-me-for-rfc.md Step 7a references insert-io-boundary-template.js and check-io-stubs.js, but both were archived to .claude/archive/ - broken references make the command non-executable.
- drill must be self-contained; depending on the grill script directory couples drill to another command and violates the "drill de o kanjitsu" (self-contained) requirement.
- AI must not interpret path values; preflight must supply them mechanically to eliminate interpretation errors.

### Constraints
- New drill scripts are CommonJS (preflight.js pattern). Session-management scripts relocated from grill-me-for-rfc are ESM; module-type integration is resolved via package.json in the drill script directory.
- [::STUB::] marker absolute obligation; zero unresolved crimes.
- TDD Red -> Green -> Refactor is mandatory.

tickets.title: drill-rfc-down Step 1 machinery - update-status.js (drill-wide progress manager) + rfc-evolution.js (evolution verification)
tickets.background:
### Goal
Implement the two core scripts that make drill Step 1 (grill) mechanically managed and verified.

### Purpose
- update-status.js: manages the ENTIRE drill pipeline (Step 1-5) at sub-step granularity (1-1, 1-2, ...). Always outputs the next AI action and the step to proceed in English. Steps 2-5 are registered as step definitions (placeholders) so they can be extended safely when implemented later.
- rfc-evolution.js: capture (baseline snapshot), verify (append-only gate, delta extraction, well-formedness, contradiction candidates), clean (baseline removal). Artifact paths are deterministic under $SESSION_DIR; no path arguments are passed.

### Motivation
- Eliminate the possibility that the AI overlooks required work - update-status.js must always tell the AI what to do next.
- RFC edits must be mechanically guarded (append-only; destructive changes forbidden).
- Steps 2-5 are not yet implemented; the step schema must be extensible without breakage.

### Constraints
- update-status.js: step definition table covering Step 1-5 with sub-steps; operations set-step/set-state/inc-loop/show; English next-action output on every invocation; unknown step rejected.
- rfc-evolution.js: capture/verify/clean; deterministic artifact paths ($SESSION_DIR/baseline.json, $SESSION_DIR/delta.json); append-only via ordered-subsequence check; contradiction candidates via token match against GRAPH/Dirs-Tree/Tickets resolved from Tickets.json; exit 1 on violations.
- TDD Red -> Green -> Refactor mandatory; no stubs.

tickets.title: drill-rfc-down Step 2 graphify - evolution delta pipeline (graph-delta analysis, graph-delta.json, safe GRAPH reflection)
tickets.background:
### Goal
Implement Step 2 (graphify) of the drill-rfc-down evolution pipeline: consume Step 1 delta.json, determine the GRAPH evolution (new/modified nodes, new edges) safely, generate graph-delta.json, and reflect it into *-GRAPH.json via crud.js with a dry-run + AI engineering-expert judgment loop.

### Purpose
- Script analyzes delta.json sections against existing graph nodes and proposes new-node / modify-node / new-edge candidates (deterministic dry-run, no writes).
- Generates graph-delta.json (machine-readable: new nodes, modified nodes, new edges) as the handoff artifact for Step 3 (boundify).
- Reflects the evolution into *-GRAPH.json only after the AI judges the plan perfect, via crud.js (the only write path), then verify.js passes all checks.

### Motivation
- Step 2 must produce a graph-delta artifact so Step 3 (boundify) consumes the exact GRAPH evolution without reinterpreting the whole graph (lockstep delta pattern).
- GRAPH is the keystone of the 5 consistencies; unsafe changes cascade to boundify/split/implementation.
- The current Step 2 is a placeholder in drill-rfc-down.md.

### Constraints
- crud.js is the ONLY write path; verify.js must pass all graph checks (isolated nodes, uncovered lines, headingRefs resolution, uniqueness).
- Deterministic analysis (scripts propose candidates); AI makes the final judgment (dry-run -> perfect-before-write).
- Destructive changes (node deletion) are forbidden by default; only AI-explicit approval may allow them.
- graph-delta.json has a validated schema.

tickets.title: drill-rfc-down Step 2 graphify AI-as-engineer refactor - candidates info, staging, granular editing via crud.js, safe promote
tickets.background:
### Goal
Refactor Step 2 (graphify) so the AI acts as the engineering expert who DESIGNS the GRAPH evolution, using scripts as information-providing tools. The step driver must not auto-generate and apply the plan; the AI crafts it via granular crud.js operations on a staging copy, then --approve validates and promotes.

### Purpose
- graphify-delta-analyzer outputs graphify-candidates.json (new/modify/edge candidates + contradiction hints) as INFORMATION for the AI, not the authoritative plan.
- graphify-step gains --stage (copy the real GRAPH to a staging path + run the analyzer to show candidates) and --approve (validate the staging GRAPH with verify.js, then promote to the real GRAPH).
- Between stage and approve, the AI uses crud.js --graph=<staging> to design the graph (add/modify/delete nodes and edges, edit contracts) - no hand-edited JSON.
- Every editing operation runs schema validation; failures produce natural-language English Error/Cause/Action messages and exit non-zero.

### Motivation
- The current step driver auto-applies the analyzer delta on --approve, forcing the AI into a passive validate-the-script role instead of an active engineering-expert role.
- crud.js already provides complete granular graph editing tools; the step driver must expose them through a staging flow.

### Constraints
- Candidates and plan are separated: graphify-candidates.json (script) vs graph-delta.json (AI-crafted plan).
- --approve promotes only after verify.js passes on the staging GRAPH; a rejected plan leaves the real GRAPH byte-identical.
- Destructive changes (node deletion) are forbidden by default; AI explicit approval only.
- All editing scripts validate schema after every operation and emit English Error/Cause/Action on failure (exit non-zero).

tickets.title: drill-rfc-down Step 3: delta-only directory/file tree generation with boundify-style template headers
tickets.background:
drill-rfc-down Step 3 (boundify-step.js --approve) currently creates src files for NEW Dirs-Tree file nodes via commitSrcStubs(), which writes only a minimal one-line declaration stub (// <title> — declaration stub). Unlike the parent /boundify-graph (generate-dir-template.js + boundify-helpers.js), it does not generate the Initial Design Artifact — RFC-driven Implementation header (graph metadata, mapped node IDs, prose cross-references, query.js exploration commands) or kind/language-appropriate declaration stubs. This severs the provenance chain protected by supreme law rule 4 for files created by drill-rfc-down. This ticket adds a delta-only generator that reuses the parent boundify's exported module functions (discover, buildHeaderContext, generateHeaderComment, getDeclarationStub) to create ONLY the new files from dirs-tree-delta.json newFiles, with the full template header, while never touching existing files or directories (no overwrite, no delete, no --force).

### Goal
Give drill-rfc-down Step 3 the same rich, traceable file generation as /boundify-graph: new files carry the Initial Design Artifact header (graph metadata, mapped node IDs, stub markers) while touching only the delta.

### Purpose
Restore the provenance chain (supreme law rule 4) for files created by drill-rfc-down and give the implementation loop a self-contained starting template per new file.

### Motivation
The current commitSrcStubs writes a one-line stub with no header, so new files lack the design-traceability header /boundify-graph guarantees; Step 5 only checks file existence, not header content, so the gap went undetected.

### Constraints
Must never modify/overwrite/delete existing files or directories; must reuse parent boundify modules read-only; must not call generate-all-dir-templates.js (a CLI wrapper, not a module) and never pass --force/--delete; must run inside boundify-step.js --approve after validation and before promote.

tickets.background:
PX-170 added delta-only NEW file generation to drill-rfc-down Step 3 (boundify-step.js --approve). However, when graphify (Step 2) updates the GRAPH, existing files Initial Design Artifact — RFC-driven Implementation headers can become stale: new nodes mapped to existing files, modified node titles/kinds, and new prose cross-references are not reflected in the actual files. This ticket adds a safe header-refresh mechanism: replace ONLY the bounded header region (opening separator .. closing separator) of header-carrying files, preserving the implementation body byte-identical and preserving [::TICKET::] provenance annotations (above and inside the header). Cross-references are recomputed from the updated GRAPH by reusing boundify-tree.js computeCrossReferences. Declaration stubs are refreshed only in template-state files; implemented files never receive stubs. Files without the header marker are skipped entirely. No file is ever deleted, and no --force/--delete is used. Step 5 verify remains PASS because header content is not a checked consistency dimension.

### Goal
Keep existing files Initial Design Artifact headers in sync with the evolved graph after each drill.

### Purpose
Restore accurate mapped-node lists and prose cross-references in existing file headers without touching any implementation.

### Motivation
PX-170 only creates NEW files; existing files headers go stale whenever graphify changes nodes, mappedNodeIds, or prose cross-references.

### Constraints
Only the bounded header region is replaced; the body stays byte-identical; [::TICKET::] annotations are preserved; header-less files are skipped; no delete and no --force/--delete; reuse parent helpers read-only.

tickets.notes:
Design: reuse boundify-helpers.js generateHeaderComment and boundify-tree.js computeCrossReferences(graph, nodeToDir, nodeIdToFilePath) read-only via createRequire. Implementation steps: (1) derive refresh targets from graph-delta (files whose mappedNodeIds include newNodes/modifiedNodes, or files connected to new/changed prose edges); (2) parse each target file into { preHeader, headerRegion, body } by locating the first and last ^// =+$ separator lines; (3) skip files lacking the marker or the closing separator; (4) regenerate the header via generateHeaderComment with recomputed crossReferences; (5) preserve [::TICKET::] annotations from the old header region by re-inserting them after the opening separator; (6) for template-state files (body is stubs/comments only), refresh the declaration-stub region to getDeclarationStub(kind, lang); (7) atomic write (temp + rename). Risks: a hand-edited header loses custom lines on refresh (accepted — the header is a machine-generated provenance artifact and the body is never touched); [::TICKET::] annotations must be preserved exactly; template-state detection must be conservative to avoid stubbing implemented files. Caveats: only touch files with the exact marker; never use --force/--delete; the refresh is complementary to PX-170 (new files) — it handles existing files only. Open items: none beyond the refresh scope. Future: optionally expose the refresh as a standalone step.

- [Implementation steps] 1. deriveRefreshTargets(graphDelta, dirsTree) → paths; 2. parseHeaderRegions(content) → { preHeader, headerRegion, body }; 3. skip if !isHeaderCarryingFile(content) or no closing separator; 4. newHeader = generateHeaderComment(headerPaths, mappedNodeIds, crossRefs, ...); 5. preserved = extract [::TICKET::] lines from old headerRegion; 6. if isTemplateStateFile(body) → replace declaration stub; 7. fs.writeFileSync(temp) → fs.renameSync(temp, path)
- [Risks] hand-edited header custom lines are overwritten (accepted, body untouched); exact [::TICKET::] preservation; conservative template-state detection

tickets.investigation:
Evidence gathered from code investigation:
1. Real siprs src/lib.rs shows the header is bounded by opening and closing separator lines: line 11 // ====...==== (opening), line 38 // ====...==== (closing); [::TICKET::] annotations sit ABOVE the opening separator (lines 1-10) AND INSIDE the header region (line 12, between the opening separator and the title). The implementation body starts after line 38.
2. HEADER_SEPARATOR = 76 = characters (boundify-helpers.js:475), detectable by the regex /^// =+$/ for rust/go/typescript line-comment syntax.
3. generateHeaderComment(headerPaths, mappedNodeIds, nodeMetaList, crossRefs, graphBasename, sourceBasename, lang) in boundify-helpers.js (exported, line 563) builds the full header; the closing separator is emitted last (line 629).
4. computeCrossReferences(graph, nodeToDirMap, nodeToFilePathMap) in boundify-tree.js (exported, line 708) recomputes prose cross-references from an updated graph; the parent calls it with nodeToDir + nodeIdToFilePath from adaptBuildDirectoryTree (boundify-graph-to-dirs.js:437).
5. siprs has 49 header-carrying files in src; a sample shows ALL are implemented (0 [::STUB::] markers, 142-998 lines). Therefore the refresh is primarily HEADER updates for real projects; declaration-stub injection applies only to template-state files.
6. boundify-step.js is ESM; the createRequire pattern (used by dirs-tree-crud.js) applies for importing the CommonJS boundify-helpers.js / boundify-tree.js.
7. generate-dir-templates-delta.js (PX-170) already creates NEW files with headers; this ticket complements it for EXISTING files.

tickets.title: drill-rfc-down: detect orphaned edge contracts to complete the graph↔ticket contract relationship network
tickets.background:
Material evidence (PX-172 investigation): when drill graphify (Step 2) adds a new edge WITH contracts, the contracts are NOT mechanically propagated to the tickets whose nodeIds the edge connects. split-step.js accepts only --tickets and --dirs-tree-delta (no --graph) and has zero contract handling; split-delta-analyzer.js has zero contract handling; merge-contracts-to-tickets.js (the propagation mechanism) is wired ONLY to the upstream /split-to-tickets, not the drill evolution flow. As a result, new edge contracts become ORPHANED: they exist in the GRAPH but are networked into no ticket contracts, so they are never implemented or tested. This ticket adds a DETERMINISTIC, READ-ONLY DETECTOR (not an auto-assigner) that surfaces orphaned edge contracts with their connecting tickets and statuses, and a Step 5 verify gate that FAILS on orphans until the AI resolves each one. This preserves AI judgment (where a contract belongs: existing ticket with R-round vs new ticket) while eliminating silent orphaning. Per the drill design principle: deterministic facts (orphan + connecting tickets) are script-decided; semantic decisions (assignment) are AI-decided.

### Goal
Make every GRAPH edge contract verifiably networked into at least one ticket contract (orphan-free) after each drill.

### Purpose
Eliminate silent orphaning of edge contracts so no contract is left unimplemented and untested.

### Motivation
Drill split (Step 4) has no contract handling; edge contracts added by graphify are orphaned; merge-contracts-to-tickets.js is upstream-only.

### Constraints
The detector must be read-only (never auto-assign); the Step 5 gate FAILs on orphans but never auto-fixes; assignment stays AI-driven; no writes to reviewed/done tickets without AI decision.

tickets.notes:
Design: add detect-orphan-contracts.js exporting detectOrphanContracts(graph, tickets) → Array<{ contract, edge, connectingTickets: Array<{key,status}> }>. For each edge with contracts, for each contract, determine the tickets whose nodeIds touch edge.from/edge.to; if no such ticket carries a contract with the same id (matching merge-contracts-to-tickets.js canonical sourceEdge label from→to / internal / inbound), report an orphan. Wire into verify-consistencies.js as an additional high-severity dimension. NEVER auto-write to Tickets.json — the detector is read-only; the AI assigns via update-ticket.js or creates a new ticket. Implementation steps: (1) build nodeId→ticket map; (2) for each edge contract, find touching tickets and coverage; (3) collect orphans; (4) add the check to verify-consistencies; (5) expose to the split step as an AI aid. Risks: contract-id collisions across different edges (matching must include the edge endpoints); hand-edited sourceEdge labels may not match the canonical format (documented). Caveats: the detector must remain read-only (C002); the gate FAILs on orphans but never auto-fixes (C004). tickets.title: conver.js Watcher: 曜日指定 (daysOfWeek) サポートと node-cron timezone 統一
tickets.background:
### Goal
Watcher モードの定期実行設定（WatcherConfig）に曜日指定 daysOfWeek を追加し、特定の曜日にのみ定期実行できるようにする。同時に node-cron の発火時刻・曜日判定を config.timezone 基準に統一し、サーバTZと config.timezone の不一致による曜日境界ずれを根絶する。

### Purpose
現在は intervalMinutes / startTime / endTime / timezone の4項目のみで「平日のみ実行」のようなスケジュールが組めない。また node-cron は timezone オプション未指定のためサーバローカルTZで発火を判定しており、サーバTZ ≠ config.timezone の環境では、時間窓層（config.timezone 基準）と cron 層（サーバTZ基準）で曜日・時刻の解釈が食い違い、設定した曜日と実際に実行される曜日がずれる潜在バグがある。

### Motivation
ユーザーから「曜日は指定できないのか」という要求があり、調査の結果 node-cron v4.5.0 が schedule(expr, fn, { timezone }) で Intl.DateTimeFormat ベースの完全なタイムゾーン対応（曜日含む全フィールドのローカライズ）を実装していること、@types/node-cron v3 の ScheduleOptions に timezone が既に存在することを確認した。曜日指定と timezone 統一は同一の設定フィールド（config.timezone）を軸に一体で実装するのが自然である。

### Constraints
- daysOfWeek はオプショナル。未指定 = 従来動作（全曜日）。既存設定ファイル・既存テスト（watcher系80件）を一切壊さない。
- 新規 npm 依存を追加しない（node-cron v4.5.0 / @types/node-cron v3 は導入済み）。
- 曜日判定の基準は config.timezone を唯一のソースとする（サーバローカルTZに依存させない）。
- 曜日は cron 式（第5フィールド）ではなく時間窓層（time-window.ts）で判定する。cron 式に曜日を埋め込むと日跨ぎ窓（例: 月22:00-火06:00 + daysOfWeek=[1]）の翌日未明が cron 上「曜日不一致」で発火しないため。
- 日跨ぎ窓（startTime > endTime）の曜日は「開始日帰属」で判定し、窓の連続性を保つ。
- TDD Red-Green-Refactor を厳守。make test-conver で全テストがグリーンであること。
scope: src/watcher.ts (modify): WatcherConfig に `daysOfWeek?: number[]`（0=日曜〜6=土曜の整数配列、任意）を追加。validateWatcherConfig に曜日検証を追加（非配列・範囲外0-6・非整数・空配列・重複を個別エラーで拒否）。loadWatcherConfig は変更不要（既存の型経路で透過）。

src/cron-scheduler.ts (modify): start() の cron.schedule 呼び出しを `cron.schedule(this.#cronExpression, callback, { timezone: this.#config.timezone })` に変更。曜日は cron 式には埋め込まない（#buildCronExpression は intervalMinutes のみで不変）。

src/time-window.ts (modify): isInTimeWindow のシグネチャに第5引数 `daysOfWeek?: number[]` を追加。Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatToParts で config.timezone の時・分・曜日（weekday）を取得し、①曜日フィルタ ②日跨ぎ窓の開始日帰属ロジックを実装。既存の時刻窓判定ロジックは維持。
src/step-timer.ts (modify): isWithinTimeWindow(config) が isInTimeWindow の第5引数に config.daysOfWeek を渡す。checkStepDeadline はシグネチャ不変（内部で isWithinTimeWindow を呼ぶ）。

テスト4ファイル (modify): watcher.test.ts（バリデーション）、cron-scheduler.test.ts（options.timezone 捕捉）、time-window.test.ts（曜日・日跨ぎ・TZ境界）、step-timer.test.ts（daysOfWeek 伝播）に RED テストを追加。conver.test.ts は変更不要（isWithinTimeWindow / CronScheduler をモック済み）。

**Scope of changes:**
  - File/module path: src/watcher.ts, src/cron-scheduler.ts, src/time-window.ts, src/step-timer.ts（＋テスト4ファイル）
  - Action: modify（4モジュール＋4テストファイルに追加・変更）
  - Detail: WatcherConfig に daysOfWeek 追加 / validateWatcherConfig に曜日検証 / cron.schedule に { timezone } 付与 / isInTimeWindow に第5引数と曜日ロジック / isWithinTimeWindow の伝播
  - Before → After: watcher.ts「4フィールドのみ → daysOfWeek オプショナル追加」/ cron-scheduler.ts「schedule(expr, cb) → schedule(expr, cb, { timezone })」/ time-window.ts「isInTimeWindow(now,start,end,tz) → (…, daysOfWeek?)」/ step-timer.ts「config 4項目を渡す → daysOfWeek も渡す」
  - API contract: WatcherConfig.daysOfWeek?: number[]（公開型）、isInTimeWindow 第5引数（公開関数）を追加。他は互換維持。
  - Data schema: Tickets.json のスキーマ変更なし。Watcher 設定JSON にオプショナル daysOfWeek を追加。
  - Config/env: Watcher 設定ファイルに daysOfWeek（0=日〜6=土の整数配列、任意）を追加。env 変更なし。
  - Dependency: 変更なし（node-cron v4.5.0 / @types/node-cron v3 既存）。

**Out of scope:**
  - cron 式の第5フィールドへの曜日埋め込み（日跨ぎ窓と干渉するため不採用）。
  - node-cron への timezone 以外のオプション（例: タイムゾーン別実行時刻の独自変換）。
  - 通常モード（-w 未指定）の挙動変更。Watcher 概念の外。
  - WatcherConfig の既存必須フィールド（intervalMinutes/startTime/endTime/timezone）の変更。後方互換を壊すため。
  - conver.ts の起動パス構造変更（isWithinTimeWindow 呼び出しは透過的に波及するためシグネチャ不変）。

**Affected areas:**
  - Affected component: watcher.ts / cron-scheduler.ts / time-window.ts / step-timer.ts（直接）。conver.ts（起動時 isWithinTimeWindow に波及）、runner.ts（checkStepDeadline に波及）はシグネチャ不変で透過。
  - Nature of impact: API 表面（WatcherConfig フィールド追加、isInTimeWindow シグネチャ拡張）、動作（曜日フィルタ追加、cron 発火時刻の config.timezone アライメント）。パフォーマンス影響なし（判定は O(1)）。
  - Corresponding change: Y — 該当4テストファイルに RED テスト追加。conver.ts / runner.ts は変更不要。

tickets.title: conver.js Watcher: 時間枠外のフェーズ境界待機 (waitForWindow) と status 再読込
tickets.background:
### Goal
Watcher モードで、実行中に時間枠外に入った場合、各フェーズ境界（make/plan/start/review/resolve/find の直前）で枠内チェックを行い、枠外なら待機して枠内復帰後に同一セッションで再開する。

### Purpose
現在はチケット境界（runner.ts:399）でのみ検知し、枠外ならラウンドを終了するため、①チケット1件分のオーバーランが発生し得る ②枠内復帰後も次回 cron 発火（intervalMinutes、例15分）まで再開が遅れる。フェーズ粒度の待機・復帰（1分以内）で枠の意味を強める。

### Motivation
オフピーク実行（例: 19:30-09:30 の DeepSeek off-peek）で、枠内に戻った瞬間から作業を再開したい。現在の設計では復帰まで最大 intervalMinutes 分の無駄が生じる。

### Constraints
- セッション分割は禁止: make→plan→start→review は1セッションを維持（実装精度のための最適な区切りであり破壊禁止）
- 待機はセッションコールバック内の runCommand 間に置く（子プロセスをアイドル保持するが、これは Claude Code の通常動作と等価）
- PX-150 再試行の再実行防止のため、各フェーズ実行直前に Tickets.json の status を再読込
- クロック（now）と sleep を注入可能にし、実時間待ちを回避してテスト可能にする
- 起動時枠外の exit(0)（conver.ts:73）は維持
- 新規依存なし、TDD Red-Green-Refactor、make test-conver 全グリーン
scope: src/step-timer.ts (modify): waitForWindow(config, sleepMs=WINDOW_WAIT_SLEEP_MS, now=()=>new Date(), sleep=defaultSleep) を新規 export。WINDOW_WAIT_SLEEP_MS = 60_000 定数。isWithinTimeWindow(config, now?) に任意第2引数 now を追加（後方互換）

src/step-timer.test.ts (modify): waitForWindow のクロック注入テスト（枠内即return / 枠外1回sleep / 枠外N回sleep / config=null no-op / 境界時刻）を追加

testExceptions: 実時間の60秒待機を単体テストで検証することはテストランナーをブロックするため不可能。これは「決定論的だが根本的にテスト不能」という設計欠陥ではなく、クロック（now）と sleep を注入可能な設計にした上での「実時間経過そのものは検証対象外」という境界。代替としてクロック注入で「枠外→sleep→枠内→復帰」のロジックを実時間なしに検証する。
実際の cron 発火との結合（待機中に cron 発火がスキップされる実時間検証）は実時間依存でテスト不能。これは設計欠陥ではなく外部スケジューラ（node-cron）との実時間結合による制約であり、設計欠陥ではない。代替として isLoopRunning ガード（conver.ts の CronScheduler コールバック）の単体検証で担保する。
acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path]** 枠外に入ると各フェーズ直前で waitForWindow が待機し、枠内復帰（sleepMs=60秒以内）後に同じセッションで続行する。待機開始・復帰のログが出力される
**[Error case]** セッションが待機中に失敗しても PX-150 再試行 + status 再読込により完了済みフェーズをスキップして再開する。完了済みフェーズの再実行がないことを withSessionFailures で検証
**[Edge case]** 非 Watcher モード（watcherConfig 未指定）では waitForWindow が no-op で既存フローが不変。枠が再び開かない設定ミスでは待機継続（SIGINT で終了可能）。クロック注入テストで「枠外→sleep→枠内→復帰」を実時間なしに検証

contracts.postcondition: 枠内の時刻なら sleep を呼ばず即 return。枠外の時刻なら sleep(sleepMs) を呼び再判定し、枠内に戻ったら return
contracts.invariant: waitForWindow は枠内判定が true になるまで sleep を繰り返す。config が null/undefined（非 Watcher）なら即 return（no-op）

contracts.precondition: bindReviewInOneSession=true（既定）でチケット処理が開始される
contracts.postcondition: make/plan/start/review が同一 runWithSession 内で実行される（セッション分割されない）
contracts.invariant: チケット1件あたりの runWithSession 呼び出し回数が変更前と同一（bindReview=true 時は Session A の1回のみ）

contracts.precondition: チケットが make/plan/start/review のいずれかのフェーズを実行しようとしている
contracts.postcondition: 各フェーズ実行直前に Tickets.json の status を再読込し、その status に基づいてフェーズを実行/スキップする
contracts.invariant: 完了済みフェーズは再実行されない（PX-150 のセッション再試行時も含む）

contracts.precondition: waitForWindow が待機中（枠外）
contracts.postcondition: 待機中は isLoopRunning=true が維持され cron 発火がスキップされる。SIGINT/SIGTERM はプロセスレベルで効く
contracts.invariant: 待機中に runLoop が二重実行されない

tickets.title: workspacify-tree Parsing & Integrity 基盤 — 入力正規化・hash・見出し・segment再構成 (G0/G1)
tickets.background:
### Goal
/workspacify-tree の最下層として、単一 Markdown 仕様書パスを読み込み、BOM/改行正規化・SHA-256・ATX 見出しツリー・##単位 segment 化と「再構成完全一致」検査を担う決定論的 Node ESM モジュール群(8 lib)を Red→Green で実装する。

### Purpose
上位工程(抽出 PX-176 / ゲート PX-177 / publish PX-178)が「固定された入力 + 位置 traceability」だけへ依存できる基盤を作る。正規化後 hash は入力固定の唯一の根拠であり、以降の全工程の entry gate が参照する。

### Motivation
長大仕様書を「AI の一回限りの印象的応答」ではなく再現可能な工程へ変えるため、まず入力の完全性(復号可能/正規化可能/構造を完全分割可能/再結合で元の bytes に戻る)を機械保証する必要がある。ここが壊れると以後の全てが無根拠になる。

### Constraints
plain JS ESM(.mjs)・Node 標準ライブラリ(node:fs/promises, node:path, node:crypto, node:process, node:url)のみ・外部 package/network/LLM API/hook/Python 禁止・source range は正規化後テキストの 1 始まり line/column と 0 始まり UTF-8 byte offset・汎用性制約により特定プロジェクト語(conver/zasso/siprs 等)をコード・変数名・テスト・fixture に埋め込まない。
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) errors/fs-safe/hash/normalization → (2) markdown/headings → (3) segmentation/verifyReconstruction → (4) canonical-json → (5) fixture・unit・property を各段の Red で先行作成。
- [Risks] fence 状態機械の曖昧性(fence 内 fence)は仕様に無いため対象外とし、単純な 3 連バッククォート/チルダのみ扱う。
- [Caveats] source range の line/column は 1 始まり、byte offset は 0 始まり。UTF-8 なので日本語も byte 単位で数える。
- [Open items] level jump の即時 FAIL 化は設定可能にする(本チケットでは警告候補のみ)。
- [Future improvements] 高速化(巨大仕様書向けストリーミング)は acceptance 後に検討。

- Implemented Parsing & Integrity foundation for /workspacify-tree as ESM(.mjs) modules under .claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/lib/.

- No stubs/crimes introduced; no [::AMBIGUOUS::] markers.

- [Normal condition] 正規化は BOM 除去→改行 LF 化の順で決定的であり、末尾改行の有無を変えない。
- [Error invariant] 入力不適格時は WorkSpacifyTreeError を返し、成果物の作成・更新・置換を一切行わない。

tickets.title: workspacify-tree Inventory 抽出 — object/claim/規範候補と source traceability (G2)
tickets.background:
### Goal
PX-175 が生成した見出し/segment 構造を input に、object/entity 候補・claim/proof 候補・規範候補(MUST/SHALL/REQUIRED/必須/禁止/してはならない 等)・不変条件/エラー/test 候補を収穫し、全候補へ source_refs(§8.1 形式)を付与する抽出器を実装する。

### Purpose
AI 設計者(PX-177 の設計工程)が長大仕様を再読まなくても、候補の canonical_name/aliases/classification/出現位置/原文 snippet へ即アクセスできる inventory を提供する。

### Motivation
候補収穫は決定論的パターン処理だが人手では必ず漏れる。スクリプトで収穫し、AI は「確認・分類・統合」という意味論判断に集中させる。抽出器は候補を削除して情報を失ってはならない(指示書§8.1)。

### Constraints
plain JS ESM(.mjs)・Node 標準ライブラリのみ・外部 package/network 禁止・自動抽出結果を最終規範要件へ自動断定しない(曖昧候補は REVIEW_REQUIRED 記録)・各候補は {id:obj-######/claim-######, canonical_name, aliases, classification, source_refs:[{section_id,line_start,line_end,byte_start,byte_end,snippet}], normalization_status, owner_package:null} 形式・汎用性制約により特定プロジェクト語を埋め込まない。
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) harvestObjectCandidates → (2) harvestClaimCandidates → (3) harvestNormativeCandidates/harvestRequirementCandidates → (4) traceability → (5) alias-normalization → (6) inventory-report、各段で fixture を Red 先行作成。
- [Risks] 抽出器が「拾いすぎ」にならないよう、収穫は表形式/識別子パターンに限定し、意味論断定は normalization_status に委ねる。
- [Caveats] source_refs の byte offset は正規化後テキスト基準(PX-175 契約)。
- [Open items] 規範語句の辞書は指示書§7.3 の列挙に限定し、将来の追加は定数化して拡張する。
- [Future improvements] 抽出ルールの設定ファイル化は acceptance 後に検討。
Implementation summary:
- Implemented G2 inventory extraction on top of PX-175 libs (buildHeadingTree/segmentAtHeadings).
- TDD: wrote unit tests first (RED module-not-found), implemented extraction/traceability/alias-normalization/inventory-report to GREEN, refactored (phrase redundancy removal, alias shape defaults, cycle detection order).
- Test results: node --test -> PX-176 20/20 PASS; full suite 55/55 PASS (incl. PX-175 regression).
- Quality: run-quality-checks -> totalIssues 0.
- Provenance: .mjs unsupported by annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff (SOURCE_EXTENSIONS has no .mjs); canonical [::TICKET::] headers added manually to the 4 new lib files; test files annotated similarly.
- No stubs/crimes/[::AMBIGUOUS::] introduced.

- Contract coverage: @verifies verified via verify-red-coverage

tickets.title: workspacify-tree モデル・ゲートエンジン・schema — workspace/所有権/DAG/整合性 (G3/G4/G5)
tickets.background:
### Goal
AI の設計判断を「decision 入力」として受け、workspace モデル/所有権一意性/過剰分割リスク検出/adapter・DB 方針/依存マトリクス/DAG/JSON Schema を決定論ゲートで PASS/FAIL/REVIEW_REQUIRED 判定するエンジン層(lib 10 + schema 2)を実装する。

### Purpose
AI による設計(workspace ツリー・package カタログ・owner 割当・依存許可/禁止)は意味論判断として残しつつ、owner 重複・循環依存・禁止層・raw SQL・DB 固有型漏れ・REVIEW 未承認放置などの客観違反だけは機械で確実に弾く。

### Motivation
設計の品質は「AI が正しく設計する」だけでなく「客観違反を gate が確実に検出する」ことで保証される。全自動ゲート PASS と未解決 review 0 が COMPLETE の前提(指示書§2)である。

### Constraints
検査は純関数(入力 = inventory + decisions → 出力 = gate 結果)・決定論ゲートは「候補発見/制約検査」までで設計を自動生成しない・manifest 検証は標準ライブラリのみで動作する自前バリデータ(外部 AJV 等に依存しない)・JSON Schema は draft 2020-12 の schema ファイルとして配置・汎用性制約により特定プロジェクト語を埋め込まない。
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) workspace-model/LAYERS → (2) ownership → (3) boundary-review → (4) adapters/database-policy → (5) dependencies → (6) dag → (7) manifest-schema/decision-input → (8) validation(runGatePipeline)、各段で負例 fixture を Red 先行作成。
- [Risks] schema 自前実装は keyword サブセットを明示し、未知 keyword を無視しない設計にする。
- [Caveats] JSON Schema は draft 2020-12 の $schema を manifest 先頭に記録する(§12.2)。
- [Open items] REASON_CODES の追加は manifest の reason_code enum と同期して行う。
- [Future improvements] 追加 keyword 対応は本 schema が必要とした場合のみ実装する(YAGNI)。

tickets.title: workspacify-tree Orchestration・atomic publish・コマンド — run.mjs/render/command .md/acceptance
tickets.background:
### Goal
PX-175/176/177 の lib を統合する run.mjs(サブコマンド parse/extract/gate/finalize)、canonical JSON レンダラ、atomic publish、報告、既存 manifest 衝突時の BLOCKED、および .claude/commands/workspacify-tree.md を実装し /workspacify-tree を完成させる。

### Purpose
AI 実行セッションが「解析 → 設計 decision 作成 → ゲート → publish」を再現可能に駆動でき、成功時は単一の正本成果物 WORKSPACIFY-TREE-MANIFEST.json だけが仕様書ディレクトリへ公開される状態を確立する。

### Motivation
「AI の一回限りの印象的応答」ではなく、入力 hash・構造・完全性ゲート・所有権・DAG・manifest 再検証に支えられた再現可能工程として /workspacify-tree を完成させるため。REVIEW_REQUIRED の残置・既存 manifest の破壊・複数成果物の出力は COMPLETE を許さない(指示書§2/§13.2)。

### Constraints
成功時の公開成果物は 1 ファイルのみ・仕様書ディレクトリへ中間ファイル不可(scratch は os.tmpdir)・hook 不使用・外部 package/network 不使用・run.mjs に巨大ロジックを集めない(解析/抽出/所有権/依存/DAG/schema/atomic publish は別 lib)・canned decision fixture により統合/acceptance を決定論テスト化・acceptance(§14.4)全条件 PASS でなければ COMPLETE にしない・汎用性制約により特定プロジェクト語を埋め込まない。
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) render(canonical+self-hash) → (2) atomic-publish → (3) report → (4) run.mjs サブコマンド → (5) command .md → (6) integration/acceptance fixture とテスト。
- [Risks] 既存 manifest を誤って置換する事故は最も重い失敗のため、atomicPublish の hash 不一致 BLOCKED を最優先でテストする。
- [Caveats] scratch(decision 等)は os.tmpdir() 配下の一意ディレクトリを使い、仕様書ディレクトリへ中間ファイルを残さない。
- [Open items] 更新モード(別コマンド)は本実装では作らない(§13.2 安全側)。
- [Future improvements] 第二段階 /workspacify-allocate は本 manifest の stage2_handoff を唯一の引数として実装する。
Implementation summary:
- Completed /workspacify-tree orchestration: render(self-hash), atomic publish, report, run.mjs subcommands, command .md, integration/acceptance tests and aggregate runner.
- TDD: wrote unit/integration/acceptance tests, implemented render/atomic-publish/report/run.mjs to GREEN.
- Test results: PX-178 13/13 PASS; full aggregated suite 96/96 PASS (unit+property+integration+acceptance; incl. PX-175/176/177 regression).
- Quality: run-quality-checks -> totalIssues 0.
- Provenance: .mjs unsupported by annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff; canonical [::TICKET::] headers added manually to libs/run.mjs/tests.
- No stubs/crimes/[::AMBIGUOUS::] introduced. Command now appears as the workspacify-tree skill.

- Contract coverage: @verifies verified via verify-red-coverage

- Annotation: [::TICKET::] provenance present on all source files

tickets.background:
### Goal
指示書 docs/WORKSPACIFY-TREE_Complete_Implementation_Instruction.md の全工程を、AI セッションが実際に遂行できる精密な /workspacify-tree コマンドへ仕立て直す。最初に .claude/commands/workspacify-tree.md を日本語で実装し切り、英訳はユーザー指示があるまで行わない。

### Purpose
現行コマンドは骨格のみ(約40行)で、実仕様書に対して COMPLETE へ到達できない。証跡: objects-table.md(候補4件)で gate が虚偽 PASS / decisions.ownership を無視 / finalize が G2 REVIEW_REQUIRED で常時失敗。他の .claude/commands(boundify-graph.md 287行 / graphify-rfc.md)と同等以上の緻密さで手順・入力契約・エラー復帰を定義し、「AI の一回限りの印象」ではなく再現可能な工程を提供する。

### Motivation
/workspacify-tree は第二段階の唯一の入力 WORKSPACIFY-TREE-MANIFEST.json を生成する第一段階。コマンドが指示書を体現できなければ、以後の全工程が無根拠になる。

### Constraints
日本語で実装を完了させる。英訳・製本は将来のユーザー指示時に別対応。機械化は検証・収穫・publish までとし、設計判断(workspace/所有権/依存理由/承認)は AI が行う。既存 PX-175..178 実装を壊さない(全96テスト維持)。追加 dependency なし・ESM(.mjs)。成功時の公開成果物は WORKSPACIFY-TREE-MANIFEST.json の1つのみ。

### Goal

### Goal

### Purpose
第二段階は tree manifest を唯一の入力として workspace ディレクトリ分解と RFC seed 配賦を行う(§8/§9/§10)。そのため manifest は workspace.tree・ownership 表・dependency 表・stage2_handoff(contract_definition_order/contract_boundaries)を自己完結で持つ。

現状 manifest は adapters は database_policy のみ・stage2_handoff は objects の列挙と空 boundary で、ALLOCATE §7 に不合格。

### Goal
.claude/commands/workspacify-tree.md(日本語)を、Step 3 の「情報レベル向上反復手順」と各ゲートの意味・終了条件を明記した実用手順書へ強化し、手順どおり反復すれば生成 manifest が ALLOCATE entry 検査(PX-181 のパリティ)に到達することを end-to-end で検証する。

### Purpose
AI 実行セッションが「設計 decision 作成 → ゲート反復 → 情報レベル向上 → COMPLETE」を再現可能に遂行し、第二段階(allocate)と grill が高精度で進められる manifest を安定的に生み出す。

### Motivation
現行 .md の Step 3 は decision の書き方を示すが「どう情報レベルを上げるか・いつ完了か」が不明確で、反復が収束しない。

### Constraints
日本語正文。削除済み記述(言語方針・英訳注記など)は復活させない。常にカレントディレクトリ出力。T1/PX-180 のモデル・ゲートと T2/PX-181 の出力・パリティを利用。既存 106+ テスト維持。

- [Caveats] gaia 台帳は「例」であって対象 spec を gaia に固定しない(汎用性維持)。

tickets.title: workspacify-tree gaia 網羅化 T1' — inventory カテゴリ拡張と所有権・tree・boundary の実質強制
tickets.background:
### Goal
第一段階を gaia 台帳と同等以上の情報レベルにする前半。invariant / state machine / error code / required test を独立カテゴリとして抽出・inventory 化し、全カテゴリへ一意 owner を機械強制(unallocated の実質化)する。さらに非空 workspace では tree を必須化し、全許容 dependency edge と contract boundary の双方向網羅ゲートを導入する。

### Purpose
ALLOCATE §9.3/§10 seed が要求する「全 object/claim/invariant/error/test の一意 semantic owner」と §7.4 の tree・boundary 完全性を、第一段階のゲートで実質保証する。

### Motivation
現状 extract はこれらのカテゴリを terms に畳み、ownership 表は object/claim のみ。unallocated==0 が空集合に対して真になる(空洞化)。tree は任意、boundary は提供分のみ解決される(網羅未強制)。

### Constraints
判断は AI・検証は機械。既存 121 テスト維持。ESM(.mjs)。追加 dependency なし。
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) extraction カテゴリ分離 → (2) inventory/prepare 配線 → (3) ownership/validation 実質強制 → (4) tree 必須・boundary 網羅ゲート → (5) entry-parity 反映 → (6) テスト。
- [Risks] カテゴリ分離により既存 terms ベースのテスト/acceptance が影響を受ける → 後方互換維持で green を担保。
- [Caveats] tree 必須化は既存の tree 無し fixture を更新する。
- [Open items] カテゴリ語句辞書の拡充。
- [Future improvements] PX-184 の ContractEdge 化で category owner を境界に接続。
Implementation summary:
- extraction.harvestCategoryInventory + run.mjs pipeline/manifest category wiring; ownership/validation real unallocated; tree mandatory; boundary coverage gate and entry parity.
- Test results: 126/126 PASS (121 prior + 5 new). Quality totalIssues 0.
- Provenance PX-183 added to extraction/run/validation/entry-parity headers.
- No stubs/crimes/[::AMBIGUOUS::].
Review report:
- Static quality check: passed
- Translatability: no issues
- Contract coverage: @verifies verified
- Category inventory / tree mandatory / boundary coverage / dependency discipline / ContractEdge verified via unit+acceptance
- No open crimes, no stubs, no [::AMBIGUOUS::]

tickets.background:
### Goal
`/workspacify-tree` を実行する AI が、非決定論的な「意味論最終承認」を明示的に実施し、`semantic_review: { status: 'APPROVED', statement, approver }` を decision に記録してから finalize できるよう、`.claude/commands/workspacify-tree.md` に操作手順と成功条件チェックリストを追記する。

### Purpose
PX-186 で `lib/validation.mjs` の G2/G3 が `semantic_review.status === 'APPROVED'` を機械要求するようになったが、doc には semantic_review への言及が皆無(Step 3 の JSON 例・フィールド表・成功の定義のいずれにも無い)。doc 通りに操作する AI は semantic_review を書けないため、finalize はブロックされるのに原因を doc から特定できない。doc と機械ゲートの不整合を解消する。

### Motivation
「AI 最終承認ゲートを非決定論ゲートとして実装した」との報告を点検した結果、機械強制だけが存在し運用マニュアルが追従していないことを確認した。成功の定義は「全自動ゲート PASS・未解決 0」のみで、AI の意味論最終判断が登場しない。これでは非決定論ゲートが形骸化する。

### Constraints
doc は日本語のまま。## 言語方針ノート・英語訳ノートは二度と復活させない。--output-dir は追加しない(出力先は常にカレントディレクトリ)。BLOCKED / 既存 manifest 保全ルールは弱めない。既存 tests/workspacify-tree 145 テストは green 維持(変更は doc と command-realize テストのみ)。

tickets.background:
### Goal
workspacify-tree の全スクリプトを「完全なテストコードで正確動作が保証される」水準へ引き上げる。現状 line 96.09% / branch 82.71% / funcs 95.77%。特に run.mjs の CLI 負経路(branch 51.35%)と低分岐 lib(database-policy 50% / decision-input 60% / adapters 58.33% / hash・inventory-report 66.67% 等)を実行網羅し、測定 branch を全モジュールで 85% 超へ。

### Purpose
点検で「145/145 PASS は実装済みパスの正しさしか保証しない」と判定された。未実行分岐(BLOCKED / stale temp sweep / reload 不一致 / 書込失敗 / JSON 不正 / raw SQL・DB 型・migration 適用判定 / CLI 引数欠落・未知サブコマンド等)をテストで実行し、「未カバー挙動は仕様外」状態を解消して、テストコードによる正確動作の保証を完成させる。

### Motivation
「完全なテストコードによってスクリプトが正確に動作することが保証されているか?」という点検質問に対し、実測の branch 82.71% と run.mjs 51.35% を示して「保証には達していない」と回答した。このカバレッジギャップを埋めるのが本チケットの動機。

### Constraints
テスト追加を主とし、テストが露呈した不具合のみコード修正(最小・一般化、disguised green 禁止)。ESM(.mjs)・外部依存なし。テスト実行は `node tests/workspacify-tree/run-tests.mjs`(ユーザー記憶: Makefile 不使用)。semantic_review 等の AI 判断・ゲート仕様・manifest 形式は変更しない。既存145テスト green 維持。.claude/commands/workspacify-tree.md は変更しない(PX-187 が担当)。

tickets.title: workspacify-allocate 基盤: tree-manifest 入力ロックと workspace directory tree の安全な実体化
tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] A manifest passes the entry gate if and only if it satisfies: artifact_kind=workspacify-tree-manifest, status=COMPLETE, integrity self-hash matches (computeSelfHash over empty-hash), integrity.reload_validation=PASS, final_audit zero-count fields (orphan_object_count, orphan_claim_count, owner_collision_count, unknown_dependency_count, forbidden_dependency_count, layer_violation_count, cycle_count, review_required_count, unresolved_count, unallocated_count) are 0 and final_audit.status=PASS, stage2_handoff.eligible=true with entry_gate.required_status=COMPLETE, dependencies.orientation=consumer_to_direct_dependency, edge<->boundary bidirectional coverage, ownership entries reference catalog packages, and the co-located specification re-hashes to input.source_hash.
- [Error invariant] On any FAIL/BLOCKED the workspace root and the manifest are never modified: no directory is created or removed, no staging artifact remains inside the workspace, and the process exits non-zero with a gate-id + human fix hint.
- [Internal state invariant] The directory plan is a pure function of (tree, packages): it enumerates every ancestor and leaf exactly once, is sorted, contains no duplicate relative path, contains no path outside the root, and its leaf set equals the package path set (bijection) whenever packages are non-empty; empty workspace (no packages) yields an empty plan only when workspace.tree is also empty.
- [Boundary invariant] For every candidate path: rejected if empty, absolute, contains a .. segment, a NUL byte, a drive letter, or a UNC prefix, or resolves outside the root via path.relative; symbolic links are never followed to write outside the root (lstat checks on every existing ancestor of a planned leaf).
tickets.background:
### Goal
Implement the stage-2 base layer of /workspacify-allocate: a machine-deterministic input lock over the stage-1 WORKSPACIFY-TREE-MANIFEST.json plus a safe, rollback-capable materialization of the workspace directory tree into the manifest's own directory. The output of this ticket is reusable modules only; no CLI subcommand is composed until PX-191.

### Purpose
The corrected stage-2 contract (see docs/WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE_Complete_Implementation_Instruction.md fatal-mistake analysis) is: take the single tree manifest as the only argument and begin by creating the real directory tree in the SAME directory as the manifest. Creating a second authoritative WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json is NOT the goal; WIC/WIG global-graph machinery (doc §11-§15) is rejected. This ticket establishes the trusted input boundary (manifest + co-located original specification re-hash) and the only deterministic half of materialization (directories), so PX-190 can place RFC seeds and PX-191 can wire the command.

### Motivation
Stage-1 (PX-175..PX-178, PX-187, PX-188) already validated ownership/DAG/layer/cardinality and published WORKSPACIFY-TREE-MANIFEST.json (status COMPLETE, integrity.manifest_hash, stage2_handoff.eligible true). Without a hardened entry gate and a path-safe directory plan, any seed written by PX-190 could land outside the workspace, collide with existing files, or be published partially. Path traversal / symlink escape / partial output on failure are the concrete risks this ticket removes by construction.

### Constraints
- Node.js ESM (.mjs) only; stdlib (node:fs, node:path, node:crypto, node:os, node:process). No external network, no hooks, no Python.
- Reuse the stage-1 sibling library by import (.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/lib/*.mjs) for hash, normalization, canonical JSON, manifest schema validation, self-hash, fs-safe, errors, workspace-model. Do not fork those modules (DRY).
- Workspace root is fixed to the manifest's parent directory (never guessed from cwd/env/branch; never an alternate root).
- Output policy: fresh workspace only. Any planned path that already exists as a file, symlink, or non-empty directory => BLOCKED (non-zero exit, nothing mutated). No merge/overwrite/delete of pre-existing entries. Update mode is a future phase and is explicitly out of scope.
- Every failure path leaves the workspace byte-identical to its pre-run state (rollback) and never writes seeds (PX-190) or any allocate manifest (rejected design).
- Determinism: identical manifest produces an identical directory plan; re-running the module functions is side-effect free except explicit publish/cleanup calls.
scope:
**Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**
  - .claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/lib/tree-manifest-input.mjs — ADD. loadTreeManifest(absPath): readability/UTF-8/non-empty/JSON-parse checks; checkAllocateEntryGate(manifest, manifestDir): schema-validate against ../workspacify-tree/schemas/workspacify-tree-manifest.schema.json (loadSchema/validateAgainstSchema), computeSelfHash equality, status/final_audit/stage2_handoff checks (mirroring entry-parity FINAL_AUDIT_ZERO_COUNTS), dependencies orientation + edge<->boundary parity, ownership entries resolve to catalog packages, category inventory ownership; readManifestSource(manifest, manifestDir): resolves <manifestDir>/<input.spec_path>, re-hashes normalized bytes with input.source_hash (mismatch/absence => WorkSpacifyTreeError gateId G0.3 BLOCKED), returns {sourceText, sourceHash}. Before: no stage-2 input path exists. After: trusted input record consumed by PX-190/191.
  - .claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/lib/path-safety.mjs — ADD. classifyUnsafePath(relPath) returns reasons (empty/absolute/.. segment/NUL/drive/UNC/mixed separators); resolvePackagePath(root, packagePath) uses path.resolve + path.relative containment (never a plain string prefix); assertContained(root, absPath, {lstat}) rejects symlink escapes by lstat-ing existing ancestors; exposes SAFE constants. Before: none. After: every planned directory is proven inside root.
  - .claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/lib/directory-plan.mjs — ADD. buildDirectoryPlan({tree, packages}): reuses validateWorkspaceTree/validatePackageCatalog, computes sorted unique relative directory set (ancestors + leaves), returns {relativeDirs, packageLeafByPackageId, consistent, errors}; enforces leaf<->package bijection when packages non-empty and tree non-empty. Before: none. After: deterministic plan object.
  - .claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/lib/tree-staging.mjs — ADD. checkExistingOutputPolicy(root, plan): any planned path exists as file/symlink/non-empty dir => BLOCKED (empty dirs along ancestors allowed); createStagingRoot(root): mkdtemp <root>/.workspacify-allocate-stage-<pid>-<rand>; materializeDirectories(stagingRoot, plan); verifyStaging(stagingRoot, plan): realized relative set equals plan, no unexpected files/symlinks; publishStagedTree(stagingRoot, root, plan): per-top-level-dir atomic fs.rename with rollbackPublished on failure, then verifyDirectorySet(root, plan); cleanupStaging. Before: none. After: real directories under the manifest dir appear only after every gate PASS, atomically, with rollback.
  - .claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/lib/errors.mjs, hash.mjs, canonical-json.mjs — REMOVE from target list if reuse-by-import wins: these are imported from ../workspacify-tree/lib/{errors,hash,canonical-json}.mjs and NOT duplicated (DRY). The final implementation target list keeps only the four new modules above.
  - tests/workspacify-allocate/unit/tree-manifest-input.test.mjs — ADD. Entry-gate unit tests (below).
  - tests/workspacify-allocate/unit/path-safety.test.mjs — ADD.
  - tests/workspacify-allocate/unit/directory-plan.test.mjs — ADD.
  - tests/workspacify-allocate/unit/tree-staging.test.mjs — ADD.
  - tests/workspacify-allocate/unit/allocate-lib-branch-coverage.test.mjs — ADD (branch-coverage hardening for the four lib modules; targets >=85% branch per module).
  - tests/workspacify-allocate/integration/materialize-tree.test.mjs — ADD (temp-dir integration for staging/publish/rollback).
  - tests/workspacify-allocate/run-tests.mjs — ADD (aggregate runner mirroring tests/workspacify-tree/run-tests.mjs).

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - RFC-SEED.md writing/rendering and seed<->manifest parity — separate ticket PX-190 (this ticket creates directories only).
  - CLI run.mjs orchestration and .claude/commands/workspacify-allocate.md — separate ticket PX-191 (composition of PX-189+PX-190 modules).
  - WIC/Workspace Integration Graph / ContractEdge / proof-lifecycle / state-effects / semantic-flow global validation — rejected by the corrected architecture; the erroneous doc §11-§15 is explicitly not implemented.
  - WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json (or any second authoritative JSON ledger) — rejected by the corrected architecture; the user identified this as the fatal mistake of the source instruction doc.
  - Update/merge mode for an existing tree and deletion of pre-existing content — future phase; existing-output policy is BLOCKED-only in the initial version.
  - Any modification to .claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/* (stage-1) — reuse by import only.
  - External packages, network, hooks, Python — prohibited by stage constraints.

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - .claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/lib/* (stage-1 lib) — reused read-only via import; no signature change; import coupling means stage-2 tests exercise them indirectly (acceptable; stage-1 suite keeps them covered).
  - The workspace output directory (manifest's directory) — new top-level package directories may appear under it only on successful publish; the spec file and WORKSPACIFY-TREE-MANIFEST.json already present are never touched.
  - PX-190 (seed placement) and PX-191 (command orchestration) — depend on the entry record, plan, and publish/reload functions defined here.
  - docs/WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE_Complete_Implementation_Instruction.md — superseded on the points above; no direct edit in this ticket.
testUnit: **UT: [Normal] — loadTreeManifest accepts a readable, UTF-8, non-empty, parseable JSON file; checkAllocateEntryGate ok on a manifest satisfying artifact_kind=workspacify-tree-manifest, status=COMPLETE, self-hash match, reload_validation PASS, final_audit zero counts, stage2_handoff.eligible true, orientation=consumer_to_direct_dependency, edge<->boundary coverage, ownership targets present, and co-located spec re-hash equals input.source_hash (precondition: file exists and schema passes; postcondition: returns {ok:true, errors:[]}).

**UT: [Error] — checkAllocateEntryGate FAILs (typed WorkSpacifyTreeError with gateId) when self-hash mismatches integrity.manifest_hash, when status != COMPLETE, when final_audit zero-count fields are non-zero, when stage2_handoff.eligible is not true, when dependencies.orientation is not consumer_to_direct_dependency, when an ownership entry references an unknown package, when a category inventory item has no ownership entry, or when the resolved spec at <manifestDir>/<input.spec_path> is absent or its normalized re-hash differs (precondition: one violating condition injected; postcondition: errors lists it; invariant: no workspace mutation).

**UT: [Normal] — buildDirectoryPlan returns a sorted unique relative directory list for a tree of nested dirs, with the leaf set equal to the package path set (bijection) whenever packages are non-empty and tree non-empty; every ancestor appears exactly once (postcondition: sorted uniqueness, no duplicate relative path, no path outside root).

**UT: [Error] — classifyUnsafePath rejects empty, absolute, ..-containing, NUL-containing, drive-letter, and UNC paths with a distinct reason each; assertContained returns false for a candidate that resolves outside root via path.relative (precondition: candidate outside root; postcondition: rejection reason recorded; invariant: containment never uses a bare string prefix).

**UT: [Boundary] — deterministic plan for deep nesting crates/protocol/alpha vs crates (prefix dedupe), empty workspace -> empty plan, single root-leaf package -> exactly one planned directory, pre-existing empty ancestor allowed (invariant: re-running buildDirectoryPlan on the same input yields byte-identical JSON; plan paths are root-relative and sorted).

**UT: [Invariant] — tree-staging: checkExistingOutputPolicy BLOCKs when a planned path exists as a file, as a symlink, or as a non-empty directory, and passes when only empty ancestors exist; verifyStaging reports PASS iff the realized relative set equals the plan with zero unexpected files/symlinks (invariant: on FAIL/BLOCKED the workspace root is byte-identical; on success the realized set equals the plan).

**UT: [Error] — publishStagedTree: simulate a mid-publish rename failure (inject a file at a second top-level destination) and assert rollback removes only the directories created by this publish and leaves pre-existing entries untouched; verifyDirectorySet reload reports FAIL when an entry is missing (postcondition: rollback restores pre-state; no partial tree remains).

**UT: [Boundary] — publish/rollback boundaries: publish onto a root where one top-level planned dir already exists (file) => BLOCKED before any rename; verifyDirectorySet against a plan containing an unexpected extra dir => FAIL; staging root name matches the STAGING_PREFIX regex and is removed after publish success and after failure cleanup (boundary invariant: no .workspacify-allocate-stage-* artifact remains inside the workspace after any terminal state).

**UT: [Normal] — readManifestSource returns the normalized source text and source hash for a co-located spec, and its sha256Hex(normalizeTextBytes(bytes)) equals manifest.input.source_hash (postcondition: sourceText is the LF-normalized text used by stage-1 extraction).

**UT: [Error] — readManifestSource BLOCKs (gateId G0.3) when <manifestDir>/<input.spec_path> is missing, is a directory, is unreadable, or re-hashes to a different value than input.source_hash (invariant: no fallback to any other spec location is attempted).

**UT: [Boundary] — schema validation boundary: loadSchema('workspacify-tree-manifest.schema.json') + validateAgainstSchema accept the minimal manifest emitted by stage-1 assembleManifest and reject a manifest missing REQUIRED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS (postcondition: schema errors list each missing key).
testIntegration: **IT: [Integration point] — tree-manifest-input -> directory-plan -> tree-staging integration over a temp manifest dir:** build a realistic stage-1 manifest (workspace.tree + packages + ownership + dependencies + stage2_handoff + integrity via assembleManifest/computeSelfHash) plus its co-located spec; run the full entry gate, plan, staging, publish, reload pipeline against an os.mkdtemp root; assert the realized directory set on disk equals the plan and the manifest/spec bytes are unchanged (precondition: fresh temp root; related: PX-175/PX-178 produced the manifest shape).

**IT: [Verification] — end-to-end BLOCKED preservation:** pre-create a non-empty directory at one planned leaf path and re-run publish; assert non-zero exit, the pre-created content is untouched, and no other planned directory appears (verifies rollback/no-merge contract at the integration seam).

testExceptions: **Exception entry:** Item: cross-filesystem atomic rename behavior of publishStagedTree (staging on a different device than the manifest dir). Reason: テスト不能 as an automated assertion because the test runner cannot reliably mount two filesystems inside a temp dir in CI; the design eliminates the class by placing the staging root inside the manifest directory (same filesystem) so rename(2) is atomic; this is not a design defect because same-filesystem staging is the implemented behavior and cross-device staging is unreachable by construction. Alternative verification: unit tests assert the staging root is created under the manifest dir (same device) and that publish uses fs.rename on top-level dirs; an integration test verifies the happy path on the local filesystem.

**Exception entry:** Item: symlink-escape race under concurrent external mutation of the workspace during publish. Reason: テスト不能 deterministically because it depends on a hostile concurrent process timing an lstat/rename race window that cannot be reproduced reliably in a unit test; this is not a design defect (not an architectural defect) because the module follows lstat-before-act on every existing ancestor and never follows symlinks for writes, which bounds the race to the same class every local file API has. Alternative verification: static reasoning plus a deterministic sequential test that pre-places a symlink at an ancestor and asserts assertContained rejects the planned leaf.

**Exception entry:** Item: real-disk durability of directory creation (fsync of directories) after publish. Reason: テスト不能 to observe power-loss durability in-process; durability is provided by the OS for directory entries and stage-1 atomic-publish already fsyncs the manifest file; this is not a design defect because the ticket's contract is logical atomicity (rollback to byte-identical state on process failure), which is fully asserted, not crash durability. Alternative verification: reload rescan after publish asserts logical completeness; crash-durability is out of the ticket's contract.

acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path] — Input manifest in the manifest's directory with the co-located spec, fresh output tree:** loadTreeManifest + checkAllocateEntryGate return ok; buildDirectoryPlan yields the sorted plan; checkExistingOutputPolicy passes; materializeDirectories + verifyStaging pass; publishStagedTree creates the real directories under the manifest dir; verifyDirectorySet reload passes; the manifest file, spec file, and any pre-existing unrelated files are untouched; exit path reports PASS.

**[Error case] — Invalid / inconsistent input or unsafe path:** a manifest failing any entry check (bad self-hash, status not COMPLETE, final_audit counts non-zero, stage2_handoff.eligible not true, spec re-hash mismatch, spec absent) or any unsafe path (absolute, .. segment, NUL, symlink escape, collision, planned path exists as file/symlink/non-empty dir) yields a typed WorkSpacifyTreeError with gateId, a non-zero exit, and the workspace byte-identical to its pre-run state; no staging artifact remains.

**[Edge case] — Boundary values:** empty workspace (no packages and empty tree) produces an empty plan and publishes nothing but still validates; a single package at the root leaf ("alpha") plans only that directory; deep nested paths (crates/protocol/alpha/...) include every ancestor once; a planned path that is a prefix of another (crates vs crates/protocol) is deduplicated; a pre-existing empty ancestor directory is allowed while a pre-existing non-empty planned leaf directory is BLOCKED; re-running the pure functions twice yields byte-identical plan output (determinism).
tickets.investigation:
Material evidence gathered from source and docs:
- .claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/run.mjs publishes the manifest with atomicPublish({dir: process.cwd(), fileName: 'WORKSPACIFY-TREE-MANIFEST.json', ...}) (lines 218-224) and always to the current directory; input.spec_path is stored as path.basename(absPath) via buildInputSection (run.mjs:449-460), so the original specification basename is the only recorded pointer and must be resolved next to the manifest.
- lib/render.mjs computeSelfHash hashes canonicalSerialize(manifest with integrity.manifest_hash=''); REQUIRED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS enumerates artifact_kind/schema_version/status/run/input/structure/inventory/requirements/workspace/adapters/dependencies/conformance/stage2_handoff/gates/final_audit/integrity.
- lib/entry-parity.mjs checkTreeEntryGate(manifest, specPath) already implements the exact ALLOCATE entry checks (FINAL_AUDIT_ZERO_COUNTS, handoff.eligible, contract arrays, edge<->boundary parity, ownership target packages, category inventory ownership, orientation, spec re-hash via normalizeTextBytes+sha256Hex); stage-2 must re-apply the same checks reading only the manifest directory (no caller-supplied specPath).
- lib/workspace-model.mjs exposes LAYERS, PACKAGE_KINDS, LAYER_FORBIDDEN_TARGETS, layerIndex, validatePackageCatalog, validateWorkspaceTree — validateWorkspaceTree({tree, packages}) returns {consistent, errors} and is the structural basis for the directory plan.
- lib/segmentation.mjs buildSegment records byte_start/byte_end/line_start/line_end/sha256 per segment but does NOT embed source text; manifest.structure.segments therefore cannot reconstruct prose, which is why the co-located specification file (resolved next to the manifest) is the source of excerpts for PX-190.
- The stage-1 manifest runtime shape (assembleManifest + run.mjs build*Section functions) is: workspace{tree, packages[], ownership{entries[{inventory_ref, canonical_name, category, owner_package}], packages[]}}, dependencies{orientation, normal_edges[], forbidden_edges[], forbidden_layer_rules[], dev_dependency_policy[], boundaries[]}, conformance{test_obligations[]}, stage2_handoff{eligible, entry_gate{...}, contract_definition_order[], contract_boundaries[], non_goals_of_stage1[]}, integrity{canonicalization, manifest_hash_algorithm, manifest_hash, input_hash_verified_at_finalize, reload_validation}.
- docs/WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE_Complete_Implementation_Instruction.md §1.3/§8.4 treat a second WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json as the protected final artifact; the corrected contract (user direction) removes that artifact entirely, so the existing-output policy keys off planned directories under the manifest directory, not off an allocate manifest.
- Test conventions: tests/workspacify-tree/run-tests.mjs aggregates *.test.mjs under tests/<area> with node --test; coverage runs via node --test --experimental-test-coverage over the sorted test file list; branch targets: run.mjs >=80%, lib modules >=85%.

- Function names are verb phrases: loadTreeManifest, checkAllocateEntryGate, readManifestSource, resolvePackagePath, assertContained, classifyUnsafePath, buildDirectoryPlan, verifyDirectorySet, materializeDirectories, publishStagedTree, rollbackPublished, checkExistingOutputPolicy.
- Variable names are domain concepts: manifestDir, sourceHash, plannedRelativePaths, stagingRoot, topLevelPlannedPaths, realizedPaths; no single-letter or generic names (no data/info/tmp).
- One function one responsibility: entry checks, path classification, plan construction, staging verification, and publish/rollback are separate modules/functions; no function chains multiple AND/THEN responsibilities.
- Hardcoded values become named constants: STAGING_PREFIX='.workspacify-allocate-stage-', MANIFEST_BASENAME='WORKSPACIFY-TREE-MANIFEST.json', SPEC_FILE_ABSENT='spec-not-found'; the FINAL_AUDIT_ZERO_COUNTS list is imported conceptually from entry-parity.
- Errors are never swallowed: typed WorkSpacifyTreeError with gateId propagates to the caller; no empty catch blocks; no console.log in lib modules (diagnostics returned as objects).
- Existing-code improvements in scope: when importing stage-1 lib modules this ticket does not modify them; if a read of entry-parity.mjs shows the gate duplicates stage-2 needs, the plan is to import and reuse checkTreeEntryGate where the specPath argument is supplied by resolving <manifestDir>/<input.spec_path> — no copy-paste.

contracts.precondition: manifest file is a readable regular UTF-8 file, non-empty, parses as JSON, passes the tree-manifest schema, self-hash equals integrity.manifest_hash, status COMPLETE, final_audit zero counts, stage2_handoff.eligible true, and the co-located spec <manifestDir>/<input.spec_path> re-hashes to input.source_hash
contracts.postcondition: checkAllocateEntryGate returns {ok:true, errors:[]} and readManifestSource returns {sourceText, sourceHash} with sourceHash === input.source_hash; on any violated precondition a typed WorkSpacifyTreeError with gateId is thrown and no workspace path is created or modified
contracts.invariant: no entry check ever consults a workspace.root_path field or the process cwd; the manifest directory is the only root basis

contracts.precondition: input.spec_path exists in the manifest directory and is a regular readable file
contracts.postcondition: the LF-normalized bytes of that file sha256Hex-match input.source_hash and are returned as sourceText; absence, directory, unreadability, or hash mismatch yield gateId G0.3 BLOCKED
contracts.invariant: no alternate spec location is ever probed; a mismatched spec never proceeds to planning

contracts.precondition: every planned relative path is non-empty, relative, has no .. segment, no NUL/drive/UNC, and every existing ancestor is not a symlink escaping the root
contracts.postcondition: resolvePackagePath(root, packagePath) yields a descendant of root verified via path.relative; classifyUnsafePath returns an empty reason list for safe paths and the specific reason for each unsafe pattern
contracts.invariant: containment is decided by path.relative + lstat on existing ancestors, never by a string prefix; no planned path resolves outside root

contracts.precondition: workspace.tree and workspace.packages are schema-valid and validateWorkspaceTree reports consistent
contracts.postcondition: buildDirectoryPlan returns a sorted, de-duplicated list of root-relative directories whose leaf set bijects to the package path set (when packages non-empty and tree non-empty), and identical inputs produce byte-identical plan JSON
contracts.invariant: empty workspace (no packages and empty tree) yields an empty plan; each ancestor appears exactly once; no duplicate relative path

contracts.precondition: every planned path is absent or an empty pre-existing directory (never a file, symlink, or non-empty dir), and all staging gates have PASSed
contracts.postcondition: after publish the realized directory set under the root equals the plan exactly (verifyDirectorySet PASS) with zero unexpected files/symlinks; on any failure or BLOCKED the root is byte-identical to its pre-run state and no .workspacify-allocate-stage-* artifact remains
contracts.invariant: publish never merges, overwrites, or deletes a pre-existing entry; rollback removes only directories created by the failed publish

tickets.title: workspacify-allocate allocation モデル・seed 執筆支援・RFC-SEED パリティゲート
tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] A package expected allocation set is exactly the entries of manifest.workspace.ownership.entries where owner_package equals the package id, grouped by category; the union over all packages equals the full ownership entry set with every inventory_ref appearing exactly once across the whole workspace (bijection: no loss, no duplicate, no cross-package placement).
- [Error invariant] On any FAIL/BLOCKED (schema-invalid decisions, parity mismatch, unknown inventory_ref, missing required heading, empty body, unresolvable source excerpt, semantic review not APPROVED, unresolved REVIEW_REQUIRED) no RFC-SEED.md is published and the workspace is left byte-identical to its pre-run state.
- [Internal state invariant] Every rendered seed contains all 15 required headings in the fixed order; the Allocation Index table (section 3) rows equal the package expected allocation set; identity/ownership/index scaffolding is derived deterministically from the manifest and is identical across renders of the same input.
- [Boundary invariant] An inventory_ref appears in exactly one package index across all seeds (exclusivity); a seed never indexes an inventory_ref that stage-1 assigned to a different package; a seed body may mention a neighbor item only as dependency_context or consumer_obligation prose, never as an ownership claim; empty workspace yields zero seeds.
tickets.background:
### Goal
Implement the allocation core of /workspacify-allocate: (1) a deterministic model that turns the stage-1 manifest ownership entries and dependency edges into per-package allocation expectations and machine-supplied authoring packets (owned inventory with source excerpts plus neighbor boundary context), (2) an RFC-SEED.md authoring and rendering and parsing contract with 15 required headings and a machine-extractable Allocation Index, and (3) the machine gates that make seed authorship honest: seed-to-manifest bijective parity, per-seed local checks, REVIEW_REQUIRED handling, and an AI semantic-approval presence gate. No CLI composition yet (PX-191).

### Purpose
The corrected stage-2 contract rejects the erroneous doc WIC JSON blocks (doc section 10.4) and Workspace Integration Graph (doc sections 13-14). Instead every package directory must receive exactly one RFC-SEED.md that (a) faithfully carries the normative material stage-1 assigned to that package (objects, claims, invariants, state machines, error codes, required tests) with source traces, (b) records the dependency and forbidden-boundary context copied from the stage-1 manifest (never re-invented), and (c) is dense enough for /grill-me-for-rfc to turn it into that package canonical RFC, after which the per-directory conver 4-loop (grill, graphify, boundify, split, make/plan/start/review) owns further integration. This ticket provides the modules and gates that make those seeds correct, complete, and exclusively owned, without over-mechanizing the AI prose authorship.

### Motivation
A seed that drops an invariant, misplaces an object into a neighbor seed, cites a source ref that does not resolve, or invents an owner that stage-1 never assigned would silently corrupt the per-directory pipeline downstream: grill would build the wrong RFC, graphify would emit edges that contradict stage-1. Because stage-1 already proved ownership/DAG/layer consistency, stage-2 must only prove faithful transfer: no loss, no addition, no displacement. Machines can and must enforce exactly that transfer; they must NOT decide the seed prose semantics.

### Constraints
- Node.js ESM (.mjs) only, stdlib only; no network/hooks/Python. Reuse stage-1 sibling lib by import (hash, canonical-json, normalization, workspace-model, errors, report) and PX-189 readManifestSource. Do not fork those modules.
- Output of this ticket = modules + schemas + tests only; no run.mjs subcommand wiring (PX-191) and no command markdown (PX-191).
- The only machine-readable source of truth for who owns what is manifest.workspace.ownership.entries (category + inventory_ref + owner_package). packages[].owns is a mirror used for cross-checks only.
- Seeds are Markdown consumed by humans and grill. Required headings are fixed and ordered; bodies must be non-empty or explicitly typed not_applicable with a reason; a machine-extractable Allocation Index (Markdown table) must list exactly the owned inventory of that package.
- WIC/WIG/ContractEdge/proof-lifecycle/state-effects/semantic-flow global machinery is explicitly NOT implemented (rejected design). Cross-package facts are copied from the manifest into each seed as context only.
- AI writes the semantic body; machine renders scaffolding, parses back, and enforces parity/local/semantic-presence gates. Machine never fabricates prose; AI never silently drops or moves an allocated item.

  - .claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/lib/seed-parity.mjs — ADD. runSeedParity({expectedByPackage, parsedByPackage}): {ok, missing[], extraneous[], crossPackage[], duplicate[], unknown[]} implementing the global bijection with exclusivity.
  - .claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/lib/seed-local-checks.mjs — ADD. runSeedLocalChecks({seed, package, expectedAllocation}): required headings present/ordered/non-empty-or-not_applicable, index equals the expected allocation for that package, no neighbor item appears in the index, seed_required consistency.
  - .claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/schemas/workspacify-allocate-decisions.schema.json — ADD. JSON Schema for the AI-authored decisions input: seeds:[{packageId, aiSections:{sectionNumber: body}}] plus semantic_review:{status (enum APPROVED/REVIEW_REQUIRED), statement, approver}.

  - tests/workspacify-allocate/fixtures/allocate-decisions-ok.json, allocate-decisions-review.json, allocate-seed-example.md — ADD.
  - tests/workspacify-allocate/unit/allocate-lib-branch-coverage.test.mjs — ADD (branch hardening to >=85% per lib module).

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - run.mjs orchestration and .claude/commands/workspacify-allocate.md — PX-191 composes these modules.
  - Tree materialization + entry gate + path safety + staging publish — built in PX-189 and reused by import.
  - WIC JSON block in seeds, Workspace Integration Graph, ContractEdge schema, proof/state/effect/semantic-flow global validation — rejected by the corrected architecture (erroneous doc sections 10.4 and 11-15 not implemented).
  - WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json or any second authoritative ledger — rejected (fatal mistake of the source instruction doc).
  - Actually invoking /grill-me-for-rfc or the conver 4-loop per directory — the per-directory pipeline consumes seeds after allocate; allocate does not run it.
  - Grading seed prose quality — left to the AI and the downstream grill; only structure and transfer are gated.

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - PX-189 modules (readManifestSource, entry record) — consumed; no signature change.
  - .claude/commands/workspacify-tree.md and the stage-1 manifest — the source of ownership truth; unchanged.
  - The per-directory conver 4-loop and /grill-me-for-rfc — downstream consumers of RFC-SEED.md; the seed format contract defined here is their input grammar.
  - docs/WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE_Complete_Implementation_Instruction.md — superseded on the seed format (WIC block removed); no edit in this ticket.
testUnit: **UT: [Normal] — deriveExpectedAllocation returns, for every manifest ownership entry, exactly one expected item on the owner package (owner_package equals package id) with role semantic_owner, and the union over packages equals the full ownership entry set (bijection: no loss, no duplicate inventory_ref, no cross-package placement).

**UT: [Error] — deriveExpectedAllocation reports duplicateRefs when two ownership entries carry the same (category, inventory_ref) and unknownRefs when an entry owner_package is absent from the package catalog (precondition: malformed ownership input; postcondition: {ok:false} with named refs; invariant: no silent deduplication).

**UT: [Boundary] — empty ownership yields empty expected allocation per package; a package with zero owned items appears with an empty list; category grouping is stable across object/claim/invariant/state_machine/error_code/required_test (invariant: grouping by category preserves each entry exactly once).

**UT: [Normal] — buildAuthoringPacket resolves each owned inventory_ref from manifest.inventory objects/claims/invariants/state_machines/error_codes/required_tests by id and copies category/inventory_ref/canonical_name/source_refs/review_status; dependencyContext lists incoming (to equals package) and outgoing (from equals package) normal edges plus forbidden edges touching the package from dependencies.normal_edges/forbidden_edges (postcondition: packet ownedItems equals the expected allocation; edges reflect the manifest DAG).

**UT: [Error] — resolveSourceExcerpt returns null (and marks REVIEW_REQUIRED) when source_refs are absent, when the co-located spec is missing (no sourceText), or when refs exceed the text bounds; an excerpt never fabricates text outside the resolved window (invariant: null excerpt, never a guessed string).

**UT: [Boundary] — resolveSourceExcerpt determinism for repeated canonical_name occurrences (first occurrence window), window clamped to EXCERPT_WINDOW_LINES, and byte-ref vs line-ref slicing agree on the same LF-normalized text (boundary invariant: same input yields the same excerpt).

**UT: [Invariant] — renderSeed produces the canonical RFC-SEED.md with all 15 required headings in the fixed SEED_REQUIRED_SECTIONS order, an Allocation Index Markdown table (headers Category | Inventory ID | Canonical Name) whose rows equal the expected allocation for that package, non-empty bodies or explicit not_applicable plus reason, and byte-identical output for identical inputs (postcondition: determinism; invariant: scaffolding sections 1/2/3-index/14 derive solely from manifest plus package).

**UT: [Error] — renderSeed rejects a decisions payload whose aiSections reference an unknown section number, whose semantic_review.status is not APPROVED, or that contains an unresolved REVIEW_REQUIRED item (postcondition: typed WorkSpacifyTreeError; invariant: no partial seed is ever emitted).

**UT: [Normal] — parseSeed recovers packageName, the ordered heading list with bodies, and allocationIndexRows for a rendered seed; parseSeed(renderSeed(model)) round-trips the Allocation Index exactly (postcondition: recovered rows equal the expected rows).

**UT: [Error] — parseSeed fails with a typed error on a malformed Allocation Index (wrong header, unknown columns, unparseable row), a missing required heading, an out-of-order heading, or an empty body that is not marked not_applicable (invariant: a seed that fails parse can never be published).

**UT: [Invariant] — runSeedParity returns {ok:true, missing:[], extraneous:[], crossPackage:[], duplicate:[], unknown:[]} exactly when each parsed seed index equals its expected allocation and the global union over seeds has no duplicate or cross-package inventory_ref; each violation category is populated with the offending package and ref on injection (postcondition: bijection and exclusivity hold).

**UT: [Boundary] — seed-local checks: missing/out-of-order required heading, empty body, an index row for a neighbor item, and a seed_required:false package producing a seed all FAIL; a seed whose body mentions a neighbor item only inside dependency_context prose (not in the Allocation Index) PASSES (boundary: prose mention is not an ownership claim).
