testExceptions: **Exception entry:** Item: verifying that a rendered seed is truly grill-able (that a human/AI grill session will produce a correct canonical RFC). Reason: テスト不能 because grill success depends on non-deterministic human/AI judgment about prose quality, which cannot be asserted by an automated test; this is not a design defect (not an architectural defect) because the ticket explicitly scopes machine gates to structural transfer (parity/local/semantic-presence) and leaves prose grading to the downstream grill, per the over-mechanization guard. Alternative verification: the grill-consumability smoke test asserts structural prerequisites (section 13 present when REVIEW_REQUIRED, identity match); prose quality is verified by the per-directory 4-loop review in later phases.

**Exception entry:** Item: proving that two different AI sessions cannot jointly misplace an item across seeds in a way that still satisfies per-package parity. Reason: テスト不能 deterministically because cross-seed displacement reflected in both seeds indexes would be a semantic lie rather than a structural one, and lies are indistinguishable from honest prose by a parser; this is not an architectural defect because the exclusivity gate (crossPackage plus global bijection in runSeedParity) makes single-sided displacement structurally impossible, and coordinated double-sided lies are exactly what the AI semantic_review APPROVED gate and the downstream graphify review catch. Alternative verification: parity unit tests inject every single-sided displacement and assert detection; the two-sided case is covered by /review-ticket and /grill-me-for-rfc.

**Exception entry:** Item: byte-for-byte determinism of excerpt slicing across all possible Unicode inputs (astral characters, combining marks). Reason: テスト不能 exhaustively because it is an unbounded input space; the design is not a design defect because slicing is done on LF-normalized UTF-8 bytes/lines via Buffer and line offsets exactly like stage-1 segmentation, which is already property-tested in tests/workspacify-tree/property/segmentation-reconstruction.test.mjs. Alternative verification: property-style tests over a representative corpus (ASCII, Japanese, astral emoji) assert no crash and window containment, and determinism is unit-asserted for identical inputs.

- [Implementation steps] (1) allocation-model: derive expected per-package allocation from ownership entries and classify roles (semantic_owner for the owner package; dependency_context and consumer_obligation for neighbors; composition_obligation for core/composition; test_obligation for required_tests and test-support/conformance kinds; rationale_only for design background). (3) seed-model: fixed SEED_REQUIRED_SECTIONS (15 titles; corrected section 7 = Integration Context (Stage-1 Manifest Edges), no WIC JSON), Allocation Index grammar (Markdown table with headers Category | Inventory ID | Canonical Name), non-empty-or-not_applicable rule. (4) seed-render: assemble the canonical RFC-SEED.md from package + manifest + expectedAllocation + aiSections; auto-scaffold sections 1, 2, 3 index, 14; place AI prose for the semantic sections; deterministic. (5) seed-parse: extract headings and Allocation Index rows; typed errors on malformed index or missing heading. (6) seed-parity: compare per-package parsed index to the expected allocation and run the global bijection. (7) seed-local-checks: heading sequence/non-empty/not_applicable typing, seed_required consistency, and forbidden-owner absence from the index. (8) decisions schema plus REVIEW_REQUIRED and semantic_review handling. TDD order per module.
- [Risks] The Allocation Index grammar is a hand-written Markdown table; the parser must fail closed on unknown columns/rows. Source excerpts depend on the co-located spec (PX-189 readManifestSource); a spec that no longer exists must produce REVIEW_REQUIRED, never fabricated excerpts. Over-mechanization risk: gates must never attempt to grade prose quality.
- [Caveats] Section 7 heading title is corrected from the erroneous doc WIC block to Integration Context (Stage-1 Manifest Edges) prose; numbering 1-15 is preserved so downstream consumers keyed to section numbers remain stable.
- [Open items] Whether decisions carry the full AI prose per section vs a pointer to an AI-authored draft file; this schema stores prose per section in a single decisions JSON (mirrors stage-1 decisions.json) and PX-191 may add a convenience authoring flow.
- [Future improvements] A seed linter that checks grill-ability (section 13 Grill Questions present when REVIEW_REQUIRED exists); cross-seed symmetry checks remain in the per-directory graphify stage (not here).

acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path] — Faithful seed set for a realistic multi-package manifest:** deriveExpectedAllocation and buildAuthoringPacket produce, for every package, exactly the owned items with excerpts resolving to real co-located spec text plus neighbor edges; renderSeed and parseSeed round-trip recover the same Allocation Index; runSeedParity over all packages reports ok with zero missing/extraneous/crossPackage/duplicate/unknown; seed-local checks pass; decisions.semantic_review.status is APPROVED; every planned directory has exactly one RFC-SEED.md carrying all 15 required headings.

**[Error case] — A seed that drops, moves, or invents an item must FAIL:** removing one row from a seed Allocation Index, adding a neighbor inventory_ref into a non-owner seed index, duplicating a row, or referencing an inventory_ref unknown to the manifest each yields a non-ok parity report naming the offending package and ref; an empty required heading, a missing/out-of-order heading, or a malformed index table yields a typed seed-parse error; decisions without semantic_review APPROVED or with an unresolved REVIEW_REQUIRED item never render to a publishable seed.

**[Edge case] — Boundary values:** empty workspace yields zero seeds and ok parity; a package owning zero items still renders a seed with an empty Allocation Index and all required headings; an object + invariant + error_code + required_test mix under one package groups rows correctly; repeated canonical_name occurrences resolve deterministically to the first occurrence; excerpt refs beyond the file yield REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than a crash; rendering identical decisions twice yields byte-identical seeds.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Compose the corrected /workspacify-allocate stage into a usable slash command: a single run.mjs entry with subcommands validate/plan/packet/gate/finalize, and a .claude/commands/workspacify-allocate.md command document that reaches the same or higher density, detail, and novelty as .claude/commands/workspacify-tree.md (the stage-1 command document is the explicit reference). The end-to-end pipeline materializes the real directory tree in the manifest directory and writes exactly one RFC-SEED.md per package, with machine parity gates and an AI semantic-approval gate, then reload-verifies and reports. No WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json is created (that was the fatal mistake of the source instruction doc).

### Purpose
PX-189 supplied the input lock, path safety, directory plan, and staged publish. PX-190 supplied allocation expectations, authoring packets, seed render/parse, and the parity/local/semantic gates. PX-191 wires these into the user-facing contract: a Claude Code slash command that a session drives through explicit steps (like stage-1 workspacify-tree) and a deterministic Node CLI whose exit codes gate publication. It also proves the whole thing end to end on a real fixture and hardens coverage to the stage-1 bar so that later /review-ticket can verify with the same discipline.

### Motivation
Modules without orchestration are not a command: a session cannot run them, cannot iterate on FAIL, and cannot be stopped from publishing partial trees. The command document is the contract the AI follows and the review target /review-ticket checks; its density must match stage-1 so the AI is not left to invent the AI/mechanical boundary or the success definition. The user explicitly required: workspacify-allocate.md must be at least as dense/detailed as workspacify-tree.md, referencing it heavily.

### Constraints
- Node.js ESM (.mjs) stdlib only. run.mjs mirrors stage-1 run.mjs structure: subcommand dispatch, optionValue parsing, guide() stderr hints, formatSuccess/formatFailure reporting, EXIT_CODES.OK/FAIL, no console.log noise.
- Reuse PX-189/PX-190 lib modules and stage-1 report/errors modules by import. No WIC/WIG. No allocate manifest file.
- run.mjs subcommands: validate <manifest>, plan <manifest>, packet <manifest> [--package=<id>], gate <manifest> --decisions=<path>, finalize <manifest> --decisions=<path>; plus usage text when args are missing.
- finalize = single atomic publication: it re-runs every gate, renders all seeds into a staging tree under the manifest directory, publish per top-level directory with rollback, then reload-verifies by re-walking and re-parsing; success summary prints workspace root absolute path, input manifest hash, directory count, package count, seed count, and the per-gate summary only.
- Command document: .claude/commands/workspacify-allocate.md must include (a) description/argument-hint frontmatter like stage-1, (b) Role, Arguments, 出力の正本と制約 (real tree + RFC-SEED.md per package; explicitly no ALLOCATE-MANIFEST, no WIC/WIG), 使用スクリプト table, 状態とゲート, 設計判断と機械化の境界 table, per-Step sections for validate/plan/authoring(packet+decisions)/gate/finalize mirroring stage-1 Steps 1-6, a 禁止事項 section, and a 成功の定義 with the two-sided condition (AI semantic APPROVED recorded in decisions AND all machine gates PASS), plus a checklist section. It must reference workspacify-tree.md and state it is the second stage of the same pipeline (the fifth layer above the conver 4-loop).
- No hooks. No external network. Deterministic given identical decisions input.

testUnit: **UT: [Normal] — run.mjs validate exits OK and prints gate:status for a valid manifest whose checkAllocateEntryGate returns ok and whose input manifest hash matches (precondition: readable co-located manifest and spec; postcondition: exit code OK, summary fields printed).

**UT: [Error] — run.mjs exits FAIL with a guide hint when given an unknown subcommand, no subcommand, a missing <manifest> argument, an unreadable or non-JSON manifest, or a manifest failing the entry gate (postcondition: typed failure, non-zero exit; invariant: nothing is created).

**UT: [Normal] — run.mjs plan prints the deterministic planned directory count and passes when checkExistingOutputPolicy passes for a fresh workspace (postcondition: printed plan equals buildDirectoryPlan output).

**UT: [Error] — run.mjs gate exits FAIL when --decisions is missing, when the decisions payload fails assertDecisionsSchema, or when a rendered seed fails runSeedLocalChecks or runSeedParity; exit OK only when every gate PASS and unresolved REVIEW_REQUIRED is zero (postcondition: gate summary names each failing gate).

**UT: [Boundary] — run.mjs gate BLOCKs (exit FAIL) when decisions.semantic_review.status is not APPROVED even if every structural check passes, and when an unresolved REVIEW_REQUIRED item exists (boundary: the AI semantic-approval presence gate is enforced by the machine).

**UT: [Normal] — run.mjs finalize on a fresh workspace creates the planned directories and one RFC-SEED.md per package, reload-rescans, re-parses each seed, re-runs runSeedParity with ok, and prints the success summary (workspace root abs path, input manifest hash, directory count, package count, seed count, gate summary); no second manifest file exists (postcondition: end-to-end atomic success).

**UT: [Error] — run.mjs finalize on an existing non-empty planned directory exits FAIL with a BLOCKED gate and leaves the directory byte-identical; a simulated publish failure rolls back created top-level directories (invariant: rollback restores the pre-state; no staging artifact remains).

**UT: [Invariant] — command-realize reads .claude/commands/workspacify-allocate.md and asserts it references workspacify-tree.md, lists all five run.mjs subcommands, contains the semantic_review APPROVED requirement, contains the two-sided success definition, does not name WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json as a goal, and does not name WIC/WIG as implementable machinery (postcondition: structural anchors hold).

**UT: [Boundary] — command-document density boundary: workspacify-allocate.md line count and heading depth are greater than or equal to those of workspacify-tree.md, and the 使用スクリプト table lists run.mjs with the same column granularity (boundary: at-least-as-dense requirement is machine-asserted).

**UT: [Error] — cli-negative-paths: every error path above asserts the exit code is non-zero and stderr carries a gate id, and stdout carries no allocate manifest path (postcondition: no false-success output on failure).

**UT: [Boundary] — determinism boundary: running gate and finalize twice with identical inputs yields identical gate summaries and byte-identical RFC-SEED.md files (invariant: same input produces the same output).

Reason: テスト不能 because it requires executing a non-deterministic AI against the markdown, which cannot be asserted in an automated test; this is not a design defect because the document is machine-checked for every structural anchor by command-realize and the deterministic CLI paths are fully tested, so the residual gap is only the AI prose quality, which the two-sided success definition and /review-ticket cover. acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path] — Full stage-2 run on a fresh manifest directory:** validate exits OK; plan lists every planned directory; packet prints dense per-package authoring material; a decisions payload with semantic_review.status APPROVED passes gate (all gates PASS, unresolved 0); finalize creates the real directories under the manifest directory and exactly one RFC-SEED.md per package; reload rescan + re-parse + re-parity PASS; the success summary prints workspace root abs path, input manifest hash, directory count, package count, seed count, and gate summary; no WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json or WIC/WIG file exists anywhere under the workspace.

**[Error case] — Every failure path is a non-zero exit with the workspace byte-identical:** a manifest that fails the entry gate, a decisions payload that fails the schema or parity (dropped/moved/invented item), a semantic_review not APPROVED, an unresolved REVIEW_REQUIRED, a BLOCKED existing non-empty planned directory, and a missing --decisions flag each exit non-zero with a gate id + reason + fix hint on stderr and leave the manifest directory byte-identical to its pre-run state.

**[Edge case] — Boundary values:** empty workspace (no packages) finalizes with directory count 0 and seed count 0 and gate PASS; a single-package workspace creates one directory and one seed; a package whose seed body only mentions a neighbor in prose (not the index) passes parity; a second finalize run against the now-populated workspace is BLOCKED; command document completeness: workspacify-allocate.md has at least as many lines and the same or deeper heading structure as workspacify-tree.md and every machine-testable anchor asserted by command-realize passes.

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] A manifest may reach status COMPLETE only if: dependencies.dag is present with edge_count, cycle_count === 0, canonical_edges identical to dependencies.normal_edges in canonical order, topological_order (the existing Kahn order over the persisted edge direction, consumers before providers) and implementation_order whose serial and levels place every provider before each of its consumers; every boundary stage2_contract_scope contains the five core clauses and only vocabulary members; structure.segments partitions the normalised spec with covered_bytes === source_bytes; every inventory item and normative candidate carries at least one source_refs[].segment_id that exists in structure.segments; every package has non-empty responsibilities; and stage2_handoff.contract_definition_order (the contract-item order) is non-empty whenever the inventory declares contract items.
- [Error invariant] When any of the above fails, finalize writes nothing: no manifest is published, the previous manifest (if any) is left byte-identical, and the failing gate id plus the offending path (for example dependencies.dag.implementation_order.levels, dependencies.boundaries[3].stage2_contract_scope, inventory.objects[2].source_refs[0].segment_id) is reported.
- [Internal state invariant] The persisted dependencies.dag is a pure function of the persisted dependencies.normal_edges plus the package catalog: recomputing runDagChecks from the persisted canonical edges reproduces identical topological_order, implementation_order.serial and implementation_order.levels arrays, and the persisted canonical edge list is identical to dependencies.normal_edges in canonical order.
- [Boundary invariant] Degenerate graphs are handled explicitly: an empty workspace (zero packages, zero edges) yields edge_count 0, cycle_count 0, topological_order [] and implementation_order {serial: [], levels: []} and is not a failure; a single package yields one level containing it; a chain of N packages yields N levels; the 15-clause vocabulary is closed, so an unknown clause name is a gate failure rather than a silently accepted string.
tickets.background:
### Goal
Make the stage-1 artifact (WORKSPACIFY-TREE-MANIFEST.json) carry the four facts stage 2 must be able to verify mechanically: (a) the persisted dependency proof (topological order + parallel levels + the canonical edge list it was computed from), (b) a frozen contract-clause vocabulary in which the five core clauses are mandatory for every dependency boundary, (c) proof that the spec segmentation is a total partition of the normalised specification and that every inventory item points at the segment it came from, and (d) non-empty package responsibilities plus a stage2_handoff whose ordering semantics are defined and machine-checked.

### Purpose
Stage 2 (/workspacify-allocate) must write, for every directory, a complete coupling contract (preconditions, postconditions, invariants) and prove that no part of the original long specification was dropped. Both proofs are impossible to compute from stage 1 today: `lib/dag.mjs` computes `topological_order` and then throws it away (only `final_audit.cycle_count` survives), `run.mjs` hardcodes the same unnamed 15-clause list onto every boundary, `structure.segments` totality is implied by `verifyReconstruction` but never stated in the manifest, inventory `source_refs` are line references with no segment identity, and `validation.mjs` merely counts packages whose `responsibilities` are empty.

### Motivation
Workspace coupling is the one artefact whose failure is unrecoverable: a directory whose I/O boundary is under-specified cannot be implemented without inventing an interface that contradicts its neighbours, and a single such directory collapses the whole workspace. The user's standing instruction is that this area decides the fate of the entire development effort, so stage 1 must hand over proof material rather than hints.

### Constraints
- Deterministic only: every new manifest field must be recomputable from the spec plus the AI's structured decisions, and must be reproducible byte-for-byte (canonical JSON, sorted keys, stable tie-breaks).
- No new dependency; Node.js standard library only (project rule from the stage-1 instruction).
- The existing manifest self-hash contract must keep holding: `computeSelfHash` covers the whole manifest, so every added field automatically enters the integrity proof.
- Existing stage-1 behaviour and tests (191 tests under tests/workspacify-tree) must stay green; new fields are additive and every added constraint must be reflected in the tree command document.
- The clause vocabulary is frozen by name: adding a clause later is a breaking change for the stage-2 contract schema and must be an explicit, reviewed edit.
scope:
**Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/lib/contract-clauses.mjs` — ADD. Export frozen `CONTRACT_CLAUSES` (input, output, preconditions, postconditions, invariants, errors, state_ownership, idempotency, atomicity, ordering, finality, canonicalization, signature, proof_verification, tests) and `CORE_CONTRACT_CLAUSES` (input, output, preconditions, postconditions, invariants), plus `buildBoundaryContractScope(connectionKind)` returning the scope for a boundary (core always included; non-core clauses selected by edge kind) and `validateContractScope(scope)` returning the offending entries.
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/run.mjs` — MODIFY the boundary builder (currently ~L395-399) to call `buildBoundaryContractScope` instead of the inline literal list; remove the duplicated literal.
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/lib/dag.mjs` — MODIFY `runDagChecks` to also return `levels` (parallel execution waves from Kahn's algorithm, each level sorted by canonical package key) and `canonical_edges` (the edge list it consumed, canonical order) alongside the existing `topological_order`, `cycle_count`, `cycles`.
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/lib/validation.mjs` — MODIFY the workspace validation (L258 region) to persist the DAG report as `dependencies.dag` on the assembled manifest and to treat empty `responsibilities` as a validation failure instead of only incrementing `missing_responsibilities_count`.
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/lib/segmentation.mjs` — MODIFY to expose `partitionStats(segments, totalBytes)` returning `{segment_count, covered_bytes, first_byte, last_byte, is_total_partition}`; `segmentAtHeadings` keeps returning `{segments, warnings}` and callers write the stats into `structure`.
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/lib/extraction.mjs` — MODIFY `buildLineRef` (module-local, feeds `harvestObjectCandidates({sourceText, headings, segments})`) so every emitted ref carries `segment_id`, resolved from the line's byte offset into the segment byte ranges the function already receives; apply the same to claim, invariant, state-machine, error-code and required-test harvesting.
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/lib/entry-parity.mjs` — MODIFY `checkTreeEntryGate` usage of `stage2_handoff`: require `stage2_handoff.contract_definition_order` (the contract-item order) to be non-empty whenever the inventory declares contract items, require `dependencies.dag.topological_order` to be a valid topological order of `dependencies.normal_edges`, and require `contract_boundaries` to mirror `dependencies.boundaries` one-to-one (same length, same ids, same consumer/provider pairs).
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/lib/render.mjs` — MODIFY the manifest skeleton comment/section list so `dependencies` documents the `dag` member (no behavioural change beyond the skeleton defaults).
  - `.claude/commands/workspacify-tree.md` — MODIFY: promote the stage-2 hand-off to a first-class section (what stage 2 may assume: DAG proof, clause vocabulary and core clauses, segment totality, segment-addressed traceability, responsibilities, order semantics), and add a dependency-proof item to the Step 4 AI approval checklist.
  - Tests — ADD/EXTEND under `tests/workspacify-tree/unit/` (dag levels and canonical edges; contract-clause vocabulary and core clauses; segmentation partition stats; ref segment_id resolution; responsibilities failure; stage2_handoff order semantics; entry-parity rejections) and `tests/workspacify-tree/acceptance/` (a real end-to-end manifest carries all four proofs).

  - [Before → After (behavior/signature)] `runDagChecks({packages, edges, forbiddenEdges}) -> {nodeIds, edge_count, cycle_count, cycles, topological_order}` becomes `-> {..., topological_order, levels, canonical_edges}`; `harvestObjectCandidates({sourceText, headings, segments})` keeps its signature but every emitted `source_refs[i]` gains `segment_id`; `validateWorkspaceTree` gains a hard failure for empty `responsibilities`.
  - [API contract change (if any)] New exports `CONTRACT_CLAUSES`, `CORE_CONTRACT_CLAUSES`, `buildBoundaryContractScope`, `validateContractScope`, `partitionStats`; no existing export changes name or arity.
  - [Data schema change (if any)] `workspacify-tree-manifest.schema.json` gains a machine-checked shape for `dependencies.dag` (object with edge_count/cycle_count/topological_order/levels/canonical_edges), for `structure.segment_count`/`structure.covered_bytes`, for `source_refs[].segment_id`, and for `stage2_handoff.contract_definition_order` being a non-empty array. The schema stays permissive on unrelated sections; the deep rules live in the validators, mirroring how stage 2 already validates.
  - [Config/env change (if any)] None.
  - [Dependency added/removed (if any)] None (standard library only).

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - Implementing any stage-2 consumption of these fields — excluded because it is PX-193/194/195; this ticket only makes stage 1 publish the proof.
  - Changing the spec segmentation anchor level or the hashing/canonicalisation scheme — excluded: total-partition proof is achievable without changing how segments are produced.
  - Adding per-boundary AI-authored clause selection driven by a new decision field — excluded: the vocabulary and the core-clause rule are the contract stage 2 needs; per-boundary refinement can be added later without breaking it.
  - Re-designing workspacify-tree's own gates or adding new gate ids — excluded: the changes attach to existing gates (G3 workspace, G4 dependency, G5 completeness).

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/` (PX-189..191 modules) — Nature: manifest input format. Response needed Y: the stage-2 entry gate must accept and re-verify the new fields, which PX-193 performs; until then the new fields are additive and the existing entry gate keeps passing.
  - Stage-1 acceptance fixtures (`tests/workspacify-tree/fixtures/`, `acceptance/gaia-grade.test.mjs`) — Nature: fixture completeness (they must now carry the four proofs). Response needed Y: extend fixtures inside this ticket so the acceptance test still describes a realistic COMPLETE manifest.
  - Manifest consumers outside this repo (any reader of WORKSPACIFY-TREE-MANIFEST.json) — Nature: additive format change, self-hash still covers the document. Response needed N (additive only).
testUnit: **UT: [Normal] — The DAG proof is persisted with both orders:** runDagChecks over pkg-d (no dependencies), pkg-b/pkg-c and pkg-a with edges a->b, a->c, b->d, c->d returns edge_count 4, cycle_count 0, canonical_edges in canonical order, topological_order placing the consumer before its providers (pkg-a before pkg-b and pkg-c, the existing Kahn semantics) and implementation_order {serial: [pkg-d, pkg-b, pkg-c, pkg-a], levels: [[pkg-d],[pkg-b,pkg-c],[pkg-a]]} derived from dependency depth with each level sorted by canonical package key; validation persists that report as dependencies.dag and recomputing it from the persisted canonical_edges reproduces identical topological_order, implementation_order.serial and implementation_order.levels (precondition: every edge endpoint is in the catalog; postcondition: dependencies.dag present with all members).

**UT: [Error] — A cyclic edge set never yields a persisted order:** adding d->a makes cycle_count 1, cycles[0].path non-empty, and the validation gate FAILs with the cycle path in the message; no manifest with status COMPLETE is assembled and topology_order is not persisted as if valid (this is the deterministic-cycle failure mode, testable in-process with no external dependency).

**UT: [Boundary] — Degenerate graphs:** zero packages/zero edges yields edge_count 0, cycle_count 0, topological_order [] and levels [] without failing; one package yields topological_order [pkg] and levels [[pkg]]; a diamond graph yields three levels; a chain of N packages yields N levels (boundary values: 0, 1, 2, N).

**UT: [Invariant] — Contract clause vocabulary is closed and core clauses are mandatory:** CONTRACT_CLAUSES is frozen (Object.isFrozen) and contains exactly the 15 documented clauses; CORE_CONTRACT_CLAUSES is a subset of it; buildBoundaryContractScope returns a scope containing every core clause for every edge kind; validateContractScope rejects an unknown clause name and rejects a scope missing any core clause; the boundary builder in run.mjs no longer contains the inline literal (assert by reading the source and by asserting the produced manifest) so every boundary's stage2_contract_scope contains input, output, preconditions, postconditions, invariants.

**UT: [Invariant] — Segmentation is a total partition and refs are segment-addressed:** for a spec with preamble plus chapters, partitionStats(segments, totalBytes) reports is_total_partition true, covered_bytes equal to the normalised byte length, no gaps (each segment.byte_start equals the previous byte_end) and no overlaps; structure carries segment_count and covered_bytes; every emitted source_refs entry from harvestObjectCandidates (objects, claims, invariants, state machines, error codes, required tests) carries a segment_id that exists in structure.segments and whose byte range contains the ref's line offset; an out-of-range line offset is rejected rather than silently dropped.

**UT: [Error] — Responsibilities are mandatory:** a package with absent or empty responsibilities makes validateWorkspaceTree return ok=false with a message naming the package id (not merely incrementing missing_responsibilities_count), and such a manifest cannot be finalized with status COMPLETE; missing_responsibilities_count stays 0 on every COMPLETE manifest.

**UT: [Invariant] — The two orders carry their distinct documented meanings:** dependencies.dag.topological_order keeps the existing Kahn semantics (consumers before providers) and dependencies.dag.implementation_order is derived from dependency depth so that every provider appears in an earlier level than each of its consumers, with serial equal to levels flattened; entry-parity rejects an implementation_order whose serial is not a permutation of the catalog ids, whose levels do not partition the serial, or in which a consumer appears in the same or an earlier level than one of its providers; stage2_handoff.contract_definition_order is separately the contract-item order (a permutation of the declared inventory items) and is rejected when empty while contract items exist or when it is not such a permutation; contract_boundaries mirrors dependencies.boundaries one-to-one (same length, same ids, same consumer/provider pairs).

**UT: [Normal] — stage2_handoff carries the proof outline stage 2 needs:** for a COMPLETE manifest, entry_gate.required_status equals COMPLETE, contract_definition_order is a non-empty permutation of the declared contract items, dependencies.dag carries canonical_edges plus both orders with implementation_order placing providers first, contract_boundaries mirrors boundaries, and every package carries responsibilities, so a stage-2 reader obtains the DAG proof, the clause vocabulary and the implementation order without recomputation.

tickets.instrumentation:

tickets.notes:
- **Implementation steps**: 1) RED — add tests under tests/workspacify-tree/unit for dag levels/canonical_edges, contract-clauses vocabulary and core clauses, segmentation partitionStats, ref segment_id resolution, responsibilities hard failure, stage2_handoff order semantics, entry-parity rejections, and a command-anchor test for the new hand-off section; they fail because the exports and fields do not exist. 2) GREEN — implement contract-clauses.mjs, extend dag.mjs, wire validation.mjs, expose partitionStats, add segment_id in extraction.mjs, tighten entry-parity.mjs, update run.mjs boundary builder and the manifest skeleton note. 3) Extend the acceptance test to assert the four proofs. 4) Update workspacify-tree.md (hand-off section + checklist item). 5) REFACTOR — remove the inline clause literal, extract the partition check into a named function, ensure every new function name is a verb phrase. 6) Re-run the full tree suite and the stage-2 entry-gate tests (PX-189..191 must stay green because the added fields are additive).
- **Risks**: (a) adding `segment_id` to every ref changes a large number of existing test expectations — update them as data, not by weakening assertions; (b) making empty `responsibilities` fatal can break the synthetic fixtures used by stage-2 tests (they build packages inline) — check tests/workspacify-allocate/helpers/build-valid-manifest.mjs and add responsibilities there rather than relaxing the rule; (c) the persisted DAG report is derived data, so the manifest must never accept a hand-written one — validation recomputes it rather than trusting it; (d) `levels` must be deterministic; sorting each level by canonical package key is mandatory, otherwise stage 2's equivalence check becomes flaky.
- **Caveats**: the manifest self-hash covers the new fields automatically, so any change to the DAG report shape is a breaking change for every consumer; the orders are three and must not be conflated: `dependencies.dag.topological_order` keeps the existing Kahn semantics (consumers first, asserted today by tests/workspacify-tree/unit/gate-engine.test.mjs:131), `dependencies.dag.implementation_order` is the providers-first wave order stage 2 injects into a seed as before/after/parallel_with, and `stage2_handoff.contract_definition_order` orders contract items (its existing meaning, built from the inventory); the schema stays deliberately permissive for unrelated sections, so the deep checks belong in the validators and must be tested there.
- **Open items**: whether stage 2 should ever re-derive the order itself rather than verify equivalence is settled as "verify equivalence, never invent" — recorded here because a future reader may be tempted to recompute and diverge.
- **Future improvements**: if a future workspace needs clause selection per connection kind beyond the current heuristic, `buildBoundaryContractScope(connectionKind)` is the single seam to extend; a machine-readable hand-off summary block in the command document could later be generated from the manifest instead of hand-maintained.
Implementation summary (PX-192):
- Changed files: .claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/lib/{contract-clauses(new),dag,validation,segmentation,extraction,entry-parity}.mjs, .claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/run.mjs, .claude/commands/workspacify-tree.md, .claude/commands/workspacify-allocate.md (receiver-side hand-off section), .claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/lib/tree-manifest-input.mjs (zero-count list), new tests under tests/workspacify-tree/unit plus helpers/build-valid-tree-manifest.mjs.

acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path] — A real spec produces a manifest carrying all four proofs:** running the stage-1 CLI over a fixture spec in a temp directory yields status COMPLETE with `dependencies.dag` (edge_count, cycle_count 0, topological_order, levels, canonical_edges), every boundary's stage2_contract_scope containing the five core clauses, `structure.segment_count`/`covered_bytes` reporting a total partition, every inventory item carrying a resolvable `segment_id`, every package carrying responsibilities, a non-empty contract-item `stage2_handoff.contract_definition_order` and a package-level `dependencies.dag.topological_order`/levels that is a valid topological order; the self-hash verification passes on reload.

**[Error case] — A malformed proof is rejected with a located message:** a manifest whose edge set contains a cycle, whose boundary scope omits a core clause, whose segment list has a gap, whose ref carries an unknown segment_id, whose package lacks responsibilities, or whose contract_definition_order is empty while contract items exist or is not a permutation of them, or whose dependencies.dag.implementation_order places a consumer before one of its providers, fails the corresponding gate with a typed error naming the exact field path, and finalize publishes nothing (the pre-existing manifest file is byte-identical afterwards).

**[Edge case] — Degenerate and boundary manifests:** a spec with no level-2 heading (single segment covering the whole document) still yields is_total_partition true with segment_count 1; a workspace with zero packages yields an empty but present DAG proof; a workspace with one package yields levels [[pkg]]; a scope list that repeats a clause is rejected as a duplicate; and a ref whose byte offset falls exactly on a segment boundary is attributed to the segment that contains that offset.

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] Every rendered seed parses into exactly the 14 required sections in order; its first section carries the machine-injected block (package identity, source spec path and hash, stage-1 manifest path and hash, stage-2 manifest canonical path, implementation order, contract ids, covered segments) and its second section carries the contract edges whose clause sets equal the boundary scopes declared by stage 1; the authoring decisions supply no text for either section.
- [Error invariant] If any of the three reference paths is missing or unresolvable, if the spec re-hash disagrees with input.source_hash, if the stage-1 manifest hash disagrees with the manifest on the command line, if the allocate manifest path differs from the canonical <manifestDir>/WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json, if a contract clause set is missing a core clause or names an unknown clause, or if any segment of the specification is referenced by no seed, then rendering or the local gate fails with a typed error naming the package and the offending field; no seed is written and no partial output survives.
- [Internal state invariant] Rendering is idempotent: rendering the same manifest plus decisions twice yields byte-identical seeds, and the machine-injected block is derived only from the manifest, the resolved files on disk and the verified order, never from AI text.
- [Boundary invariant] Degenerate cases are explicit: a package with no edges renders no_external_contracts with a typed reason and no contract ids; a specification reduced to a single segment is covered by whichever seeds reference it; a package whose boundary scope contains only core clauses renders exactly those clauses; a clause group that genuinely does not apply is written as not_applicable with a reason and at least one segment id.
tickets.background:
### Goal
Rewrite the stage-2 authoring half so that a rendered RFC-SEED.md (a) opens with the section that proves the directory is an independent implementation that is not independent, (b) carries its complete I/O boundary as machine-readable coupling contracts with typed clause groups (preconditions, postconditions, invariants and the rest of the frozen stage-1 vocabulary), (c) proves that every segment of the original long specification is carried by at least one seed, and (d) receives its three reference paths (original spec, WORKSPACIFY-TREE-MANIFEST.json, WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json) by machine injection so an AI can neither omit nor rewrite them.

### Purpose
The 15-heading grammar shipped by PX-190 puts integration context in the middle of the document and explicitly forbids a machine-readable contract block; the authoring packet offers only the package's own owned items. Both choices came from the discarded reading of the instruction document that treated the contract machinery as the fatal mistake. The contract machinery is in fact the point: a workspace in which one directory cannot state its coupling completely collapses as a whole, which is why coupling and dependency must be the first thing every seed states and the only thing every gate cross-checks.

### Motivation
Every downstream directory loop (grill, graphify, boundify, split, make/plan/start/review) starts from the seed. If the seed does not carry the counterpart package, the required clause list and the surrounding dependency order, the implementing AI must invent an interface, and invented interfaces are exactly the failure mode this command exists to prevent.

### Constraints
- The stage-1 contract from PX-192 is the input authority: clause names come from the frozen vocabulary, core clauses are mandatory, order comes from the verified DAG proof and is never invented by stage 2.
- Determinism: rendering is a pure function of (manifest, expected allocation, authoring decisions, machine facts); identical inputs must produce byte-identical seeds, and the machine-injected block must not depend on the wall clock, environment or process id.
- A seed must never contain a TODO/TBD placeholder for a coupling or dependency fact; unresolved design choices belong in the grill-questions section.
- No new dependency (Node.js standard library only) and no change to the publish/atomicity model delivered by PX-189/191.
- The three reference paths are written relative to the workspace root so the workspace stays portable, and the allocate manifest is referenced by path only (no hash) to avoid a circular hash with the manifest that records seed hashes.

### Language note
Seed bodies are English (the language the implementing AI reads most reliably); the surrounding command document stays Japanese for the operator.

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] For a workspace to be COMPLETE: every normal edge of the stage-1 manifest appears as exactly one contract in the consumer seed and exactly one mirror contract in the provider seed; the extracted graph has zero violations of every listed class; every clause of every contract carries at least one test obligation; and the derived implementation order equals the stage-1 topological order and levels exactly.
- [Error invariant] A violation never mutates a seed, never rewrites a contract and never publishes: the run exits non-zero with the violation class, the contract id and the package pair, and the workspace remains byte-identical to its pre-run state.
- [Internal state invariant] The graph is a pure function of the parsed seeds plus the manifest: walking the same tree twice yields identical node, edge and violation lists, and the derived order is stable across runs (canonical tie-break by package id).
- [Boundary invariant] Degenerate inputs are explicit: a workspace with a single package and no edges yields an empty graph, an order of one package and a wave list of one; a package declaring no_external_contracts contributes no edges but is still a node; a manifest edge whose boundary scope is core-only yields a contract whose non-core clause groups may be absent with a reason; unknown packages appearing only in a seed are reported as unknown rather than silently dropped.
tickets.background:
### Goal
Add the cross-seed verification layer that turns a set of individually valid seeds into a proven workspace: (a) every declared dependency edge is present as a contract in both the consumer seed and the provider seed with mirror-identical clause content, (b) the extracted contracts form a Workspace Integration Graph whose violations (unknown package, self-loop, duplicate contract id, reverse edge, undeclared edge, forbidden edge, layer violation, cycle, owner collision, proof-lifecycle break, state-mutation conflict, side-effect race, forbidden semantic-flow path, missing test obligation) are all zero, (c) the verified graph yields a deterministic implementation order (serial order plus parallel waves) that must be equivalent to the stage-1 DAG proof, and (d) a walker reads the machine block and the contract block from every RFC-SEED.md in the directory tree so the same verification runs over the published artefacts rather than over renderer state.

### Purpose
The single most dangerous failure of this command is a workspace whose directories cannot actually be coupled: one directory's postcondition that no neighbour can meet, one owner claimed twice, one state mutated by two packages, one forbidden edge that the composition nevertheless requires. Those are invisible per seed and obvious across seeds, so the verification must be a cross-seed proof and must run as a gate, not as an advisory report.

### Motivation
The user's standing requirement is that if the coupling cannot be satisfied the whole workspace is a collapse, and that the implementation order must be derivable mechanically once the contracts are proven. Today stage 2 verifies only allocation parity (seed versus manifest ownership) and never looks across seeds, so nothing prevents a mutually contradictory seed set from being published.

### Constraints
- Verification is read-only over the seeds: it must never repair a seed, and a violation must fail the gate rather than be normalised away.
- Determinism: graph construction, violation ordering and order derivation must be canonical (sorted keys, stable tie-breaks) so that the same seeds always produce the same verdict and the same order.
- The order is verified, never invented: stage 2 derives it and must prove equality with the stage-1 proof; a mismatch is a FAIL even if stage 2's own derivation looks self-consistent.
- No new dependency and no network access; the walker reads only the workspace tree and the manifest.
- Gate identifiers must map onto the stage-1 instruction's gate taxonomy (G4 contract edges/bilateral boundary, G5 WIG, G6.5 re-extraction) so the design stays traceable to the reference document.

### Failure policy
Any violation stops the run before publication and reports the offending contract id, package pair and clause, in English, so the authoring AI can repair the decisions and re-run.

testUnit: **UT: [Normal] — Bilateral symmetry holds for a coupled pair:** given a manifest edge pkg-a -> pkg-b with a boundary, and a seed pair carrying the same contract id with mirrored content, runBilateralSymmetry returns every list empty; the contract index contains one contract with both sides resolved; the mirror comparison ignores only the consumer/provider swap and the direction label and requires clause equality after canonicalisation (precondition: both seeds parse; postcondition: no mismatch reported).

**UT: [Error] — Broken symmetry is located:** removing the contract from the provider seed yields missing_in_provider; changing a postcondition on one side yields content_mismatch naming the contract id and the clause; duplicating a contract id across packages yields duplicate_contract_ids; flipping the direction yields direction_errors; a contract for a pair the manifest does not declare yields undeclared_edge; none of these mutate a seed and each reports the package pair.

**UT: [Error] — Every graph violation class is detected:** a contract naming an unknown package yields unknown_package; a contract whose consumer equals its provider yields self_loop; an edge against a forbidden edge yields forbidden_edge; a contract that inverts a declared edge direction yields reverse_edge; an edge crossing layers contrary to layer rules yields layer_violation; a cycle among state transitions yields cycle with a non-empty path; two packages declaring the same semantic owner for one canonical name yields owner_collision; a proof without a verification contract yields proof_lifecycle_break; two packages directly mutating one canonical state yields state_mutation_conflict; two packages initiating one external effect yields side_effect_race; a path from a forbidden source class to a forbidden target class yields forbidden_semantic_flow_path; a contract clause without a test obligation yields missing_test_obligation.

**UT: [Invariant] — Order derivation is deterministic and verified:** deriveImplementationOrder over a diamond graph yields levels [[d],[b,c],[a]] with each level sorted by canonical key and a serial order that lists every provider before its consumers; verifyOrderAgainstStage1 returns no divergence when compared with the stage-1 proof and returns the first differing index when the persisted order is perturbed; describeOrderForPackage returns before/after/parallel_with consistent with the levels for every package; deriving twice yields identical arrays.

**UT: [Invariant] — The walker reads the published artefacts, not renderer state:** walkSeedContracts over a staged tree returns one parsed seed per planned leaf, reports missingSeeds for a leaf without RFC-SEED.md, reports unreadableSeeds for a malformed one, and reports missingReferences for a seed whose section 1 lacks the original spec path, the stage-1 manifest path or the stage-2 manifest path; walking the same tree twice yields identical results and never writes to the tree.

**UT: [Boundary] — Degenerate graphs and orders:** a single-package workspace yields an empty graph, zero violations and an order of one package in one wave; a package declaring no_external_contracts contributes no edges but remains a node; a manifest edge with a core-only scope yields a contract whose non-core groups are absent with a reason and no violation; a package referenced only by a seed is reported unknown rather than dropped.

BLOCKER 1 - a dropped ownership entry is masked by the package catalog, so stage 1 reports a clean audit while an inventory object has no owner.

  Blast radius: stage 2 refuses the manifest at G3.5 (`allocation is incomplete: 1 inventory item(s) allocated to no package`) and publishes nothing, so no material is lost - the coupling built in PX-196/PX-197 is doing the work here. But the stage-1 manifest, which stage 2's entry gate accepts, carries a false audit, and the AI loses the count that would tell it to fix the ownership entry.

MAJOR 2 - reasonCode is unenforced in both directions.
  (a) A value outside REASON_CODES is accepted (`totally-made-up` published unchanged); lib/dependencies.mjs checkDependencyMatrix() exists for exactly this but is never called by the pipeline.

The command document carried this misspelling in three places until this review's documentation pass corrected it, which is how the trap was found.

MINOR 3 - an unknown clause group is silently discarded.
  lib/contract-model.mjs canonicalizeClauses() iterates only CONTRACT_CLAUSES, so `clauses.made_up_clause` vanishes without an error and the gate passes. Contrast: an authored contract id with no declared boundary throws and stops the run. Authored content should not disappear quietly.

With two candidates of the same kind the AI cannot tell which chapter each one is about. Documented in the command doc during this review (Step 3 item 5), but the input itself is still unreachable before authoring.

WHAT IS PROVEN STRONG.

acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path] — A coupled workspace is proven before publication:** for a manifest with several packages and edges, the pipeline reads every staged seed, finds one contract per edge on both sides with mirrored clauses, reports zero violations across every class, derives an implementation order equal to the stage-1 proof, and exposes per-package before/after/parallel_with blocks for injection into the seeds.

**[Error case] — A contradictory workspace stops the run:** a provider seed whose postcondition is weaker than the consumer's assertion, a contract for an undeclared pair, a cycle among state transitions, a duplicate contract id and an order that diverges from the stage-1 proof each fail with a located violation naming the class, contract id and package pair, and nothing is published.

**[Edge case] — Degenerate and isolated packages:** a single-package workspace, a package with no external contracts, a core-only clause scope, a seed whose section 1 lacks one of the three references, and a planned leaf without a seed are each handled with the specific message that names the artefact rather than a generic failure.

tickets.title: workspacify-allocate 正本と公開: ALLOCATE-MANIFEST・reload 再構築・cleanup・command 改訂
tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] A run reports COMPLETE only if: every earlier gate passed, the derived implementation order equals the stage-1 proof, the coverage proof shows zero uncovered segments, the published allocate manifest re-hashes to its recorded self-hash, the publish summary reports the tree, seed and manifest counts, and the reload pass reproduces the pre-publication contract registry, graph hash, order and coverage exactly.
- [Error invariant] On any failure the workspace root is left byte-identical to its pre-run state: no directory, no seed, no manifest and no staging or intermediate file remains; the previous allocate manifest, if one existed, is untouched.
- [Internal state invariant] After a successful run the workspace contains exactly the tree, one RFC-SEED.md per seed_required package, and WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json; the manifest is canonical JSON whose self-hash covers every field, and every seed hash recorded in it matches the file on disk.
- [Boundary invariant] Degenerate cases are explicit: a workspace with a single package publishes a manifest whose seed index has one entry; a workspace whose plan is empty cannot be published (fresh-workspace policy already blocks a non-empty target); an interrupted run (SIGINT during publish) leaves staging removable by a subsequent run without touching published content; a second run against a published workspace is BLOCKED rather than merged.
tickets.background:
### Goal
Complete stage 2 by publishing, alongside the directory tree and the seeds, the machine final authority WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json; by proving after publication that the published artefacts still satisfy every gate (reload: rescan, re-parse, re-extract contracts, rebuild the graph, re-derive the order, re-prove coverage); by removing every intermediate artefact mechanically so the workspace keeps only the tree, the seeds and the manifest; and by rewriting .claude/commands/workspacify-allocate.md so the operator instructions match the corrected design.

### Purpose
Without the manifest the contract verification has no durable, hash-protected record: a consumer cannot tell which contracts a workspace was proven against, and a later change to a seed could not be detected. Without reload verification the manifest would be a claim rather than a proof. Without mechanical cleanup the workspace accumulates staging and intermediate files, which the discarded instruction's 'no extra artefacts' rule correctly forbade but which the corrected design permits only transiently.

### Motivation
The user's requirement is explicit: the coupling must be verifiable one hundred percent mechanically from the stage-1 manifest and the stage-2 manifest together, and intermediate or temporary files are acceptable during the workflow provided the script cleans them up mechanically at the end. This ticket delivers exactly that, plus the operator document that makes the behaviour reproducible.

### Constraints
- The three published artefact families are: the directory tree, the RFC-SEED.md files, and WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json. Nothing else may remain at the workspace root after a successful run except what pre-existed (the stage-1 manifest and the co-located specification).
- The reference from a seed to the allocate manifest is one-way (canonical path only) because the manifest records every seed hash; embedding the manifest hash in the seeds would create a hash cycle.
- Publication is atomic with rollback, extending the staging model already delivered by PX-189: a failure leaves the workspace byte-identical.
- Cleanup runs on both success and failure paths and must be idempotent; it must never delete a pre-existing user file, and it must never delete the stage-1 manifest or the specification.
- The command document must stay at least as dense as the stage-1 command document (the density assertion in the command test remains in force) and must not resurrect the discarded framing (manifest as the goal, WIC as forbidden).
- No new dependency; Node.js standard library only.

### Success definition
Success is two-sided: the machine gates all pass on the published artefacts, and the AI records semantic approval; the run reports COMPLETE only when both hold, and never publishes a second time into a non-fresh workspace.
scope:
**Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/lib/allocate-manifest.mjs` — ADD. buildAllocateManifest({manifest, manifestPath, sourceText, plan, parsedByPackage, contractIndex, graph, order, coverageProof, gateResults, semanticReview}) assembling: artifact_kind, schema_version, status, run, input_tree_manifest {path, hash, spec {path, sha256}}, seed_index [{package, path, sha256}], source_coverage {segments_total, segments_covered, uncovered}, contract_registry [canonical ContractEdge], wig {summary, counts, hash, violations}, implementation_order {serial, levels}, allocation {ownership_parity, category_counts, item_count}, gates [], semantic_review, integrity {canonicalization, manifest_hash_algorithm, manifest_hash, reload_validation}, completion_decision; computeAllocateSelfHash + renderAllocateManifest reusing the canonical-JSON helpers from the stage-1 render module.
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/publish-allocate-manifest.mjs` — ADD. publishWorkspace({manifestDir, plan, seeds, allocateManifest}) staging the tree, the seeds and the manifest inside one staging root, verifying the staged set, then moving the top-level entries into place with rollback; the published set is exactly {planned directories, RFC-SEED.md files, WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json}; a second run against a published workspace is BLOCKED by the existing fresh-workspace policy.
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/cleanup-workspace-artifacts.mjs` — ADD. removeWorkspaceArtifacts({workspaceRoot, stagingRoot}) removing the staging root and any intermediate file the pipeline created (rendered seed scratch, graph dump, order dump) and verifying that the residue equals the published set; idempotent, safe when called twice, and never touching pre-existing files (it removes only paths the run itself created and still present in the staging root or in the run's declared scratch list).
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/run.mjs` — MODIFY runFinalize to: re-run every gate, derive the order, build the manifest, publish tree + seeds + manifest atomically, run the reload pass (rescan the tree, re-parse every seed, re-extract contracts, rebuild the graph, re-derive the order, re-prove coverage) and compare with the pre-publication values, then call cleanup; the success payload becomes {published, workspaceRoot, inputManifestHash, allocateManifestPath, allocateManifestHash, directoryCount, packageCount, seedCount, contractCount, waveCount, segmentCoverage, gateSummary}; the failure path calls cleanup and exits non-zero.
  - `.claude/scripts/workspacify-allocate/lib/allocate-reload.mjs` — ADD. reloadAndVerify({workspaceRoot, plan, expected}) performing the reload pass and returning per-artefact equality verdicts (seed set, contract registry, graph hash, order, coverage, manifest self-hash) with the first divergence located.
  - `.claude/commands/workspacify-allocate.md` — REWRITE: Step 2 becomes "coverage basis and dependency proof" (segment→owner coverage, inventory→package allocation, edge→clause scope, order derivation, plus the path-safety and fresh-workspace preconditions) instead of deciding the directory set; Step 3 authors the seed bodies and the coupling contracts; Step 4 becomes the gate loop including contract completeness, bilateral symmetry and graph verification; a new Step 5 confirms the order and builds the manifest; Step 6 publishes and reload-verifies; Step 7 cleans up; the output section lists the three artefact families and states that the allocate manifest IS published while no ledger, WIC-as-separate-file or integration-graph file is; the seed grammar appendix is updated to the 14 sections with the machine-injected section first; the AI approval checklist gains coupling and dependency items; the document must remain at least as long as workspacify-tree.md and must not contain the discarded framing.
  - Tests — ADD/EXTEND under `tests/workspacify-allocate/unit/` (manifest build, self-hash, cleanup idempotence, reload divergence) and `tests/workspacify-allocate/acceptance/` (end-to-end: real stage-1 manifest -> tree + seeds + allocate manifest, reload equal, residue exactly the published set, second run BLOCKED).

  - [Before → After (behavior/signature)] runFinalize's success payload gains allocateManifestPath/allocateManifestHash/contractCount/waveCount/segmentCoverage and loses the assertion that no allocate manifest exists; the workspace after a run contains one more file than before (the manifest).
  - [API contract change (if any)] New exports buildAllocateManifest, computeAllocateSelfHash, renderAllocateManifest, publishWorkspace, removeWorkspaceArtifacts, reloadAndVerify.
  - [Data schema change (if any)] NEW schemas/workspacify-allocate-manifest.schema.json describing the published manifest; the decisions schema is unchanged by this ticket.
  - [Config/env change (if any)] None. No environment variable may alter the published set.
  - [Dependency added/removed (if any)] None.

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - Any change to stage 1 — excluded because it is PX-192 and must land first.
  - Any change to the seed grammar, the contract model or the verification taxonomy — excluded because they are PX-193 and PX-194; this ticket consumes them and must not fork them.
  - Keeping the graph or the order as separate workspace files — excluded: they are intermediate artefacts and are published only as the manifest's canonical summary, counts and hash.
  - A repair mode that fixes an existing published workspace — excluded: the fresh-workspace-only policy is deliberate, and repair would require a redesign of the atomicity model.

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - `tests/workspacify-allocate/acceptance/end-to-end-allocate.test.mjs` and `unit/runmjs-handlers.test.mjs` — Nature: assertions pinning the discarded direction (they currently assert that WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json does not exist). Response needed Y: reverse those assertions to assert the manifest exists, re-hashes and matches its seed index.

  - Downstream per-directory loops (grill and beyond) — Nature: seeds now point at the stage-2 manifest, so a downstream reader can resolve the contract registry. Response needed N (the seeds already carry the path).
testUnit: **UT: [Normal] — The allocate manifest is built, hashed and self-verifying:** buildAllocateManifest over a verified workspace produces every declared section (input_tree_manifest with path/hash/spec hash, seed_index with one entry per seed and matching sha256, source_coverage with zero uncovered, contract_registry canonical, wig summary with hash, implementation_order, allocation, gates, semantic_review, integrity, completion_decision); computeAllocateSelfHash over the canonical rendering equals integrity.manifest_hash and recomputing after a one-byte change detects the change (precondition: seeds are parsed and the graph is verified; postcondition: manifest_hash equals the recomputed hash).

**UT: [Error] — Reload divergence is located:** mutating one published seed after publication (a clause, a reference path, an allocation row) makes reloadAndVerify report the first divergence naming the artefact (seed package id plus field), and a mutated manifest self-hash is detected by the self-hash check; the reload never repairs the artefact and never rewrites the manifest.

**UT: [Boundary] — Cleanup is idempotent and bounded:** removeWorkspaceArtifacts removes the staging root and the declared scratch files, is safe to call twice, leaves pre-existing files (the stage-1 manifest, the specification, unrelated files) untouched, and reports the residue set; a stale staging directory left by an interrupted previous run is removable without touching published content; when the published set is already the residue the call is a no-op.

**UT: [Invariant] — The published set is exactly three artefact families:** after publishWorkspace the workspace root contains the planned directories, one RFC-SEED.md per seed_required package, exactly one WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json, and no file matching the intermediate patterns (staging prefix, graph dump, order dump, rendered scratch); the counts in the success payload equal the counts on disk, and a second run is BLOCKED with the fresh-workspace reason and leaves everything byte-identical.

**UT: [Invariant] — Reload reproduces the pre-publication verification:** for a successful run the reload pass rescan, re-parse, re-extract, graph rebuild, order re-derivation and coverage re-proof produce values equal to the pre-publication ones (seed set, contract registry, graph hash, order arrays, coverage counts); any inequality fails the run even though the files were written successfully.

**IT: [Prerequisites] — PX-192, PX-193 and PX-194 landed:** the manifest must carry the DAG proof, seeds must carry machine and contract blocks, and the verification layers must be available for the reload comparison.
**IT: [Related tickets] — PX-192 (stage-1 hand-off), PX-193 (authoring), PX-194 (verification), and the discarded instruction document whose gate taxonomy (G0..G6, G6.5) this pipeline mirrors.

tickets.notes:
- **Implementation steps**: 1) RED — write unit suites for manifest build/self-hash, cleanup idempotence, reload divergence, published-set residue, and the command anchors; write the acceptance test that expects the allocate manifest to exist and to re-verify; reverse the existing assertions that pin its absence. 2) GREEN — implement allocate-manifest.mjs, then allocate-reload.mjs, then publish-allocate-manifest.mjs and cleanup-workspace-artifacts.mjs, then wire runFinalize, then add the manifest schema. 3) Rewrite .claude/commands/workspacify-allocate.md (Step 2 redefined, Steps 3-7 updated, output section corrected, seed grammar appendix replaced, approval checklist extended). 4) Run the full allocate and tree suites, the quality checks, the stub scan and the crime scan. 5) REFACTOR — extract the canonical rendering/hash pair so stage 1 and stage 2 share one implementation; ensure every new function is a verb phrase.
- **Risks**: (a) reversing the existing 'no allocate manifest' assertions touches several tests — change them to assert the new invariant rather than deleting them, or the reversal becomes an untested behaviour; (b) the reload comparison must use the same canonicalisation as the build path, so share the helper instead of duplicating it; (c) cleanup must be conservative: it may delete only paths the run created, and the test must prove that a pre-existing unrelated file with a similar name survives; (d) the command document rewrite is the operator's only source of truth, so a stale sentence that still forbids the manifest would make a future operator contradict the machine.
- **Caveats**: the allocate manifest is referenced by canonical path from every seed and holds every seed hash — never add the manifest hash to a seed; the graph and order are published only as the manifest's summary and hash, never as separate workspace files; the fresh-workspace-only policy means a re-run against a published workspace is BLOCKED by design, and the operator must remove the workspace deliberately rather than expect a merge.
- **Open items**: whether a future revision should support an explicit --repair mode is left open and deliberately not implemented; the residue check is the enforcement that keeps the option honest if it is ever added.
- **Future improvements**: the manifest schema can be tightened to make loadSchema/validateAgainstSchema the entry gate for stage-3 consumers (the per-directory loops), giving them a machine-checked way to read the contract registry.

Review report (PX-192..PX-201, workspacify-tree + workspacify-allocate):

VERDICT: not yet complete. Machine verification is strong and the two-stage coupling is what saves it, but three defects remain, one of them a false clean bill of health in the published stage-1 manifest.

BLOCKER 1 - a dropped ownership entry is masked by the package catalog, so stage 1 reports a clean audit while an inventory object has no owner.
  Evidence: decisions with `pkg-b.owns.objects=[obj-000002]` but no `ownership` entry for it -> finalize exits 0, published manifest has `inventory.objects[1].owner_package = null`, `workspace.ownership.entries` has no row for it, and `final_audit` reports `orphan_object_count: 0, unallocated_count: 0, status: PASS`.
  Root cause: lib/ownership.mjs resolveOwners() unions the inventory owner with every package's `owns.*`, so `owns` masks the missing ownership entry, while buildOwnershipTable() (and stage 2) use the ownership-derived owner only.
  Blast radius: stage 2 refuses the manifest at G3.5 (`allocation is incomplete: 1 inventory item(s) allocated to no package`) and publishes nothing, so no material is lost - the coupling built in PX-196/PX-197 is doing the work here. But the stage-1 manifest, which stage 2's entry gate accepts, carries a false audit, and the AI loses the count that would tell it to fix the ownership entry.

MAJOR 2 - reasonCode is unenforced in both directions.
  (a) A value outside REASON_CODES is accepted (`totally-made-up` published unchanged); lib/dependencies.mjs checkDependencyMatrix() exists for exactly this but is never called by the pipeline.
  (b) The field spelled `reason_code` instead of `reasonCode` is silently ignored: the edge survives with reasonCode undefined and the published boundary records null. The command document carried this misspelling in three places until this review's documentation pass corrected it, which is how the trap was found.

MINOR 3 - an unknown clause group is silently discarded.
  lib/contract-model.mjs canonicalizeClauses() iterates only CONTRACT_CLAUSES, so `clauses.made_up_clause` vanishes without an error and the gate passes. Contrast: an authored contract id with no declared boundary throws and stops the run. Authored content should not disappear quietly.

WORKFLOW GAP 4 (AI-semantic dimension) - the pulse candidates are invisible while the AI authors their settlements. run.mjs computes structure.spec_pulse inside gate/finalize only; `extract` prints stats alone, and the failure message names the candidate id and kind but not its observation or chapter. With two candidates of the same kind the AI cannot tell which chapter each one is about. Documented in the command doc during this review (Step 3 item 5), but the input itself is still unreachable before authoring.

WHAT IS PROVEN STRONG.
  - Machine (stage 2): one-sided contract, emptied core clause, machine-section authoring, empty body, missing focus, unconverged pass, thin residual, banned phrase, unapproved semantic_review and a dropped stage-1 residual are all refused with a located message (G3 / G3.6 / G3.7 / G5).
  - Machine (stage 1): owner collision, edge outside the catalog, cycle, missing tree leaf, orphan boundary, uncovered edge, unsettled pulse candidate, unanswered review candidate, missing semantic_review and a banned phrase are all refused.
  - Coupling: a real stage-1 run drives a real stage-2 publish over a specification containing a material-free prose segment, and the false-audit manifest above is caught by the allocation proof rather than accepted.
  - AI-semantic loop: focus coverage, convergence (the final pass must list no finding), residual shape, verbatim stage-1 carry (candidate id and topic), reachability into seed section 12 and into handoff_summary are all machine-forced; no path asks a human anything.

RESIDUAL RISK (inherent, stated not hidden): the machine cannot tell a real critique from a performed one. A payload whose five focuses all report zero findings converges on pass 1 and is accepted - the project's own test fixtures do exactly that. The defence is the residual list plus the later per-directory human grill, not the gate.

REVIEW PROCESS: 430/430 tests pass; run-quality-checks reports 0 issues; scan-crimes 0; find-all-stubs 0; validate-no-external-excuses 0; no [::AMBIGUOUS::] markers; every changed source file carries its ticket annotation.

STATUS: /review-ticket stops before Step 11 (reviewed). A BLOCKER finding is open, so the tickets stay `done` until the defects are fixed and re-reviewed.

PROPOSED TICKETS: (1) ownership/owns must agree - make a package `owns` entry without a matching ownership entry fail G3, with the count that names it; (2) wire checkDependencyMatrix into the gate and reject an unknown clause group instead of dropping it; (3) surface structure.spec_pulse candidates before authoring (extract or a new subcommand).

Re-probed independently of PX-202's own suite.
- The MAJOR (reasonCode unenforced in both directions) is CLOSED: G4 runs checkDependencyMatrix, refusing an unknown code and the misspelled reason_code key.
- The MINOR (an unknown clause group vanished) is CLOSED: canonicalizeClauses rejects it naming the contract id and the key.
- The WORKFLOW GAP (the pulse candidates were invisible while the AI authored their settlements) is CLOSED: run.mjs extract prints spec_pulse with kind, chapter_ref, observation and evidence_refs.
- A fifth defect of the same class, found while planning PX-202, is CLOSED: forbidden edges are passed into the pipeline, G4 reports how many arrived, and a pair declared both normal and forbidden is refused.
- Tests: 452/452 pass (was 430). Quality: four remaining findings, all pre-existing many-parameters options objects (contract-model.mjs:80, seed-local-checks.mjs:27, reference-block.mjs:30, seed-authoring-packet.mjs:141); reported to the operator for a decision rather than churned during review.

acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path] — A complete workspace is published and re-verified:** from a stage-1 manifest and an approved decisions payload the run publishes the directory tree, one RFC-SEED.md per seed_required package and WORKSPACIFY-ALLOCATE-MANIFEST.json; the manifest self-hash verifies, its seed_index hashes match the files, the coverage proof reports zero uncovered segments, the reload pass reproduces the contract registry, graph hash, implementation order and coverage, and the residue check reports exactly the published set.

**[Error case] — A failure publishes nothing and leaves no debris:** a gate failure, a reload divergence, a manifest self-hash mismatch or an interrupted publish leaves the workspace byte-identical to its pre-run state, removes the staging root and every intermediate file, and reports the failing gate with the located artefact; a second run against an already-published workspace is BLOCKED rather than merged.

**[Edge case] — Degenerate and boundary workspaces:** a single-package workspace publishes a manifest with a one-entry seed index and one wave; a package with no external contracts appears in the registry with no contract edges; a workspace whose plan is empty is refused by the fresh-workspace policy; a stale staging directory from an interrupted run is cleaned without touching published content.
