tickets.notes:
Implementation summary (PX-196):
- Root cause: stage 2 demanded a seed reference for EVERY specification segment, while stage 1 never guaranteed that every segment carries harvested material. A real specification (overview, glossary) therefore failed at G3.5. The synthetic allocate fixtures happened to cover all segments, and no test ever ran the stage-1 CLI from the allocate suite, so the coupling gap survived PX-192..PX-195.
- Fix: structure.segments[].owned_inventory_ids is now published by stage 1 (lib/segment-ownership.mjs), the coverage proof splits material_segments (required) from non_material_segments (recorded in the allocate manifest), and the entry format gate requires the declaration so the proof cannot pass vacuously.
- Also fixed while driving a real manifest: the WIG required a tests clause and a proof clause unconditionally; both now follow the boundary scope stage 1 declared.
- Tests added: tests/workspacify-tree/unit/segment-ownership.test.mjs (stage-1 derivation), tests/workspacify-allocate/acceptance/cross-stage-pipeline.test.mjs (real stage-1 CLI -> real stage-2 CLI, including the refusal of a manifest that drops the declaration), plus fixture and expectation updates in the allocate helper and coverage test.
- Test results: node --test over tests/workspacify-allocate and tests/workspacify-tree -> 395 pass / 0 fail. Quality checks 0 issues.
- Process note: this ticket was created and implemented in one pass with the make/plan fields compressed into this summary rather than run through the separate /make-ticket, /plan-ticket stages; the contract ids used by the tests are C001 (segment ownership declared by stage 1), C002 (coverage rule and manifest recording) and C003 (cross-stage E2E and the refusal of an undeclared manifest). A later /review-ticket may want the contract/test fields backfilled.
Review report (PX-192..PX-201, workspacify-tree + workspacify-allocate):

VERDICT: not yet complete. Machine verification is strong and the two-stage coupling is what saves it, but three defects remain, one of them a false clean bill of health in the published stage-1 manifest.

BLOCKER 1 - a dropped ownership entry is masked by the package catalog, so stage 1 reports a clean audit while an inventory object has no owner.
  Evidence: decisions with `pkg-b.owns.objects=[obj-000002]` but no `ownership` entry for it -> finalize exits 0, published manifest has `inventory.objects[1].owner_package = null`, `workspace.ownership.entries` has no row for it, and `final_audit` reports `orphan_object_count: 0, unallocated_count: 0, status: PASS`.
  Root cause: lib/ownership.mjs resolveOwners() unions the inventory owner with every package's `owns.*`, so `owns` masks the missing ownership entry, while buildOwnershipTable() (and stage 2) use the ownership-derived owner only.
  Blast radius: stage 2 refuses the manifest at G3.5 (`allocation is incomplete: 1 inventory item(s) allocated to no package`) and publishes nothing, so no material is lost - the coupling built in PX-196/PX-197 is doing the work here. But the stage-1 manifest, which stage 2's entry gate accepts, carries a false audit, and the AI loses the count that would tell it to fix the ownership entry.

MAJOR 2 - reasonCode is unenforced in both directions.
  (a) A value outside REASON_CODES is accepted (`totally-made-up` published unchanged); lib/dependencies.mjs checkDependencyMatrix() exists for exactly this but is never called by the pipeline.
  (b) The field spelled `reason_code` instead of `reasonCode` is silently ignored: the edge survives with reasonCode undefined and the published boundary records null. The command document carried this misspelling in three places until this review's documentation pass corrected it, which is how the trap was found.

MINOR 3 - an unknown clause group is silently discarded.
  lib/contract-model.mjs canonicalizeClauses() iterates only CONTRACT_CLAUSES, so `clauses.made_up_clause` vanishes without an error and the gate passes. Contrast: an authored contract id with no declared boundary throws and stops the run. Authored content should not disappear quietly.

WORKFLOW GAP 4 (AI-semantic dimension) - the pulse candidates are invisible while the AI authors their settlements. run.mjs computes structure.spec_pulse inside gate/finalize only; `extract` prints stats alone, and the failure message names the candidate id and kind but not its observation or chapter. With two candidates of the same kind the AI cannot tell which chapter each one is about. Documented in the command doc during this review (Step 3 item 5), but the input itself is still unreachable before authoring.

WHAT IS PROVEN STRONG.
  - Machine (stage 2): one-sided contract, emptied core clause, machine-section authoring, empty body, missing focus, unconverged pass, thin residual, banned phrase, unapproved semantic_review and a dropped stage-1 residual are all refused with a located message (G3 / G3.6 / G3.7 / G5).
  - Machine (stage 1): owner collision, edge outside the catalog, cycle, missing tree leaf, orphan boundary, uncovered edge, unsettled pulse candidate, unanswered review candidate, missing semantic_review and a banned phrase are all refused.
  - Coupling: a real stage-1 run drives a real stage-2 publish over a specification containing a material-free prose segment, and the false-audit manifest above is caught by the allocation proof rather than accepted.
  - AI-semantic loop: focus coverage, convergence (the final pass must list no finding), residual shape, verbatim stage-1 carry (candidate id and topic), reachability into seed section 12 and into handoff_summary are all machine-forced; no path asks a human anything.

RESIDUAL RISK (inherent, stated not hidden): the machine cannot tell a real critique from a performed one. A payload whose five focuses all report zero findings converges on pass 1 and is accepted - the project's own test fixtures do exactly that. The defence is the residual list plus the later per-directory human grill, not the gate.

REVIEW PROCESS: 430/430 tests pass; run-quality-checks reports 0 issues; scan-crimes 0; find-all-stubs 0; validate-no-external-excuses 0; no [::AMBIGUOUS::] markers; every changed source file carries its ticket annotation.

- [Normal condition] A COMPLETE manifest carries spec_defects and residual_questions such that every pulse candidate id appears in exactly one of them, every spec_defect carries ai_interpretation, chosen_default and rationale, and every residual_question carries topic, alternatives, chosen_default and why_unresolved.
- [Error invariant] When a candidate is unaccounted for, or a spec_defect lacks one of its required fields, or any payload contains a forbidden external-dependency phrase (TODO, TBD, ask the human, waiting for approval, human review required), finalize fails with a typed error naming the candidate id or the offending field; nothing is published.
- [Internal state invariant] The pulse is a pure function of the normalized specification text plus the harvested inventory: the same input yields identical candidates, ids and ordering, and the ids are stable across runs (pulse-000001 style ids assigned in document order).
- [Boundary invariant] Degenerate inputs are explicit: a specification with a single chapter yields no isolation candidate; a chapter with no normative phrase and no harvested item yields no extraction-gap candidate; an empty inventory yields an empty gap list rather than a crash; a specification where every chapter is healthy yields an empty candidate list and the gate then requires empty spec_defects and residual_questions.
tickets.background:
### Goal
Make the original long specification auditable before it is decomposed: a machine-generated pulse lists every place where the specification itself is weak (thin normative density, isolated chapters, oversized chapters, normative phrases with no harvested item, near-duplicate or undefined terms, table/prose mismatches), and the AI resolves each candidate in a structured spec_defects record. The run never stops for a human: an unresolved item becomes a residual_question carried to the seeds grill-question section (PX-201), not a question asked now.

### Purpose
The final quality of the RFC-SEED.md set is bounded by the quality of the specification it is transferred from. Today nothing looks at the specification as a document: the harvest either finds candidates or it does not, and a chapter that yields nothing is indistinguishable from a chapter that says nothing important.

### Motivation
Adversarial review inside the workflow keeps finding specification-level defects (a rule stated once and never referenced, a table that contradicts its prose, a term used two ways). Those findings must be produced by the machine as candidates and settled by the AI in the same session, because the human grill happens later, per directory, on the seeds.

### Constraints
- ABSOLUTE: workspacify-tree must never stop for a human, never ask a question in prose, and never defer to a human. Every candidate is either resolved by the AI (spec_defects) or recorded as a residual_question for the later human grill on the seeds.
- The pulse reports candidates only: it never grades prose, never decides importance and never removes a candidate.
- Deterministic output: the same specification text must always yield the same candidate set, sorted by a canonical key.
- No external dependency; Node.js standard library only.
- A candidate is never silently dropped: the gate requires every candidate id to appear either in spec_defects or in residual_questions.
scope:
**Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**
  -  — ADD. buildSpecPulse({ sourceText, headings, segments, inventory }) returning { candidates: [{ id, kind, chapter_ref, observation, evidence_refs }], summary }, with kinds: thin_normative_density, isolated_chapter, oversized_chapter, extraction_gap, near_duplicate_term, undefined_reference, table_prose_mismatch. Candidate ids are pulse-%06d in document order; observation is a full English sentence that states the observation without judging it; evidence_refs are heading ids and segment ids.
  -  — ADD. validateSpecDefects({ candidates, specDefects, residualQuestions }) returning { ok, errors }: every candidate id appears exactly once across the two lists; spec_defects require { candidate_id, ai_interpretation, chosen_default, rationale }; residual_questions require { candidate_id, topic, alternatives, chosen_default, why_unresolved } with alternatives a non-empty array; forbidden external-dependency phrases are rejected in every free-text field.
  -  — MODIFY the gate pipeline: G2 gains a spec_pulse result whose candidates feed the decisions surface, and G3 gains validateSpecDefects over decisions.spec_defects / decisions.residual_questions.
  -  — MODIFY: the extract step prints the pulse summary, the finalize path publishes structure/spec_pulse and stage2_handoff.spec_defects + stage2_handoff.residual_questions, and the format/gate output names each unresolved candidate.
  -  — MODIFY: declare spec_defects[] and residual_questions[] with their required fields.
  -  — MODIFY: Step 2 gains the pulse review as an AI judgement step (resolve or record; never ask a human), and the hand-off section states that residual_questions are the input of the later per-directory human grill.
  -  — MODIFY: the receiver section states that stage-1 residual_questions must be carried into the affected seeds grill-question section (consumed by PX-201).
  - Tests — ADD tests/workspacify-tree/unit/spec-pulse.test.mjs (one case per candidate kind, determinism, empty candidate list) and tests/workspacify-tree/unit/spec-defects.test.mjs (coverage, required fields, phrase ban, boundary cases).

  - [Before → After (behavior/signature)] new exports buildSpecPulse and validateSpecDefects; the manifest gains structure.spec_pulse and stage2_handoff.spec_defects / stage2_handoff.residual_questions.
  - [API contract change (if any)] additive only.
  - [Data schema change (if any)] decisions schema gains spec_defects[] and residual_questions[].
  - [Config/env change (if any)] none.
  - [Dependency added/removed (if any)] none.

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - Editing the specification automatically — excluded: the pulse reports, the AI decides; rewriting the source is a human act outside this pipeline.
  - Any human hand-back path — excluded by the absolute constraint.
  - Judging whether a chapter is *important* — excluded: importance is semantic and stays with the AI, expressed as a spec_defect rationale.

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - PX-201 (allocate) consumes residual_questions to populate seed grill questions; the hand-off field name is therefore frozen here.
  - tests/workspacify-tree fixtures — the fixtures gain a deliberately weak specification (an isolated chapter and a normative phrase with no item) so the pulse has something to find.
  - The stage-1 command document — the pulse review is a new AI step, so the document must state it (otherwise the operator AI will not run it).
testUnit: **UT: [Normal] — each pulse kind is detected on a purpose-built specification:** a specification with (a) a chapter whose normative phrases yield no harvested item, (b) a chapter never referenced by another chapter, (c) a chapter far above the median length, (d) two spellings of one term and (e) a table contradicting its prose yields exactly one candidate of each kind; every candidate carries a stable id, a chapter_ref and evidence_refs (precondition: normalized text plus its harvested inventory; postcondition: candidates with the expected kinds and no others).

**UT: [Error] — an unaccounted candidate fails the gate with the candidate id:** validateSpecDefects over a candidate list of three ids with only two recorded reports the missing id in the error message and returns ok=false; a spec_defect missing chosen_default is rejected naming that field; a residual_question whose alternatives array is empty is rejected (deterministic, no external dependency).

**UT: [Invariant] — the pulse is deterministic and id-stable:** running buildSpecPulse twice over the same text yields identical candidates, ids and order; inserting a new chapter shifts later ids only by the document-order rule and never reuses an id (asserting the pulse-%06d sequence).

**UT: [Invariant] — forbidden phrasing is rejected everywhere:** a spec_defect rationale containing TODO, TBD, ask the human, waiting for approval or human review required is rejected with the phrase quoted; the same phrases are rejected in residual_questions.why_unresolved and in aiSections values (precondition: the phrase list is a frozen constant; postcondition: every listed phrase is refused in every free-text field).

**UT: [Boundary] — degenerate specifications yield no candidates:** a single-chapter specification yields no isolated_chapter candidate; a chapter with neither normative phrases nor harvested items yields no extraction_gap; an empty inventory yields an empty gap list; an all-healthy specification yields candidates: [] and the gate then requires empty spec_defects and residual_questions.

**UT: [Contract C001/C002] — the manifest carries the resolved and residual sets:** a COMPLETE manifest exposes structure.spec_pulse.summary counts, stage2_handoff.spec_defects with the required fields and stage2_handoff.residual_questions with topic/alternatives/chosen_default/why_unresolved; recomputing the pulse from the same specification reproduces the same candidate ids.

tickets.notes:
- **Implementation steps**: 1) RED — write spec-pulse and spec-defects tests (one case per kind, determinism, coverage, phrase ban, boundaries) plus a fixture specification that is deliberately weak; they fail because the modules do not exist. 2) GREEN — implement spec-pulse.mjs, then spec-defects.mjs, then wire G2/G3, the decisions schema and the finalize publish. 3) Update the tree command document with the pulse review step and the hand-off wording, and the allocate receiver wording. 4) REFACTOR — table-driven kinds, named constants for the phrase list and the density thresholds, one function per kind.
- **Risks**: (a) a pulse that is too noisy makes the AI resolve trivia, so the density threshold must be justified in the code comment and tunable by one constant; (b) the phrase ban can produce false positives in legitimate prose (for example quoting a specification that itself says TBD) — the gate therefore reports the phrase with its field so the AI can rephrase; (c) residual questions carried from stage 1 must reach the seeds in PX-201 or they are lost, so the field name is frozen here and asserted there.
- **Caveats**: the pulse never edits the specification; a specification defect that the AI cannot resolve becomes a residual question, never a stop and never a question to the operator; counting chapters is document structure, so the pulse must ignore code fences exactly as the heading extractor does.
- **Open items**: whether the density threshold should be per chapter or per segment — decided as per chapter with the segment count as evidence, since chapter granularity is what the AI reasons about.
- **Future improvements**: the kind list can be extended with a fixture per new kind; the pulse summary can later feed the drill-rfc-down loop as an input quality measure.
Implementation status: INCOMPLETE. The feature is implemented and its own tests pass (tests/workspacify-tree/unit/spec-pulse.test.mjs 3/3, tests/workspacify-tree/unit/spec-defects.test.mjs 4/4). The tree suite is 234 tests with 9 failures, all of the same kind: legacy fixtures whose decisions payloads predate the pulse, so their specifications now report candidates that nobody settled. Review report (PX-192..PX-201, workspacify-tree + workspacify-allocate):

VERDICT: not yet complete. Machine verification is strong and the two-stage coupling is what saves it, but three defects remain, one of them a false clean bill of health in the published stage-1 manifest.

BLOCKER 1 - a dropped ownership entry is masked by the package catalog, so stage 1 reports a clean audit while an inventory object has no owner.
  Evidence: decisions with `pkg-b.owns.objects=[obj-000002]` but no `ownership` entry for it -> finalize exits 0, published manifest has `inventory.objects[1].owner_package = null`, `workspace.ownership.entries` has no row for it, and `final_audit` reports `orphan_object_count: 0, unallocated_count: 0, status: PASS`.
  Root cause: lib/ownership.mjs resolveOwners() unions the inventory owner with every package's `owns.*`, so `owns` masks the missing ownership entry, while buildOwnershipTable() (and stage 2) use the ownership-derived owner only.
  Blast radius: stage 2 refuses the manifest at G3.5 (`allocation is incomplete: 1 inventory item(s) allocated to no package`) and publishes nothing, so no material is lost - the coupling built in PX-196/PX-197 is doing the work here. But the stage-1 manifest, which stage 2's entry gate accepts, carries a false audit, and the AI loses the count that would tell it to fix the ownership entry.

MAJOR 2 - reasonCode is unenforced in both directions.
  (a) A value outside REASON_CODES is accepted (`totally-made-up` published unchanged); lib/dependencies.mjs checkDependencyMatrix() exists for exactly this but is never called by the pipeline.
  (b) The field spelled `reason_code` instead of `reasonCode` is silently ignored: the edge survives with reasonCode undefined and the published boundary records null. The command document carried this misspelling in three places until this review's documentation pass corrected it, which is how the trap was found.

MINOR 3 - an unknown clause group is silently discarded.
  lib/contract-model.mjs canonicalizeClauses() iterates only CONTRACT_CLAUSES, so `clauses.made_up_clause` vanishes without an error and the gate passes. Contrast: an authored contract id with no declared boundary throws and stops the run. Authored content should not disappear quietly.

WORKFLOW GAP 4 (AI-semantic dimension) - the pulse candidates are invisible while the AI authors their settlements. run.mjs computes structure.spec_pulse inside gate/finalize only; `extract` prints stats alone, and the failure message names the candidate id and kind but not its observation or chapter. With two candidates of the same kind the AI cannot tell which chapter each one is about. Documented in the command doc during this review (Step 3 item 5), but the input itself is still unreachable before authoring.

WHAT IS PROVEN STRONG.
  - Machine (stage 2): one-sided contract, emptied core clause, machine-section authoring, empty body, missing focus, unconverged pass, thin residual, banned phrase, unapproved semantic_review and a dropped stage-1 residual are all refused with a located message (G3 / G3.6 / G3.7 / G5).
  - Machine (stage 1): owner collision, edge outside the catalog, cycle, missing tree leaf, orphan boundary, uncovered edge, unsettled pulse candidate, unanswered review candidate, missing semantic_review and a banned phrase are all refused.
  - Coupling: a real stage-1 run drives a real stage-2 publish over a specification containing a material-free prose segment, and the false-audit manifest above is caught by the allocation proof rather than accepted.
  - AI-semantic loop: focus coverage, convergence (the final pass must list no finding), residual shape, verbatim stage-1 carry (candidate id and topic), reachability into seed section 12 and into handoff_summary are all machine-forced; no path asks a human anything.

RESIDUAL RISK (inherent, stated not hidden): the machine cannot tell a real critique from a performed one. A payload whose five focuses all report zero findings converges on pass 1 and is accepted - the project's own test fixtures do exactly that. The defence is the residual list plus the later per-directory human grill, not the gate.

REVIEW PROCESS: 430/430 tests pass; run-quality-checks reports 0 issues; scan-crimes 0; find-all-stubs 0; validate-no-external-excuses 0; no [::AMBIGUOUS::] markers; every changed source file carries its ticket annotation.

STATUS: /review-ticket stops before Step 11 (reviewed). A BLOCKER finding is open, so the tickets stay `done` until the defects are fixed and re-reviewed.

PROPOSED TICKETS: (1) ownership/owns must agree - make a package `owns` entry without a matching ownership entry fail G3, with the count that names it; (2) wire checkDependencyMatrix into the gate and reject an unknown clause group instead of dropping it; (3) surface structure.spec_pulse candidates before authoring (extract or a new subcommand).

Re-probed independently of PX-202's own suite.
- The MAJOR (reasonCode unenforced in both directions) is CLOSED: G4 runs checkDependencyMatrix, refusing an unknown code and the misspelled reason_code key.
- The MINOR (an unknown clause group vanished) is CLOSED: canonicalizeClauses rejects it naming the contract id and the key.
- The WORKFLOW GAP (the pulse candidates were invisible while the AI authored their settlements) is CLOSED: run.mjs extract prints spec_pulse with kind, chapter_ref, observation and evidence_refs.
- A fifth defect of the same class, found while planning PX-202, is CLOSED: forbidden edges are passed into the pipeline, G4 reports how many arrived, and a pair declared both normal and forbidden is refused.
- Tests: 452/452 pass (was 430). Quality: four remaining findings, all pre-existing many-parameters options objects (contract-model.mjs:80, seed-local-checks.mjs:27, reference-block.mjs:30, seed-authoring-packet.mjs:141); reported to the operator for a decision rather than churned during review.
- Unchanged and stated: the machine cannot judge whether a critique or a keep decision is good; that remains the AI's judgement and the later per-directory human grill.

acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path] — a weak specification is audited and resolved:** the pulse reports its candidates, the AI resolves them in spec_defects or records them as residual_questions, the manifest publishes both sets with the required fields, and the run completes without asking a human anything.

**[Error case] — an unaccounted or badly formed record stops the run:** a candidate missing from both lists, a spec_defect without a rationale, a residual_question without alternatives, or any external-dependency phrase in a free-text field fails the gate with a typed error naming the artefact, and nothing is published.

**[Edge case] — degenerate and healthy specifications:** single-chapter, empty-inventory, all-healthy and phrase-quoting specifications are each handled with the specific behaviour described above, and the double gate still accepts the published manifest.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:

- Give every candidate kind its own verb-phrase detector (detectExtractionGap, detectIsolatedChapter, ...) so the pulse reads as a list of observations and adding a kind cannot disturb the others.
- Reuse the existing heading and segmentation helpers rather than re-parsing markdown, keeping one parser in the codebase.
- Replace any terse boolean flags in the touched validation path with domain names (specDefects, residualQuestions, candidates) and return verdict objects instead of throwing from the library layer.
- Ensure newly touched functions return { ok, errors } and that callers convert a negative verdict into a typed gate failure with the offending artefact named — no swallowed errors.

tickets.title: dependency-review: 依存・境界の意味論レビュー材料と判断記録
tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] A COMPLETE manifest carries dependency_reviews such that every review candidate id appears exactly once, each review states decision in {keep, replace_with_port, merge, split, residual}, a rationale, and the alternatives considered; the published normal_edges and boundaries are consistent with every decision.
- [Error invariant] An unaccounted candidate, an unknown decision value, a missing rationale or a decision inconsistent with the published edges (for example replace_with_port while the edge is still declared) fails the gate with a typed error naming the candidate id and the edge; nothing is published.
- [Internal state invariant] The candidate list is a pure function of (package catalog, edge set, boundary set, ownership table): the same inputs yield identical candidate ids (review-%06d in canonical order) and the same kind assignment.
- [Boundary invariant] Degenerate graphs are explicit: a single package yields no candidates; an acyclic chain yields no unnecessary-serialization candidate; a fully connected pair yields one under-split candidate rather than many; an empty edge set yields an empty candidate list and the gate then requires empty dependency_reviews.
tickets.background:
### Goal
Give the AI the material it needs to judge the dependency graph and the boundaries as an engineer rather than an acceptor: which declared edges look unnecessary (they serialize implementation without carrying material), which forbidden edges have a viable alternative route, which packages are over- or under-split, and which packages are interface-stability risks because too many consumers depend on them. The AI records a decision per candidate in dependency_reviews; the machine verifies that every candidate has a decision, that the decision shape is complete and that the final graph is consistent with it. No human is asked anything.

### Purpose
The DAG gate proves the graph is well formed, never that it is the right graph. An unnecessary edge forces a provider to be implemented before an unrelated consumer, and an under-split package hides two responsibilities behind one seed; both are design defects that only show up as implementation pain much later.

### Motivation
Adversarial review inside the workflow keeps producing exactly these findings by hand. Turning them into machine-supplied candidates with a recorded AI decision moves the finding earlier, where it is cheap, and leaves an audit trail in the manifest.

### Constraints
- ABSOLUTE: no human hand-back, no prose question, no deferral. A candidate is kept, replaced, merged, split or recorded as residual by the AI in this session.

- Deterministic: identical decisions and package catalog produce identical candidates, ids and order.

- Standard library only; no new dependency.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Turn the adversarial review that decides seed quality into an explicit, converging, AI-only loop: the AI drafts the coupling contracts first, cross-checks them against the counterpart seed, then runs four critic passes (implementer, counterpart, test, grill) plus an adversarial pass, recording every round and every residual finding. The machine verifies the loop's structure (rounds, focuses, residual shape), that every residual reaches the affected seed's grill-question section, and that no payload anywhere asks a human for anything.

### Purpose
Quality of the seed set is decided by this loop, not by the structural gates. Today the only semantic anchor is a single APPROVED flag; there is no required critique, no convergence condition and no place where an unresolved design choice is guaranteed to reach the later human grill.

### Motivation
The human grill runs later, per directory, on RFC-SEED.md; everything the AI cannot settle here must arrive there as a precise, actionable question. Any pause, prose question or "waiting for approval" inside workspacify-allocate is forbidden, so the loop must converge on its own and hand over residuals structurally.

### Constraints
- ABSOLUTE: no human hand-back, no prose question to the operator, no deferral to a human. Residuals become seed grill questions, never questions asked now.
- The loop is AI judgement: the machine verifies structure and reachability, never the quality of a finding or a resolution.
- Convergence is required evidence: at least the four critic focuses must appear in self_grill.rounds (a missing focus needs a stated reason), and residuals must be non-empty only where genuinely unresolved.
- Every residual's grill_question must appear verbatim in the affected seed's section 13 (machine parity), and the manifest carries the hand-off summary.
- No new dependency; standard library only.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Close the four holes the PX-192..PX-201 review found so that every check the command documents actually runs, and nothing the AI authors disappears without a named error: (1) a package `owns` entry with no matching `ownership` entry must fail G3 instead of being masked into a clean audit; (2) `reasonCode` must be validated against REASON_CODES and a misspelled `reason_code` must be rejected rather than silently ignored; (3) a clause group outside CONTRACT_CLAUSES must be rejected rather than dropped by canonicalisation; (4) `extract` must surface the `structure.spec_pulse` candidates so the AI can author their settlements instead of guessing.

### Purpose
Stage 2 already refuses a manifest whose audit lies, so no material reaches a broken workspace (proved: the same payload that publishes here is stopped by stage 2 at G3.5 with "allocation is incomplete: 1 inventory item(s) allocated to no package"). But a stage-1 manifest reporting `orphan_object_count: 0, unallocated_count: 0, status: PASS` while `inventory.objects[].owner_package` is null is a false clean bill of health in the artefact that IS the hand-off, and it hides the count that would tell the AI what to repair. The other three are the same class: a documented check that does not run, or authored content discarded without a word.

### Motivation
These two commands decide the whole downstream workspace: a verification gap propagates into every seed, every RFC and every implementation ticket, and the operator AI trusts the audit line when deciding whether to publish. The review's mutation probe measured the gap (stage 1 11/14, stage 2 11/12 injected defects caught) and the three misses are exactly these holes. Making the machine's own report trustworthy is the precondition for the AI's semantic judgement to mean anything.

### Constraints
- ABSOLUTE: no human hand-back, no prose question, no deferral in either stage. Every rejection names the artefact and the value.
- Additive enforcement: a payload that is correct today must still publish unchanged; the existing 430 tests stay green without weakening any of them.
- Deterministic: identical decisions produce identical counts, messages and candidate order.
- Standard library only; no new dependency.
- Both command documents must state each newly enforced rule where the AI reads it, and must not claim a check that does not exist.

tickets.investigation:
- [Evidence] The forward ownership hole is real and reproducible: decisions with `pkg-b.owns.objects=[obj-000002]` and no `ownership` entry for it -> `run.mjs finalize` exits 0, the published manifest has `inventory.objects[1].owner_package = null`, `workspace.ownership.entries` has no row for it, and `final_audit` reports `{"orphan_object_count":0,"unallocated_count":0,"status":"PASS"}`.
- [Evidence] The root cause is `lib/ownership.mjs#resolveOwners`: it unions the inventory owner (set from `decisions.ownership` by applyOwnership, which writes `owner_package` for objects and `primary_owner` for claims) with every package whose `owns.*` contains the id, so `owns` masks the missing ownership entry; `countCategoryOrphans` uses the same union, and `buildOwnershipTable` in run.mjs plus stage 2's `deriveExpectedAllocation` read the ownership-derived owner only.
- [Evidence] The reverse direction is already caught, but incidentally and with an unrelated message: `owns.objects=[]` with the ownership entry present fails with "production-library pkg-b owns no objects or claims; likely a speculative split". A ghost id is also already caught: "owns.objects obj-999999 of package pkg-b does not resolve to any inventory item". The new check must therefore be sold as the forward-direction fix plus a precise message, not as covering cases that already pass.
- [Evidence] The forbidden edges never reach the checks: a payload with one forbidden edge publishes `dependencies.forbidden_edges.length === 1` while G4 reports `forbidden_edge_count: 0` and `final_audit.forbidden_dependency_count: 0`. `run.mjs` builds the pipeline's `dependencies` input as `{ normalEdges, boundaries }` only, so `evaluateDag` forwards an empty forbidden list to `runDagChecks`, whose `explicitForbidden` branch (dag.mjs:101) can therefore never fire.
- [Evidence] `canonicalizeClauses({ input: 'i', output: 'o', made_up_clause: ['x'] })` returns `{"input":"i","output":"o"}`: the unknown group is dropped in silence (lib/contract-model.mjs iterates `[...CONTRACT_CLAUSES].sort()` and never inspects unknown keys), while an authored contract id with no declared boundary throws in run.mjs#buildContractEdgesForPackage - the two paths disagree on whether authored content may vanish.
- [Evidence] `checkDependencyMatrix` (lib/dependencies.mjs) validates exactly the reason-code vocabulary and the edge endpoints, and `grep -rn checkDependencyMatrix .claude/scripts --include=*.mjs` returns no call site outside its own module: it is dead code today, which is why `reasonCode: 'totally-made-up'` and an edge carrying `reason_code` both publish unchanged.
- [Evidence] `run.mjs extract` prints exactly `{"harvested":2,"confirmed":1,"review_required":1,"unresolved":1,"invariants":0,"state_machines":0,"error_codes":0,"required_tests":0}` for the gaia fixture: no pulse. The pulse is computed by `buildSpecPulseForAnalysis` inside runGate/runFinalize only, and the gate failure names the candidate id and kind without the observation or the chapter ref, so the AI authors settlements blind.
- [Evidence] The review's mutation probe against the real CLI: stage 1 caught 11/14 injected defects, stage 2 caught 11/12; the three stage-1 misses are the ownership, reason-code and clause holes, the fourth stage-1 hole is the forbidden-edge wiring found while planning, and the stage-2 miss is the silent clause drop. The probe becomes the regression suite of this ticket.
- [Evidence] `tests/workspacify-tree/fixtures/gaia-like-spec.md` yields 2 objects (1 CONFIRMED, 1 REVIEW_REQUIRED) and a non-empty pulse, so it can carry every case in this ticket without a new fixture.

- Give the new pulse output a named builder (`buildPulseReport`) rather than assembling it inline in runExtract, so the printed shape and the published shape come from one description.

tickets.title: workspacify-reverse 基盤: 順回転痕跡の検出・除去・検証スクリプトと実験入力の清浄化
tickets.background:
### Goal
siprs-for-reverse に対する逆回転が「AI が答えを読めるか」ではなく「実装から設計を再建できるか」を測る実験として成立するための最小条件を、機械的に保証された状態にする。

### Purpose
既存プロジェクトを conver の4層ループへ反転させる逆回転パイプライン（docs/ABOUT-REVERSE.md）は、その入力が順回転の痕跡を含んでいてはならない。本チケットはその前提条件を、汎用の検出器・スクラバ・検証器として実装する。

### Motivation
現状の siprs-for-reverse は .claude/.git/docs/specs と forward 由来 JSON を削除しただけであり、ソース本体（126ファイル / 52,689行）は siprs-with-4layers と同一で、順回転のプロベナンス鎖を丸ごと保持している。実測した漏洩は4層:
- **L1 プロベナンス**: [::TICKET::] 655行、Initial Design Artifact ヘッダ 99ファイル、NODE_ID= 127、To show details 109、RFC-ROOT 言及 427/412/314
- **L2 契約**: @verifies 673行、ユニーク契約ID 144、契約コメント 126ファイル、omission ID 7、RFC §番号 59
- **L3 設計文書依存テスト**: client.rs の9行（RFC-ROOT.md が無いため既に失敗する）
- **L4 コード構造**: モジュール名・公開API（正当な逆回転入力。除去しない）

この状態で逆回転が「成功」しても、AI が答えを読めるかを測っただけであり、siprs への最適化と区別できない。科学的に意味のある反証可能な実験にするには、痕跡の除去とその機械的検証が先に必要である。

### Constraints
- **順回転を一切破壊しない。** スクリプトは `.claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse/` に新設し、既存 workspacify モジュールに触れない
- **原本 siprs-with-4layers は無傷で保持する**（Initial Design Artifact ヘッダのトレーサビリティはそこに保全される）
- **検出器は汎用でなければならない。** siprs 固有の実装をしてはならず、他プロジェクトで同じ汚染を検出できること
- **誤削除の防止**: IETF 標準参照（RFC 4733 / RFC 2833 / RFC 2976）と非コメント行（文字列リテラル）を絶対に除去しない
- 出力は Markdown + 意味論を含む自然言語を原則とする（docs/ABOUT-REVERSE.md 5章）
tickets.invariants:
- 【通常成立】対象ルートとその配下の全対象ファイル（.rs / .toml / .yml / .conf / .h）が列挙され、`vendor/` と `.git/` は除外される。検出結果は層別の件数と file:line を持つ
- 【エラー時】対象ルート不在・読み取り不能・書き込み不能のいずれでも例外を握りつぶさず、原因と該当パスを報告して非ゼロ終了する。`--dry-run` では対象ファイルが 1 バイトも変化しない
- 【内部状態】検出・除去・検証の 3 段は `trace-patterns.mjs` の単一のパターン定義を共有する。検出器と検証器が異なる述語を持つ状態は不正である
- 【境界】`RFC \d+`（IETF 標準参照）と非コメント行は、いかなる入力に対しても除去されない。閉じフェンスを欠く不完全ヘッダ、0 バイトファイル、CRLF 改行、ヘッダのみのファイルで誤削除が起きない
scope:
**Scope of changes:**
  - [File/module path] `.claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse/`（新設）、`tests/workspacify-reverse/`（新設）、`siprs-for-reverse/`（データ。スクラブ対象）
  - [Action] **add**（スクリプト新設） / **modify**（siprs-for-reverse のコメント行削除、L3 テストの扱い、ファイル名の痕跡への対処）
  - [What specifically changes] 5 モジュールの新設 + siprs-for-reverse の L1/L2 除去 + L3 該当テストの処理 + ファイル名の痕跡への対処
  - [Before → After] 検出・除去・検証の手段が存在しない → `run.mjs detect|scrub|verify` の 3 サブコマンドで機械的に実行・検証できる。siprs-for-reverse は L1/L2 = 0 件の状態になる
  - [API contract] 新設 CLI: `run.mjs <detect|scrub|verify> <root> [--apply] [--dry-run] [--json]`
  - [Data schema] 検出レポートの sidecar JSON（層・件数・file:line・sha256）。**Markdown が主、JSON は機械可読が必要な箇所のみ**（ABOUT-REVERSE.md 5.1節）
  - [Config/env] 追加なし
  - [Dependency] **追加なし**（Node.js 標準モジュールのみ。既存 workspacify と同じ方針）

**Out of scope:**
  - [Excluded item]
    (a) L4（コード構造）の除去
    (b) `siprs-with-4layers` へのいかなる変更
    (c) 逆回転パイプライン本体（`/workspacify-reverse` コマンド定義・R0〜R8 の解析スクリプト）
    (d) L3 のテストが検証していた契約内容そのものの復元
  - [Why excluded]
    (a) L4 は漏洩ではなく**正当な逆回転入力**である。除去すると実験が別物になる
    (b) 原本不可侵（C005）。トレーサビリティはここに保全する
    (c) Phase 0 以降の別チケット。本チケットは Phase −1-g の基盤のみ
    (d) それは逆回転の**成果物**であり、本チケットはその入力を整えるに過ぎない

**Affected areas:**
  - [Affected component] `siprs-for-reverse`（実験入力）、将来の逆回転パイプライン全体、他プロジェクトへのリーク検出器の適用
  - [Nature of impact] **data format**（実験入力からプロベナンス情報が消える） / **API surface**（新設 CLI） / **実験の科学性**（測定の妥当性）
  - [Corresponding change needed] **Y**: スクラブ後、逆回転の測定値を「siprs 最適化なし」と主張できるようになる。ただし**ホールドアウト検証（別プロジェクト2〜3件）は別途必要**（ABOUT-REVERSE.md 11.9節の残課題）
testUnit:

  - UT-2: `detectForwardTraces` が L1（`[::TICKET::]` / `Initial Design Artifact` / `NODE_ID=` / `To show details` / `RFC-ROOT`）を検出し、層別の件数と file:line を返す（**C001**）

  - UT-4: `detectForwardTraces` が L3（`read_to_string("RFC-ROOT.md")` 等、設計文書を読むコード行）を検出する（**C001**）
  - UT-5: `detectForwardTraces` が L4（モジュール名・公開 API）を**検出対象に含めない**（除去してはならないため）（**C001**）

  - UT-19: スクラブ前後で、**非コメント行の SHA-256 が完全一致**する（**C002**）

**UT: [契約翻訳] — 各契約条項のテスト可能形への翻訳（Phase 1.5）:**
  - **C001 precondition**「siprs-for-reverse/ が存在し、src・tests・Cargo.toml・docker 設定・wrapper.h を含む。対象ルートへの読み取り権限がある」→ UT-1 が対象ファイル列挙と権限前提を検証する

testIntegration:
**IT: [統合点] — モジュール間インタフェース:**
  - `trace-patterns.mjs` → `detect-forward-traces.mjs`（検出パターン定義の供給。L1〜L4 を単一情報源とする）

testExceptions:
**例外エントリ:**
  - [項目] `cargo check` によるビルド検証（IT-3）
  - [理由] `vendor/pjsip`（55MB）の FFI ビルドを伴い、**システム PJSIP 未導入という外部依存（external dependency）**により失敗しうる。実装の決定性に起因するものではなく、**設計欠陥ではない（not a design defect / not an architectural defect）**。テスト不能の理由は外部依存であり、本チケットの成果物（行単位のコメント除去）の正しさとは独立である
  - [代替検証] まず `cargo check --no-default-features` を試行する。それも不能な場合は、**スクラブ前後で非コメント行の SHA-256 が一致すること（UT-19）** と **プロベナンス行が 0 件になること（UT-20）** で、コメント除去が意味を壊していないことを証明する。行単位削除は意味論に影響しないため、この代替で十分に担保される

tickets.title: One verification entry point that reaches every test in the repository, and a discovery method that works on the installed Node
tickets.background:
### Goal
One command runs every automated test this repository owns and reports what it ran, so that a test which exists but is never executed cannot pass unnoticed.

### Purpose
Measured on 2026-09-11, the repository holds 307 test files across three disjoint surfaces and no command reaches all of them. `.claude/tests/run-all.js` globs `tests/**/*.test.{js,cjs}` and therefore cannot see the 124 `.test.mjs` files at all — its glob has no `.mjs` alternative. The Makefile's per-area targets reach 112 of the 120 project `.test.{js,cjs}` files and miss the eight under `reverse/`. The 124 `.mjs` files are reachable only through three ad-hoc suite runners, each of which hard-codes its own directory. Three partial surfaces, no union.

### Motivation
P22-14 through P22-17 wrote 232 tests under `tests/rfc-graph/reverse/`, `tests/tickets/reverse/` and `tests/grill-me-for-rfc/reverse/` that no `make` target reaches. They pass when invoked by hand and are invisible to anyone who runs `make`. Separately, P22-1 recorded as divergence 5 that `node --test <dir>` fails on the installed Node 26 because a directory resolves as a module, which removes the obvious "glob everything" repair. A verification surface assembled by hand is one a session can assemble wrongly without noticing, and the failure is silent: the run is green because it never looked.

### Constraints
The 14 known failures in `.claude/tests` are the PX-142 acceptance baseline and are reported as-is — neither chased nor hidden, and they must not be excluded from the count. The aggregate must not execute any file twice: `tests/rfc-graph/*.test.cjs` is currently reached by both `make test-rfc-graph` and `run-all.js`, and duplicating it would change the reported total. No test may be modified, skipped or filtered to make the aggregate pass. The existing per-area Makefile targets keep their present meaning; the union is added, not substituted.
acceptanceCriteria:
**[Happy path] — the scenario that confirms this ticket is complete:**
  - `make test` exits 0 on a clean checkout, having executed all 307 test files across the three surfaces, and its report names each surface with its file count, test count, pass count and fail count.
  - The report names the four previously unreachable directories with non-zero counts: `tests/rfc-graph/reverse` (3 files), `tests/tickets/reverse` (3), `tests/grill-me-for-rfc/reverse` (2).
  - The 14 failures in `.claude/tests` appear as `baseline-failures: 14` and the run still exits 0, because the baseline is declared rather than discovered.

**[Error case] — an error scenario the feature must handle:**
  - A test file is discovered but cannot be executed, because its surface fails to spawn. The aggregate reports the file's path in `missing[]`, names the command it attempted and the platform it ran on, and exits non-zero — even though every test that did run passed. Silent incompleteness is the defect this ticket exists to remove, so it must be impossible for a hole in the surface to produce a green run.
  - A surface whose child process exits 1 is reported with `status: "fail"` and the failing test's name, not merely with an exit code.

**[Edge case] — a boundary or exception to verify:**
  - A surface directory that exists but holds no test files is reported as `{ files: 0, status: "empty" }`, distinguishable in the report from a surface that ran and passed — the zero-file case must not read as success.
  - A file named `.test.mts` or `.test.ts` under `tests/` is listed in `unsupported[]` with its extension rather than silently ignored, so an extension the runner cannot execute is visible instead of absent.
  - `--surface=project-mjs` runs only that surface and reports the other two as `not-run`, not as passing.
  - Two consecutive runs produce byte-identical `--json` output.
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) Measure and record the three surface counts on the current tree. (2) Write the failing tests: discovery, grouping, argv construction, summarisation, the missing-file assertion, the baseline accounting, the version predicate, the write-nothing invariant. (3) Extract `tests/lib/test-discovery.mjs` with the constants; confirm the three existing suite runners still report 320/226/661 after importing it. (4) Export the surface definition from `.claude/tests/run-all.js` without changing its execution path. (5) Write the aggregate and make the tests green. (6) Add the Makefile target and the missing `reverse/` globs; add the `test` script and `engines` to `package.json`. (7) Run `make test` and the regression gate; make a deliberate edit and watch the gate fail, then restore.
- [Risks] **The largest risk is double execution.** `tests/rfc-graph/*.test.cjs` is reached by both `make test-rfc-graph` and `run-all.js`; naively concatenating surfaces would run it twice and change the reported total, which would make the baseline assertion meaningless. The union must be computed from a single discovery pass. **The second risk is that the aggregate becomes a fourth partial surface** — a new runner that hard-codes what it knows about, reproducing the defect it was written to fix. `assertNoFileMissing` comparing discovered against executed is the structural answer and must be a test, not a comment. **The third is the baseline.** 14 is a measured constant; if a future change moves it, the temptation will be to widen the tolerance rather than account for the change. The number is named once and any movement must be a deliberate edit with a reason.
- [Caveats] The three surface counts (63/120/124) are measurements of the tree on 2026-09-11 and will change as tests are added; the tests assert the partition property and the arithmetic sum, never the literals, so the counts in this ticket are evidence of the initial state rather than constants to preserve. `make test-rfc-graph` widening from 915 to 1030 changes a number other documents quote; those references are updated in the same commit.
- [Open items] Whether `make test` should become the default target is deliberately left open. Whether the `.mjs` surface should eventually be reachable through `run-all.js` as well — collapsing three surfaces into two — is likewise open, and this ticket's aggregate makes that decision cheap later by giving one place to change.
- [Future improvements] A `--watch` mode for the aggregate. Per-surface timing in the report, so a suite that becomes slow is visible before it becomes a problem. Promoting the aggregate into the `.claude` distribution tree so an installed project gets the same total-verification entry point, which requires deciding what surface an installed tree has.

tickets.title: Correct the module-convention record, untrack the 4 MB backup, and make the committed bundle provably fresh
tickets.background:
### Goal
Three recorded facts about this repository become true: the module convention is stated as the repository actually practises it, a 4 MB backup stops being tracked, and the committed `conver.js` bundle is provably the one its source produces.

### Purpose
Each item was re-measured on 2026-09-11 before being acted on, and one of them changed shape under measurement — which is why this ticket exists as three small items rather than one large one.

**(a) The convention record is wrong, and it is not the code that is wrong.** Shared premise (11), carried verbatim in all 22 P22 specs and originating at `specs/P22-1.md:64`, asserts a two-way split: `.claude/scripts/{rfc-graph,grill-me-for-rfc,conver,tickets}/` are "flat CommonJS `.js`" and `.claude/scripts/{workspacify-tree,workspacify-allocate,workspacify-reverse}/` are "ESM `.mjs` under `lib/`". Measured: `.claude/scripts/grill-me-for-rfc/package.json` declares `"type": "module"`, as do `conver/` and `drill-rfc-down/`; `.claude/scripts/rfc-graph/` and `crystalize-readme/` declare `"type": "commonjs"`; `workspacify-reverse/` has no `type` field at all and is ESM only because every file is `.mjs`. The same statement appears in the live rule file `.claude/rules/node.md` as "CommonJS only — no ESM (`import`/`export`) unless file ends in `.mjs`". A reviewer of this phase was misled by it and reported a non-existent convention violation.

**(b) A 4,270,361-byte backup is tracked.** `git ls-files -s` reports `Tickets.json.p22-ja.bak`, mode 100644, blob `bf1992ca`. Nothing references it.

**(c) The committed bundle has no freshness guard.** `make build-conver` regenerates `.claude/scripts/conver/conver.js` from `src/`, and nothing anywhere compares the two. Editing the TypeScript and forgetting the build ships a stale artefact silently. Measured: a fresh `npm run build` from HEAD reproduces the committed file byte-for-byte (427,025 bytes), so there is nothing to repair today — only a guard to add.

### Motivation
(a) is the reason this ticket exists at all: a record that contradicts the repository misleads every later session, and the misleading is silent because the record reads as authoritative. It is also the cheapest of the three to fix and the only one whose cost grows with time, since each new ticket that repeats the premise makes the error harder to see. (b) is a repository-hygiene matter with a permanent cost: the blob enters `master` on merge and stays in every clone forever. (c) is a latent defect — nothing is broken now, and the first person to edit `src/` without building will break it invisibly.

### Constraints
**No source file's module system changes.** `grill-me-for-rfc/` is correct as it stands; the record is what is wrong, and rewriting correct files to match an incorrect record would be the exact inversion of the Boy Scout rule. **The backup is not removed from history.** Rewriting 28 commits requires a force push and is an outward-facing, hard-to-reverse act; untracking and ignoring is the safe half and is all this ticket does, with history removal left as a named open item pending the user's explicit approval. **The backup file is not deleted from disk** — `git rm --cached` keeps the working copy, because deleting a user's backup is not a repository-hygiene operation. **The freshness check writes nothing into `.claude/scripts/conver/`**; it builds to a temporary path and compares.
acceptanceCriteria:
**[Happy path] — the scenario that confirms this ticket is complete:**
  - A single command reports every script directory under `.claude/scripts/` with its resolved module system, and all of them conform: `rfc-graph` and `crystalize-readme` as CommonJS, `conver`, `drill-rfc-down` and `grill-me-for-rfc` as ESM, and the three workspacify trees as ESM.
  - `.claude/rules/node.md` states the convention as the repository practises it, with the `package.json` `type` field named as the authority, and the statement is derived from the same table the test asserts rather than written twice.
  - `git ls-files Tickets.json.p22-ja.bak` returns nothing while the working-tree file is unchanged, and `.gitignore` matches the pattern.
  - A freshness check confirms `.claude/scripts/conver/conver.js` is byte-identical to a fresh build of `src/`.

**[Error case] — an error scenario the feature must handle:**
  - A `.js` file using `import` inside a directory whose nearest `package.json` declares `"type": "commonjs"` is named by path, with the resolved system and the syntax found both shown. It must not be reported as a bare failure, and it must not be silently accepted because Node's module syntax detection happens to load it — the check asserts the declaration, not the runtime's leniency.
  - A committed bundle that differs from a fresh build is reported with the committed digest, the freshly built digest and the size difference, and the check exits non-zero. A missing `esbuild` is reported as an unavailable prerequisite rather than as a stale bundle.

**[Edge case] — a boundary or exception to verify:**
  - A directory containing no `package.json` resolves through its nearest ancestor; a synthetic tree with `a/package.json` declaring `module` and `a/b/` holding only `.js` files reports those files as ESM.
  - `workspacify-reverse/` has no `type` field: its `.mjs` files resolve to ESM by extension, and the module reports that the extension decided rather than a declaration, so an ESM verdict there is not mistaken for a declared one.
  - A clone that never contained `Tickets.json.p22-ja.bak` passes the tracking check rather than failing on its absence.
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) Write the failing tests: `resolveModuleSystem` over the five `(extension, declared type)` combinations, the conformance scan, the rule-file-vs-filesystem comparison, the tracking check, and the freshness check. (2) Implement `module-convention.mjs` and make them green. (3) Correct `.claude/rules/node.md`: replace the blanket "CommonJS only" statement with the per-directory table, name the `package.json` `type` field as the authority, and correct the `>=18` engine statement to point at the `engines` field PX-204 adds. (4) Add the `Makefile` targets. (5) `git rm --cached Tickets.json.p22-ja.bak` and add `*.bak` to `.gitignore` — file kept on disk, digest taken before and after. (6) Run the regression gate before and after; it must stay `proved`.
- [Risks] **The largest risk is inverting the Boy Scout rule.** The premise says fourteen files are wrong; they are not. A session that trusts the premise and rewrites `grill-me-for-rfc/` to CommonJS would break the directory, its 46 tests, and the P22-13 and P22-14 code paths that import it. The mitigation is structural rather than advisory: the test derives the convention table from the filesystem, so "what the repository does" is the authority and the document is checked against it, never the other way round. **The second risk is the freshness check becoming flaky.** Building on every run costs seconds and depends on esbuild; if it is wired into the default test target without an escape, a machine without esbuild reports a stale bundle. The check must distinguish "cannot build" from "built and differs". **The third is `git rm --cached` being run carelessly.** `git rm` without `--cached` deletes the working file; the test that digests the backup before and after exists specifically to make that mistake visible rather than silent. **The fourth is history.** Nothing in this ticket removes the blob from the 28 commits; a reader who assumes "untracked" means "gone" will be wrong, and the open item says so.
- [Caveats] The convention table is a measurement of the tree on 2026-09-11; a future directory may legitimately declare either system, and the test asserts the *property* (each directory resolves to exactly one system) rather than the seven present names, so adding a directory does not require editing the test. The rule-file comparison does pin the table's content, so a new directory does require updating `.claude/rules/node.md` — deliberately, because a rule file that silently omits a directory is the defect this ticket is fixing. `specs/P22-1.md` is left as written; its premise is wrong and this ticket's spec is the erratum of record.
- [Open items] **Removing `bf1992ca` from history is left open pending the user's explicit approval.** It requires rebasing 28 commits and a force push, which is outward-facing and hard to reverse; the repository's recorded position is that such an act needs authorisation rather than assumption. Until then the blob remains in every clone and the repository grows permanently by 4.27 MB. Also open: whether the freshness check belongs in the default `make test` target or in a slower target of its own.
- [Future improvements] Extend the conformance scan to the `fe/` frontend and the `tools/conver/src/` TypeScript tree, which have their own conventions. Add a pre-commit hook that runs the freshness check, so a `src/` edit without a rebuild fails at commit time rather than at review time. Generalise the freshness guard into a declaration — a list of `(source entry, committed artefact)` pairs — so a second bundled artefact does not need a second check.
Implementation summary

Changed files (new unless marked):
- tests/lib/module-convention.mjs (new) — resolveModuleSystem reads the extension and the nearest package.json `type` and never a file's contents; syntaxOf reads the module-level construct separately; scanScriptDirectories reports one entry per script directory with any contradicting file named; parseConventionTable reads the rule document's table so the two can be compared rather than trusted.
- tests/lib/repo-hygiene.mjs (new) — assertBackupUntracked reports tracked / ignored / working-tree digest, and returns `unavailable: not-a-repository` rather than a clean-looking null when there is no git tree to ask.
- tests/lib/bundle-freshness.mjs (new) — readBundleComparison runs the build script declared in package.json into a temporary directory, digests both artefacts, and removes its output on every path. An unresolvable bundler is reported as unavailable, never as a stale bundle.
- tests/conventions/{module-convention,repo-hygiene,bundle-freshness}.test.mjs (new) — 22 tests covering C001 to C004 clause by clause.
- tests/check-conventions.mjs, tests/check-bundle-fresh.mjs (new) — the two CLI entry points.
- .claude/rules/node.md (edit) — the four false claims corrected, with a per-directory table.
- Makefile (edit) — check-conventions and check-bundle-fresh, both added to .PHONY.
- .gitignore (edit) — the *.bak rule with its reason.
- .claude/scripts/drill-rfc-down/generate-checklist.js (edit) — Boy Scout, below.
- Tickets.json.p22-ja.bak — removed from the index with `git rm --cached`; the file is untouched on disk.

Test results
- make test: exit 0 in 160 s. 313 files discovered, 313 executed, 0 missing. claude-tests 2097/2083/14 (the PX-142 baseline); project-js-cjs 1984/1984/0; project-mjs 130 files / 1276 / 1276 / 0.
- make check-conventions: exit 0 — 12 directories, 441 files, 0 contradictions.
- make check-bundle-fresh: exit 0 — committed and freshly built digests equal at 4610b162....
- The forward-rotation regression gate reports proved.
- Quality checks report 0 issues across all nine changed files.
- The backup's SHA-256 is 8544aa64... before and after the removal, so untracking deleted nothing.

Four findings the work produced, all measured
1. The first scan reported 32 directories, because it enumerated every nested folder. A rule table naming lib/__pycache__ is one nobody maintains, so the granularity moved to the script directories the convention is actually stated at, while every file beneath is still measured and attributed. __pycache__ joined the exclusion list at the same time.
2. `utils` holds one shell script and no module-bearing file. Its system is `unknown`, which is a verdict rather than a gap, and the table says so instead of asserting a convention for an empty directory.
3. resolveEsbuildVersion originally read process.cwd(). A check that answers about wherever it was run from would report the bundler missing while standing next to it, so it takes the project root.
4. spawnSync does not search node_modules/.bin, so the declared `esbuild ...` build failed with a null status that read as a failed build rather than as a missing executable. resolveBundlerCommand resolves it the way a shell would.

Divergences from the ticket, all measured
1. The rule table has 12 rows, including `utils` as `unknown` and workspacify-reverse as `module` decided by extension rather than by declaration.
2. Two tests changed with the design rather than to pass: the nested-directory case now asserts attribution to its top-level directory, and the ignore-rule assertion compares text rather than compiling a glob into a regular expression, which `*.bak` cannot be.
3. The history still carries blob bf1992ca. Removing it needs a rebase and a force push and is left as an open item for explicit authorisation, with its cost stated: every clone carries 4.27 MB permanently.

Review report — PX-204, PX-205, PX-206, PX-207

Verification performed independently of the implementation notes.

Static quality check: passed — 0 issues across every file the four tickets touched.
Tests: make test exits 0 in 165 s. 315 files discovered, 315 executed, 0 missing. claude-tests 2097/2083/14 (the PX-142 baseline, reported not chased); project-js-cjs 1984/1984/0; project-mjs 132 files / 1309 / 1309 / 0. Adversarial checks, which are the point of a review
1. Perturbed HEADER_MARKER_TEXT by one character. The gate exited 1 and named the header-output surface with both values; restoring it returned the gate to proved.
2. Reintroduced the [object Object] collapse in mappedNodeIdOf. The gate exited 1 and named the node-id-path-map surface. This is the exact defect class P22-14 repaired, now detectable rather than merely fixed.
3. Ran the aggregate over the whole repository rather than file by file. This found four defects that per-file runs hid — see below.

Findings raised by this review and fixed

F1 (major) The annotator is not idempotent, and it corrupted a frozen fixture. `annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff.js` inserted a second provenance marker into tests/rfc-graph/fixtures/forward-surfaces/marker-rewrite/PX-1-sample.js on a repeat run, alongside the marker already there. That shifted the stub from line 2 to line 3, which changed the frozen marker-rewrite value, which made the gate report not proved, which failed fourteen downstream tests across four files — every one of them a symptom of a duplicated comment line. The fixture is restored to its intended five lines and the baseline re-captured. Reported rather than worked around: the tool is used by Step 5a of every ticket, so the defect affects every future ticket's annotation pass, and nothing in the pipeline detects accumulating markers.

F2 (major) Two functions were added to forward-surface-baseline.mjs after its annotation pass and carried no provenance. `--verify` named them. Re-annotated, and the annotation state now reports 22 files with none missing and none ambiguous.

F3 (minor) `--verify` scoped to one ticket reports every file of the other three as missing, because it compares the whole working-tree diff against one ticket's annotations. With four tickets' changes uncommitted together this is expected rather than a defect, and it is why the four were verified under the ticket that annotated last. Committing per ticket removes the ambiguity; the pipeline currently runs make/plan/start/review without a commit between tickets, which is the cause.

F4 (minor) Verifying the annotation regenerated markers on three files that had already been resolved, because resolving and verifying are separate passes over the same non-idempotent tool. Resolved; the final state is clean.

- The annotator's non-idempotence (F1) is pre-existing: it belongs to P22-1's tooling, not to any of these four tickets.
- tests/drill-rfc-down/ regenerates CheckList.md against the repository root and removes a hand-written AI supplement section from it. Observed during PX-205, restored from git, and confirmed intact after every run since. Recommended as a separate ticket.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- **Functions as verb phrases.** `resolveModuleSystem`, `readNearestPackageType`, `scanScriptDirectories`, `groupFilesByDirectory`, `readBundleComparison`, `buildBundleToTemp`, `assertBackupUntracked`, `renderConformanceReport` — the call sequence in the entry point reads as the narrative: resolve, scan, compare, assert, report.
- **Variables as domain concepts.** `resolvedModuleSystem`, `decidedBy`, `nonConformingPaths`, `committedDigest`, `builtDigest`, `byteSizeDelta`, `ignoredPatterns` — no `data`, `info`, `tmp`, `result2`.
- **Hardcoded values become named constants.** `MODULE_SYSTEM = { ESM: 'esm', COMMONJS: 'commonjs', UNKNOWN: 'unknown' }`, `DECIDED_BY = { EXTENSION: 'extension', PACKAGE_JSON: 'package.json' }`, `SCRIPT_ROOT = '.claude/scripts'`, `CONVENTION_RULE_PATH = '.claude/rules/node.md'`, `COMMITTED_BUNDLE_PATH = '.claude/scripts/conver/conver.js'`, `BUNDLE_ENTRY = 'src/entry.ts'`, `UNTRACKED_BACKUP_NAME = 'Tickets.json.p22-ja.bak'`. The esbuild invocation is read from `package.json`'s `build` script rather than re-spelled, so the check cannot drift from the build it is checking.
- **One responsibility per function.** Resolution is pure and reads only the filesystem; scanning owns enumeration; comparison owns the build; rendering never decides and deciding never renders.
- **No error swallowing.** A missing `package.json` ancestor is a stated default, not a swallowed failure; a missing `entry.ts`, a missing esbuild and a missing git tree each name what was absent and what would provide it.
- **Boy Scout beyond the immediate scope.** `.claude/rules/node.md` contradicts the repository in a second place as well: it states "Node.js >=18" while the toolchain measured here is v26.0.0 and `node --test` semantics differ across that range — PX-204 records the Node 26 directory defect. The engine statement is corrected in the same edit, and the new `engines` field PX-204 adds to `package.json` becomes the single declaration both documents point at. `.claude/rules/node.md`'s file-naming and test-layout claims are checked against the filesystem by the same scan rather than left as prose.

tickets.title: Make the forward rotation independent of the reverse tree: invert the dependency that P22-10 introduced
tickets.background:
### Goal
`forward-extensions.mjs` lives in a forward tree, so no file that existed before this branch depends on `.claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse/`, and a test asserts that property structurally rather than by inspection.

### Purpose
P22-10 introduced a module declaring the reverse-only field vocabulary and placed it inside the reverse tree. Two pre-existing forward files import it, which makes the forward rotation depend on the reverse tree's continued existence — the one direction the whole phase promised not to disturb.

**The measurement that settles the placement question.** A scan of every `.mjs`, `.js`, `.cjs` and `.ts` file in the repository, distinguishing real imports from prose mentions, returns exactly eight files: two real importers inside script trees (`tickets/update-ticket.js` at line 13, `workspacify-allocate/lib/seed-render.mjs` at line 14), four test files, and two files that merely name the module in a comment. **Not one of the eight is inside `workspacify-reverse/`.** `forward-extensions.mjs` is a forward-rotation module that happens to be filed in the reverse tree. Nothing about it is reverse-specific except the field names it declares.

That reframes the defect. It is not that the dependency direction is wrong in the abstract; it is that the module was filed in the wrong tree and the wrong tree then acquired two dependents. The fix is a move, not an inversion.

### Motivation
Measured 2026-09-11, the move happened and the edge is real: the directory-level graph now contains `workspacify-allocate -> workspacify-reverse`, which did not exist before P22-10. The repository already carries two directory-level cycles — `workspacify-tree <-> workspacify-allocate` and `rfc-graph <-> tickets` — so a cycle is not by itself novel, and this ticket does not claim to remove them. What is novel is that a forward tree now depends on the reverse tree. If `workspacify-reverse/` were ever removed, relocated or shipped separately, `update-ticket.js` — the writer the implementation loop uses on every ticket — would fail to load.

### Constraints
**There must remain exactly one declaration of the reverse-only field vocabulary.** Breaking the dependency by copying the field-name list into a forward file would leave two lists that drift, and the drift would be silent: a field added to one and not the other produces an artefact that passes one guard and fails another, or worse, passes both. **The module's forward-mode contract is load-bearing and must survive the move**: in forward mode `extendForwardArtifacts` returns the artefact *itself*, not a copy, because `manifest_hash` participates in the WIG and in reload validation, and a copy that serialised identically today could stop doing so tomorrow. **The regression gate must be run before and after and must stay `proved`.** **No new directory cycle may be introduced**: the destination is chosen so that the edges it creates already exist or run in the permitted direction.
acceptanceCriteria:
**[Happy path] — the scenario that confirms this ticket is complete:**
  - `workspacify-allocate/lib/forward-extensions.mjs` exists, `workspacify-reverse/lib/forward-extensions.mjs` does not, and every importer resolves to the new path.
  - The assertion reports the complete set of files importing `workspacify-reverse/**` from outside it, and that set equals the declared allowlist: `conver/red-reconstruction.js`, `grill-me-for-rfc/normative-decision.js` and `tickets/lib/reverse-split.js`, each of which this branch created and each of which is a reverse-mode entry point.
  - `tickets/update-ticket.js` and `workspacify-allocate/lib/seed-render.mjs` no longer appear in that set, and the directory-level edge `workspacify-allocate -> workspacify-reverse` is gone.
  - The regression gate reports `proved`, and the three suite counts are unchanged: workspacify-tree 320, workspacify-allocate 226, workspacify-reverse 661.

**[Error case] — an error scenario the feature must handle:**
  - A new forward-tree import of `workspacify-reverse/**` — for instance an `import` added to `rfc-graph/crud.js` — is reported with the importing path, the imported path and the fact that it is not on the allowlist, and the assertion fails. The check must catch this without being told which files to look at, which is what makes it a guard rather than a checklist.
  - An allowlist entry for a file that has since stopped importing the reverse tree is reported as a stale permission rather than ignored, so the list reflects the present coupling rather than the historical one.
  - A file that names `workspacify-reverse/...` only inside a comment is not reported as an importer — `tickets/lib/return-refs.js:30` is exactly this case and must stay out of the set.

**[Edge case] — a boundary or exception to verify:**
  - A dynamic import constructed from a joined path — `path.join(PROJECT_ROOT, '.claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse/lib/red-reconstruction.mjs')` in `tickets/lib/reverse-split.js` — is detected as an importer, because a string-literal path is enough to find; the check does not attempt to evaluate the expression.
  - A `.mjs` file imported from a CommonJS `.js` file through `require()` resolves and loads on the installed Node, asserted directly: `tickets/update-ticket.js` still loads after the move, because Node 26 supports `require` of an ES module and the repository already relies on it.
  - The reverse tree's own files are excluded from the assertion even though they import each other, so a self-import inside `workspacify-reverse/` is not reported as a violation.
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) Record the baselines: the three suite counts and the gate verdict. (2) Write the failing assertion: collect importers, collect the allowlist, assert equality, plus the purity and export-surface tests. (3) Move `forward-extensions.mjs` to `workspacify-allocate/lib/` with `git mv` so the history follows it. (4) Update the six real importers (two script files, four test files) and correct the two comment references so they do not point at a path that no longer exists. (5) Re-run the three suites and the gate; they must reproduce the baselines exactly. (6) Make one deliberate forward import of the reverse tree and watch the assertion fail, then remove it.
- [Risks] **The largest risk is a partial move.** If `workspacify-reverse/lib/forward-extensions.mjs` is left behind as well as copied, there are two declarations of the field vocabulary and the constraint that forbids it is violated silently — every import still resolves and every test still passes. UT-12 exists specifically to make the leftover file a named failure. **The second risk is a missed importer.** `tickets/update-ticket.js` spells its require across two lines, so a line-oriented search for the import misses it; the move must be verified by loading the module rather than by grepping for the string. **The third is the `.mjs`-from-CommonJS boundary.** If the destination were a `.js` file under a CommonJS tree, `update-ticket.js` would still load but the reverse tree's ESM importers would break; the destination stays `.mjs` for that reason. **The fourth is the gate.** Two of the six files this ticket edits are forward-path files, so a mistake here is a forward-rotation regression, and the gate is the only instrument that would catch it.
- [Caveats] The allowlist is a permission list, and permission lists rot. The stale-entry check is what keeps it honest, and the ticket accepts that a future reverse entry point must be added to it deliberately — that cost is the point, because an unreviewed new dependency is exactly the failure being guarded against. The assertion deliberately does not attempt to remove the two pre-existing cycles (`workspacify-tree <-> workspacify-allocate`, `rfc-graph <-> tickets`); they predate this branch and are out of scope, and claiming otherwise would misrepresent what the test proves.
- [Open items] Whether the reverse tree's dependence on `grill-me-for-rfc/normative-decision.js` should be removed in the same way — it is the same class of shared-vocabulary coupling in the permitted direction. Open because the direction is permitted and the change has no defect behind it, only symmetry. Whether the two pre-existing cycles should be broken is likewise open and is a much larger piece of work.
- [Future improvements] Emit the directory-level dependency graph as a committed artefact so the two cycles and every edge are visible in review rather than recomputed by each session that wonders. Extend the assertion from "no forward file imports the reverse tree" to a declared layer order over all seven script directories, which would also catch the two pre-existing cycles — a separate ticket, because it would require changing code that currently works.

- The forward-rotation regression gate reports proved, with 25 fixtures, no pipeline disagreement and no command-file loss.
