- Quality checks report 0 issues across all eight changed files.
- `require('./.claude/scripts/tickets/update-ticket.js')` loads, which is the direct evidence that no forward-path file depends on the reverse tree any more.

The measurement that decided the shape of this ticket
Nothing inside `.claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse/` imported `forward-extensions.mjs`. It is a forward module that P22-10 filed in the reverse tree, so the repair is a move rather than an inversion of the dependency. The destination was chosen by measurement too: `workspacify-allocate/lib/` creates no new cycle, because `workspacify-allocate -> workspacify-tree` already exists and no `workspacify-allocate -> tickets` edge does. `workspacify-tree/lib/` was rejected because `SEED_REQUIRED_SECTIONS` would add `workspacify-tree -> workspacify-allocate` and close a cycle that is currently one-directional.

Three findings the tests produced
1. `grill-me-for-rfc/normative-decision.js` imports two reverse modules, so it appeared twice in the importer list. The comparison is over importing files, not over imports: two imports from one file are one permission.
2. The first attempt to assert "one destination" reused the reverse-importer scan, which cannot see the module any more — it has left the reverse tree. The scan was generalised to collectImportersOf, and the assertion is now that every specifier resolves to one absolute path, whatever it is spelled from.
3. The scanner needed to catch a dynamic import built from `path.join(PROJECT_ROOT, '...')`, because no module resolver can follow it and it is exactly the shape that would otherwise escape.

Divergences from the ticket, all measured
1. The scan reports twelve directories' worth of files and four importer entries across three files, all allowlisted.
2. The two pre-existing directory cycles — workspacify-tree <-> workspacify-allocate and rfc-graph <-> tickets — remain. The ticket states it does not remove them, and the test asserts nothing about them.
3. The annotation pass attributes PX-205's uncommitted changes to PX-206 as well, because it reads the diff against the last commit rather than against the ticket's own work. Committing per ticket before starting the next removes this; it is recorded here rather than worked around.

Review report — PX-204, PX-205, PX-206, PX-207

Verification performed independently of the implementation notes.

Static quality check: passed — 0 issues across every file the four tickets touched.
Tests: make test exits 0 in 165 s. 315 files discovered, 315 executed, 0 missing. claude-tests 2097/2083/14 (the PX-142 baseline, reported not chased); project-js-cjs 1984/1984/0; project-mjs 132 files / 1309 / 1309 / 0. The forward-rotation regression gate reports proved with 25 fixtures, no pipeline disagreement, no command-file loss and no forward-surface disagreement. check-conventions and check-bundle-fresh both exit 0. Contract coverage 100% on all four. crimes 0, stubs 0, no-excuse gate exit 0, AMBIGUOUS markers 0.
Translatability: no issues in code. Three grep hits are single-letter declarations inside string literals — fixture content for the module-convention tests — not declarations. No console.log in any new file.

Adversarial checks, which are the point of a review
1. Perturbed HEADER_MARKER_TEXT by one character. The gate exited 1 and named the header-output surface with both values; restoring it returned the gate to proved.
2. Reintroduced the [object Object] collapse in mappedNodeIdOf. The gate exited 1 and named the node-id-path-map surface. This is the exact defect class P22-14 repaired, now detectable rather than merely fixed.
3. Ran the aggregate over the whole repository rather than file by file. This found four defects that per-file runs hid — see below.

Findings raised by this review and fixed

F1 (major) The annotator is not idempotent, and it corrupted a frozen fixture. `annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff.js` inserted a second provenance marker into tests/rfc-graph/fixtures/forward-surfaces/marker-rewrite/PX-1-sample.js on a repeat run, alongside the marker already there. Measured: a second run changed the file's digest. That shifted the stub from line 2 to line 3, which changed the frozen marker-rewrite value, which made the gate report not proved, which failed fourteen downstream tests across four files — every one of them a symptom of a duplicated comment line. The fixture is restored to its intended five lines and the baseline re-captured. Reported rather than worked around: the tool is used by Step 5a of every ticket, so the defect affects every future ticket's annotation pass, and nothing in the pipeline detects accumulating markers.

F2 (major) Two functions were added to forward-surface-baseline.mjs after its annotation pass and carried no provenance. `--verify` named them. Re-annotated, and the annotation state now reports 22 files with none missing and none ambiguous.

F3 (minor) `--verify` scoped to one ticket reports every file of the other three as missing, because it compares the whole working-tree diff against one ticket's annotations. With four tickets' changes uncommitted together this is expected rather than a defect, and it is why the four were verified under the ticket that annotated last. Committing per ticket removes the ambiguity; the pipeline currently runs make/plan/start/review without a commit between tickets, which is the cause.

F4 (minor) Verifying the annotation regenerated markers on three files that had already been resolved, because resolving and verifying are separate passes over the same non-idempotent tool. Resolved; the final state is clean.

Pre-existing defects found by the review, outside the four tickets' scope
- The annotator's non-idempotence (F1) is pre-existing: it belongs to P22-1's tooling, not to any of these four tickets.
- tests/drill-rfc-down/ regenerates CheckList.md against the repository root and removes a hand-written AI supplement section from it. Observed during PX-205, restored from git, and confirmed intact after every run since. Recommended as a separate ticket.
- The two directory-level cycles workspacify-tree <-> workspacify-allocate and rfc-graph <-> tickets remain. PX-206 states it does not remove them and asserts nothing about them.

Stub evaluation
None to evaluate. find-all-stubs.js reports 0 across the repository, and the no-excuse gate exits 0. No unmarked stub was found in the changed code, so no marker was inserted and no crime recorded.

Notes on the four tickets' own findings
The eight defects PX-204 found, the four PX-205 found, the three PX-206 found and the four PX-207 found are recorded in each ticket's own notes. Each was found by a test before the implementation, and the two adversarial perturbations above re-confirm the two surfaces whose whole purpose is to catch the P22-14 defect class.

  - [Affected component] `siprs-with-4layers/.claude/scripts/` — the answer-key mirror.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- **Functions as verb phrases.** `collectReverseImporters`, `resolveImportSpecifier`, `isRealImport`, `collectAllowlist`, `assertLayersOneWay`, `reportViolations` — the entry point reads as: collect the importers, collect the allowlist, assert they are equal, report.
- **Variables as domain concepts.** `importingPath`, `importedPath`, `allowlistedPaths`, `stalePermissions`, `violations`, `resolvedDestination` — no `data`, `list`, `tmp`, `x`.
- **Hardcoded values become named constants.** `REVERSE_TREE = '.claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse'`, `SCRIPT_ROOT = '.claude/scripts'`, `REVERSE_ENTRY_ALLOWLIST` (each entry carrying the ticket that created it), `IMPORT_SPECIFIER_PATTERN`. The three allowlist entries name their tickets — P22-19, P22-13, P22-16 — so a permission is never anonymous.
- **One responsibility per function.** `isRealImport` is a pure predicate over source text; `resolveImportSpecifier` is a pure path function; `collectReverseImporters` owns the walk; `assertLayersOneWay` owns the comparison and never renders.
- **No error swallowing.** An unresolved specifier is reported with the importing file and the specifier; a missing tree is reported as unavailable rather than as clean; a skipped binary is counted and named.
- **Boy Scout beyond the immediate scope.** `workspacify-reverse/lib/security-lane.mjs` imports `recordAuthority` from `grill-me-for-rfc/normative-decision.js`, which is the reverse tree depending on a forward tree — the permitted direction, and left as it is. What is worth naming while this code is open is that the reverse tree's dependency on `workspacify-tree/lib/canonical-json.mjs` and `errors.mjs` is duplicated across `regression-gate.mjs`, `scope.mjs`, `forward-extensions.mjs` and `reflexion.mjs` through four separately spelled relative paths; those paths are corrected in one pass as part of the move rather than left to drift. The directory-level graph is also emitted by the new test as a by-product, so the two pre-existing cycles are recorded in a machine-readable place for the first time.

contracts.sourceEdge: the repository tree -> collectReverseImporters(root) -> the importer set
contracts.precondition: `.claude/scripts/` exists and holds the seven script directories; source files are readable UTF-8 text.
contracts.postcondition: The function returns every file outside `workspacify-reverse/` whose source contains a real import or require resolving inside that tree, each with the path it imports; files naming the tree only in a comment are excluded; the reverse tree's own files are excluded.
contracts.invariant: The set is recomputed from the tree on every call and is never read from a stored list, so it cannot go stale.

contracts.sourceEdge: the importer set -> assertLayersOneWay({ importers, allowlist }) -> the verdict
contracts.precondition: A declared allowlist of reverse-mode entry points exists, each entry naming the ticket that created it.
contracts.postcondition: The assertion returns `ok: true` when the importer set equals the allowlist, and `ok: false` naming every importer not on the list and every allowlist entry that no longer imports the tree; the test exits non-zero on `ok: false`.
contracts.invariant: The comparison is set equality, not containment: a missing allowlist entry and an extra one both fail, so the list cannot silently accumulate permissions.

contracts.sourceEdge: extendForwardArtifacts(artefact, { kind, mode }) -> the returned artefact
contracts.precondition: An artefact object of a declared kind; a mode of `forward` or `reverse`; in reverse mode, a `reverseFields` object.
contracts.postcondition: In forward mode the function returns the identical object reference it was given; in reverse mode it returns a new object carrying the reverse fields, and `assertReverseAdditions` accepts it.
contracts.invariant: Reference identity in forward mode is the contract, not deep equality: `manifest_hash` participates in the WIG and in reload validation, and a copy that serialised identically today could stop doing so tomorrow. Asserted with strict equality.

contracts.sourceEdge: the moved module -> its six importers -> path resolution
contracts.precondition: `workspacify-allocate/lib/forward-extensions.mjs` exists and `workspacify-reverse/lib/forward-extensions.mjs` does not.
contracts.postcondition: Every importer resolves to the new absolute path; every file importing `forward-extensions.mjs` resolves to the same single destination; `tickets/update-ticket.js` loads and the three suites reproduce 320/226/661 with the gate `proved`.
contracts.invariant: The vocabulary has exactly one declaration — the set of distinct resolved destinations has exactly one element — and the module's exported names are unchanged.

changes.before: `forward-extensions.mjs`, the single declaration of the reverse-only field vocabulary, lived in `.claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse/lib/`. tickets.title: Extend the regression gate to every forward surface P22 modified: freeze a reproducible value for each, and report drift by name
tickets.background:
### Goal
Every forward-tree source file that P22 modified is covered by at least one frozen value the regression gate reproduces, so a future change to any of them is reported by name rather than discovered by accident.

### Purpose
The gate built by P22-1 covers the workspacify surfaces and nothing else, measured on 2026-09-11 as 25 fixture digests, three forward pipeline pairs, five allocate fixture digests and nine command-file digests. The changes P22 made to `rfc-graph` and to `tickets` sit entirely outside it and rest on unit tests alone.

The difference matters and is the reason this ticket exists. A unit test asserts what its author thought of. A frozen value asserts that nothing moved — including moves the author did not think of. `generateHeaderComment`'s signature changed from seven arguments to five and the header bytes it emits changed with it; no frozen value covers that. `dump-node-context-to-spec.js` carried a defect in which every node id collapsed to the string `[object Object]`, so the map it built was one unusable key; that defect survived because nothing compared the map against a known-good result.

### Motivation
The four uncovered modifications are, measured by `git diff --numstat master...HEAD` on 2026-09-11: `rfc-graph/boundify-helpers.js` +17/-4 (the `HEADER_MARKER_TEXT` extraction and the signature change), `rfc-graph/dump-node-context-to-spec.js` +43/-11 (the `mappedNodeIdOf` repair), `rfc-graph/phasify-omissions.js` +58/-4 (PX-142's `verifyMarkerRewrites` and the plan-text fallback), and `tickets/update-ticket.js` +34/-0 (P22-10's reverse-contamination guard). Each is a forward-path change to a tree the phase promised not to disturb, and each is currently protected only by tests the same ticket wrote.

### Constraints
**The gate must not acquire a value it cannot reproduce.** A volatile field frozen by mistake makes the gate fail on every run, and a gate that always fails is ignored — which destroys the only thing it has. P22-1 already met this problem once: `manifest_hash` was not reproducible across runs because `assembleManifest` hashes `run.generated_at`, `run.run_id` and `run.generator`, and the fix was `stableManifestDigest`, which removes exactly those fields. The same discipline applies here: a value is frozen only after proving it reproduces across two runs and two working directories. **Baselines are captured after the forward code is final, never to make a red gate green.** **The gate must distinguish "cannot build the surface" from "built and differs"** — an unavailable prerequisite reported as drift would make the gate cry wolf. **No forward behaviour may change**: exporting a previously-private pure function is permitted, changing what it computes is not.
acceptanceCriteria:
**[Happy path] — the scenario that confirms this ticket is complete:**
  - `run.mjs regression capture` freezes a value for every covered surface, and a second capture in a different working directory produces byte-identical JSON — the idempotence property P22-1 established for the workspacify surfaces now holds for the new ones.
  - `run.mjs regression check` exits 0 and its report names each covered surface: the existing 25 fixture digests, three pipeline pairs, five allocate digests and nine command-file digests, plus the new header-output, node-id-map, marker-rewrite, ticket-guard and checklist surfaces.
  - Each new frozen value is accompanied in the baseline by the surface's name, the input it was produced from, and how it was obtained, so a reader can tell what the value covers without reading the gate's source.

**[Error case] — an error scenario the feature must handle:**
  - A one-byte change to a covered surface is reported by name with the expected and the observed value, and `check` exits 1. For `generateHeaderComment` the change under test is a single character in `HEADER_MARKER_TEXT`; for the node-id map it is one character in a fixture's `mappedNodeIds`; for the marker rewrite it is a stale key left in a fixture file.
  - A surface that cannot be produced is reported as unavailable with the reason and does not count as reproduced: a missing fixture names the path, an absent prerequisite names the command that would provide it, and neither is reported as drift.
  - A newly non-deterministic surface is reported as such rather than frozen: if two capture runs disagree on a value, the gate reports the surface as `non-deterministic` with both values instead of writing the last one.

**[Edge case] — a boundary or exception to verify:**
  - A pure function is frozen as a golden output for a fixed input, with the input stored beside the value so the comparison is reproducible rather than dependent on the current source. `generateHeaderComment` is the fixture: five arguments in, one string out.
  - A surface whose input includes a timestamp or a path that varies by working directory is normalised before freezing, and the normalisation is declared in the baseline rather than applied silently.
  - An empty surface — a directory with no inputs to freeze — reports that it has nothing to freeze and is distinguishable from a surface that was frozen and reproduced.
  - The baseline file after this ticket still parses against the schema P22-1 declared, with the new surfaces added under a new key rather than by widening an existing one.
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) Record the baselines: the gate's present `proved` state, its three key digests, and the three suite counts. (2) Write the failing tests: one freeze-and-drift pair per surface, the non-deterministic refusal, the read-only invariants, the byte-identity of the existing keys, and the coverage assertion derived from the git diff. (3) Export `mappedNodeIdOf` and `firstReverseFieldOnForwardTicket` — the only source change, additive. (4) Create the fixtures under `tests/rfc-graph/fixtures/forward-surfaces/`. (5) Write `forward-surface-baseline.mjs` and wire it into the gate's capture and check paths; make the tests green. (6) Run `capture` twice in two directories and diff the baselines. (7) Run `check`, then perturb `HEADER_MARKER_TEXT` by one character and confirm the gate names the header surface and exits 1; restore and confirm `proved`.
- [Risks] **The largest risk is freezing a value that does not reproduce.** P22-1 met this exactly: three runs in one directory produced three different `manifest_hash` values because `assembleManifest` hashes `run.generated_at`, `run.run_id` and `run.generator`. The same trap waits here — a path that varies by working directory, a timestamp in the checklist output, an object key order that depends on insertion history. The mitigation is procedural and must not be skipped: capture twice in two directories and diff before declaring any surface frozen. **The second risk is a gate that fails on every run being ignored.** A gate whose failure is noise has no authority, and this repository has already demonstrated the cost of an instrument nobody trusts. The unavailable-versus-drifted distinction exists for this reason. **The third is scope creep into re-capturing the existing keys.** They are `proved`; touching them would erase the evidence that the surfaces P22-1 froze are intact. UT-25 exists to make that mistake visible. **The fourth is that this ticket freezes what it just wrote.** The tests and the frozen values come from the same session as the surfaces they cover, which is exactly the co-conspirator arrangement the design warns about elsewhere; the mitigation is that the frozen values are derived from the *pre-existing* functions rather than from the tests, and the adversarial step in step 7 is performed against a surface the test author did not write.
- [Caveats] The new frozen values cover the specific units P22 modified, not the whole of `rfc-graph` or `tickets`. A future change to an untouched part of those trees will still be caught only by unit tests. The surface table is a maintained list, and adding a surface is a deliberate act; the coverage assertion derived from the git diff keeps it honest for the P22 changes specifically, and will need re-pointing if the phase boundary moves. The `.mjs`-versus-`.cjs` split matters here: `forward-surface-baseline.mjs` is ESM and must import from CommonJS modules through `createRequire` or a dynamic import, and that boundary is asserted rather than assumed.
- [Open items] Whether the whole of the `phasify-omissions.js` pipeline is deterministic is unmeasured and is left open; the ticket freezes its two modified units and says so rather than implying broader coverage. Whether the git-diff-derived coverage assertion should be a permanent test or a one-time check is open — as a permanent test it will fail once the branch is merged and `master...HEAD` becomes empty, so it must be written to tolerate an empty diff by reporting that it has nothing to check rather than passing vacuously.
- [Future improvements] A general declaration of `(source revision range, forward surface, frozen value)` so coverage is recomputed for any phase rather than the P22 range specifically. Extending the freeze mechanism to `drill-rfc-down`'s header refresh, which shares `generateHeaderComment` and would become cheap once the header surface exists. Emitting the gate's report as a machine-readable sidecar so PX-204's aggregate can include the verdict without parsing prose.

contracts.sourceEdge: a forward surface's producer -> captureForwardSurfaces() -> the frozen baseline entry
contracts.precondition: The surface's input fixture exists; the producer is either a pure function imported from a forward module or a CLI invocable from the repository root; the surface is named in the FORWARD_SURFACES table.
contracts.postcondition: The entry is `{ surface, kind, producedFrom, value, normalisation }`; a second capture produces a byte-identical entry; a capture from a different working directory produces the same value.
contracts.invariant: A surface whose two captures disagree is written as `kind: 'non-deterministic'` with both observations rather than frozen to either.

contracts.sourceEdge: the frozen baseline -> compareForwardSurfaces() -> the proved / not proved verdict
contracts.precondition: A baseline exists holding at least one forward-surface entry; the producers are still resolvable.
contracts.postcondition: Each entry is recomputed and compared; a mismatch is reported by surface name with the expected and observed values; a producer that cannot be run is reported as unavailable with its reason, distinctly from a mismatch; the gate exits 1 on a mismatch and 0 otherwise.
contracts.invariant: An unavailable surface never counts as reproduced, and no surface is silently dropped from the comparison when the set of entries changes.

contracts.sourceEdge: generateHeaderComment(headerPaths, mappedNodeIds, crossRefs, sourceBasename, lang) -> the emitted header string
contracts.precondition: Five arguments: a header-paths object carrying graphRelPath, dirsTreeRelPath and sourceRelPath; an array of mapped node ids; a cross-reference list; a source basename; a language key present in COMMENT_SYNTAX.
contracts.postcondition: The function returns a string whose first content line carries HEADER_MARKER_TEXT, which names the graph path, the directory path and the source path, and which lists one line per mapped node; the same five arguments produce an equal string on every call.
contracts.invariant: The function is pure — it performs no I/O and writes no file — and the returned string always contains the exact marker text `Initial Design Artifact — RFC-driven Implementation`, which supreme law 4 forbids altering.

contracts.sourceEdge: the repository's forward-tree diff -> the covered surface set -> the gate's report
contracts.precondition: Every forward-tree source file P22 modified is derivable from `git diff --numstat master...HEAD`.
contracts.postcondition: Each such file is covered by at least one frozen surface, and the report names the surface that covers it; `captureBaselines` leaves the existing `fixtures`, `manifestHashes` and `commandFileDigests` keys byte-identical.
contracts.invariant: The set of surfaces the gate covers is a superset of the set of forward files P22 modified, asserted by a test that recomputes the diff rather than by a stored list.

tickets.title: Preserve what the tools do not own: annotation idempotence and generated-region fencing
tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] Running the annotator twice with the same ticket key over an unchanged file leaves the file byte-identical (sha256), and the second run reports `skipped:already-annotated` for every definition it inspects. Regenerating a checklist twice leaves every byte outside the fence identical.
- [Error invariant] No failure path destroys content. The annotator writes a file only when it has changed it; a generator that cannot determine the fenced region — a file with two fence pairs, or neither fences nor the trailing AI-supplement comment — names the path on stderr, exits non-zero, and leaves the file untouched.
- [Internal state invariant] The count of lines carrying an annotation for a given ticket key is non-increasing across runs. The generator's ownership boundary is the fence, not "everything after the last line it wrote": a human region placed between two generated sections is preserved.
- [Boundary invariant] A zero-length file, a file consisting only of a fence pair, and a file whose definitions sit adjacent to their annotations are each handled without throwing. For an input carrying no human content, generated output is byte-identical to the pre-fix generator's output after timestamp normalisation.
tickets.background:
### Goal
Make two tools that rewrite files they do not wholly own stop destroying content they did not author. Concretely: (1) `annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff.js` becomes idempotent for a given ticket key, so running it twice leaves a file byte-identical; (2) both `generate-checklist.js` generators rewrite only a fenced region and preserve every byte outside it.

### Purpose
Both defects are violations of a single invariant, stated once here and enforced twice: **a tool that rewrites a file it does not wholly own must be idempotent, and must preserve every byte it did not author.** The project already states the positive half of this — CLAUDE.md's "Everything as Code" requires source modified under a ticket to carry a provenance annotation. A tool that can silently add a second copy of that annotation, or delete a hand-written section, undermines the very traceability it exists to provide.

### Motivation
The annotator defect is not hypothetical and not new: it has produced surviving corruption in four separate ticket generations — PX-159 (three files, each tripled), P22-8, P22-9 (three files), and PX-207, whose frozen fixture drifted and failed 14 downstream tests before being diagnosed. Every workstream that runs `/start-ticket` re-arms it. The generator defect is worse in kind: it destroys human work rather than duplicating machine output, and the command file *instructs* the AI to produce exactly the content the next run deletes (`drill-rfc-down.md:183`), with `--no-backup` on the invocation. `./CheckList.md:137` is a live specimen awaiting the next run.

### Constraints
- The supreme law forbids deleting or altering the `Initial Design Artifact` header; the fence constants must not collide with it or with `[::STUB::]`, `[::TICKET::]` or `[::AMBIGUOUS::]`.
- TDD Red-Green-Refactor is mandatory; every behaviour above is deterministic and directly testable, so no item may be excused as untestable.
- The fix must be a superset of current behaviour: the frozen `checklist-output` forward surface must still reproduce (contract C003). For an input with no human content the fix must produce identical bytes.
- `make check-conventions` must remain green; no new row may appear in `.claude/rules/node.md` by accident.
- The two generators must not drift apart — PX-207 already fixed a defect in one sibling and left the other, and that omission is the reason target B names both files.
scope:
**Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**
  - `.claude/scripts/tickets/annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff.js` (CommonJS) — the annotator.
  - Action: modify.
  - What specifically changes: (a) `detectAnnotationAtLine` (106-114) stops reading `defLine - 2` as the sole location and instead scans upward from the definition while lines are annotations or blanks, stopping at the first line that is neither; (b) the file-level guard in the AMBIGUOUS branch (313-317) recognises a marker for the key in either flavour, so a resolved `[::TICKET::]` marker suppresses a fresh insertion; (c) both paths return `skipped:already-annotated` and write nothing.
  - Before → After: a second run with the same key on a file whose annotation is separated from its definition by an interposed line reports `annotated` and inserts a duplicate → reports `skipped:already-annotated` and writes nothing. No CLI flag, exit code or output format changes.
  - API contract change: none externally. The internal contract of `detectAnnotationAtLine` widens from "the line above the definition" to "the contiguous annotation block above the definition".
  - Data schema change: none.
  - Config/env change: none.
  - Dependency added/removed: none.
  - `.claude/scripts/grill-me-for-rfc/lib/checklist-fence.mjs` — new shared module.
  - Action: add. (A `lib/` subdirectory is not a row in the conventions table; the directory inherits `grill-me-for-rfc`'s `type: module`, and the extension decides regardless.)
  - What specifically changes: exports the fence constants and three pure functions — split a file into generated and preserved regions, regenerated content from preserved content, and a migration for a legacy file. Reads and writes are separated so the pure half is testable without a filesystem.
  - API contract change: new module; no existing caller changes.
  - `.claude/scripts/grill-me-for-rfc/generate-checklist.js` — action: modify. Lines 124 and 126 stop being a bare `writeFileSync` of the whole file and become: compose the generated body, hand it and the existing file's text to the shared module, write the merged result. The trailing AI-supplement comment is written *inside* the fenced region as its last line, so everything a human appends after it falls outside the fence and survives.
  - `.claude/scripts/drill-rfc-down/generate-checklist.js` — action: modify, identically, importing the shared module from `../grill-me-for-rfc/lib/checklist-fence.mjs`. Direction is downstream → upstream (`/drill-rfc-down` refines what `/grill-me-for-rfc` produces) and matches the existing `*/lib` cross-import idiom.
  - `./CheckList.md` (tracked) — action: modify. Its `## AI補足` section (line 137 of 146) is preserved by the first run under the fixed generator; the file may be regenerated by that run to establish the fences, provided the human region is byte-identical afterwards.
  - `.claude/rules/node.md` — action: modify only if `make check-conventions` reports a change; the conventions table must stay equal to the filesystem.
  - `Makefile` — action: modify only if a new target is needed; tests are reached by `make test` through `tests/run-all-surfaces.mjs`, which discovers files rather than listing them, so a new test directory needs no Makefile edit.

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - `siprs-with-4layers/.claude/scripts/` — excluded. It is a tracked but vendored snapshot of a different project (3675 files, no `.git` of its own, already divergent from this toolchain: `diff` reports its `generate-checklist.js` differs from the canonical one). Editing a vendored copy in place would be reverted by the next vendor refresh. The root fix still protects it, because the annotator lives in the canonical tree and the defect there is duplicate annotation lines rather than lost content.
  - The annotator's architecture — excluded. It parses definitions by pattern and inserts positionally; a rewrite to a token-stream model would change every call site and is not needed to make it idempotent.
  - The remaining unreferenced duplicate annotations, if any are found that are *not* consecutive — excluded from the mechanical removal, because a non-consecutive repeat can be legitimate (several definitions in one file each correctly carrying the key) and is not evidence of the defect. Only consecutive duplicates are removed.

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - `workspacify-reverse/forward-surface-baseline.mjs` `checklist-output` surface, covering `grill-me-for-rfc/generate-checklist.js`.
  - Nature of impact: data format — the generated artefact gains fence markers, so its byte content changes for any file that has human content. For a file with none, contract C003 requires it not to change at all.
  - Corresponding change needed: no source change, but the regression baseline must be re-captured *only if* the gate reports drift, and the drift must be explained as the fence markers rather than waved through. The gate reporting `proved` unchanged is the expected outcome and is asserted by an IT.
  - `workspacify-reverse/lib/staleness.mjs` — emits material addressed to `/drill-rfc-down` (`385-387`), so it is downstream of the generator. Nature: behavioural. Response: none needed; the preservation makes its output safer to re-drill.
  - `/start-ticket` Step 5a and `/review-ticket` Step 5 — both invoke the annotator. Nature: process. Response: none needed; they simply stop re-inserting.
  - `tests/run-all-surfaces.mjs` — discovers test files rather than listing them, so new tests are picked up. Nature: verification surface. Response: none.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] C001 postcondition — a file whose annotation sits immediately above its definition, annotated again with the same key, is byte-identical (sha256) and reports skipped:already-annotated.

UT: [Error] C001 postcondition — the shape that fails today: a file carrying [::TICKET::] K, then an interposed comment line, then the definition. The pre-fix guard reads checkIndex = defLine - 2, finds the interposed comment rather than the annotation, and inserts a second identical line. The post-fix guard must report skipped:already-annotated and insert nothing. This is the exact shape of tests/workspacify-reverse/regression/baseline.test.mjs lines 313-314.

UT: [Error] C001 postcondition — the PX-207 incident, inverted into a guard: resolve-ambiguous-markers.js --mode=inject-at has replaced an [::AMBIGUOUS::] marker with a [::TICKET::] marker for K. The current AMBIGUOUS branch tests lines.some(l => l.includes('[::AMBIGUOUS::]') && l.includes(K)), which cannot see the resolved marker, so it inserts a fresh one.
UT: [Boundary] C001 invariant — three consecutive runs over a file whose definitions are separated from their annotations; sha256 after run 1 === after run 2 === after run 3.

UT: [Boundary] C001 invariant — the count of lines matching [::TICKET::] K is measured before and after each run and never increases. Applied to a file already carrying a consecutive duplicate, the count must stay at 2 rather than growing to 3.

UT: [Normal] C001 — two different ticket keys landing on the same definition yield ONE annotation line naming both keys, not two lines. mergeAnnotation() already documents itself idempotent for this; the test pins the property so a rewrite cannot lose it.

UT: [Boundary] C001 — a file with no parseable definitions at all takes the file-level path; a second run with the same key inserts nothing. The AMBIGUOUS branch guard is widened to recognise either marker flavour for K.
UT: [Invariant] C001 — the annotator never writes a file it did not change: for every path it reports skipped, the mtime and digest are unchanged.
UT: [Normal] C002 postcondition — a checklist file with a fenced region and hand-written content after it is regenerated; the human region's digest is unchanged and the generated region is replaced.
UT: [Normal] C002 postcondition — hand-written content placed BETWEEN two generated sections survives, proving the fence is the unit of ownership and not 'everything after the last generated line'.
UT: [Invariant] C002 — two regenerations in succession leave the human region's digest identical; the second run is a no-op on every byte outside the fences.

### Evidence — the annotator's non-idempotence (target A)

`.claude/scripts/tickets/annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff.js`, CommonJS (the directory has no package.json of its own and inherits `.claude/package.json` = `commonjs`). Introduced by `bb098474 feat(PX-59): implement code ticket-key annotation and pipeline integration` on 2026-07-23; 7 commits in total, the last `a185494e` on 2026-07-31. P22-1 did not modify it (`git show --stat be80f414` matches `annotate-ticket` zero times); in this branch only P22-14 touched it (+4/-1).

The guard, lines 106-114:

```js
function detectAnnotationAtLine(lines, defLine) {
  const checkIndex = defLine - 2; // line above the definition (0-indexed)
  if (checkIndex < 0 || checkIndex >= lines.length) return null;
  ...
}
```

It reads **exactly one line above the definition**. A file whose annotation sits two or more lines above — because a comment or blank line was interposed by a later edit — is invisible to it. The definition branch at 344-347 then finds `existingAnnot === null` and inserts a second identical annotation. `mergeAnnotation` (121-124) *is* idempotent for the multi-key case ("If the key already exists, returns the original line unchanged"); the defect is the adjacency test, not the merge.

```js
const alreadyHasMarker = lines.some(

);
```

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
The two files this ticket rewrites are themselves the Boy Scout target, because both defects are translatability failures before they are logic failures.

- **One function, one responsibility.** `detectAnnotationAtLine(lines, defLine)` currently encodes two ideas at once — "where an annotation may live" and "which ticket keys it names" — and the first is frozen into the expression `defLine - 2`, a magic offset with no name. It is split into `findAnnotationBlockAbove(lines, definitionLine)` returning the contiguous block, and the key lookup moves to the caller. The offset becomes a named constant, or disappears entirely.
- **Function names as verb phrases.** The new shared module exports verbs, not nouns: `splitFencedRegions`, `composePreservedFile`, `migrateLegacyFile`. The existing generator bodies are a single long function that pushes into a `lines` array and then writes; the write becomes `writeFencedChecklist(...)`, so the call site reads as prose.
- **Domain names over generic ones.** `lines` is acceptable inside a renderer, but the module's boundary must not traffic in it: the preserved region is `preservedText`, the generated body is `generatedBody`, and the fence constants are `FENCE_OPEN` / `FENCE_CLOSE` rather than inline string literals. The generator's current `checklistPath` stays as it is; `sessionDir` versus `rfcDir` in the two siblings is left alone, since renaming across the pair would obscure the diff that this ticket's IT exists to compare.
- **Hardcoded values as named constants.** The trailing AI-supplement comment is currently a template literal duplicated verbatim in two files (line 128 and line 124). It moves to the shared module as a single constant, so the two generators cannot drift — the same failure mode PX-207 found when one sibling was fixed and the other was not.
- **No error swallowing.** The generator's current silent `writeFileSync` becomes a write that either succeeds or reports why it refused by path. No `catch` is added that would convert a refusal into a success.
- **Comments must not lie.** The comment above the AMBIGUOUS guard currently describes a check that does not cover the resolved-marker case; it is rewritten to state what the widened guard actually covers, or removed if the code now speaks for itself.

contracts.precondition: A source file already carries an annotation naming ticket key K, in either flavour ([::TICKET::] or an unresolved [::AMBIGUOUS::]), at any position within the contiguous run of comment lines that ends at the definition, or anywhere in a file that has no parseable definition.
contracts.postcondition: processFile(file, K, ...) leaves every byte of the file unchanged and returns an action matching /already-annotated/, on every insertion path.
contracts.invariant: For any N >= 1, sha256(file after run N) === sha256(file after run 1). The count of lines carrying the marker for K is non-increasing across runs.

contracts.precondition: A checklist file exists whose content outside the fence pair was authored by a human or an AI session, so the file is not wholly the generator's output.

tickets.title: The extension set is a decision, not an omission: .cjs, and the census that keeps it honest
tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] Every extension present in the repository at three or more tracked files outside the vendored roots is a member of SOURCE_EXTENSIONS or of EXCLUDED_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS, and every member of the exclusion map carries a non-empty reason. A `.cjs` file changed by a ticket is annotated; a second run over it reports `skipped:already-annotated`.
- [Error invariant] An extension present but undecided makes the check fail and names the extension. The check never guesses and never widens the set on its own: reporting is the whole of its behaviour, and the decision to include or exclude stays with a human editing the constants.
- [Internal state invariant] The census is derived at check time from `git ls-files`. It reads no stored extension list, so it cannot inherit the defect it exists to catch. The exclusion is by path prefix against a declared root list, so a vendored `.rs` and a vendored `.h` are excluded identically.
- [Boundary invariant] An extension with fewer than three tracked files outside the vendored roots requires no decision, so a one-off file does not force a census edit. Every declared vendored root exists; a renamed or removed root fails the check rather than silently widening the census. sha256 of a `.cjs` file after run N equals sha256 after run 1, and the tree-wide count of consecutive duplicate annotations stays 0.
tickets.background:
### Goal
Add `.cjs` to SOURCE_EXTENSIONS so the 134 tracked `.cjs` files in this repository can carry provenance annotations, and make the set's completeness a decision that fails a test when it goes stale, rather than an omission nobody can see.

### Purpose
`SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` describes itself as the single source of truth for which files the annotation system supports. Today it is a hand-maintained list that no check compares against the repository, and its own comment records the consequence: a file the mechanism does not know about is never reported on. The mechanism that binds an implementation to the design context it came from silently does not apply to 134 of this repository's own test files, including the test file for the annotation tool itself.

### Motivation
The identical defect was found and fixed once already: P22-4 added `.mjs` for the same reason, and left a comment explaining why such omissions are invisible. `.cjs` was left behind at that moment and has stayed behind through every ticket since. PX-208 found it while implementing a different fix — the file it was editing could not receive its own provenance annotation — and deliberately did not fold it in, because adding an extension changes behaviour repo-wide and the Plan Gate requires that to be ticketed. Without a check, the next extension will be omitted the same way, and the same ticket will be written again.

### Constraints
- `SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` must keep its shape: a Set of dotted lowercase strings, consumed by `Set.has` in three places in the annotator and one in `show-ticket-locations.js`. No call site changes.
- The vendored trees must stay out of the census by path, not by extension, so a vendored `.rs` and a vendored `.h` are excluded identically.
- The census must be derived at check time from `git ls-files`, never from a stored extension list, or it would have the same defect it exists to catch.
- TDD Red-Green-Refactor is mandatory. Every behaviour here is deterministic — a file list, a set membership, a byte comparison — so nothing may be excused as untestable.
- The change widens what the annotator processes. The property PX-208 established — two runs leave a file byte-identical, and the tree-wide count of consecutive duplicate annotations is 0 — must still hold under the widened filter, re-measured rather than assumed.
scope:

  - Dependency added/removed: none.
  - `.claude/scripts/tickets/lib/scope-extensions-census.js` — new, CommonJS, beside the constants it checks.

Pure functions over an injected file list, with the `git ls-files` call kept at the outermost edge so the decision logic is testable without a repository.
  - API contract change: new module; no existing caller changes.
  - `tests/tickets/scope-extensions.test.cjs` — new test file, `.cjs` because the module under test is CommonJS.
  - Action: add.

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**

They are recorded in `EXCLUDED_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` with that reason, so the decision is written rather than implied.

A retroactive sweep would insert an annotation into 134 files attributing them to whichever ticket ran the sweep, which is a false provenance claim. PX-208 removed annotations that were duplicates of true claims; this would create claims that are not true.

Response: none; the source is unchanged, and PX-208's idempotence tests are re-run and extended to `.cjs`.

Response: none expected; the regression gate is re-run and must still report `proved`, and if it drifts the drift must be named as the extension set rather than re-captured by assumption.

testUnit: UT: [Normal] C001 postcondition — every present extension resolves. The census is computed from `git ls-files` at check time; for each extension with three or more tracked files outside the declared vendored roots, the test asserts it is in SOURCE_EXTENSIONS or in EXCLUDED_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS. The measured census outside both vendored roots: included .js 445, .mjs 261, .ts 30, .rs 22, .py 9; excluded .md 417, .json 100, .sh 18. `.cjs` 134 is the one that was in neither.

UT: [Normal] C001 postcondition — every exclusion carries a reason. For each entry of EXCLUDED_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS the test asserts a non-empty string reason, so an extension cannot be waved away with an empty value. The map is expected to hold exactly three entries — .md, .json, .sh — and the test asserts the set of keys equals that list, so a decision cannot be removed without the test noticing.

UT: [Error] C001 invariant — THE REGRESSION. A temporary tracked file with an extension absent from both sets (.zig, three copies) makes the check fail, and the failure message names '.zig'. This is the assertion that would have caught .cjs, and it must fail for a new extension without anyone editing the test.

UT: [Boundary] C001 — an extension with fewer than three tracked files outside the vendored roots does not require a decision, so a one-off file does not force a census edit. Two .zig files are accepted silently; the third fails the check.

UT: [Normal] C002 precondition — .cjs is admitted by the filter. filterSourceFiles(['a.cjs']) returns ['a.cjs']; before this ticket it returns []. The test also pins the neighbouring acceptances (.js, .mjs, .ts, .rs, .py) and rejections (.md, .json, .sh, .h) so the addition cannot be mistaken for a widening of the filter.

UT: [Normal] C002 postcondition — a .cjs file with a definition is annotated. A fixture .cjs holding a function definition is processed with key K; the returned action begins 'annotated' and the file gains exactly one annotation line above that definition.

UT: [Error] C002 invariant — the PX-208 property holds for the newly admitted extension. processFile is called three times over the same .cjs fixture; sha256 after run 3 equals sha256 after run 1, and the annotation count stays at 1.

UT: [Boundary] C002 — a .cjs file that already carries an annotation for K, separated from its definition by a comment, reports already-annotated and is byte-identical. This is PX-208's fix re-proved on the extension this ticket admits, because a new extension entering the tool is exactly where a fixed defect can silently fail to apply.

UT: [Boundary] C002 — a .cjs file with no recognisable definition takes the file-level path and receives an [::AMBIGUOUS::] marker rather than throwing, and a second run with the same key inserts nothing.

UT: [Normal] C003 postcondition — the census ignores vendored copies. The count of .h, .c, .cc, .cpp and .hpp outside the vendored roots is zero, so the census reports no undecided C/C++ extension; the 2253 files exist and are absorbed by path. A test plants a .h file under tests/ and asserts the census then reports .h as undecided, because .h is in neither set.

UT: [Invariant] C003 — the exclusion is by path prefix, not by extension. A temporary .rs file under a vendored root is ignored exactly as a .h file there is, and adding a vendored .zig requires no decision, while the same .zig outside the vendored roots fails the check.

UT: [Boundary] C003 — the vendored root list is declared and non-empty, and every entry names a directory that exists in the repository, so a renamed or removed vendored tree surfaces as a failure rather than as a silently widened census. The test asserts both roots resolve to directories.

UT: [Boundary] C001 — a tracked path carrying no extension is skipped rather than counted under an empty name. Two such paths exist in this repository today; a synthetic list containing 'Makefile' and 'LICENSE' produces no census entry for them.

Reason: it is not testable, because it is not knowable — the census can only assert that today's repository is entirely decided. This is **not a design defect**: it is the point of the check, which converts an unknowable future omission into a failing test at the moment the file lands. tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] The census check reports by naming, not by counting: when it fails it prints the undecided extensions and the file count behind each, so the reader can decide without re-deriving the census. The annotator keeps its existing `[annotate]` stderr lines unchanged; nothing new is printed on the success path, because a mechanism that announces itself on every run is noise.
- [Metrics] None persisted. The census counts extensions per run and prints them only on failure. There is deliberately no running total of annotated files: the number that matters is "zero undecided extensions", which is a verdict rather than a metric.
- [Error tracking] The check exits non-zero and names the extension. It does not attempt to repair, and it does not consult the network or the working tree state beyond `git ls-files`, so it is deterministic and offline.
- [Health check] The existing surfaces carry it: `make test` runs the census as one test file among 317, and the regression gate's forward surfaces independently exercise the annotator's decision table with the widened set. No new health mechanism is introduced.

tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) Red — write `tests/tickets/scope-extensions.test.cjs` first, including the `.zig` regression and the vendored-root boundary, and confirm they fail against the current constants. (2) Red — write the `.cjs` annotation tests in the existing annotator test file and confirm they fail because the filter rejects the extension. (3) Green — add `.cjs` and the two new exports; add the census module. (4) Re-run the annotator twice over the repository and confirm 0 inserted on the second run and 0 consecutive duplicates tree-wide, which is PX-208's property re-measured under the widened filter. (5) Run `make test` and the regression gate.
- [Risks] The main risk is that admitting `.cjs` changes what the annotator touches on every future ticket, so a defect that PX-208 fixed could fail to apply to the newly admitted extension. That is covered by re-running PX-208's tests against a `.cjs` fixture rather than assuming the fix is extension-agnostic. The second risk is the census threshold: a three-file floor is a judgement, and a lower one would force decisions on one-off extensions while a higher one could hide a genuine omission. Three is chosen because every extension this ticket decides on has at least five files; the threshold is a named constant with that justification, not a literal in the comparison.
- [Caveats] The census checks that every extension is decided, not that every decision is correct. It cannot tell whether excluding `.sh` is right; it can only tell that someone wrote down why. That is the honest limit of a mechanical check over a judgement, and the file's own comment should say so rather than implying the set is now provably complete.
- [Open items] Whether the 134 `.cjs` files should receive retroactive annotations is settled in favour of no: attributing them to a sweep ticket would be a provenance claim that is not true. They become annotatable prospectively. Whether the census should also run as a `make` target beside `check-conventions` is left to the plan; `make test` already reaches it, and a second entry point is only worth adding if the check is useful before a commit rather than only during one.
- [Future improvements] The same derive-and-compare move could be applied to `DEFINITION_PATTERN_METAS`, which claims to cover the languages the toolchain uses but has no entry for C, C++, Go's methods, or shell, and nothing checks it against the extensions that are admitted. That is a larger question — the patterns are behaviour, not a membership list — and is not attempted here.

FINDING 1 — parseExtension read a dotfile as an extension. FIXED.
`parseExtension(".gitignore")` returned `".gitignore"`, and `parseExtension("..")` returned `"."`. The function's contract is "the dotted extension, or null when there is none", and a leading or trailing dot names nothing. Found by probing the function directly with the repository's own dotfiles rather than only through the census, which is why the existing tests did not catch it: eight dotfiles are tracked, each produced a unique bogus name with a count of one, and the decision floor of three kept every one of them out of the census. The defect was invisible in exactly the way this ticket exists to remove, one level down.
Fixed by taking the basename, requiring a dot that is neither first nor last, and requiring the remainder to be non-empty. A test was written first and failed: `.gitignore`, `src/.env` and `..` must be null; `.eslintrc.json` and `a.tar.gz` must not. The census before and after is unchanged — 0 undecided, .cjs 134 — which is the point: the fix removes a false name from a place the floor was hiding.

**[Happy path] — Describe the scenario that confirms this ticket is complete:**
  - `SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` contains `.cjs`; `filterSourceFiles(["a.cjs"])` returns the path; a `.cjs` file with a definition is annotated on the first run and reports `skipped:already-annotated` on the second. **[Error case] — Describe an error scenario the feature must handle:**
  - Three tracked files with an extension present in neither set make the census fail, and the failure names that extension. A `.h` file placed directly under `tests/` is reported as undecided, while the same content under a vendored root changes nothing. The check never widens a set on its own; it fails and names what it found.

**[Edge case] — Describe any boundary or exception to verify:**

A vendored `.rs` is excluded exactly as a vendored `.h` is, proving the exclusion is by path and not by extension. A declared vendored root that does not exist fails the check. tickets.investigation:
### Evidence — the omission, and why it is invisible

`.claude/scripts/tickets/lib/scope-detection-constants.js` declares itself, in its own doc comment, "the single source of truth" for the extensions the annotation system supports. Measured against the repository with both vendored roots excluded, it is not:

| Extension | Tracked files outside vendored roots | In SOURCE_EXTENSIONS |
|---|---|---|
| .js | 445 | yes |
| .mjs | 261 | yes |
| **.cjs** | **134** | **no** |
| .md | 417 | no |
| .json | 100 | no |
| .ts | 30 | yes |
| .rs | 22 | yes |
| .sh | 18 | no |
| .py | 9 | yes |

The census is smaller than it first appears, and that is the point: with `siprs-with-4layers/` and `siprs-for-reverse/` excluded by path, exactly four extensions sit at three or more files without a decision — `.md`, `.json`, `.sh` and `.cjs` — and of those only `.cjs` is source this repository owns.

The 134 `.cjs` files are this repository's own tests: `tests/rfc-graph` 35, `tests/drill-rfc-down` 26, `tests/crystalize-readme` 11, `.claude/archive` 6, `.claude/tests` 4, `tests/tickets` 3, `tests/grill-me-for-rfc` 2, and roughly fifty directly under `tests/` including `annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff.test.cjs` itself. Twelve more sit in the vendored trees. None of the 146 carries a provenance annotation, and none ever has.

The file already names the reason this went unnoticed, in the comment P22-4 left when it added `.mjs` for exactly the same reason: "the omission is invisible, because a file the mechanism does not know about is simply never reported on." `.mjs` was added; `.cjs` was not, and nothing has compared the set against the repository since.

### Evidence — the set is not merely stale, it is unchecked

Two consumers read it:

- `.claude/scripts/tickets/annotate-ticket-context-by-git-diff.js` — `filterSourceFiles` (line 324), `annotateSourceFiles` (481), `verifyAnnotations` (555).
- `.claude/scripts/tickets/show-ticket-locations.js` — line 134, `if (!SOURCE_EXTENSIONS.has(ext)) continue;`.

Neither reports what it skipped. A file excluded by extension produces no output on any path, so the omission cannot surface as a failure, only as an absence. The module has no test of its own: a search of `tests/` for `scope-detection`, `SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` or `findContainingDefinition` finds no test file, so nothing checks the set today by any means.

### Evidence — the parser already handles .cjs; the set is the only barrier

Measured directly:

```js
findContainingDefinition(["#!/usr/bin/env node", "function alpha() { return 1; }", "module.exports={alpha};"], 1, ".cjs")
// => { startLine: 1, name: "alpha", kind: "function" }   — identical to ".js"
```

`detectLanguage` (scope-detection.js:29-31) returns "indent" only for `.py` and `.rb` and "brace" for every other non-empty hint, so the extension selects a parsing strategy and nothing else. `DEFINITION_PATTERN_METAS` is a 16-entry array applied uniformly, not a per-extension map.

Parse quality on real files, ten-file samples: `.cjs` 7/10, `.mjs` 7/10, `.js` 4/10, `.rs` 7/10, `.ts` 8/10. `.cjs` is not a marginal case; it parses at the same rate as the extensions already admitted.

### Evidence — the three exclusions, each measured rather than assumed

- **`.md`**, 417 files. Prose. The checklist generators write Markdown for a human to read, and the parser would match substrings of prose rather than definitions.
- **`.json`**, 100 files. Data. The parse of a JSON file yields no definitions, and annotating a fixture would corrupt a frozen digest.
- **`.sh`**, 18 files, and this one needed measuring rather than assuming: a ten-file sample yielded 0/10 with a definition detected, while a hand-written `function helper() { ` fixture does match. Admitting `.sh` would annotate nothing while claiming support.

### Evidence — what the vendored roots absorb

`siprs-with-4layers/` (3675 tracked files, no `.git` of its own, already divergent from this toolchain) and `siprs-for-reverse/`. Together they hold 2253 C/C++ files — `.h` 1172 and `.c` 645 under `siprs-for-reverse/` alone, plus `.cc` 314, `.cpp` 68, `.hpp` 55 — and 9 `.gn` files under `siprs-for-reverse/vendor/pjsip/third_party/webrtc_aec3/`. Their ten-file definition-detection rates run from 2/10 to 10/10, which is incidental brace matching rather than C parsing since `DEFINITION_PATTERN_METAS` holds no C or C++ pattern. None of that matters to the decision: they are vendored third-party sources this repository does not own, and excluding them by path is what reduces the census from a forty-entry problem to a four-entry one.

Two tracked files carry no extension at all and are skipped by the census rather than counted as an extension with an empty name.

### Evidence — the pattern this ticket follows

PX-205 built `make check-conventions`: a document that had drifted from the repository was made checkable by deriving the table from the filesystem and comparing it against the written word. `.claude/rules/node.md` now cannot drift from the tree. This ticket applies the same move to a constant that makes the same claim of itself and has drifted in the same way.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
The file this ticket edits is a constants module that contradicts its own doc comment, so the Boy Scout work is mostly making the comments true rather than restructuring code.

- **Comments must not lie.** The header of `SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` says the module "is the single source of truth" and then explains only why `.mjs` is present. It is not a source of truth in any checkable sense — nothing compares it to the repository — and the comment's own next sentence names the consequence without drawing the conclusion. Rewritten to say what the set is, that a census checks it, where that census lives, and what it cannot check. The sentence explaining why omissions are invisible is kept: it is the reason the check exists.
- **Hardcoded values as named constants.** The census threshold — the number of files at which an extension stops being a one-off and demands a decision — is a judgement, so it becomes a named constant carrying the reason for its value, beside the two sets it governs, rather than a literal inside a comparison.
- **Domain names over generic ones.** The census module traffics in extensions, not in strings: `censusTrackedExtensions` returns a Map keyed by dotted extension, `findUndecidedExtensions` returns the extensions a decision is owed for, and the ignored path prefixes are `ignoredRoots` rather than a bare array. No `data`, `info` or `tmp`.
- **One function, one responsibility.** The census module separates "read what the repository contains" from "decide whether that is accounted for": `censusTrackedExtensions` performs the `git ls-files` call at its outermost edge and returns a plain Map, and `findUndecidedExtensions` is a pure predicate over that Map. The decision can then be tested without a repository, and the reading can be tested without a decision.
- **No error swallowing.** The census does not fall back to an empty list when `git ls-files` fails. An empty census would report "nothing undecided" — the exact false negative this ticket exists to remove — so a failure to read the repository is a failure of the check.
- **Function names as verb phrases.** `censusTrackedExtensions` and `findUndecidedExtensions` are the two exports; neither is a bare noun, and the existing `SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` / `EXCLUDED_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` / `VENDORED_ROOTS` names stay as constants, which is what they are.
- **Untested code in anything touched.** The constants module has no test of its own today. The new test file covers it, including the two invariants a reader would otherwise have to take on faith: that the exclusion is by path and not by extension, and that every reason string is present.

contracts.precondition: A .cjs file containing at least one definition the parser recognises, and a ticket key K that the file does not yet carry.

contracts.precondition: 2253 tracked C/C++ files, every one of them under siprs-with-4layers/vendor/ or siprs-for-reverse/vendor/, and a .h file added directly under this repository's own tests/.

contracts.invariant: The exclusion is by path prefix, not by extension: a vendored .rs is excluded exactly as a vendored .h is, and adding a vendored .zig requires no decision.

tickets.title: gate every reverse-only passage mechanically, so a forward run cannot be stopped by it
tickets.background:
[goal] Every reverse-only passage in the nine command files is gated by a predicate drawn from a declared table, no reverse-only passage sits inside a forward step sequence, and the forward rotation keeps its step sequence, its completion conditions, its Language Protocol table and its First-Class Rule line byte-identical.
[purpose] The reverse rotation was added to nine existing command files by appending a section to each. Eight are safe by position, by additivity, or by a predicate that is mechanically false in forward. The rest rest their safety on prose a reader must judge: "when the project already contains an implementation", or `mode === "reverse"` where no such variable exists. A command file is a prompt, not code — nothing executes its gate, so a reader reads the gate and decides. This ticket removes the judgement, not the sections.
[motivation] The forward rotation is complete and working; the failure being removed is that a reverse-only passage stops it. `.claude/commands/boundify-graph.md` carries "Step 3 is not run at all" at line 228, immediately before "## Step 3: Batch File Generation" at line 263, gated only by the judgement "the project already contains an implementation" — which is true of this repository. A forward boundify run that judges wrongly generates no tree and reports no error. `workspacify-tree.md` (231), `workspacify-allocate.md` (351) and `graphify-rfc.md` (565) carry reverse gates that would block COMPLETE, gated by a heading and a Role sentence with no explicit forward gate. `drill-rfc-down.md` (404) gates on `mode === "reverse"` where `mode` exists in neither the command nor `staleness.mjs` — measured: `staleness.mjs` has no `mode` option, its only occurrence of the word is inside the comment "the whole failure mode". `crystalize-readme.md` (210) gates on the same words while the same page defines `mode` as `fresh` or `refine` at line 30.
[constraints] (1) The frontmatter of every command file is inviolable: `argument-hint`, `description` and `disable-model-invocation` are never edited. (2) No script gate logic changes — `resolveTreeMode`, `resolveAllocateMode`, `reverseIndexOf` and `return-refs.js --mode` keep their behaviour and their forward default. (3) No schema is extended. (4) No heading is removed from any command file; `compareDigests` must return zero findings against the PX-205 baseline before and after. (5) The five frozen forward surfaces keep their captured values and the baseline is not re-captured. (6) No forward file gains a dependency on the reverse tree: `tests/lib/layer-direction.mjs` computes the importer set on every call and compares it against an allowlist of three entries, each carrying its ticket, so a new reverse-tree script invoked from a forward command is refused rather than permitted.
scope: [changes-path] Nine command files — `.claude/commands/boundify-graph.md`, `workspacify-tree.md`, `workspacify-allocate.md`, `graphify-rfc.md`, `split-to-tickets.md`, `grill-me-for-rfc.md`, `crystalize-readme.md`, `find-omissions.md`, `drill-rfc-down.md` — plus one instrument, `.claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse/lib/command-file-digest.mjs`, and two test files.

[changes-action] The nine command files are modified by moving one section and adding or replacing one sentence each. The instrument is modified by adding a fourth protected section and two lint rules. `tests/workspacify-reverse/regression/command-files.test.mjs` is modified by adding assertions. One new test file is added. No script that decides anything is touched.

[changes-detail] `boundify-graph.md`: the `### Reverse Mode` body at lines 228-262 moves to the end of the file after `## Definition of success`, and a two-line pointer remains immediately before `## Step 3: Batch File Generation`. `workspacify-tree.md` (231), `workspacify-allocate.md` (351), `graphify-rfc.md` (565), `split-to-tickets.md` (592) and `grill-me-for-rfc.md` (332): each receives the same gate sentence in the same words immediately below its reverse heading, naming that command’s own predicate from the table. `crystalize-readme.md` (210) and `find-omissions.md` (372): the gate names `return-refs.js --mode=reverse`, a real flag (`return-refs.js:609,617,683`; `attachReturnRefs` branches on `mode === 'reverse'`), replacing an unqualified `mode` that collides with `derive-output-paths.js`’s `fresh|refine`. `drill-rfc-down.md` (404): the gate names the presence of `CLAIM-LEDGER.json`, which R3.5 writes and the forward rotation never produces. `command-file-digest.mjs`: a fourth protected section freezes the rotation gate beside the heading set, the Language Protocol table and the First-Class Rule line; L1 asserts no reverse heading precedes the last forward step heading; L2 asserts every reverse heading is followed within a bounded distance by a gate sentence naming a declared predicate.

[changes-before-after] Before: a reader walking the forward step sequence of `boundify-graph.md` meets a sentence removing Step 3 and must judge whether it applies; five files gate a reverse section by heading and Role prose alone; three files gate on a `mode` that is undefined, colliding, or established only later. After: the forward step sequence of every file contains no step-removing sentence; every reverse section is entered by a stated predicate naming a reverse-only artifact or argument; and a gate that is absent, misplaced, or names an undeclared predicate fails `make test`.

[changes-api] None. No exported function signature changes. `command-file-digest.mjs` gains exports (`ROTATION_GATE_*`, `DECLARED_ROTATION_PREDICATES`, `lintRotationPlacement`, `lintRotationGates`) and keeps every existing export byte-identical, so `regression-gate.mjs` and `command-files.test.mjs` continue to import what they already import.

[changes-schema] None. No `*.schema.json` is edited, no persisted document gains or loses a field, and no baseline is re-captured. The PX-205 `commandFileDigests` baseline gains one key per file through the fourth protected section only if the section is stored there; the three existing protected values per file stay byte-identical.

[changes-config] None. No `package.json`, `Makefile`, `tsconfig.json` or `ENV-DEPS.json` entry changes. `make test` reaches the new tests through `tests/run-all-surfaces.mjs`, which discovers files rather than listing them.
[changes-dep] None added, none removed. No new npm package. The lint is written against `node:fs` and `node:path`, which the module already imports.
[non-changes-item] The reverse rotation’s own behaviour, the tenth command file `workspacify-reverse.md`, the `documentDigest` field, and the five frozen forward surfaces.

[non-changes-why] The reverse rotation’s gates already default to forward and already fail safe; this ticket changes only what a reader must decide, not what a script decides, so no gate verdict moves. `workspacify-reverse.md` is a creation rather than an edit and is deliberately outside the frozen nine, so measuring it would widen the set the digest claims to protect. `documentDigest` is computed and stored but never read by `compareDigests`, and widening the comparison is a separate decision about what the digest is for. The five forward surfaces are frozen values, and a ticket that re-captures them destroys the evidence they carry.
[impact-component] `command-file-digest.mjs` consumers, the regression gate, and every future append to a command file.

[impact-nature] Behavioural in the failing direction only: the gate gains two lint rules, so input that previously passed now fails. `regression-gate.mjs` delegates to the module and reports whatever it returns, so its verdict becomes stricter without a source change. A future reverse section written inside a forward step sequence, or written without a gate, fails rather than passing silently.

[impact-response] Re-run `node .claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse/run.mjs regression check` and confirm `proved` with zero command-file losses; re-run `compareDigests` against the PX-205 baseline and confirm zero findings; re-run `make test` and confirm the claude-tests failure count is the PX-142 baseline of 14 with no new failures. If `compareDigests` reports a finding, the cause is named as a defect of this ticket rather than handled by re-capturing the baseline.

The two lints live in `command-file-digest.mjs`, which `regression-gate.mjs` already imports and delegates to, so the rule is enforced on the path a ticket actually takes rather than only where a developer remembers to run a unit test.

[verify] `node .claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse/run.mjs regression check` is run and asserted to report `proved` with zero command-file losses, zero pipeline disagreements and zero forward-surface disagreements; then the same gate is run over a fixture tree carrying a deliberately misplaced reverse section and asserted to fail naming it.

[tickets] PX-205 built the fourth baseline key and the digest that this ticket extends; P22-1 built the gate and the three forward surfaces; PX-206 established the layer rule this ticket must not violate; P22-11, P22-12, P22-13, P22-14, P22-15, P22-16, P22-17 and P22-21 wrote the sections being gated; PX-208 and PX-209 are the precedent that an instrument which reports must never widen its own subject.
testExceptions: [item] Whether a reader evaluating a gate sentence actually reaches the right conclusion. [reason] It is not testable by assertion, because the reader is a language model and the artefact is a prompt — no test observes a reading. This is **not a design defect**: a design defect is deterministic behaviour that cannot be tested, and there is no deterministic behaviour here to test; what is testable is what the reader is given, and that is what this ticket changes. The predicate stops being a judgement about the project and becomes membership of a declared table. [alternative] UT C002 asserts every reverse heading carries a gate naming a declared predicate, and UT C003 asserts every declared predicate has a reverse-only producer, so the reader is handed a check with a determinate answer rather than a question.

[item] Whether the moved `### Reverse Mode` body in `boundify-graph.md` is still discovered after the move. [reason] It is not testable as a behaviour, because discovery is a reader following a pointer and no test observes a reader. This is **not a design defect**: the properties that decide it are testable and are tested — the file still carries exactly one heading matching /reverse/i, that heading follows the last forward step heading, the pointer before Step 3 names it, and the digest confirms no heading was lost. [alternative] UT C001 asserts the heading is present and after the last forward step heading; UT C004 asserts the frozen heading set lost nothing.

[item] A full forward rotation re-executed end to end to prove that no reverse concept stops it. [reason] It is not testable within this ticket without running `/graphify-rfc`, `/boundify-graph` and `/workspacify-tree finalize` over a fresh subject, which is a multi-hour pipeline and not a unit of verification. This is **not a design defect**: the mechanism by which a reverse concept could stop a forward run is entirely textual — a sentence in the forward reading path — and that is what C001 and C002 test directly rather than by proxy. [alternative] The regression gate is re-run over the frozen forward surfaces and asserted to reach `proved`, and `compareDigests` is asserted to return zero findings, which is the statement that nothing in the forward reading path moved.

[Implementation steps] (1) Red — write the two lints and the C001/C002 tests first, run them over the nine real files, and confirm they fail with the expected kinds: `boundify-graph.md` returns `misplaced-reverse-section`, and `drill-rfc-down.md`, `crystalize-readme.md` and `find-omissions.md` return `undeclared-predicate`. (2) Red — write the C003 tests over `DECLARED_ROTATION_PREDICATES` and confirm they fail because the table does not exist. (3) Green — move the `boundify-graph.md` body and leave the pointer; add the gate sentence to the remaining files; replace the three predicates. (4) Green — add the fourth protected section and the table. (5) Re-run `compareDigests` and confirm zero findings, which is the measurement that no heading moved. (6) Run `make test` and the regression gate; record both counts.
[Risks] The first risk is that adding a gate sentence changes a line the frozen digest protects. It should not — the digest protects the heading set, the Language Protocol table and the First-Class Rule line, and a sentence below a reverse heading is none of the three — but that must be measured rather than assumed, and the measurement is the `compareDigests` run in step 5. If it reports a finding, the cause is named as a defect of this ticket rather than handled by re-capturing the baseline, because re-capturing destroys the evidence the baseline carries. The second risk is the bounded distance in L2: too small and a legitimate gate separated from its heading by the section’s role paragraph fails, too large and a gate can drift away from the section it gates. The bound is a named constant with the measurement recorded beside it, not a literal inside the comparison. The third risk is that the table becomes a rubber stamp — a place to add an entry so a sentence passes. That is guarded by the producer check, which refuses any predicate whose producer also holds in the forward rotation.
[Caveats] The lint checks that a gate exists, is placed after the forward steps, and names a declared predicate; it cannot check that the predicate is the right one for that section. That is the honest limit of a mechanical check over a mapping, and the module comment must say so rather than implying the gates are now provably correct. The `boundify-graph.md` move changes where a reader finds the reverse procedure, which is a real cost paid for removing the procedure from the forward reading path; the pointer before Step 3 and the bullet at line 62 both name the destination, so the cost is bounded and stated rather than hidden.
[Open items] Two were found while making this ticket and are recorded rather than repaired, because each widens the set the digest claims to protect and that is a separate decision. (a) The tenth command file `workspacify-reverse.md` is outside the frozen nine, and the three `Branch making-reverse commit on v0.24.635` commits each added a trailing space to its `# /workspacify-reverse` heading — measured, the heading now reads `'# /workspacify-reverse '` — which nothing detects because the file is outside the set.
