It is a stored value that looks like a check, which is the shape PX-208 and PX-209 each repaired once.
[Future improvements] The same move — replace a judgement in a prompt with membership of a declared table — applies wherever else a command file asks a reader to decide between two modes. It does not generalise to a token printed by a script, and that was investigated: `mode` is never read from a file anywhere in this repository. `resolveTreeMode` and `resolveAllocateMode` are called only with an in-process `{ mode }` that the `reverse` subcommand sets, and `staleness.mjs` has no `mode` option at all, so a token-printing resolver would have nothing to resolve from except a name it was handed — circular — and for the seven commands whose reverse path invokes a different script rather than a different subcommand, no subcommand name exists to map at all. The Boy Scout work is confined to what the ticket touches, and the rule that shapes it is that a comment must not lie.

Once a fourth protected section exists that sentence is false, so it is rewritten to name the four and to say why the fourth is different in kind: the first three are sections a reader relies on directly, the fourth is the property that a reverse-only section cannot reach a forward step. The `COMMAND_FILE_NAMES` comment also gains the measurement it currently lacks — that P22-9 created a tenth file which is deliberately absent, and that the three `v0.24.635` commits added a trailing space to that file’s heading with nothing to detect it.

`tests/workspacify-reverse/regression/command-files.test.mjs` — the eight existing assertions are kept unweakened and the new ones are added in the same shape: a fixture file per rule, a finding whose kind and file are asserted, and an assertion that the fixture is byte-identical after the check.

The nine command files — each new sentence is written to be translatable: one imperative sentence per rule, no clause that requires the reader to hold two conditions at once. Function names in the new lint are verb phrases (`lintRotationPlacement`, `lintRotationGates`, `parseGateSentence`); the predicate table is a noun (`DECLARED_ROTATION_PREDICATES`); the bounded distance is a named constant (`GATE_SEARCH_WINDOW_LINES`) with the measurement that chose it recorded beside it rather than a literal inside a comparison. tickets.title: query.js — BFSマルチホップ探索＋行番号動的解決＋Markdown整形
tickets.referenceSection: RFC-GRAPHIFY.md (3.7 CLI契約, 4.4 query.js詳細設計), crud.js, verify.js, embed-markers.js, tests/rfc-graph/*.test.cjs
tickets.background:
query.js は graphify-rfc パイプラインの Layer 2（グラフ探索機構）の中核。ノードID起点のBFS幅優先探索で最大Nホップ先までグラフを探索し、マーカー（::REF<N>-START::/::REF<N>-END::）を起点に行番号を動的に再計算し、結果をMarkdown形式で整形出力する。読み取り専用で副作用ゼロ。

既存スクリプト（crud.js P13-2、verify.js/embed-markers.js P14-1）は完了済み。query.js はそれらが生成したグラフファイルとマーカー付きソース文書を読み取り専用で使用する。

tickets.title: Forward-rotation regression gate and the environment entry point: freeze baseline manifest hashes, digest the command files, and make a single command bring a conver project fully up
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P22-2 (provides to: the regression gate every later ticket runs after its own step), P22-4 (provides to: the environment declaration its analysis toolchain is added to)
tickets.background:
**Shared premises — binding on all 22 P22 tickets. Read this first.**

P22 implements the reverse rotation: taking a project that already contains a substantial implementation and turning it into conver's four loops (upstream / implementation / release / evolution). Forward rotation already works completely; reverse rotation does not exist yet. `docs/ABOUT-REVERSE.md` is the full design. The implementation loop runs one ticket per session and context does not carry across tickets, so this block is repeated verbatim in all 22 tickets. A session that sees only its own ticket must still know what the whole is for and what it may not break.

(1) **Never break the forward rotation.** The four existing loops work. No change in P22 may alter forward behaviour. A byte-identical `manifest_hash` over the forward fixtures, captured before any change and reproduced after, is the only accepted proof. P22-1 builds that gate; every later ticket runs it after its own step. "It looks fine" is not evidence and is not accepted.
(2) **Rewriting any `.claude/commands/*.md` is strictly forbidden.** Only edits are permitted — append, or correct the minimum number of lines. The Language Protocol table, the First-Class Rule, the workflow steps and the script list must survive character for character. The nine existing command files are: `workspacify-tree`, `workspacify-allocate`, `grill-me-for-rfc`, `graphify-rfc`, `boundify-graph`, `split-to-tickets`, `find-omissions`, `crystalize-readme`, `drill-rfc-down`. P22-9 additionally *creates* `workspacify-reverse.md`, which is a new file, not an edit.
(3) The full design lives in **`docs/ABOUT-REVERSE.md`**. Each ticket cites the exact sections it depends on. Read those sections before implementing; they are the specification of record.
(4) The machine may only ever say **"proved" or "not proved"**. "Succeeded" and "failed" are not in its vocabulary, because whether reverse engineering succeeded is a judgement a human makes after several loop rounds. Any script that emits a boolean success verdict is wrong by construction.
(5) What is deterministic, a script decides and the AI accepts the verdict. Only genuinely semantic judgement is left to the AI, and the material it needs is placed in front of it — as plain, deliberately helpful English — immediately before the decision. Do not widen the AI's judgement surface beyond what the design calls for.
(6) The `[::STUB::]` marker discipline is absolute and admits no exception. Any incomplete implementation carries a marker naming the ticket that will resolve it.
(7) Output format: emit JSON only when another script consumes it, a schema validates it, a hash covers it, or a gate uses it as a predicate. **Anything the AI reads in order to decide is Markdown, written in plain and deliberately helpful English.** Struggling to read a script's output is a defect in the script, not a cost of doing business.
(8) The `Initial Design Artifact — RFC-driven Implementation` header is never deleted, altered or commented out (supreme law 4). This holds without exception, including in files this phase touches.
(9) **The paired trees are the measuring instrument.** `siprs-with-4layers` is the same project taken through the forward rotation to RESIDUE 0 and therefore holds what reverse rotation is trying to reconstruct; `siprs-for-reverse` is that project with those artefacts stripped and is what the analysis runs against. Comparing an output against the answer key yields a list of disagreements, never a score and never a verdict — classifying each disagreement is a human's work. P22-2 builds the harness; the tickets whose output is comparable run it.
(10) **The source-analysis technology is decided once, in P22-4, and never re-decided.** Four separate sessions (P22-4, P22-5, P22-6, P22-7) must parse the same Rust source, and no context passes between them. P22-4 evaluates the candidates **against the expert consultation recorded in `docs/ABOUT-ANALYSIS-TECH.md`**, records the choice and its rationale in **`docs/P22-ANALYSIS-TECH.md`**, and every later analysis ticket reads that document instead of choosing again. The repository offers no precedent to inherit — `.claude/scripts/rfc-graph/analyze-source-structure.js` is regex-based and is not equal to extracting guards, invariants and state machines — so the decision is genuinely open and must be made deliberately and written down. **The scope is six languages, not one**: Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Python and C/C++, because a technology that only handles the first target would be an implementation tuned to that target, which is explicitly forbidden. Two sessions independently choosing different parsers would produce mutually unreadable output and no test would catch it, because each session's tests would pass against its own choice. **The chosen toolchain is recorded in two places, and both are required**: the reasoning in `docs/P22-ANALYSIS-TECH.md`, and the machine-readable declaration in `ENV-DEPS.json` built by P22-1, where each new tool is added with the rotation that needs it and the ticket that provides it. Adding a tool is an entry in that declaration — never a new installation mechanism, and never a dependency left undeclared because it happened to be present on the machine where it was developed.
(11) **Match the surrounding directory, do not invent a layout.** The repository uses two conventions and they are not interchangeable. `.claude/scripts/rfc-graph/`, `grill-me-for-rfc/`, `conver/` and `tickets/` are flat CommonJS `.js` with no `lib/` subdirectory; `.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/`, `workspacify-allocate/` and `workspacify-reverse/` are ESM `.mjs` under `lib/`. A ticket that names a path must name one that matches its siblings, and must not introduce a `lib/` directory into a flat tree or a CommonJS module into an ESM one. The same applies to test files: `.test.cjs` beside CommonJS, `.test.mjs` beside ESM.
(12) **The expert answer received in `docs/ABOUT-ANALYSIS-TECH.md` (the section headed 「専門家の回答」, with the request-side verification record in its §7) is binding on the analysis design. Three of its corrections outrank any earlier wording in this repository, including the wording of earlier P22 tickets.** (a) `observed` may only ever mean *a fact read from the source text or its syntax tree*. Runtime behaviour, dynamic dispatch targets, post-preprocessing composition and generated code are not `observed` without execution, build or trace evidence, so every evidence item carries `evidence_mode`: `source_static` | `build_semantic` | `runtime_dynamic`. (b) `derivation_group` is **not** a deterministic identifier for a human design intent — that cannot be computed from file contents. It is a lineage graph over observable relations (same AST span, same generator, same commit, same data-flow origin), and independence is an explicit stored aggregation policy over that graph; `independence_assessment: "unknown"` is a legal and expected value, not a failure. (c) E13 is **TCE** (trivial / syntactic / compiler-normalisation equivalence). General semantic equivalence is undecidable and is not a goal; an AST-normalised match proves syntactic equivalence under a named configuration and nothing more. (d) Where the answer separates a *candidate* from a *decided* fact (E11, E13, E14), the separation is enforced at the type level — a candidate cannot be passed, stored or serialised where a decided fact is required — and a candidate carries `requires_human_approval`. A session that finds itself asserting a contract, an equivalence or a generated test as settled has violated this premise. **§7 of that document also records one error of ours that the answer exposed: the claim that CodeQL does not support Rust was wrong.**

---

## This ticket — P22-1

**Goal**: Put the project in a state where it is mechanically provable that no P22 change has altered forward-rotation behaviour, and where running one command resolves the whole environment on macOS, Windows and Linux.

**Purpose**: Every one of the 21 later tickets touches an asset the forward rotation already depends on. Without a frozen baseline there is no way to detect breakage, and "we were careful" is not evidence. This ticket builds the instrument that makes breakage visible — and builds the thing that instrument runs inside, because a gate whose environment cannot be reproduced is not a gate. A session that cannot resolve its dependencies cannot run it, and a user who cannot set the project up cannot run anything at all.

**Motivation**: The self-audit recorded in ABOUT-REVERSE 11.9 found that no golden manifest has ever been saved and that the allocate side has no fixtures at all. Measured on 2026-09-10: `tests/workspacify-allocate/fixtures/` does not exist, and no file matching `*MANIFEST*`, `*golden*` or `*expected*` holds a captured manifest. The design has asserted "never break the forward rotation" since it was written, but the assertion has never been executable. **The environment half was measured on the same day and is also concrete.** A conver project touches eight npm roots, of which three are installed and five are not; `.claude/package.json` declares `sql.js ^1.14.2` and `.claude/package-lock.json` records it, yet `.claude/node_modules/sql.js` is absent, so `require(".claude/scripts/lib/state-store/index.js")` fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND and takes three dependent modules with it. External tools are split the same way: `node cargo rustc go python3 clang gcc java rg` are present, while `zg tree-sitter codeql joern` are absent. **Nothing in the repository aggregates any of this.** `tools/conver/install.js` and `install-deps.cjs` install a `.claude` tree and resolve that tree's npm dependencies, which is the right home, but they stop there.

**Constraints**: This ticket changes no forward code path. It adds tests and measurement only. Baseline capture must complete before any other P22 change, because a baseline taken after a change cannot distinguish a pre-existing value from a regression. Malformed input must produce a descriptive error rather than a silent pass: a gate that fails open is worse than no gate. **The environment entry point must be non-interactive.** Running it must not block on stdin, because a prompt cannot be answered by an automated session and cannot be answered by a user who does not know which of several hundred files they are expected to accept; the decision of what to overwrite is the installer's to make and to report, not the caller's to supply. It must also never destroy pre-existing content, which is the principle `install-deps.cjs` already follows for `node_modules`.

**Where this ticket sits in the 22.** **→1 regression gate** · 2 experiment design (holdout + answer key) · 3 spike · 4 R0-R2 scope and structure · 5 R3-R3.5 semantics and ledger · 6 R4-R5.5 history, gaps, oracle · 7 R6-R6.5 Red plan and falsification · 8 R7-R8 serving and origin spec · 9 command and zg · 10 forward schemas · 11 workspacify-tree reverse · 12 workspacify-allocate reverse · 13 grill reverse · 14 graphify reverse · 15 boundify reverse · 16 split-to-tickets reverse · 17 omission and RESIDUE return · 18 dynamic analysis · 19 Red execution · 20 logical/physical two-layer · 21 staleness into drill · 22 security lane

**Step 0 — before you write anything.** `node .claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse/run.mjs regression check` — if this command does not yet exist, you are on P22-1 and must build it; if it exists, it must exit 0 before you start. **Then run the environment entry point with no arguments and read its report.** If it does not yet exist you must build it; if it does, the report must show the forward rotation ready and must name anything still missing together with the command that would provide it. Two measured facts from 2026-09-10 tell you whether the report is telling the truth: `.claude` declares `sql.js` and has no `sql.js` in `node_modules`, and `zg`, `tree-sitter`, `codeql` and `joern` are absent — the last four being the reverse-rotation toolchain, whose absence is expected at this point in the phase and is not a failure.
tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】Every fixture under `tests/workspacify-tree/fixtures/` and `tests/workspacify-allocate/fixtures/` has its `manifest_hash` frozen in JSON, and a later `check` reproduces the identical value. Every one of the nine command files has its heading set, Language Protocol table and First-Class Rule line digested. **A single entry point resolves the whole environment**: every declared npm root is installed, every declared external tool is probed, and the outcome is recorded in `ENV-MANIFEST.json`. Each declared dependency states which rotation needs it, so the report can say "the forward rotation is ready, the reverse rotation is not" rather than emitting one undifferentiated verdict that hides the difference.
- 【On error】A missing baseline file, an unreadable fixture, or a non-UTF-8 input produces a descriptive error naming the path and the reason, and exits non-zero. No failure is swallowed into a passing gate. **An unresolved dependency is reported by name together with the exact command that would provide it on this operating system**, and never silently skipped; a dependency that cannot be resolved leaves the run non-zero rather than producing a report that reads as ready. A spawn failure names the command it tried to run and the platform it ran on — "npm install failed" is not an acceptable message for "npm was not found".
- 【Internal state】Measurement is read-only: the SHA-256 of every target file is identical before and after both `capture` and `check`. `capture` is idempotent — running it twice produces byte-identical JSON. **The installer decides what to do with an existing file by comparing three things — the target, the source, and what it installed last time — and never by asking.** A file the user has modified is reported and left untouched; a file that differs from the source only because conver has moved on is updated.
- 【Boundary】Zero allocate fixtures exits 0 with the explicit message that there is nothing to check, rather than being confused with success or failure. A single byte changed in a single fixture is detected. **Running the environment entry point twice is safe**: the second run changes nothing and says so. A declared tool whose absence is expected at this point in the phase is reported as unavailable rather than as an error, and never aborts the run.

【Implementation steps】Red: unit tests for capture, compare and digest; then unit tests for environment resolution, tool probing and the three-way file decision. Green: `regression-gate.mjs`, `command-file-digest.mjs`, `ENV-DEPS.json`, the `env-manifest.cjs` recorder, the `install.js` and `install-deps.cjs` extensions, and the two launchers. Prove detection works by making a deliberate edit and watching the gate fail.
【Risks】Deferring baseline capture makes later breakage undetectable, so capture must happen first, before any other P22 change. A non-deterministic fixture produces false positives that will be ignored and thereby destroy the gate's authority; freeze the inputs and assert idempotence. **On the environment side the first risk is the interactive prompt.** It looks considerate and it makes the command unrunnable: an automated session cannot answer it, and a user facing several hundred questions will answer them wrongly. Removing it is not a simplification, it is the requirement. **The second risk is overwriting a user's work**, and the answer is not a `--force` flag but the three-way comparison, because a flag asks the caller to know something the installer can determine. **The third risk is the opposite failure**: refusing to touch anything, which would leave the installation permanently stale while reporting success. **The fourth is testing.** `install-deps.cjs` is fully tested and every test injects a fake command runner, so the real spawn path has never executed — which is exactly how a Windows-only failure survived. The Windows path must be exercised, and since it cannot be exercised on this machine, the spawn must be constructed so the platform decision is a pure function that a test can assert directly.

The installer suite passes via `node --test tools/conver/tests/` — note that this path is outside the `tests/` convention that drives the other verification commands. Review report

Verification performed independently of the implementation notes.

Adversarial checks (the point of the review)
1. Perturbed the forward implementation (schema_version 1.0.0 -> 1.0.1 in render.mjs) and re-ran the gate. It reported not proved and named all three pipeline pairs with expected and observed values, then returned to proved once the file was restored from git. This proves the gate detects forward-code change, not merely fixture edits — which is the ticket's whole purpose.
2. Restored the perturbation byte-exactly (git reported 0 changes) and confirmed the gate returns to proved.
3. Confirmed P22-1 modified none of the nine command files (git status: 0 entries) and that all nine digests are frozen.
4. Confirmed the baseline has exactly the three declared schema keys.
5. Ran the entry point with stdin closed and no arguments: exit 0, no prompt characters in the output.

Findings raised by this review and fixed
F1 (major) When a pipeline pair could no longer run, runTreePair threw and the operator saw an exception message instead of a verdict. C003's invariant says the gate speaks only of proved and not proved, so the failure vocabulary was wrong even though the exit code was right. checkBaselines now captures a failed run as an observation ("unavailable: ...") and reports it as a pair finding, so one broken pair no longer hides the results of the others. New test asserts the report rather than the throw.
F2 (major, acceptance criterion) The acceptance criterion for the error case requires the expected and the actual value to be shown. Drifted fixtures were reported by name only. checkBaselines now returns fixtureFindings with both digests and renderCheckReport prints them; new test asserts the rendered report contains both.
F3 (major, acceptance criterion) The environment error case requires the run to exit non-zero when a dependency cannot be resolved. The installer printed the missing entries but always exited 0, so a report that named a problem still read as ready. It now exits 1 when the forward rotation is not ready, using rotationIsReady, which also stopped counting not-yet-required as satisfied. New tests cover the predicate for all three cases.
F4 (minor) env-manifest.cjs used a generic `data` variable for the parsed Tickets document; renamed to ticketsDocument.

Stub and crime discipline
- 0 [::STUB::] markers repository-wide; 0 open crimes; no-excuse gate exit 0.
- No incomplete implementation patterns (todo!/unimplemented!/panic!/TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX/empty bodies/commented-out code/mocks/suppression) in the changed source.
- One [::AMBIGUOUS::] marker was raised by the annotation tool against tools/conver/.claude/scripts/conver/conver.js, a minified build artefact this ticket did not modify. It was removed rather than annotated, because labelling it P22-1 would have been false.

Boy Scout work beyond the plan (all verified by tests)
- isDependencyInstalled replaces require.resolve as the installed-ness probe: require.resolve reported an installed ESM package (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED) as missing, which made the report cry wolf.
- install.js console calls became explicit process.stdout/stderr writers, matching the other CLI entry points and clearing 24 quality-check findings.
- The 7-parameter resolveEnvironment was reduced to 5 by grouping the environment descriptor.
- install.js comments were translated from Japanese to English (Language Protocol), and the stdin prompt and its readline import were deleted rather than left unused.

Residual risk carried forward
The gate's frozen digests are machine-independent except through node version, which is normalised away with the rest of run provenance; the node version actually used is recorded in ENV-MANIFEST.json instead. A future ticket that changes forward behaviour will trip the gate and must re-capture deliberately — that is the intended workflow, and no re-capture should be performed to make a red gate green.
acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path]:** `capture` freezes the baselines and `check` exits 0 on an untouched tree. All nine command-file digests are recorded.
**[Error case]:** A modified fixture or a damaged command file is reported by name and exits 1, with the expected and actual values shown.
**[Edge case]:** A second `capture` produces byte-identical JSON, and the SHA-256 of every target is unchanged across both capture and check.

**[Environment — happy path]:** Running the entry point once, with no arguments, resolves every declared dependency and prints a Markdown report that separates forward readiness from reverse readiness.

**[Environment — error case]:** A dependency that cannot be resolved is named with the exact command that would provide it on this platform, and the run exits non-zero rather than reporting readiness.

**[Environment — edge case]:** Running it a second time changes nothing; a file the user modified locally is preserved and reported; and a tool whose absence is declared normal, or whose providing ticket has not converged, is reported as unavailable or not yet required rather than as an error.

- **The environment surface, measured on 2026-09-10.** Eight npm roots exist. `.claude` holds five packages (`ajv`, `fast-deep-equal`, `fast-uri`, `json-schema-traverse`, `require-from-string`) and is **missing `sql.js`**, which its `package.json` declares as `^1.14.2` and its `package-lock.json` (lockfileVersion 3) records under `node_modules/sql.js`. The consequence is measured, not inferred: `require(".claude/scripts/lib/state-store/index.js")` fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, and three modules import it — `.claude/scripts/lib/skill-evolution/tracker.js`, `.claude/scripts/lib/state-store/schema.js` and `.claude/scripts/lib/session-adapters/canonical-session.js`. `tools/conver` holds 105 packages and `fe` holds 379. `.claude/scripts/rfc-graph` declares `ajv ^8.20.0` with **no `node_modules` of its own**, and resolves it only by upward traversal into `.claude/node_modules` — which works today and is not guaranteed to, which is why the declaration must name every root explicitly rather than relying on where Node happens to look.
- **External tools, same date.** Present: `node` (v26.0.0), `npm`, `cargo` (1.96.0), `rustc` (1.96.0), `go`, `python3`, `clang`, `gcc`, `java`, `rg`. Absent: `zg`, `tree-sitter`, `codeql`, `joern`. The four absent ones are precisely the reverse-rotation toolchain, which is why the declaration needs a way to say *not yet required* rather than *missing*.
- **The installer already exists and is the right home, which changes this ticket's shape.** `tools/conver/install.js` (250 lines) mirrors `tools/conver/.claude` into a target `.claude`, with `-t` for the target, `-y` to auto-accept overwrites, and `--no-install-deps`. It delegates dependency work to `tools/conver/install-deps.cjs` (151 lines), whose design is already the correct one: verify first and do nothing if everything resolves; never modify an existing `node_modules`; install only where none exists, with `--no-audit --no-fund --ignore-scripts`; and roll back the `node_modules` it created on failure. **Nothing here should be rebuilt.** The work is to widen what it resolves and remove what blocks it.
- **Two defects in that installer, both measured.** First, `defaultCommandRunner` at `install-deps.cjs:74` calls `spawnSync(command, args, { cwd, encoding: "utf8" })` with no `shell` option, and the caller at line 90 passes the bare command `npm`. On Windows `npm` is `npm.cmd`, and a shell-less spawn cannot resolve a `.cmd`, so the call fails with ENOENT and returns `status: null` — which the caller converts into the message `npm install failed`. The failure names the symptom and hides the cause. Second, `tests/install-deps.test.cjs` injects a fake `commandRunner` at all nine call sites, so `defaultCommandRunner` has never executed in any test; the injection is right for testability, and the consequence is that the platform-dependent path is the one path with no coverage. **The fix must make the platform decision a pure function that a test can assert directly**, because the Windows branch cannot be exercised on this machine.
- **`install.js` blocks on stdin.** `promptOverwrite` at lines 108-125 opens a readline interface and asks per file. For a first-time user this never fires, because nothing exists to overwrite; for an existing user it fires once per changed file. A prompt cannot be answered by an automated session, so this is the specific mechanism that makes "one command sets everything up" impossible today.
- **The state-tracking machinery this needs already exists in the repository.** `.claude/scripts/lib/install-state.js` (313 lines) and `.claude/schemas/install-state.schema.json` belong to a different installer — the multi-target rules distribution under `.claude/scripts/lib/install-targets/` covering claude-home, cursor, codex, gemini, opencode, codebuddy and antigravity — but the concept is the same and the schema is worth reading before inventing a second one. **The two systems must not be merged**: one installs conver into a project, the other distributes rules into AI tools. Reuse the idea and, where it fits, the code; never the entry point.
- `scripts/deploy-installer.mjs` at the repository root is a third, unrelated thing: it packages Tauri installer artefacts for the zasso application. It must not be wired to either of the above.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- New code is written for translatability first: functions as verb phrases (`captureBaselines`, `checkBaselines`, `digestCommandFiles`, `compareDigests`, `resolveEnvironment`, `probeTools`, `decideFileAction`), variables as domain concepts (`fixturePath`, `expectedHash`, `observedHash`, `driftedNames`, `declaredRoot`, `providedBy`, `previousDigest`), one responsibility per function, and no hardcoded path — the fixture roots and the declaration path are named constants.
- **`install.js` violates the Language Protocol and is fixed while touched.** Its header comment (lines 2-8), `showUsage` (lines 62-75) and the JSDoc on `parseArgs`, `collectFilesWithRelative`, `promptOverwrite`, `copyFileWithPrompt`, `showSummary` and `main` are written in Japanese. Code comments must be English. The user-facing usage text may be localised separately, but the explanatory comments must not be.
- **`defaultCommandRunner` is rewritten so the platform decision is testable without a Windows machine**: the command name is resolved from a pure function of the platform, and that function is asserted directly for both `win32` and the POSIX case. A comment explaining why Windows needs `.cmd` is not a substitute for a test that says so.
- `install.js` is at 250 lines and `install-deps.cjs` at 151; the environment work goes into `env-manifest.cjs` and the declaration reader rather than growing either of them past the 800-line limit, and `promptOverwrite` and its readline import are deleted rather than left unused.
- Any `unwrap`-style or throwing access encountered in the touched region of `run.mjs` is replaced with explicit error propagation that names the offending path.
- The usage text in `run.mjs` is updated in the same commit as the subcommand list, so the help output cannot rot into a lie.
- The new gate module is kept under the 800-line limit by separating digest computation from comparison, following the existing `lib/` convention in this directory.

tickets.title: Experiment design: a frozen holdout for generality, and the paired-tree answer key that makes the analysis falsifiable
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P22-1 (depends on: shares run.mjs), P22-3 (provides to: the protocol and the answer key the spike runs against), P22-8 (related: the analysis exit whose output the answer key measures)
tickets.background:
**Shared premises — binding on all 22 P22 tickets. Read this first.**

P22 implements the reverse rotation: taking a project that already contains a substantial implementation and turning it into conver's four loops (upstream / implementation / release / evolution). Forward rotation already works completely; reverse rotation does not exist yet. `docs/ABOUT-REVERSE.md` is the full design. The implementation loop runs one ticket per session and context does not carry across tickets, so this block is repeated verbatim in all 22 tickets. A session that sees only its own ticket must still know what the whole is for and what it may not break.

(1) **Never break the forward rotation.** The four existing loops work. No change in P22 may alter forward behaviour. A byte-identical `manifest_hash` over the forward fixtures, captured before any change and reproduced after, is the only accepted proof. P22-1 builds that gate; every later ticket runs it after its own step. "It looks fine" is not evidence and is not accepted.
(2) **Rewriting any `.claude/commands/*.md` is strictly forbidden.** Only edits are permitted — append, or correct the minimum number of lines. The Language Protocol table, the First-Class Rule, the workflow steps and the script list must survive character for character. The nine existing command files are: `workspacify-tree`, `workspacify-allocate`, `grill-me-for-rfc`, `graphify-rfc`, `boundify-graph`, `split-to-tickets`, `find-omissions`, `crystalize-readme`, `drill-rfc-down`. P22-9 additionally *creates* `workspacify-reverse.md`, which is a new file, not an edit.
(3) The full design lives in **`docs/ABOUT-REVERSE.md`**. Each ticket cites the exact sections it depends on. Read those sections before implementing; they are the specification of record.
(4) The machine may only ever say **"proved" or "not proved"**. "Succeeded" and "failed" are not in its vocabulary, because whether reverse engineering succeeded is a judgement a human makes after several loop rounds. Any script that emits a boolean success verdict is wrong by construction.
(5) What is deterministic, a script decides and the AI accepts the verdict. Only genuinely semantic judgement is left to the AI, and the material it needs is placed in front of it — as plain, deliberately helpful English — immediately before the decision. Do not widen the AI's judgement surface beyond what the design calls for.
(6) The `[::STUB::]` marker discipline is absolute and admits no exception. Any incomplete implementation carries a marker naming the ticket that will resolve it.
(7) Output format: emit JSON only when another script consumes it, a schema validates it, a hash covers it, or a gate uses it as a predicate. **Anything the AI reads in order to decide is Markdown, written in plain and deliberately helpful English.** Struggling to read a script's output is a defect in the script, not a cost of doing business.
(8) The `Initial Design Artifact — RFC-driven Implementation` header is never deleted, altered or commented out (supreme law 4). This holds without exception, including in files this phase touches.
(9) **The paired trees are the measuring instrument.** `siprs-with-4layers` is the same project taken through the forward rotation to RESIDUE 0 and therefore holds what reverse rotation is trying to reconstruct; `siprs-for-reverse` is that project with those artefacts stripped and is what the analysis runs against. Comparing an output against the answer key yields a list of disagreements, never a score and never a verdict — classifying each disagreement is a human's work. P22-2 builds the harness; the tickets whose output is comparable run it.
(10) **The source-analysis technology is decided once, in P22-4, and never re-decided.** Four separate sessions (P22-4, P22-5, P22-6, P22-7) must parse the same Rust source, and no context passes between them. P22-4 evaluates the candidates **against the expert consultation recorded in `docs/ABOUT-ANALYSIS-TECH.md`**, records the choice and its rationale in **`docs/P22-ANALYSIS-TECH.md`**, and every later analysis ticket reads that document instead of choosing again. The repository offers no precedent to inherit — `.claude/scripts/rfc-graph/analyze-source-structure.js` is regex-based and is not equal to extracting guards, invariants and state machines — so the decision is genuinely open and must be made deliberately and written down. **The scope is six languages, not one**: Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Python and C/C++, because a technology that only handles the first target would be an implementation tuned to that target, which is explicitly forbidden. Two sessions independently choosing different parsers would produce mutually unreadable output and no test would catch it, because each session's tests would pass against its own choice. **The chosen toolchain is recorded in two places, and both are required**: the reasoning in `docs/P22-ANALYSIS-TECH.md`, and the machine-readable declaration in `ENV-DEPS.json` built by P22-1, where each new tool is added with the rotation that needs it and the ticket that provides it. Adding a tool is an entry in that declaration — never a new installation mechanism, and never a dependency left undeclared because it happened to be present on the machine where it was developed.
(11) **Match the surrounding directory, do not invent a layout.** The repository uses two conventions and they are not interchangeable. `.claude/scripts/rfc-graph/`, `grill-me-for-rfc/`, `conver/` and `tickets/` are flat CommonJS `.js` with no `lib/` subdirectory; `.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/`, `workspacify-allocate/` and `workspacify-reverse/` are ESM `.mjs` under `lib/`. A ticket that names a path must name one that matches its siblings, and must not introduce a `lib/` directory into a flat tree or a CommonJS module into an ESM one. The same applies to test files: `.test.cjs` beside CommonJS, `.test.mjs` beside ESM.
(12) **The expert answer received in `docs/ABOUT-ANALYSIS-TECH.md` (the section headed 「専門家の回答」, with the request-side verification record in its §7) is binding on the analysis design. Three of its corrections outrank any earlier wording in this repository, including the wording of earlier P22 tickets.** (a) `observed` may only ever mean *a fact read from the source text or its syntax tree*. Runtime behaviour, dynamic dispatch targets, post-preprocessing composition and generated code are not `observed` without execution, build or trace evidence, so every evidence item carries `evidence_mode`: `source_static` | `build_semantic` | `runtime_dynamic`. (b) `derivation_group` is **not** a deterministic identifier for a human design intent — that cannot be computed from file contents. It is a lineage graph over observable relations (same AST span, same generator, same commit, same data-flow origin), and independence is an explicit stored aggregation policy over that graph; `independence_assessment: "unknown"` is a legal and expected value, not a failure. (c) E13 is **TCE** (trivial / syntactic / compiler-normalisation equivalence). General semantic equivalence is undecidable and is not a goal; an AST-normalised match proves syntactic equivalence under a named configuration and nothing more. (d) Where the answer separates a *candidate* from a *decided* fact (E11, E13, E14), the separation is enforced at the type level — a candidate cannot be passed, stored or serialised where a decided fact is required — and a candidate carries `requires_human_approval`. A session that finds itself asserting a contract, an equivalence or a generated test as settled has violated this premise. **§7 of that document also records one error of ours that the answer exposed: the claim that CodeQL does not support Rust was wrong.**

## This ticket — P22-2

**Goal**: Establish, before any analysis code is written, both how generality will be judged and how the analysis will be measured against known ground truth.

**Purpose**: Two questions have to be answered by measurement rather than assertion: does the method work on a project other than the one it was developed against, and how much of a known correct answer does it actually recover. The first needs a frozen holdout. The second needs an answer key, and one already exists in the repository.

**Motivation**: This is the open item recorded in ABOUT-REVERSE 11.9, and the user has stated the constraint directly: an implementation or analysis test tuned to siprs such that it only appears to succeed must never be produced. `siprs-with-4layers` is the same project taken through the forward rotation to RESIDUE 0, so it holds the RFC, the graph, the partition, the tickets and the contract annotations that reverse rotation is trying to reconstruct. Comparing against it converts "does the analysis look plausible" into a concrete, falsifiable disagreement list. The paired-tree method is not new here — PX-203's `tests/workspacify-reverse/integration/real-tree.test.mjs` already names `siprs-with-4layers` as `PRISTINE_ROOT` — but it has never been used as a validity instrument for the analysis stages.

**Constraints**: The holdout is frozen the moment it is selected. Any adjustment to the analysis after seeing holdout results invalidates those results, and only the first run is reported. The protocol must prevent the executor from reaching ground truth (`*-GRAPH.json`, `RFC-*.md`, `Tickets.json`, `README.md`). Eligibility is decided by a human; the machine supplies a capability profile and never a boolean. The answer key is likewise frozen and held outside the target root, and reconciliation produces a disagreement list — never a score, a ratio presented as a grade, or a pass/fail verdict, all of which would be the mechanical success judgement this design rejects.

**Where this ticket sits in the 22.** 1 regression gate · **→2 experiment design (holdout + answer key)** · 3 spike · 4 R0-R2 scope and structure · 5 R3-R3.5 semantics and ledger · 6 R4-R5.5 history, gaps, oracle · 7 R6-R6.5 Red plan and falsification · 8 R7-R8 serving and origin spec · 9 command and zg · 10 forward schemas · 11 workspacify-tree reverse · 12 workspacify-allocate reverse · 13 grill reverse · 14 graphify reverse · 15 boundify reverse · 16 split-to-tickets reverse · 17 omission and RESIDUE return · 18 dynamic analysis · 19 Red execution · 20 logical/physical two-layer · 21 staleness into drill · 22 security lane

**Step 0 — before you write anything.** Confirm `siprs-with-4layers/RFC-ROOT-GRAPH.json`, `RFC-ROOT-Dirs-Tree.json`, `Tickets.json` and `omissions/` all exist and that `git status --porcelain -- siprs-with-4layers` is empty. A modified answer key invalidates every measurement taken against it. **Also record the known delta described in this ticket** — without it the first reconciliation reports eleven phantom disagreements that are known and intentional, and a human will waste the classification pass on them.
tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】The ledger loads, every recorded sha256 recomputes, and `verifyIsolation(root)` confirms that no ground-truth artefact is reachable from the target root. The answer key is extracted into a frozen oracle bundle recording, for `siprs-with-4layers`, the 113 graph nodes and 153 edges, the Dirs-Tree, the 146 tickets across 21 phases, the 8 omission files, the 232 `@verifies` annotations, the 379 files carrying `[::TICKET::]` and the 143 files carrying an `Initial Design Artifact` header. Each ineligible candidate is accompanied by the reason it was rejected. **The bundle also records the known structural delta between the two trees**, measured rather than assumed, so that a known difference is never presented as a finding.
- 【On error】A post-freeze modification of a holdout or of the answer key is detected as a sha256 mismatch naming the artefact. Planted ground truth is reported by filename. Neither condition is silently tolerated, and a reconciliation run against a modified oracle is refused rather than reported.
- 【Internal state】The ledger and the oracle bundle are append-only: a frozen sha256 cannot be rewritten. Verification never writes to the holdout tree, and never writes to `siprs-with-4layers` — that tree is the answer key and any modification to it destroys every measurement taken against it.
- 【Boundary】Zero holdouts exits 0 with the explicit statement that none were selected, rather than being read as failure. A holdout whose language cannot be determined is reported as unknown rather than raising. A reconciliation that finds zero disagreements is reported as a finding requiring scrutiny, because zero disagreement between two independent derivations is a signal of contamination rather than of accuracy.
scope: **Scope:**
- [File] `tests/workspacify-reverse/holdout/`, `tests/workspacify-reverse/oracle/`, `lib/oracle-bundle.mjs`, `lib/reconcile.mjs`, `docs/HOLDOUT-PROTOCOL.md`, `docs/ANSWER-KEY.md` (new)
- [Action] add

- [Detail] **Record the known structural delta between the two trees.** The subject is not a byte-copy of the answer key: PX-203 removed forward artefacts, stripped trace comments and headers from 146 shared files, renamed ten ticket-keyed test files to content-hash names, and removed one L3 test function (`purpose_scope_remains_audio_only` in `src/client.rs`, which read `RFC-ROOT.md`). The bundle records each of these as an expected difference with its evidence, so the reconciliation can label them `expected` instead of emitting them as disagreements. The rename map is recoverable rather than guessed: the answer key names the originals, and `Cargo.toml` line alignment recovers `verify_spec_p9_1 → verify_spec_e0606bc3`, `p10_1 → a4ecaf0f`, `p8_2 → 0963da9b` and `p9_2 → f330ed39`.

- [Detail] Select and freeze two or three projects from domains and languages other than siprs, and document the blind protocol: executor isolation, no reachable ground truth, first-run-only reporting. Selection follows the eligibility conditions in ABOUT-REVERSE 3.6 — the project builds, its tests run, it has meaningful history, its primary language is analysable, and its directory structure carries meaning. **In the same ticket, extract the answer key from `siprs-with-4layers` into a frozen oracle bundle and build the reconciliation harness**: for each reverse-rotation stage, name the oracle artefact it is comparable against, extract the comparison, and emit a disagreement list. The stage-to-oracle mapping is: R1/R2 structure against `RFC-ROOT-Dirs-Tree.json`; R3 contract candidates against the 232 `@verifies` annotations; R5 gaps against the 8 `omissions/OMISSIONS-*.json` files; R6 absent-Red against the 379 `[::TICKET::]` files and the ten `verify_spec_*.rs` tests; R8 claims against `RFC-ROOT.md`; P22-11 partition against the Dirs-Tree; P22-14 grounding against the 113-node graph; P22-15 headers against the 143 `Initial Design Artifact` files; P22-16 mapping against the 146 tickets.
- [Before→After] Whether the analysis is any good can only be asserted → every comparable stage can be measured against known ground truth and its disagreements listed

- [API] `run.mjs holdout` to build and verify the ledger; `run.mjs oracle freeze` to extract the answer key; `run.mjs oracle compare --stage <r1|r2|r3|r5|r6|r8|partition|grounding|headers|mapping>` to emit a disagreement list; `verifyIsolation(root)` as a callable check

- [Schema] `{ holdouts: [{ id, path, language, sha256, frozenAt }], protocolVersion }`; `ORACLE-BUNDLE.json` shaped `{ source, frozenAt, sha256, artefacts: { graph, dirsTree, tickets, omissions, verifies, ticketMarkers, designHeaders } }`
- [Config] None
- [Dependency] None

**Out of scope:** Running the reverse rotation against the holdout. That happens only after every P22 ticket is complete, under this protocol. Deciding what a disagreement means is also out of scope — the harness lists them and stops.

**Affected areas:** The validity of the entire experiment. P22-3 runs under this protocol and takes the first measurement; P22-5, P22-6, P22-8, P22-11, P22-14, P22-15 and P22-16 each run the comparison for their own stage.
testUnit: **UT:[normal]** UT-1 `loadLedger()` reads the ledger and recomputes every recorded sha256. UT-2 `verifyIsolation(root)` returns clean for a root from which ground truth has been removed. UT-3 `evaluateEligibility(candidate)` emits a capability, observability, falsifiability and risk profile. UT-4 `freezeOracle()` extracts the answer key and records, for `siprs-with-4layers`, 113 graph nodes, 153 edges, 146 tickets across 21 phases, 8 omission files, 232 `@verifies` annotations, 379 `[::TICKET::]` files and 143 design-header files.

**UT:[error]** UT-5 a holdout modified after freezing is detected as a sha256 mismatch naming the holdout id. UT-6 ground truth planted inside the target root is reported by filename. UT-7 `evaluateEligibility` never emits a boolean `eligible` field — asserted by inspecting the returned object keys, which is what prevents the machine from silently acquiring the authority to decide. UT-8 a reconciliation requested against an oracle whose sha256 does not match the frozen value is refused rather than run. UT-9 `extractKnownDelta()` records each expected difference — the artefact-only files, the 146 trace-stripped shared files, the ten renames and the one removed test function — with its evidence, and a reconciliation over a known difference labels it `expected` rather than emitting it as a disagreement.

**UT:[boundary]** UT-10 an empty ledger exits 0 and states that none were selected. UT-11 a candidate whose primary language cannot be determined is reported as unknown rather than throwing. UT-12 a single holdout is a valid ledger. UT-13 zero disagreements is reported as a finding requiring scrutiny rather than as agreement. UT-14 a stage whose analysis could not run over part of the target is reported with **the kind of unobserved** — the region, the phase at which it stopped, and the reason — as a first-class entry alongside the disagreements, and is never rendered as "no disagreement found" for that region. UT-15 a run over a corpus whose language the chosen stack cannot semantically resolve emits a lower `analysis_mode` for that corpus, and the reconciliation carries that mode beside every disagreement it produced from it.

UT-18 the reconciliation never writes to `siprs-with-4layers` — asserted by comparing that tree's digest before and after every comparison. UT-19 `reconcile()` returns a list of disagreements, each tagged with a kind, and carries no score, ratio or verdict field — asserted by inspecting the returned object keys.

testExceptions: **Item**: Deciding what a reconciliation disagreement means. **Why it is not testable**: each disagreement is one of three things — the analysis missed something the forward rotation had, the analysis found something the forward rotation did not have, or the forward rotation's own artefact was a free choice rather than a necessary one — and distinguishing them depends on intent, which neither tree records. This is not a design defect; it is the deliberate boundary of the design, which builds the instrument that makes the question concrete and leaves the judgement to a human. Mechanising it would be exactly the mechanical success judgement the design rejects. **Alternative verification**: assert that `reconcile()` returns a list of individually named disagreements, that it carries no score, ratio or verdict field, that the run refuses to proceed against an oracle whose sha256 has changed, and that `siprs-with-4layers` is byte-identical afterwards. Those four assertions are UT-8, UT-18, UT-19 and IT-4.

**Item**: The final eligibility judgement for a holdout candidate. **Why it is not testable**: eligibility is a human decision, and mechanising it would invent a fixed threshold that is a false criterion — exactly the failure ABOUT-REVERSE 7.7.2 warns against. This is not a design defect; it is the core principle of the design, which places success judgement with a human and not with a script. **Alternative verification**: assert that `evaluateEligibility` returns capability, observability, falsifiability and risk dimensions and never returns a boolean `eligible` key. That assertion is UT-7 and it is executable.

Green: `holdout-ledger.mjs`, `isolation-check.mjs`, `oracle-bundle.mjs`, `reconcile.mjs`. Add the `holdout` and `oracle` subcommands to `run.mjs`. Select and freeze the candidates. Freeze the answer key. Write both protocol documents. Prove isolation, drift detection and non-modification of the answer key with deliberately planted violations.

tickets.investigation:
- **Measured 2026-09-10.** `siprs-for-reverse` is now clean of forward traces after PX-203: L1 3923→0, L2 1538→0, L3 10→0, L4 160 kept, 52,689→46,565 lines, with all 20 IETF RFC references preserved. This is the prerequisite for treating it as a legitimate experiment input.
- No holdout of any kind exists yet. There is no second project under `tests/workspacify-reverse/`, so generality currently rests entirely on assertion.
- **The answer key is present, quantified and untouched.** Measured 2026-09-10: `siprs-with-4layers` holds `RFC-ROOT.md`, `RFC-ROOT-GRAPH.json` (113 nodes, 153 edges), `RFC-ROOT-Dirs-Tree.json` (26,820 chars), `Tickets.json` (21 phases, 146 tickets), eight `omissions/OMISSIONS-*.json` files, 232 `@verifies` annotations, 379 files carrying `[::TICKET::]` and 143 files carrying an `Initial Design Artifact` header, across 4,272 files outside `target/`. `siprs-for-reverse` holds 0 of each of the trace kinds across 2,791 files. `git status --porcelain` is empty for both trees, so the answer key is pristine.
- The paired-tree method is already precedented in this repository rather than invented here: `tests/workspacify-reverse/integration/real-tree.test.mjs:24` already resolves `siprs-with-4layers` as `PRISTINE_ROOT`. PX-203 used the pair to prove the scrub was complete and non-destructive. What is new in this ticket is using the pair to measure the *analysis*, not the scrub.
- Neither tree is its own git repository; both are tracked inside the conver repository, so `git status --porcelain -- <tree>` is the correct non-modification check and is available without any new tooling.
- **The delta was measured, not assumed, and it is larger than "only the forward artefacts".** Comparing all files outside `target/`: 4,272 in the answer key against 2,791 in the subject; 2,781 shared; 1,491 present only in the answer key (`.claude` 1,239, `specs` 115, `drills` 82, `tests` 10, `omissions` 8, `docs` 6, `tickets` 4, plus `RFC-ROOT.md`, `Tickets.json`, `Status.json`); 10 present only in the subject, these being the renamed test files; and **146 shared files whose content differs**. Checking those 146 with the comment character appropriate to each file type leaves only four, and all four are trace-related: `Cargo.toml` carries the rename references, two `.conf` files lost a `;` comment line, and `src/client.rs` lost the test function `purpose_scope_remains_audio_only`, which read `RFC-ROOT.md` and asserted its content — an L3 test removed whole by PX-203. **No line of production code changed.** That is what makes a disagreement attributable to the analysis rather than to a difference in the subject.
- **The expert answer appended to `docs/ABOUT-ANALYSIS-TECH.md` adds one requirement to this harness that the original design did not carry: reconcile by KIND, not by count.** Its eighth recommendation is explicit — when comparing against the forward-rotated corpus, record the kinds of error and the kinds of unobserved rather than an accuracy figure. Three consequences follow. (i) Every disagreement carries a kind, and the three existing kinds (missing from the analysis, extra in the analysis, divergent) are joined by a fourth class that is not a disagreement at all: **regions the analysis could not observe**. A stage that could not semantically resolve its input has not agreed with the answer key and has not disagreed with it; it never looked, and summing that into a disagreement count destroys the only signal that matters. (ii) Each disagreement carries the `analysis_mode` that produced it, so a low-confidence finding is distinguishable from a confident one. (iii) The output remains scoreless — this requirement adds structure, not a grade, and a per-kind tally is data rather than a verdict.
- **This is the instrument the technology decision is judged by.** `docs/ABOUT-ANALYSIS-TECH.md` §付録C states that the existence of this reconciliation is what fixes the selection criterion: a technology is not acceptable merely because it runs, but because it can say concretely where it diverged from a known-correct answer. This ticket therefore builds the thing that decides whether P22-4 chose well, which is why it is a separate ticket converging before the decision is used.
- The rename map is recoverable from the answer key rather than guessed. `Cargo.toml` line alignment yields `verify_spec_p9_1 → verify_spec_e0606bc3`, `p10_1 → a4ecaf0f`, `p8_2 → 0963da9b`, `p9_2 → f330ed39`. The content hashes do not match their originals because PX-203 hashed the scrubbed content, so the remaining six need content-based recovery.
- **The answer key names the ticket that produced each test.** `siprs-with-4layers/tests/` holds ten files named `verify_spec_<phase>_<ticket>.rs`: `p0_1`, `p7_3`, `p8_2`, `p8_3`, `p8_7`, `p9_1`, `p9_2`, `p9_3`, `p9_5`, `p10_1`. That is direct ground truth for P22-16's test-to-ticket mapping, and it is the reason that stage can be measured at all.
- The concrete risk is not hypothetical: every measurement so far — layer counts, rename behaviour, `include_str!` detection — was developed against siprs. A method that only handles siprs's single-crate Rust layout with a `vendor/` directory would pass every existing test while being useless in general.
- ABOUT-REVERSE 3.6 lists five eligibility conditions (builds, tests run, history exists, primary language analysable, directory structure meaningful). These are stated as conditions for a human to assess, not as a scoring function.
- ABOUT-REVERSE 7.7.2 explicitly rejects a fixed threshold for scope selection. That is the reason the ledger stores a profile rather than a verdict.
- Ground-truth artefact names to be treated as contaminated: `*-GRAPH.json`, `RFC-*.md`, `Tickets.json`, `README.md`. These are the shapes the reverse rotation would otherwise be able to read directly.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- Functions are verb phrases (`loadLedger`, `freezeHoldout`, `verifyIsolation`, `evaluateEligibility`, `freezeOracle`, `reconcile`); variables are domain concepts (`holdoutId`, `frozenDigest`, `isolationViolations`, `capabilityProfile`, `oracleArtefact`, `disagreementKind`). The `is`/`has` prefix convention is used for booleans as the coding-style rule requires.
- The contamination filename list is a named constant, not an inline literal repeated in three places.
- The stage-to-oracle mapping is a declared table rather than a chain of conditionals, so adding a stage means adding a row and the comparison for every stage is readable as a list.

C002 precondition — "a holdout has been frozen": loadLedger() refuses a ledger that does not exist rather than inventing one.
```js
assert.throws(
  () => loadLedger({ projectRoot: emptyProject }),
  (error) => { assert.match(error.message, /HOLDOUTS\.json/); assert.match(error.message, /holdout freeze/); return true; },
);
```

C002 invariant — "the ledger is append-only": a second freeze of the same id with different content is refused.
```js
assert.throws(() => freezeLedger({ projectRoot, candidates: [ELIGIBLE_A], frozenAt: FROZEN_AT }), /append-only|already frozen/i);
```

C003 precondition — "a target root for reverse rotation is given": verifyIsolation() refuses a root that does not exist.
```js
assert.throws(
  () => verifyIsolation(join(projectRoot, 'absent-root')),
  (error) => { assert.match(error.message, /absent-root/); return true; },
);
```

assert.throws(
  () => reconcile({ stage: 'r99', candidate: R3_CANDIDATE, bundle, knownDelta: EMPTY_DELTA }),
  (error) => { assert.match(error.message, /r99/); assert.match(error.message, STAGE_ORACLE_STAGES.map((row) => row.stage).join('|')); return true; },
);
```

assert.throws(
  () => freezeHoldout({ candidate: { id: 'file-not-tree', path: 'README.md' }, projectRoot, frozenAt: FROZEN_AT }),
  (error) => { assert.match(error.message, /not a directory|file-not-tree/); return true; },
);
```

tickets.background:
**Shared premises — binding on all 22 P22 tickets. Read this first.**

P22 implements the reverse rotation: taking a project that already contains a substantial implementation and turning it into conver's four loops (upstream / implementation / release / evolution). Forward rotation already works completely; reverse rotation does not exist yet. `docs/ABOUT-REVERSE.md` is the full design. The implementation loop runs one ticket per session and context does not carry across tickets, so this block is repeated verbatim in all 22 tickets. A session that sees only its own ticket must still know what the whole is for and what it may not break.

(1) **Never break the forward rotation.** The four existing loops work. No change in P22 may alter forward behaviour. A byte-identical `manifest_hash` over the forward fixtures, captured before any change and reproduced after, is the only accepted proof. P22-1 builds that gate; every later ticket runs it after its own step. "It looks fine" is not evidence and is not accepted.
(2) **Rewriting any `.claude/commands/*.md` is strictly forbidden.** Only edits are permitted — append, or correct the minimum number of lines. The Language Protocol table, the First-Class Rule, the workflow steps and the script list must survive character for character. The nine existing command files are: `workspacify-tree`, `workspacify-allocate`, `grill-me-for-rfc`, `graphify-rfc`, `boundify-graph`, `split-to-tickets`, `find-omissions`, `crystalize-readme`, `drill-rfc-down`. P22-9 additionally *creates* `workspacify-reverse.md`, which is a new file, not an edit.
(3) The full design lives in **`docs/ABOUT-REVERSE.md`**. Each ticket cites the exact sections it depends on. Read those sections before implementing; they are the specification of record.
(4) The machine may only ever say **"proved" or "not proved"**. "Succeeded" and "failed" are not in its vocabulary, because whether reverse engineering succeeded is a judgement a human makes after several loop rounds. Any script that emits a boolean success verdict is wrong by construction.
(5) What is deterministic, a script decides and the AI accepts the verdict. Only genuinely semantic judgement is left to the AI, and the material it needs is placed in front of it — as plain, deliberately helpful English — immediately before the decision. Do not widen the AI's judgement surface beyond what the design calls for.
(6) The `[::STUB::]` marker discipline is absolute and admits no exception. Any incomplete implementation carries a marker naming the ticket that will resolve it.
(7) Output format: emit JSON only when another script consumes it, a schema validates it, a hash covers it, or a gate uses it as a predicate. **Anything the AI reads in order to decide is Markdown, written in plain and deliberately helpful English.** Struggling to read a script's output is a defect in the script, not a cost of doing business.
(8) The `Initial Design Artifact — RFC-driven Implementation` header is never deleted, altered or commented out (supreme law 4). This holds without exception, including in files this phase touches.
(9) **The paired trees are the measuring instrument.** `siprs-with-4layers` is the same project taken through the forward rotation to RESIDUE 0 and therefore holds what reverse rotation is trying to reconstruct; `siprs-for-reverse` is that project with those artefacts stripped and is what the analysis runs against. Comparing an output against the answer key yields a list of disagreements, never a score and never a verdict — classifying each disagreement is a human's work. P22-2 builds the harness; the tickets whose output is comparable run it.
(10) **The source-analysis technology is decided once, in P22-4, and never re-decided.** Four separate sessions (P22-4, P22-5, P22-6, P22-7) must parse the same Rust source, and no context passes between them. P22-4 evaluates the candidates **against the expert consultation recorded in `docs/ABOUT-ANALYSIS-TECH.md`**, records the choice and its rationale in **`docs/P22-ANALYSIS-TECH.md`**, and every later analysis ticket reads that document instead of choosing again. The repository offers no precedent to inherit — `.claude/scripts/rfc-graph/analyze-source-structure.js` is regex-based and is not equal to extracting guards, invariants and state machines — so the decision is genuinely open and must be made deliberately and written down. **The scope is six languages, not one**: Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Python and C/C++, because a technology that only handles the first target would be an implementation tuned to that target, which is explicitly forbidden. Two sessions independently choosing different parsers would produce mutually unreadable output and no test would catch it, because each session's tests would pass against its own choice. **The chosen toolchain is recorded in two places, and both are required**: the reasoning in `docs/P22-ANALYSIS-TECH.md`, and the machine-readable declaration in `ENV-DEPS.json` built by P22-1, where each new tool is added with the rotation that needs it and the ticket that provides it. Adding a tool is an entry in that declaration — never a new installation mechanism, and never a dependency left undeclared because it happened to be present on the machine where it was developed.
(11) **Match the surrounding directory, do not invent a layout.** The repository uses two conventions and they are not interchangeable. `.claude/scripts/rfc-graph/`, `grill-me-for-rfc/`, `conver/` and `tickets/` are flat CommonJS `.js` with no `lib/` subdirectory; `.claude/scripts/workspacify-tree/`, `workspacify-allocate/` and `workspacify-reverse/` are ESM `.mjs` under `lib/`. A ticket that names a path must name one that matches its siblings, and must not introduce a `lib/` directory into a flat tree or a CommonJS module into an ESM one. The same applies to test files: `.test.cjs` beside CommonJS, `.test.mjs` beside ESM.
(12) **The expert answer received in `docs/ABOUT-ANALYSIS-TECH.md` (the section headed 「専門家の回答」, with the request-side verification record in its §7) is binding on the analysis design. Three of its corrections outrank any earlier wording in this repository, including the wording of earlier P22 tickets.** (a) `observed` may only ever mean *a fact read from the source text or its syntax tree*. Runtime behaviour, dynamic dispatch targets, post-preprocessing composition and generated code are not `observed` without execution, build or trace evidence, so every evidence item carries `evidence_mode`: `source_static` | `build_semantic` | `runtime_dynamic`. (b) `derivation_group` is **not** a deterministic identifier for a human design intent — that cannot be computed from file contents. It is a lineage graph over observable relations (same AST span, same generator, same commit, same data-flow origin), and independence is an explicit stored aggregation policy over that graph; `independence_assessment: "unknown"` is a legal and expected value, not a failure. (c) E13 is **TCE** (trivial / syntactic / compiler-normalisation equivalence). General semantic equivalence is undecidable and is not a goal; an AST-normalised match proves syntactic equivalence under a named configuration and nothing more. (d) Where the answer separates a *candidate* from a *decided* fact (E11, E13, E14), the separation is enforced at the type level — a candidate cannot be passed, stored or serialised where a decided fact is required — and a candidate carries `requires_human_approval`. A session that finds itself asserting a contract, an equivalence or a generated test as settled has violated this premise. **§7 of that document also records one error of ours that the answer exposed: the claim that CodeQL does not support Rust was wrong.**

## This ticket — P22-3

**Goal**: Find out whether the design actually runs, at the lowest possible cost, before building all of Phase 0.

**Purpose**: Building every Phase 0 component and only then discovering that the approach does not work is the worst available outcome. One vertical slice through the three load-bearing stages tests the hypothesis early.

**Motivation**: ABOUT-REVERSE 6.13.1 item −1-c, and the resolution of question R-7 recorded in 11.5. How many decision cards a real project produces cannot be estimated on paper; the spike converts that question into a measurement instead of an argument. More importantly, the spike is the first point at which the analysis can be run against the answer key from P22-2, so it is the first honest test of whether the design recovers anything true.

**Constraints**: The spike may be thrown away; the measurement report may not. The report is a Phase 0 completion condition per 6.13.3. Run it on `siprs-for-reverse`, not on a holdout, and follow the P22-2 protocol so the run is recorded as a first run. The answer key stays outside the target root: the spike's executor must not read `siprs-with-4layers`, and the comparison is performed afterwards against the frozen bundle.

**Where this ticket sits in the 22.** 1 regression gate · 2 experiment design (holdout + answer key) · **→3 spike** · 4 R0-R2 scope and structure · 5 R3-R3.5 semantics and ledger · 6 R4-R5.5 history, gaps, oracle · 7 R6-R6.5 Red plan and falsification · 8 R7-R8 serving and origin spec · 9 command and zg · 10 forward schemas · 11 workspacify-tree reverse · 12 workspacify-allocate reverse · 13 grill reverse · 14 graphify reverse · 15 boundify reverse · 16 split-to-tickets reverse · 17 omission and RESIDUE return · 18 dynamic analysis · 19 Red execution · 20 logical/physical two-layer · 21 staleness into drill · 22 security lane

**Step 0 — before you write anything.** `node .claude/scripts/workspacify-reverse/run.mjs regression check` exits 0, and P22-2's oracle bundle is present and frozen.

Findings the report records, in order of importance:
1. UNRESOLVED RATE 85.5%. The blanket `#[cfg(...)]` trigger is what premise 12(a) literally requires (post-preprocessing composition is not `observed` without build evidence), and these seed files keep their assertions inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`. Verified this is not brace drift: the gate closes on exactly the module's closing line in all four files (117/55/350/85 lines, last gated claim 114/52/343/78). The consequence for R-7 is direct: most cards become requests for a judgement rather than recovered contracts. P22-5 must decide whether the test profile deserves its own scope value instead of `unresolved`.
2. CONTRACT-ID COMPARISON IS DEGENERATE. Stage r3 returns 267 disagreements: 198 missing (every C### in the answer key) and 69 extra (every claim id this ledger produces). PX-203 removed every @verifies comment from the subject, so the two namespaces cannot intersect. Recorded as the measured gap it is; no attempt was made to fabricate C### correspondence, which would be the rubber-stamp failure mode itself.
3. A STRUCTURAL DISAGREEMENT WAS EXCUSED BY A CONTENT LABEL. src/model/dtmf_spec.rs exists in both trees and is absent from RFC-ROOT-Dirs-Tree.json, so the slice should report it as extra_in_analysis. It does not: KNOWN-DELTA records the file as trace-stripped, and reconcile keys expectedDifferences by name only, so the content-level expectation also excuses the partition-level disagreement. This is a P22-2 instrument limitation, reported rather than patched (reconcile.mjs is outside this ticket's declared files).
4. DECISION TIME NOT RECORDED. This session had no observer for it; humans-supplied samples were not invented. The report renders `not recorded` rather than 0, because a 0 would read as instant when it means unobserved.
